[h3]Summary[/h3]
I picked up Hydroneer for five bucks, and got 24 hours out of it. However, I wish I spent that time playing other titles. Not a bad game, just not for me.

[hr][/hr]
Once you have a fully automated mining setup, it's great to look at. [b]Completing long-term objectives feels good![/b] There isn't a de jure objective, but the player is free to sandbox and make their own goals. 

Unfortunately, no matter how nice it feels to have fully exploited a dig site, it's soured by the agony of the moment-to-moment gameplay getting to that point. I have five major gripes that stop me from recommending this to others. Consider how you, a prospective purchaser, would feel about the following:

[h3]Pre-Automation Gameplay & Controls[/h3]
Before you can buy your first drill and conveyor belts, you manually dig dirt and pan for ore to make money. Sounds good at face-value, but ohhh boy... The devs have stated that to improve realism, the game has no inventory system and your character can only use one arm at a time. Here's what you can expect upon clicking New Game:

Press E to pick up pan. Go to river and press E to drop pan into river. Press E to pick up your pan with water in it. Go to dig site. Press E to drop pan on ground. Press E to pick up shovel. Left click ground, left click bucket. Press E to drop shovel. Press E to pick up bucket. Left click to dump bucket into water-filled pan. Press E to drop bucket. Press E to pick up brush. Left click pan to exchange slurry for ore nuggets. Press E to drop brush. Press E to pick up ore-filled pan.

I just pressed E [u]eleven times[/u] to manage the tools in my hand, and that's not mentioning the camera swinging around to look at the various vessels, or movement between them if you don't think to move everything as close as possible to speed up the process. You may notice that you can put dirt directly in the pan and skip the bucket - you can (and I did, thinking I had found a shortcut), but lo and behold the tutorial doesn't mention that you can fill the bucket with four scoops of dirt at a time. What do I get for this rigamarole? About thirty coins. You need to pick up those coins and move them around like a tool, by the way, since pockets have yet to be invented.

[h3]Obtaining and Placing Buildings[/h3]
Just like handling tools, every building block of your operation needs to be carried one by one and placed manually. I found myself frequently needing to pick up tens of items at a time to complete a build I had in mind, and to do that I need to pick up each item, hit a 180 and place it in a "checkout" rectangle, then run back and forth however many times it took to amass the pile. If you need more than nine conveyor belts at a time, good luck fitting them on that rectangle! I really wish I could submit an order to the shop owner and have them load up a box containing my goods.

Getting more than one drill is even stranger - you can't just buy a second drill with coins. You need to pump out a certain weight of ore (more on weight in the next section), smelt it into a bar, and take it across the map [spoiler]into a mystical dwarven-esque super forge with cartoonishly large anvil[/spoiler] to hand craft a new drill. This is also how you can get better drills, but even if you drive, you still need to ferry your materials into the spot by hand. A small gripe, but it was an "ugh" whenever I had to make the trip.

There was clearly some attempts to make this better - you start with a cart and vehicle to move items longer distances, and you can buy a pallet that will lock items in place for carrying shorter distances. I used the pallet myself towards the end, but you still need to carefully stack as much as you can on the thing by hand to make it worthwhile. Physics is the enemy here.

Putting a mining setup together is mostly good. I ran into a few issues accidentally picking up belts that I had placed when I was aiming for the ore that it held, but that's remedied by a construction hammer tool that disables the ability to pick buildings up. The issue comes when you need to move anything at all; it's the same story of mashing E to pick up a building, move it to a pile, drop the thing, and repeat until you're ready to do that again in reverse. Tearing down my Tier 1 setup and building the Tier 2 setup didn't leave me with joy as much as relief that it was done and I could continue smelting the good stuff.

[h3]NPC Requests & Weight[/h3]
NPCs can give you requisition request in exchange for tokens, used to buy late-game pipes and tools. I grabbed a few requests, but ran into another thing the tutorial didn't mention: weight. The game's de facto quantity, it doesn't matter if you have a thousand bars of steel if they only weight a kilogram combined. All NPC requests are for a single item that weighs at least X units, and buddy, you don't start with a scale. There ain't even a scale in the shop that you start by! The wiki had to help me out on this one, because as far as I've seen, it's just not discussed in the game.

Now that I'm writing this, I'm reminded of a small gripe: even had I walked into the another town's shop, all the items for sale are just scattered about piecemeal on tables. There's a very real chance you just don't notice that there's, say, a single grey chisel next to all those grey wrenches, and the chisel lets you do X game mechanic. I say this because I missed the chisel that sits on the table full of wrenches, of course.

[h3]Non-Mining Content[/h3]
This section is devoted entirely to farming, something that also wasn't in the tutorial. Aye, there's fishing too, but that's content that I just never interacted with at all. You fish and sell fish for coins, done and dusted.

Half of the NPC requests are for mining-related goods, and half are for bowls of soup that you make out of vegetables you grow. This is mostly fine, I suppose; I didn't put too much time into farming as I only discovered how to do it when I was already winding down. The main issue is how you're expected to actually grow the veg - put pipes over each crop and have them drip to water the plot. This looks and feels very strange, and leads to a sort of idle game where you leave your sprouts to grow while you do anything else. A basic tomato plant takes about ten minutes to grow, and results in very little surplus if you turn crops back into more seeds.

There are tools to help with this, but anything related to farming beyond the bare necessities is gated behind tokens gained by completing farming requests in the first place. Give a bowl of soup, get about thirty tokens. That'll get you a watering can, which is super useful and... wait, a sprinkler to more effectively water crops automatically is [b]OVER TWO-THOUSAND TOKENS????[/b] Time to abort this venture.

[h3]No Sauce[/h3]
This is a small thing that's very understandable for a small dev team to have difficulty with, but the game has no sauce. What do I mean by sauce? I mean there's a lack of aesthetic polish that tickles the player's brain while playing. Click new game, and you're just plopped into the game world with no frills or showmanship. Digging by hand or by machine doesn't feel like it has any weight to it. In general, gameplay feels static and non-reactive.

Y'ever play Peggle? In Peggle, when you fire at the last peg on the screen, the camera zooms in and time slows down to show the weight of that last hit. I'm not saying that every game needs to have, like, Vampire Survivors' sensory overload levels of sauce, but it's really just about giving feedback to the player. There is some satisfaction seeing a row of drills all spit out a little plop of dirt together, but I was hoping for something more visceral about the pounding of machine versus nature. This is a skill that can be honed, and I'm sure their next title will be all the better for it.

Immediately repetitive and not fun. Here's how the game works: You can only hold one item at a time. You need to drop the item you're holding onto the ground before you can pick up something else. Nothing in the game has an "interact" button, you instead interact with them by dropping objects on top of them. This is interesting at first, but it gets boring really fast. You can't just refill your bucket from the river. You have to drop your bucket into the river, run after it if it tumbles away from you, and pick it back up. Next you have to pour that water into your pan, but you can't just interact with your pan. You instead have to aim the bucket correctly for the water to pour in. And that wouldn't be such a problem if the bucket got poured where you aim. Instead, it gets poured a feet to the right of where you aim, so you have to aim to the left of the pan. You then have to add dirt to your pan and use a brush on it, but again you can only hold one item at a time. So you have to pick up the shovel, put a shovelful of dirt into the pan, then drop the shovel onto the ground. Pick up the brush, click once, drop it onto the ground again. So you're constantly grabbing and dropping objects, and they do all have physics so if anything rolls away from you, better start chasing!

Okay, you finally have a bunch of ores and gems. Great, right? Well except "you can only hold one item" also applies to these. So you can't just pick all of them up. You either have to keep them all in your pan and carry your pan, or move them to a cart and pull the cart behind you. If you do put them on the cart like I did, woe to you because once you get to where you sell them, you can't just sell everything on your cart. You need to move each ore and gem, one by one, onto the merchant's table (in the game's defense, if you keep everything in your pan then you can put the whole pan down on the table).

Yes, now you have sold the fruits of your labor and you have some cash. Except, again the "1 item only" applies to the money too. You can't just put the money in your pocket. You have to carry it around as a physical object, haul it to the merchant where you buy stuff, and drop it into their payment bucket. It is also funny to note: if you put two piles of money together they merge, but you know how you split a pile? You have to use a saw. Like this is just ridiculous, I can't just right click to split a stack or something. No you have to use a saw. Wow.

And the worst part is you do all of this, and they you have a tiny amount of money. So you're gonna have to keep repeating this a bunch so you can earn enough to buy equipment so you can start crafting things like jewelry to make a bit more money. After about 20 minutes, I've had enough. I don't want to have to spin my camera around chasing a shovel and a bucket so I can make a tiny bit of money, to maybe see what the game has next.

Ok, this is definitely a niche game.  You have to love go-at-your-own-pace gaming and be willing to set your own goals in a sandbox. It's pretty satisfying for the Minecraft crowd.  
There are quirks, some of them are pretty hard to overcome, like the dropping of held items off-center.  When you eventually get used to this as a feature, you can pick rocks, ore, fish, vegetables up and drop them in your container offset to the side rapidly. Learning to position correctly makes a ton of difference in gameplay quality of life.
Also, you can hold the drop button to instead place the item at your cursor, that can be really helpful for handing off quest requests or precision placement of buckets and the like.  
I've got 100 hours, I'm not done with all the goals I've come up with, I know there's a few other easter eggs out there, but mostly I relax with an audiobook and full buckets with dirt, looking for those rare ores.

鉄や金を採掘・加工してお金を稼ぐゲームです。
効率化や試行錯誤、自動化の仕組みを作ることが好きな人におすすめです。

序盤はすべて手作業で行う必要があり、正直かなり大変です。
しかしお金を稼ぎ、設備を少しずつ整えていくことで作業は自動化され、効率が一気に上がっていきます。
この「不便な状態から仕組みを作り上げていく過程」が本作の核です。

一方で、システム面はかなり不便です。
アイテムバックのようなものがないため、アイテムをまとめて持つ手段はなく、基本的に一つずつ運ぶ必要があります。
お金も財布のような概念がなく、手に持って運びます。
買い物も一つずつ選択する必要があり、効率よく進めるには工夫が求められます。

また、操作ミスでバケツやパンニング皿をひっくり返してしまい、せっかく集めた資源を散らばせてしまうこともあります。
アイテムを落とす位置も最初は分かりにくく、設定で表示を調整することでようやく扱いやすくなります。

自動化が進むと別の問題も出てきます。
資材が詰まるとアイテムが溜まり続け、動作が重くなる原因になります。
不要な土や素材を削除するなど、安定して動かすための管理も必要になります。

このように不便な点はいくつもありますが、それらを乗り越えて自動化設備が完成し、安定してお金が流れ始めたときの達成感は非常に大きいです。

効率化や試行錯誤、自動化の仕組みを作ることが好きな人には強くおすすめできます。
不便さを受け入れ、その先の達成感を楽しめる人向けのゲームです。

This game gets very repetitive after you begin to get drills and conveyers because its the same cycle of melting down iron/core + clot in icehelm, making drills, buying needed pipes and conveyers, waiting for more ore to build up, then repeating this cycle.

This is one of those were I wish there was a "Meh" recommendation.

I watched RCE play it and years later I pulled the trigger while it was on sale and for that, it gave me enough entertainment to totally justify the money spent. BUT

While many lament the slow start, with which I have no issue, for me it's the missing endgame,... or lategame... or midgame XD
Once you have your first machines up and running, making money becomes trivial, since you have to wait FOREVER for your machines to further enough Cloutium to build a T2 drill, the gold and gemstones mount up and you can easily buy the logic stuff to automate repairing your machines - which is urgently needed as they break sooooooooo quickly. 
And once you have a T2 drill waiting for enough Coreore to get a T3 has you swimming in so much money you could nuke very plot 10 times over, but what for? 
Advancing a drill tier doesn't make your life easier, the buying and selling stays as tedious as it is in the very beginning, no "craftable coinpurse" our fasttravel or progressively better vehicles or locomotion or transportation. There is one kind of conveyor that never changes, there are only 3 tiers of rake pickaxe and shovel, with their differences being not that wild especially shovel and rake only means you can do the same thing further down but not a bigger area. There is nothing you can build helping you in finding relics...

Like I said it's fun for a while but it quickly goes nowhere, and it's balanced poorly in terms of how quickly you get later stage resources vs how much gold and iron you amass in the meantime. 

I got it with the Volcalidus DLC and it seems that adds a little more story and maybe progression, also maybe some QoL improvements but I am kind of spent on bulding for the sake of building. Much potential, little done since I watched RCE years ago.

TL:DR - here is just no real progression, the fishing and farming is even more rudimentary - so once you can build a T3 drill and place it your left wondering, what to even still do, and what to even work towards.

review:
Very tedious; and a walking simulator.

The first part of the game, doing things manually, is very slow. Repeat an action a hundred times, and walk from one place to the other again and again. Long paths just to sell, get money, and buy.

The second part, you start to automate things a bit, with machines that... Launch the items... And you have to invest a lot of time placing the baskets correctly. Not something you would expect from a pseudo-automation game.

The third part, where you start building a lot of logic and things... I didn't reach it. Making enough money is pure hell.

Controls are complicated, ores fall again and again, because it's hard to see where you're dropping the ores exactly. It gets better with experience, but anyway. Even placing the "buildings" is tedious.

And finally, I finished 1 quest with all the materials I had, dropped te coin on the floor to keep it there, and it disappeared behind a rock. Amazing moment to uninstall.

In general, the game is promising, but QoL is terrible, and I don't really see much "late game", apart of some random things distributed through the map. And there's really nothing tellling me "let's get there!".

As a technical detail, it lags every time it auto-saves the game.

Bought this a while ago. Thought that this would be the perfect game since it's just about starting small to progress to essentially a giant automated factory.

Most of what this game shows on the store page is incredibly misleading. In the first place, this isn't a base builder.
You CAN in fact "build a base" but what it boils down to is that some of the parts you can buy from shops include things like walls and a floor, then a tool that will make these impossible to pick up. It doesn't get more complicated than walls floors and ceilings, maybe a window in one shop, but there's no use for them anyways, which I could easily see someone looking at this page and the videos and assume it intertwined with the mining operation, allowing things like the automated smelter pouring out the metal, or being able to build elevator shafts. These are already pre-built locations in the game which you can't build or place. Completely removed from the actual game really.

Also by "dynamic weapon and jewelry crafting" Don't expect weapons to matter at all. They're simply another item to sell so smelting iron actually has some purpose. Which feeds into another massive issue I have being that you don't actually craft or make any of the tools to help with your mining or automation. Buckets, shovels, picks, pipes, anvils, smelters, furnaces, crucibles? None of it craftable, the game FORCES you to walk across an ENTIRE ISLAND in order to buy items like conveyer belts which are necessary for automation. Because of this the actual process of mining and creating this whole system just feels entirely unsatisfying. You may pick up the ore for the ultra powerful cloutium pipes, but all you'll do with it is smelt it into a bar, stack it in a bucket and sell it by walking a mile to the next town.

Then there are the quests, these are meant to be a way to force some amount of interest and engagement with the systems, because no longer are you just making rings and daggers since they're the easiest items to craft at the highest value, because john doe a town over might pay you 800 hydrocoins if you make him a gold dagger. Wait scratch that he wants a 200 weight gold bar composed dagger.

This is one of the starter quests, each gold ore is less than 1 weight, and you'll only be finding on average 0-2 gold ore every bucket of dirt. You also can't check the weight when you're smelting, so you'll have to be a freak like me where you'll take one ore, smelt it into a bar, craft a dagger, which will THEN show the weight, learn a 1 ore bar is .8 weight, so you'll need roughly 250 ore which which when 32 ore crafted into a gold dagger is 400 hydrocoins already, why the ♥♥♥♥ would I bother?

It's very much just busywork to make you feel like there's more under the surface.
Largely this entire game is a mess of scope. I genuinely think the no inventory system is a really fun challenge, and interesting way to do it. Just it leads to it being pick up, drop, pick up, and over the course of a few hours you'll pretty much get mad more at you're lack of depth perception for dropping things, and the physics system. I genuinely think this would have been an amazing game if they just didn't have an open world, and just had like a square plot of land that you could dig into rather endlessly, and then the ore smelting, crafting, digging and automation all fed into further building itself, rather than basically injecting 30 home depots with tools I don't need into the game not allowing the game about smelting and crafting to let you smelt and craft your tools, and then try to use money as some sort of pity reward for not having a better idea of how to make the player feel like they accomplished something.

There is NO INVENTORY system. You have to manually pick up each individual item off the ground to use it, EVEN MONEY!!! This suuuuuucks! Last time i'll ever by a "mostly positive reviews" game without playing the demo first to see if  it's good. TOTAL WASTE OF TIME.

review: GOOD GAME

I keep wanting to like this game, and then keep getting reminded how horribly tedious it gets, as well as how quickly.

Want more money? Figure out going deeper. Okay, cool.

Want starter automation? Buy a couple easy-to-reach machines and some pipes. Alright.

Want conveyor lines? Well, now you're going to have to invest in a lengthy pipeline, lay it out such that your conveyors can run directly above it, as they all hook to pipes; and while you're at it, you're going to want to manage your pipes' pressure and water quality, because every pipe lowers pressure, and you need quality water. Oookay... why does the quality matter?

Oh, remember that automation you wanted? Turns out it breaks down every so often, and every time you need to repair it, you have to buy a new item to repair it with, which is used up on repair. Also, the water purifiers you're buying to slow that down also break, at a MUCH faster rate. Well, I mean, I don't know if...

Also, those cruddy used things you bought are slow, huh? Well, if you want more, you have to climb a mountain, then slowly trudge your way all the way down an utterly MASSIVE underground complex, all the way to the bottom; and THEN, and only then, are you going to be informed that you needed to bring not only money, but also specific amounts of potentially multiple different materials, then walk all of them one by one to a giant anvil that's equally far away from all of these things. Did I mention you can only move one thing at a time?

It feels like everything is just designed to be exponentially more of a slog. It's miserable; and if you dare to install mods to make it less miserable, you're not allowed to earn achievements. It gets me to back off so quickly, every time I give it another go.

Hydroneer is a base building, mining, and automation game where you start out with a shovel and a dream… and eventually end up running a fully operational industrial water-powered money factory.

The digging is satisfying, the automation is addictive, and building out your base feels like pure chaos in the best way. Every upgrade makes you feel like a genius… until one pipe is angled wrong and your entire system collapses like my mental stability after a long day of parenting.

This game is honestly fantastic, but it has one major problem:

I wish there was more DLC.

Not because the game feels unfinished, but because once you get your mining operation running smoothly, you just want more machines, more areas, more progression, and more reasons to build an even bigger ridiculous base that you swear will be “organized this time.”

Hydroneer is the kind of game that makes you say “just one more upgrade” and then suddenly it’s midnight and you’re standing in a river fixing pipes like it’s your second job.

Rating: 9/10

I know plenty of YouTubers are pushing this game but unfortunately this game is a grind fest, and not in any good way. It takes way too much money to be able to set up even the most basic of automation. An example is you'll get paid about 200 tokens on average for a ring (at the start of the game). To get that ring you'll have to dig for about 15 minutes to get enough ore and a gem then time to cut and smelt. An auto digger costs a few hundred tokens, then there's intake, pipe, pressure valves, repair tools, etc just to get an auto digger. You still will have to hand wash all the soil. Doing this saves you roughly 30% of your time, so 10 minutes per ring. By the time you get to getting auto washers and sorter or whatever that stuff is called, pipe costs go up, and these other devices are costing 1200+ tokens. It's hard to explain everything, but it works out very badly. You'll just be stuck washing soil for hours and hours. I think the dev forgot about early game and he kept expanding late game, leaving new players holding wet dirt and a brush for hours on end. I can not express the depth of misery that early game is. I wouldn't buy this game because I NEVER want to play early game ever again.

The game itself is good. overall 7/10 The best part is how the game does not take itself too seriously. you are able to do whatever you really want which allows for open-ended creativity. however this game is decently buggy. they have buttons that restore the players location and vehicle location because it is very easy to get stuck. but my main issue with the game is how the saves work.

Hydroneer is a sandbox mining and automation game. focusing on fairly simple mechanics that work effectivly to make a good game in the genre. there is no end goal or clear objectives that leave the player wondering what to do next. the answer is simple: expand your mine. simply put the enjoyment in the game is from you can derive fun through your own creativity. however after about 2o hours into a save file you are left with little to do but wait for meaningless numbers or you find a different game.

Why a gave a bad review: 
this game has been released for more that 5 years and every one of those has had save corruption glitches. out of the 54 hours I have played in this game roughly 50 of them were wasted, lost to various saving bugs. the devs once published patches for the game but over time they have slowly abandoned the game. they have not officially called it quits but the last tiny patch was march 2025 (featuring an incomplete bug patch). This is generally disapointing because they really had an interesting game on their hands but slowly replaced it with other products and ideas before this game was let to shine. their current project is a completely different genre, art style and game than Hydroneer. I am glad they are able to explore different ways of expressing their ideas but its a shame their founding was left to rot with numerous issues with a simple solution that would not require to much effort on their part.

How to get a better view on this game:
initially I discovered this game through LGIO (Lets game is out) videos on youtube. his format consists of pushing games to their limit through glitches and dedication. LGIO is the borderline mascot for this game (same as satisfactory) where most long term players know his name. not only because he is one of the bigger creators but many respect his dedication and efforts to point out bugs which do get reported to the devs where in most cases are patched. He is basically a QA tester that publishes good content. For 6 years he has published 9 (as of jan 2026) Hydroneer videos. each video showcases his creativity and that expressed through the game. if you are interested in purchasing the game but need more detail on the games style I would highly recommend those videos. Each video highlights a major bug, dedication, or pushing the game to its limits which fits into Hydroneers dream style. 


overall a fun and quirky little game with no handholding but overshined by the numerous amount of bugs and little effort from the devs

7/10 game*
* if you can find a way to avoid the constant save corruption bugs plaguing the game

Le jeu possède plein de petits problèmes qui, isolé, ne sont pas dérangeant mais mit bout à bout rendent le gameplay fastidieux pour rien. Vous voulez installer un mod pour arranger certains points ? Vous ne pouvez plus débloquer les succès Steam, y compris si c'était juste pour tester sans sauvegarder. Reprendre une ancienne sauvegarde ? Les succès sont également désactivés sur la save de backup. C'est vraiment complétement stupide de faire cela. Ça n'apporte rien sauf de la frustration.

Vous me direz que ne plus pouvoir débloquer de succès n'est pas si grave. C'est vrai, sauf que dans un jeu comme celui-ci, où il n'y a pas réellement de fin, l'objectif que je me fixe est le 100%. Recommencer ? Non, juste non. Le début du jeu est incroyablement lent, à telle point que le moyen le plus simple de gagner "beaucoup" d'argent est via la pêche.

Hydroneer is a good game to relax and clear your mind thanks to its simplicity.
The gameplay is calm and satisfying, especially for players who enjoy management and farming-style games.

However, the game still has quite a few bugs and can lag heavily if you build a very large mining setup or if too much water is flowing at the same time. In my case, I had to set up a 20-second timer system to properly water my crops, otherwise the game became unstable.

I completed the base game 100% in about 68 hours. This includes a discovery phase, manual mining using a pickaxe and a rake, and building a large mining farm within the first 10 hours. The manual mining part alone took around 10 hours. The farming phase at the end of the game took the most time, with over 20 hours spent AFK.

As for the DLC, it took me around 25 hours in total to reach 100% completion. The final achievement, “Unlucky Roll”, alone took about 4 hours to complete.

В кратце: Ожидал большего.

развернуто: 
Есть такой тип разработчиков, которые работают по принципу "хз, я так вижу". Это обычно 1-2 человека с тихим безэмоциональным голосом, пустым взглядом и упорством груженого товарняка на 45градусном спуске, упершегося в стену. Они что-то делают, что-то крутят, что-то вертят - долго, упорно. И, зачастую - с минимальным выхлопом.

Что такое гидронир:
В целом тут уже много раз писали - лопаткой клик в землю, клик ведерко, 4 раза. Потом ведерко над тазиком, клик. Потом берешь тазик и бросаешь в водичку (физика-шмизика. перевернется - ничего не будет). ПОтом берешь веник и под приятное "фш-фш" получаешь 1-2 кусочка руды(железо(~75%), золото(~23%), корстоун(~1-2%) или клотиум(~1-2%). Ну и еще иногда выпадают всякие ценные камушки (рубины, изумруды и прочая шелупонь) которые можно на специальном верстачке почистить. 
Руды можно плавить (никакой системы легирования, сплавов или чего-то типа сталелитья тут нет. Просто банки на жаровне, из которых можно потом получить слиток руды, которую вы сплавили). Плюс есть наковальня, на которой штук 5 рецептов (нож, меч, топор, кольцо, ожерелье). 

Все это можно продавать. ТОЛЬКО. Ну еще отдавать челикам на улице (это тут квесты такие). т.е. "продавать но по другому"

Технически, это вся игра. 
"стоп-стоп-стоп! Но там же есть автоматизация! там есть конвейеры! Там есть буры! там есть машины, в конце концов!"

Да. Но фишка в том, что оно все в итоге приводит к единой идее: добудь, помой, расплавь, скуй, продай. 
ВСЁ. 

В игре есть ферма, рыбалка и вроде как готовка еды, но они, формально, вообще тут ни к селу ни к городу - все это надо исключительно вам, если вдруг вам не нравится продавать руды. Тут нет угроз, банкротства, урона, голода, жажды, хоть одного параметра персонажа, который бы вас мотивировал двигаться и шевелиться. Есть смена времени суток, которая толком ни на что не влияет и вообще не очень понятно зачем она. Ну ночью не очень удобно ведро ставить, точку плохо видно на полу. Фермерство, рыбная ловля, постройка дома: хотите - занимайтесь. Не хотите - не занимайтесь.

В игре нет как таковой прогрессии (в понимании некоего сюжета или хотя бы мало-мальского изменения окружающей действительности - мир статичнее чем ваши обои). То, чем ты занимаешься в начале игры и все что ты увидишь в начале игры проехав на грузовичке (карта в игре проходится от края до края минут за 5. грузовичок нужен только для перевозок барахла) побырику - все это будет с тобой до конца. Ни одной закрытой двери перед тобой не откроется, а открытой - не закроется. Ты можешь купить участок побольше. Достаточно быстро (часов за 7-10) перейдешь на примитивную автоматизацию (бур копает, конвейеры катят, фильтры делят, плавильни плавят) и все такое - чиллово, расслабленно, без закидонов, как скринсейвер. Но при этом никогда не произойдет чего-то, что бы ты не ожидал или сказал "ого, прикольно!" Весь контент игры можно увидеть глазами за, формально, первые 20 минут (грузовик бесплатно и, видимо, бесконечно заправленный стоит в метре от вас при спавне). Попробовать руками - конечно, придется покорпеть подольше. Ожидать, что твои действия приведут хоть к какому-то фидбеку от мира - вообще забей. тут все можно заменить на серые монохромные коробки и игра не сильно потеряет в геймплее (и графике).

Я играл в эту игру (пиратку) года 2 назад - тогда я подумал "интересный концепт, будет любопытно пощупать ее чуть позже". Пару недель назад я решил игру купить. Я думал что там изменилось хоть что-то. Нет. 

Я бы сказал, что у разработчиков нет какой-то глобальной идеи или желания создать прям игру, которая бы будоражила возможностями или хотя бы перспективами. У них нет какой-то глобальной идеи, к которой игрок смог бы прийти в конце. 2 года назад я играл в игру, похожую на студенческую поделку с интересным концептом(автоматизация в коузи-стиле, это ощущалось любопытно). С тех пор в игре появилось... Фиг знает что, если честно. За 10 часов игры я не столкнулся еще ни с 1 новым предметом. Даже карта не поменялась. Даже графика не изменилась. Даже какой-то маломальский шейдинг не появился. Ничего! 

Есть подозрение, что разрабы не шибко много времени и внимания уделяют игре и, в перспективе, этот подход не изменится. И да, если вы тут ожидаете что-то уровня... хотя бы 1/10 факторио - забудьте. Это игра грустных людей с грустными глазами и тихим голосом, которые разочарованы в жизни и не уверены, что хотят проектом заниматься. Цена игре - рублей 200, играть в нее можно только если вам надоело смотреть на стену, но игры типа факторио и сатисфактори кажутся вам слишком... обильными и принуждающими действовать?

И да, с коопом я еще не возился, но отзывы вроде "можно мне норм кооп, а не сплит-скрин" меня тоже настраивают на не очень хорошее отношение к игре.

Listen, this is a great game—I’ve put in over 500 hours, so I know what I’m talking about. However, there are a few things that feel incomplete. It’s like the developer finished about 85% of the game, everyone bought it, and then the base game was never truly completed. There are several incomplete features, bugs and just sloppy features. 

For example:  
- Task requests for version 1.5 feel half-baked. You Can’t even make a “.5”. 
- Why are there no ramps that vehicles can use without getting stuck?  
- Why do vehicles constantly get stuck on the “hot spots” for ore resources?  
- Why isn’t there a better map system that clearly shows whose task you completed, instead of making you guess?  
- Harvester should have a toggle to empty, I don't need to hold e for 10 minutes. 
- Frame rate near end game is horrible... With 500 hours I've optimized everything and it still sucks. 
- Carrots get stuck in funnels and without funnels creating a jam. 
- Putting seeds in the hydro copper... Complete after thought. Can't scale at all dropping bags of seed in a small compartment. 

These are just a few examples, but overall, it feels like the developer should finish the base game before focusing on paid maps which feels like a money grab seeing that the base game has several incomplete features and many bugs.
developer_response:
Hey there
Thanks for the review! I'd just like to address a few points you've made here, I hope they help out. Firstly, I'd really recommend not playing the 1.5 version of the game. The current version is 3.0.9, which contains an entire rework of the game since 1.5 as well as tons of optimisations, new features, and resolutions to issues you've listed here.

- Task requests for version 1.5 feel half-baked. You Can’t even make a “.5”.
(You're able to submit tasks above the required limit, so for this instance, giving the NPC a bar of 1 weight instead of .5 will help. You can also cut that bar in half using a saw to get a value of 0.5)

- Why are there no ramps that vehicles can use without getting stuck?
(The store in Bridgepour sells metal tin sheets that allow you to make ramps for vehicles)

- Why do vehicles constantly get stuck on the “hot spots” for ore resources?
(I'm not sure about this one. In older versions there were sometimes tiny bits of the diggable terrain that vehicles would get stuck on, but that got fixed in an update after the version you're playing)

- Why isn’t there a better map system that clearly shows whose task you completed, instead of making you guess?
(I agree the map system could be better. Currently you can only see which tasks can be started and which have been accepted)

- Harvester should have a toggle to empty, I don't need to hold e for 10 minutes.
(I agree this takes a while, the new digging vehicle does not have this feature)

- Frame rate near end game is horrible... With 500 hours I've optimized everything and it still sucks.
(The latest version of the game has lots more optimisations for large scale bases)

- Carrots get stuck in funnels and without funnels creating a jam.
(For larger objects try not using funnels, as they can get stuck in these funnels, especially in the older version)

- Putting seeds in the hydro copper... Complete after thought. Can't scale at all dropping bags of seed in a small compartment.
(This is a bit of a pain, but you can combine the  seed bags to be larger and then drop them in that way)

As I've mentioned, the latest version of the game is MUCH better than previous versions.
Hope that helps :)

Graphics / Visuals: 6/10
A simple, stylized low‑poly look that’s clear and functional but rarely impressive. The world feels more like a practical workspace than a place you want to explore. Lighting and water effects occasionally add charm, but overall the visuals serve the mechanics rather than elevate them.

Sound / Music / Atmosphere: 5/10
The audio design is minimal and easy to forget. Nothing stands out, nothing offends — it’s just background noise. After a short while I switched to podcasts and shows, and the game fits that passive atmosphere almost too well.

Single‑Player Gameplay: 7/10
A repetitive but satisfying loop of digging, selling, and upgrading. Automation is the highlight, though getting there involves a lot of small annoyances: repairing machines, adjusting pipes, and buying items one at a time. Optimization isn’t difficult; the real challenge is tolerating the monotony.

Multiplayer Gameplay: –/10
There is no multiplayer mode.

Story / Narrative: –/10
There’s almost no story. Hydroneer is a pure sandbox that leaves all goals and motivation entirely up to the player.

Content & Replay Value: 7/10
There’s plenty to do — mining, farming, fishing, automation, and logic systems. The Volcalidus DLC adds a new biome and a slightly different progression curve. Each new run can play out differently, but the core routine remains the same, so replay value depends on how much you enjoy rebuilding from scratch.

Technical Performance: 9/10
The game runs smoothly with no major issues. Even large automated setups maintain solid performance, which is impressive for an indie title. Occasional physics quirks appear, but nothing that breaks the experience.

Achievements / Progression: 6/10
Achievements are simple but time‑consuming, with many requiring long stretches of repetitive grinding. Progression starts fast but eventually slows into a predictable routine.

Hydroneer is a calm, methodical sandbox that works best as a “background game” — something to play while watching shows or listening to podcasts. Building up your automated mining empire is genuinely satisfying, but the journey is filled with repetitive tasks and small inconveniences. If you enjoy slow, incremental progress and watching machines come to life, Hydroneer offers dozens of relaxing hours. If you’re looking for depth, variety, or a stronger sense of purpose, you’ll hit the limits fairly quickly.
I love this game

As a concept, the game is great. It has a simple gameplay loop: mine, process, sell, expand. 
The problems start when you try to do more advanced stuff or have a bigger mining capacity. The UI for placing objects is horrible, building systems is so infuriating because you need a very specific angle for placing an object(mostly pipes) where you want. Good luck when you are building in a tight space and have little room to move around. 
And then even if you get a proper mining setup running, If you funnel resources into a single output and have a pan that collects everything then have fun staring at a frozen screen for 20 seconds while your CPU tries to process the sheer amount of ♥♥♥♥ you just picked up. I have no idea how the devs intended for this to work properly.

Which brings me to my next sorrowful feeling: The lack of information is abhorrent, seriously. The tutorial is barebones and you are never given a full overview or smth about the things you can and cannot do, including item descriptions. If you have to alt+tab to google every time something is not working right, because there is no UI for errors in systems you are trying to build, then it's just bad game design.
Example: Was building a seven miner setup on the first plot of land, over the bridge, I mined out all the dirt with a pickaxe to get as deep as possible, pretty quickly you arrive at a layer where you can't mine any further, I thought it just a soft boundary of depth, the layer looks like dirt so I didn't think about it too much, now I had a nice cleared out space to set down my miners, I made all of them, set them down, connected them all up and imagine my surprise when none of them worked. After half an hour of troubleshooting I gave up and googled the problem. And lo! the game has bedrock, which cannot be mined by hand or drills, resources cannot be extracted from it, my whole setup was built wrong, Luckily it didn't take too much to fill in a bit of dirt and get the setup moving, but so much of my time could've been saved by a simple popup that reads: ''This is bedrock and cannot be mined by hand or machine'', shortly after I quit the game and started writing this. 

All in all, the game is not bad per se, and I'm sure that the devs poured their heart into it, but it all just feels like cramming a family of 9 into a mini cooper. the game just feels like it doesn't have room to do it's thing. Maybe it's the engine or some other limitations. I'm genuinely curious as to how the devs felt that this type of game design and this product was an okay thing to sell to people, when even high end PC's struggle with certain things.

I hope this game gets a sequel and a fresh start, because the concept deserves a fair chance to shine and I hope the devs are willing to do it over again. I hope my money is going to the right place and this doesn't turn into abandonware.

I bought this game July 18th 2020 a few months after it was released. It was playable but not much content back then.

It has since evolved into quite a nice little game but with some pretty glaring gameplay issues still.

I would def recommend this game at its price point of $14.99 and goes on sale often at around $5-$10 depending on the sale.

It is a great art style and i enjoy the look and feel of the game. Its not to serious and is fun to play around with.


Lets start with the pros.

You have multiple dig sites to mine and also you can do farming as well. Now, a lot of people will question what does a mining game have to so with farming? Dont look at it as a mining sim game, it is Hydroneer, master of water is how i look at it. You grow food and mine for materials, who know where this could take the game, maybe hydro dams for electricity? In any case, there is a lot to do that will certainly take up more than 40+ hours of learning and trial and error.

There are quests in the form of crafting equipment like swords, daggers, jewelry etc. or gather specific materials gold, iron, tomatoes. You then turn them in and get currency or guild tokens for farming or mining.

You advance through three tiers of mining for different depths of material, the deeper you go the better the yield or more rare resources. There are artifacts at each dig site you can find and then put on display in the artifacts cave near the starting area.

Now for the cons.

1. Mining gets very boring, once you hit tier 2 you honestly do not need to do tier 3. Its just a waiting game to get enough cornerstone to make the top tier 3 mining equipment. So this is basically where the game just gets stale.
2. The tiers of equipment have their water intakes all located in different areas, so once you upgrade, you need to 100% redo all of your pipes to accommodate the new equipment. This is very boring to have to keep doing over and over again.
3. You have to carry ALL ITEMS one by one. If you need 50 pipes, you need to go buy 50 pipes. You hop in your tractor, drive to the merchant that sells them. Load them onto the buy platform 1 by 1 50 times. Then you need to get your money, place it in the basket, then press the button to buy the items. Then you need to load all the 50 pipes 1 by 1 into the tractor, then go back get your money and load it into the tractor. Then you haul them back to the mining site, unload them 1 by 1 and place them 1 by 1 where you want them. This is for every. little. thing. you do and it get so boring to do. Now, you can eliminate this sort of by parking your tractor on or as near as possible to the purchase zone and just load them into the tractor, but still its 50 pieces on and then 50 pieces off. Super slow and just annoying for ne reason.
4. conveyor belts and smelting. These things get clogged up all the time, i have tried funnels, i have tried centering tools on the belts, everything. There will reach a point where you will have so much of a backup you have no choice but to press escape and then clear all dirt material, its a nice feature, but i feel this was a purposeful band aide put in place by the dev to clear the issue instead of solving the root cause. Useful, but not optimal, it would be like putting a switch on the dash of your car to just turn the check engine light off... yea you wont see the issue anymore but the issue still exists.
5. you get super rich very quickly. By the time i left the starting area i could buy everything i wanted or could ever want, again, its just time. you can just let it run run run and get a huge bar of gold which is not really used for anything but for cash and crafting some items for the mini quests. Other than that within maybe 30 mins on tier 1 with 4 drills going you can make 100s of thousands of coins just off gold alone, not to mention the iron ore sells very well too.
6. Repair, repair, repair - Aside from running around building things and moving pieces 1 at a time, you then need to repair everything and often. Unless you use 4 water filters on your main line on 1 pipe. Then you put more filters close to your drills and harvester that will keep them typically at 100% for hours and hours. but you will be repairing water filters very frequently to keep everything running. It is NOT HANDS OFF for an extended period of time. This then cuts the ability to manage multiple mines at a time, not that you really NEED to but it just eliminates that as a possibility as then your only job at that point will be driving mine to mine to mine, then repair repair repair, rinse and repeat.


There are far many more cons than pros, but again, for $15 bucks, you will have fun and enjoy the game.

I recommend the game because it is cool, it is a new take on the genre, and i have seen a great deal of improvement over the last 5 almost 6 years. However, the core base of the game is flawed with no inventory management, no sell back (other than scrapping which then forces you to load up AGAIN and unload AGAIN). Maybe in the future this will be solved or reduced with something like bulk carry or an actual inventory.

Give it a try it plays well and maybe the micro task style of this game is what you like. For me it just gets old very quickly and i am unable to overcome that as my number 1 con to the game.

Happy mining to you all!

The game is good, don't get me wrong, but there is certainly a lot of room for improvement.

The moment you get early automation going, it turns into a massive waiting game while you sit around twiddling your thumbs until you can afford to forge more T1 drills, then you go back to twiddling until you can get T2s, then it's more twiddling while you wait to be able to forge more T2s, and it's the same with T3s.

There are only nine minable resources, four are metals, four are gems, and one just boosts water pressure. With the eight that you can forge with, there are only five things you can smith, not including the nine devices you forge in Icehelm.

The entire gameplay loop after getting your first automated equipment is waiting, travelling to Icehelm to forge new drills, and repeating from step one.

I bought this game because it looked great and I wanted to play it with a friend. But right at the start, in the tutorial, it tells me to “press E to use the lantern” — and nothing happens.

I tried using a keyboard + mouse while my friend used a controller, but the game treated it as if we were both controlling the same character. There was no proper way to assign inputs separately or actually split the controls between two players.

So yeah — it claims to have co-op, but in practice it’s broken or extremely poorly implemented.

Hydroneer is the kind of game that doesn’t hook you—it gently loops a conveyor belt around your free time and never lets go. There’s no flashy intro, no dramatic stakes. Just dirt. Innocent, harmless dirt. And somehow that dirt ends up owning you.

You start small: a shovel, a bucket, a dream. Then suddenly you’re managing an elaborate maze of pipes that looks like it was designed by a caffeine-addicted dwarf with a grudge against straight lines. Everything is just broken enough that you have to fix it, and just functional enough that you want to make it better.

Time behaves strangely in Hydroneer. Minutes compress. Hours evaporate. The sun rises and sets in real life while you’re standing there staring at a smelter, whispering, “Why aren’t you working?” like it personally betrayed you. There is no pause button for your sense of responsibility.

What makes it worse—better—is that the game never pressures you. No timer. No enemies. No urgency. Just a calm, pastoral environment encouraging you to sink another five hours into perfecting a system that will save you ten seconds per dirt load.
It is OK game but once I automated it I lost the goal and reason to continue playing.

I love this game. It's a really well made game, and pretty low spec friendly, I struggle running a lot of games because of my laptop, but this game runs pretty well on lowest graphics. Only downside is the dirt is hardd to make out in 3d. This game is really addictive aswell, and is really fun, I just wish i could have a guide as to how to progress further into the game without manually having to find everything. I probably am going to find a video on how to progress, and how to use the logic machines. But overall this game is amazing.

I will say the tedium was expected, but the way you interact with everything is total ass. 
I like the manually doing things and carrying stuff, but specifically trying to put dirt and water into the pan genuinely just made me quit for today. 
There's not a clear placement indicator, you don't just click on the pan with the full bucket. 
You have to offset it, angle and pour it, hoping it gets in. 
It's not too hard to get the hang of and most things have a tiny little dot shadow so you can tell where it'll drop, but it's just poorly done. 
I don't like guessing where the objects will go. 
Filling the bucket is dumb, you have to literally drop the bucket into the water and pick it back up, half the time I miss it or it doesn't register the first click to grab it. 
Then go fill the pan and miss. I try to drop the shovel and it just wont if you're too close to the ground or angled a certain way so you have to readjust constantly just to drop it. 
Too obtuse and finicky. 
Otherwise I understand the tedious nature is intended as its very interactive, but I think some things like clicking the pan with the bucket of water should just fill the pan. 
You have to do it quite a bit in the early game and I dislike it. 
Putting anything into a pan or cart to move around is also hard because you don't know exactly where it'll drop. 
You have to turn 45 degrees to the side to drop it in front of you. 
Otherwise it'll just fall from you hip. 
Sometimes when I try to fill the pan with dirt it'll physically place the dirt under the pan which is also just annoying. 
This happens when its not fully highlighted but you have to do this process so much and when you do it fast it makes it more common. 
Feels purposefully made to aggravate you in a disrespectful way. 
For whatever reason this game in particular just irritated me.
 

The game design seems to try to make the user interface as hostile as possible. 
For example, placing objects happens a fixed distance away from the player and this distance is far enough to make any attempt to work in narrow spaces fraught, (y'know... like underground the main place you might want a drill?). 
Another big thing is the way purchasing items is handled, say you want to buy and use 1 section conveyor belt, well first you need to grab your money and drop it in a bucket at the first shop, then buy the pipes you need to power the conveyor belt and then take the money to a different shop to buy your conveyor belt, all while only being able to hold 1 item at a time. 
The point seems to be to incentivise the use of the vehicles but they barely hold enough to make them worth using. 
Good general concept but just a really frustrating user experience, felt like I was wasting my time.

Currently the game just doesn't feel good and i general feel irked by it, the single inventory system burns you out quickly because, i soooo do enjoy trying to put an item in the back of the car to only to jump into the car because we're just making the whole truck interactable including the bed of the truck so when im trying to load it up to take it back to my base not only to have to deal hopping in and out each time i want to drop an item i then get back to base to deal with unloading the bloody thing and because i can't store items i have to shuttle it from the car too the base one item at a time.

The automation gets clunky quickly because trying to set up a belt to feed my furnace but the sorter spits out below the belt so you have to then build down a level but i need to dig it out with a pickaxe because the economy of the game pushes you away from trying to automate early so you just have to slowly, painfully start trying to put together a machine bit by bit but your machines start breaking because adding a repair mechanic to a game about automation really is the twist of the knife you need when looking around at the lack of real gameplay loop that isn't a man requesting soup or a sword because god forbid i try to understand anything without looking it up somewhere else.

Settings, visual, map.
So, the LOD system is good awful and it's noticeable quickly because if you do any driving you notice the terrain melting into it's normal state.
Saving on a HDD freezes the game for a solid second.
There is no map button it is an item you pick up to read of the map...
Hated the whole fact the UI is that there isn't a UI, the dropping of items is bad because it's at an off angel, you do not get a way to store money in a pocket, you need to walk around with it in your main hand or in a dam bucket!

I generally don't understand the point of trying to show automation in the game when you're trying to work with a voxel system and the drills don't mine the voxels, at that point you're not using the voxels for anything but a cheap gimmick.

The map doesn't make a lick of sense either as guess what, there is multiple places to set up to "mine" but you're not going to be doing that because if you want to mine more you'll need to go to the mountain forge to trade a bunch of the iron and 300 coins (because god forbid we just craft the thing) to then get another bit of automated mining.

The gameplay loop doesn't work, im sorry but it doesn't there is needless mechanics that feels they're here just to stop people being able to refund the game, you added a farming, cooking and fishing parts to the game about mining and still only have 4 resources of metals and 4 of gemstones while farming has 6 vegetables, fishing has 13 fish!? 
And the cooking is there too.

After getting this far writing up this review (it's just a rant at this point) i fully get the way this game direction has gone, it feels like it was once an attempted to make a cute little mining voxel game that had to be pulled back creatively from an open world farming, trading, rpg thing due to either technical restraints or just inexperience.

You have a nice idea but you haven't really thought how to build it out.

Unfortunately, I’m disappointed with Hydroneer. The game has been out for 5 years and the most basic problem still hasn’t been fixed. The developer releases PAID DLC while the core issues of the game remain unsolved. Let me explain what I mean: the game is about automating the extraction of resources from the ground and then processing them into bars, jewelry, etc. (I’m intentionally skipping the vegetable section – I haven’t reached that part yet, and in the current state of the game I probably never will)…

You can then sell the products, which allows you to buy increasingly better equipment for processing resources and expanding production. And this second aspect is the biggest flaw of the game. Once you add around 20 drills, the game starts slowing down; with 30 drills we’re talking 20–30 FPS – and this is not the computer’s fault but the game’s optimization. You can also forget about long conveyor belts like in Factorio, because to keep the game running somewhat smoothly, the player is forced to shorten all transport paths as much as possible. The longer the path from the ore to the final furnace, the worse the FPS gets.

Sadly, in its current state, the game is unplayable for fans of the previously mentioned Factorio. The game offers many plots where you can dig, and you could theoretically place hundreds if not thousands of drills on them, but with around 30 working drills (and not even the fastest ones), the game starts having serious problems. I should also mention that after about 4–5 hours of intensive gameplay, you already have money for everything – there’s nothing left to spend it on. Devices (conveyors, pipes, furnaces) are so cheap that after 8–9 hours you don’t need to sell anything anymore, because the gold you generated earlier is enough to buy hundreds or thousands of items. Drills aren’t purchased; you have to “cast” them in the mountain forge from extracted resources, so you need a lot of them, but you can’t acquire them quickly because the game becomes unplayable.

Multiplayer mode is, unfortunately, a joke – shared screen? In 2025? It makes sense in some games, but not in a single-player automation simulator (remember the stuttering caused by drills? In multiplayer you have to multiply that lag by 3 or 4).

For a fan of massive automated factories and long conveyor belts filled with materials, this game is not for me. The frustration I felt when reading the forums looking for a solution to my problem was huge – everyone basically says, “Yeah, that’s just how this game is. Sure, it’s about automation… but not too much, because the developer never optimized it well enough to let you build a true ‘mining empire.’”

I could list many more of the game’s shortcomings, but there’s no point. In its current state, if you're mainly interested in resource extraction (not making soups, not programming logic gates), the game lasts about 20–30 hours, depending on how fast you progress.

It is okay. But in the end it is just a mining game. There are 4 ores, and 4 gems. Drills provide infinite amount of ores and gems, but with different probabilities. Mining in the beginning is time consuming, and then you have to kind of exploit a specific car to go deeper very quickly. After that, the only activity is to tediously pick up stuff at the shops, bring it back to you mining site and place it in a weird interface. No inventory. The actual "clue" of this game, that you need water/hydro power for every machine is not deep at all. 3 levels of pumps, pipes. and a specific item which increases the pressure to its acutal max withou ANY hustle. So no need to plan your pipes, no need to think, just build your pipes as you want and in the end, just in front of your machines, put this pressure increase part and thats it. The "open world" is boring and not immersive at all, the NPS are just there, nothing else. Sometimes they want specific items from you, like a sword with 5kg iron and 2kg gold - but that is not hard at all to achieve. In early midgame you basically just forge one sword out of 1ton of iron and 1ton of gold. Money is not an issue. Maybe the second currency. But there is nothing you want to wait for. I get that some people want to build huge mining facilites here, but the building takes so much time and the mechanic are so simple, it is not rewarding at all. Go for Satisfactory or Factorio instead - there is literally nothing this game will offer you instead.

[h1]HOWEVER[/h1]
There are several statements I need to address before I can really enjoy this game....

- The lack of placement options for buckets, pans and other gravity effected items not associated to building or furniture content. These items (like the pan and bucket) will spill its resources if you don't **set them down** because of a random piece of land or a gem.

- The lack of a MASS PICKUP option. You cannot tell me that a prospector will not pick up a handful/cupped hand worth of resources to move them around. Picking up a [b]single piece of ore[/b] is insanely tedious, and EXTREMELY un-fun when things fall over. [b]Or maybe even an option to hit **right click** when carrying a bucket or pan to pick up individual pieces of ore[/b]... SOMETHING to help pick up early game!

- Steering the wagon is fine, but there should be some kind of collision with it, so you're not accidentally trying to let it go clipped into a fence and just constantly getting "hmm!?" over and over as you inch your character in a circle.

- having to DROP the bucket to pick up water and scooping dirt into a shove... [b]just to re-dump it back into the pan[/b].... can we not just get a "scoop water" option with the bucket and shovel dirt directly to the pan?? 
Right now it's a 10 step process (literally) to scoop dirt, dump in pan, pick up water and scrub... Also, [i] what is the purpose for the need to shovel dirt in the bucket before the pan??[/i]

All you need is to shovel dirt into the [b]pan[/b], scoop [i]water[/i] into the bucket, dump it into the pan and scrub. 10 steps suddenly drop to 4 or 5, and is much smoother and more gratifying without as much headache of picking up and dropping in the early game, where your player retention is most important!

I haven't spent long in this game... I love the concept, i'm enjoying it. but it's the little things [b]early one[/b] that is very quickly building on my nerves and making me want to step away from boredom and irritation as i spill material unintentionally.

There's also the idea of having to carry the currency... [i]you're seriously telling me we can't have a coin-purse or some leather pouch on the belt that can hold money and be pulled out by a keybind?[/i] Unless i'm not far enough to have found such a tool, but i would think it'd be something in this world with how everyone has leather gloves or other leather clothing....

Again, the game is fun, but these small headaches are very quickly getting tiresome for someone who has 1-2 hours before having to sleep for work the following day, and is choosing a game to play before dredging through another 14 hour work shift... [i] I know this is a rant... but like... there's so much I want to like about this game. the automation is fun, the planning involved is awesome, and the physics of the gems is very fun to see because you can create to take advantage of it using the terrain.[/i] But you end up getting exhausted from small things ruining the entertainment through repetition and tedious activity. 

I like the game... I enjoy what the company is aiming for... but some QoL additions would be very much appreciated.

review:
I'm not sure if they're still working, but the UI is so extremely clunky.  Your center reticle and your drop location aren't the same, so if you pick something up, it instantly get's moved down and to the left on your screen.  If you're looking down and pick something up, the object is in the center of your forward looking view, so if you're picking stuff up you have to move your view up to look at the item.  

The drop collision is rough, like sometimes you pick something up, and it's the wrong thing, so you go to drop it, but there's somehow now not room to drop it, so you have to jump or move or go somewhere else just to drop it?  It's rough.   

Why can't there just be an inventory system?  Just let me hold my money.  The money is an object that you have to remember where it is every time and carry it around.  Every item you buy something you have to carry it around one at a time and put it on a wagon / car.  If you want to get ten new pipes, then it's pick / place x 10 at the store, buy, then pick / place x 10 to the wagon / cart.  It's a weird tedium that isn't necessarily fun or rewarding.  

The concept of the game is fun in theory, but the UI / world interaction / game play is too tedious to be enjoyable.

[b]Completing the main island[/b] involved a grueling process of taking a long time getting started up and then managing to afford upgrades by engaging in hours-long periods of AFKing until my setup generated enough resources to get me across the line. This later turned into completing dozens of quests for small sums of guild currency since Hydrocoins quickly become completely irrelevant and incredibly easy to obtain. 
The dirt and tool tiers were easy to learn and did feel good to achieve - but the basic gameplay mechanics and the unbalanced currencies take away from the experience. Many of the shops are cramped and relatively closed off so it becomes impossible to position your truck on the sell platforms and every time you want to buy multiple items you'll have to pick up each one and walk them to the sell platform, buy them, and only then can you move them into your truck. I have watched Let's Game it Out play Hydroneer and I think the devs might have designed the stores in a closed-off way to combat an old bug where you could steal shop items by placing them in your truck as a result of LGIO's play-style, but that was back then. Now? It's just frustrating and makes buying items repetitive and painful.

[b]In comparison, Journey to Volcalidus is incredibly refreshing and well-paced.[/b] The Journey to Volcalidus DLC is worth being a game in its own right and operates similarly to the main island, but adding the usage of lava as your main "fuel" for your mining setups. The progression of wealth and upgrades feels more natural and satisfying. Once my mines were automated, I did quickly end up with a surplus of Hydrocoins just like on the main island, but for the guild tokens it was much easier to earn the currency I needed to continue playing. Even when I needed to build up resources there were plenty of other things to do on the island, like hunting for bones or abandoned mines or otherwise just discovering the island in general, so I rarely ever went AFK while playing the DLC. This DLC truly feels like the devs applied everything they learned from developing the main game and created an even better experience than what I expected from Hydroneer in the first place. Also, this is just a feeling, but I'm pretty sure the DLC is bigger than the base game...

Overall, I would say I got my money's worth out of the main game and DLC. I bought both at the same time because I knew I wanted to 100% this game and I'm glad that I enjoyed the DLC as much as I did after struggling with the main island. There is so much else I could say but this review is already long, so I'll close out with thanking the developer for this game and saying that I am looking forward to Hydroneer 2.

Do you like mining? Well this does mining fairly well if you kinda liked the gold mining sim games but wanted a tad more automation.

Is it fun? Sure, the games fun, i am having a blast getting my ocd out on it, i have a lot to nitpick over. But for 5 years of dev, the game feels...shallow? like where did all the dev time go?

This game is a shame for me. The building systems are really cool, and the progression is slow but rewarding. However, the complete lack of inventory coupled with the complete lack of any real objective make this game nearly impossible for me to want to come back to. I dealt with the non-inventory for 16 hours and built an incredibly efficient machine that fills its own filters and filters all the raw material into separate buckets and processes the gems. I was basically printing money, and suddenly all the items were within my budget. But I didn't have any reason to buy anything. Because there's nothing going on in the game. It's just a sandbox with no motivation. I had my machine and could easily make money, so I do not see any reason to build more machines just to make more money. 

The lack of any inventory would be much easier for me to deal with if the game provided motivation. But I don't want to play a game I have to manually move a pile of literally 44 individual pieces of rock into a bucket because I mis-clicked and spilled the contents. When the only thing I get out of doing so is...fake video game money. And nothing else. No cutscenes. No story progression. Nothing. Just more of the sandbox.

So, i used to watch a youtuber play this game a lot, and when watched him i was very jealous because this game always looked like a lot of fun, and eventually i got a gaming pc and i am actually able to afford this game now, and so i purchased it. First off its actually a lot harder then you would think, the first thing i want to talk about is the tutorial, now it covers a lot of basic things about the game like crafting and forging which is quite crucial to overall game, when you first get into the actual game you will spend multiple hours digging just to get a couple hundred coins, and then you able to buy things like upgraded tools and drilling machines. After this normally you buy another plot of land and go bankrupt over the amount of items and pipes you need to buy for your operation. Honestly the amount of pipes required for an efficient farm is silly but its very fun creating your own piping system. I would heavily recommend getting the expanded pipes mod because the base game pipes are honestly not enough and when you first get it you might "I do not need a 6-way pipe" but trust me I've used it in some of my builds. A complaint i have is that the icehelm crafting isn't exactly the most clear thing ever, i am currently trying to upgrade my drilling machines from the base machines to the next metal up, but the crafting is very confusing and i will probably have to search it up at some point which sucks. This game is very fun and there's lots to do, my next project once i'm done with everything in my current world will to do a complete vanilla game play through in order to get some achievements. This game is very fun and I recommend it to anyone and everyone, there is so much to do.

I really enjoyed this game when it first came out and was very bare bones, but I think my enjoyment was because I always had in the back of my mind that it was a single dev and still extremely early in its release. Here it is years later and the game, while having tons of added on content, still feels like baby's first video game programming project. There are so many things that feel like they were done simply because the dev couldn't figure out how to properly program it in game, such as having an inventory, putting coins in a wallet instad of carrying them, having an extremely odd drop zone for items that doesn't at all match the use zone, and many many many more. Instead of trying to fix these things, he leaned into them and the entire game becomes tedium: the game. The first area starts out kind of interesting because it has limited space, but every zone after is a complete waste of time. You can spend 8 hours just clicking over and over and over and over with a pickaxe trying to clear just enough space to find water or fit a few machines. Maybe the giant drilling and rolling machines will help, but the controls are so god awful that they only make things worse. Then, when you get to the real brass tax of the game, building the giant automated machines, you find out that one little machine doesn't work the way it's supposed to and you have thousands upon thousands of ores spilled all over the ground to pick up one at a time. Forget it. Unless you are 10 years old and on summer vacation, nobody has time for this mess.

Проходя обучение у меня было чувство того что обьяснение механик могло быть полнее, ну да ладно, начал я игру и не понял что мне делать, никаких заданий ничего обьясняющего, понятно что надо крафтить и добывать ресы, а для чего? Что бы добывать больше ресов? А конечный результат есть? В ручную копать очень долго и скучно, а понимая принципы факторок оптимизация тут кажется не сложной. побегав по первому городу я увидел задание, нужно принести 44.5 кг слитков, я сразу обратил внимание на вес, но подумал что можно просто принести ему кучу слитков и он сам выберет вес, но принеся ему 10 слитков я понял что сам он не умеет. Я начал думать про прилавок продавца, вдруг он показывает не деньги а вес, это не правда. Я пошел в другой город, по пути увидел старый храм и подумал может это и есть цель игры - сражение с мобами? В храме мобов не оказалось. Пройдя еще дальше я нашел весы, довольно далеко от спавна, денег у меня с собой, да и в целом конечно же не было, в ещё вернувшись и четко зная как выглядят весы я их не нашел в первом городе, а как тогда выполнять задания в начальном городе? Сразу закрался вопрос "А надо ли вообще?" ведь они дают монеты гильдии а не деньги. Бесит что персонаж не может взять горсть монет и ведро, а монеты в ведро не помещаются, я часто бегал несколько раз, потому что брать тележку ради одного ведра это очень тупо. Я потратил 3 часа и накопал только 20 кг железа, это слишком нудно, я решил все продать и слить на покупку дробилки, что бы не тереть руками землю. Оказалось что выход из дробилки при таком же количество земли стал раза в три меньше (стабильно два кусочка руды, а руками могло быть 4-5), посмотрев на руду которую я добыл я представил как нудно сейчас буду переплавлять её в слитки я был готов закрыть игру. Внезапно заметил что вес руды увеличился, и за пару минут я собрал 8 кг железа. Весы внесли существенные коррективы в игру и она стала гораздо понятнее, из за того что при переплавке руды я не видел разницы в размере получившегося слитка, независимо от того сколько кусочков я бросил в тигель слиток получался обычного размера. Так как размер НЕ МЕНЯЛСЯ я сделал вывод что лишние кусочки которые я кидал переплавляться - ПРОПАДАЮТ из за бага, повторю еще раз в обучении не было НИ СЛОВА про вес, я первые пол часа даже не знал что он существует. Я три с половиной часа просто переплавлял по одному кусочку руды, я крайне крайне разражён этим фактом. Буквально за пол часа я выполнил задачу и получил жетоны гильдии, как вы поняли я не знаю куда их девать. Побегал по городу и нашел какие то крутые промышленные машины за эти монеты, и крутые материалы для рудника.

В итоге мне игра понравилась, визуал хороший, только из за этого я сидел и делал нудную работу. Сейчас эта игра для меня не подходит, но я бы оценил её лично для меня как "игра на 100 часов"

Disclaimer: I have not tried the DLC, this is a review for the base game only.

This game is fun for a while, but there are some fundamental issues that prevent me from enjoying it in the long term. 

- The economy is unbalanced. Money is so easy to make it's quickly irrelevant, and other currencies are not too bad, but add tedium, not fun. The cost of items doesn't keep pace with how much money it's possible to make, in a way that feels unbalanced. 

- There are a lack of late game goals to motivate progression. Which would be fine, as there are lots of games I enjoy that are primarily progression for progression's sake alone (shapez 1+2), but...

- Progression and expansion is tedious. All pipes, belts, machines, logic components, must be bought, loaded into vehicle/palette, transported, then unloaded and placed, one at a time, by hand. There is no bulk build, mass disassemble, blueprint system, or any quality of life tool to speed up factory construction. It's hard to get into the sort of flow state that makes games like this satisfying.

- Core machines must be manufactured one by one in a slow process separate from buying other equipment. All machines are available to construct from the start, but are gated by needing to obtain quantities of rare materials. Often this results in needing to wait for your existing factory to generate the materials in order to expand it. 

The best games slow your expansion by challenging your organizational skills, logic, etc, and let the building itself be fairly quick. Hydroneer gets this a little backwards, which limits the fun for me. Some progression you'd expect would be gated (blacksmithing ability, item cost, build locations) aren't gated, and other things that typically let the player move fast (building, logistics, item handling) are slowed down. 

After early game, the only real limiter is how fast you can gather rare materials, which is limited by the number of machines you have. The number of machines you have is limited by how much rare material you've gathered (and how LONG it takes to build things). This loop ends up causing lots of waiting at first, and then scales quadratically, meaning you quickly have more of that material than you'd ever need. It's either feast or famine, rather than being balanced carefully in the middle, which is what would actually be satisfying. 

TL;DR: Building is slow, resources are either frustratingly scarce/slow or you have so much they don't matter any more, and there's no goal other than the tedious progression. Can be fun, but maybe not for long.
