This is the kind of game you play if you enjoy repetition and tedium. That's not an insult, either. There's a true joy to the small actions of repetition and continuity. The beginning is as simple as it gets; Grab a bucket and brush and pan for resources. It's something you actually do even later down the line so it's good to get familiar with it. This game takes the approach of most factory builder games and forces you to do everything by hand. This means you don't have any means to automate the individual tasks without a lot of ingenuity. And some things you just can't make any faster. These aspects of the game may turn some people away and you wouldn't be blamed for being one of them. Crafting is very out-of-the-way and doesn't hold your hand through the process. Digging is slow and takes a lot of fiddling around. You either run around a lot or drive back and forth often. You can't be hurt, even by lava, and the game really does not have any to challenge you besides biding your time. Which isn't hard since making money is easy and the most expensive purchases in the base game are the dig sites. The problem is you'll start selling items for only a few dozen coins, then as soon as you buy the first few major items, you'll be selling for several thousands. You'll be able to afford anything you want. It's more like a sandbox in that way than anything. 

All that said, it's a soothing experience to just progress and work on improving your builds. I haven't tried the DLC yet, it claims to have a vastly improved amount of content but I am of the belief that a game should use it's DLC to build OFF of the game, rather than replace it. Still, if you enjoy watching your progress over time, I would still call this game a worthwhile experience.

I think having some tips initially is alright in any game, then as you get it, they become less needed. review:
This one is certainly a doozy to review. Game's execution was done well, however there might be a crowd that doesn't like how this one played out. Hydroneer isn't for the faint hearted or lazy. In a weird way (in regards to time) every move that the player makes requires careful planning. If you're the type that likes to run back and forth between boxes this may not be the one for you. If you're looking for something that's heavier on the realistic side of crafting (in regards to carrying materials) - this might be for you! Players should be warned that the tutorial is very quick and sweet, and the game does not like holding the players hand for any reason. This game's physics is one of its biggest talking points - both good and bad. 

Hydroneer's [b]gameplay[/b] follows a creative and crafting scheme in which players use water in creative ways. Players find ways to most efficiently collect resources by digging them up from the ground in order to sell them, turn a profit, and further create more complex creations. There is automation in the game that can streamline processes for the player. Belts, melters, crushers, and a whole bunch of options are available for the player to use. The process of putting it all together is what poses the challenge, especially when each part essentially requires water to function (including conveyer belts)! The BIGGEST [b]gameplay[/b] difference in Hydroneer (which I haven't really seen in any other game) is the fact the player's character can only hold ONE item at a time. Yes, that's right, the player can only hold one item at a time. That means every item that is harvested requires to be picked up one by one, by hand. That also means if the player misplaces a bucket or dumps ore incorrectly over an oven that these items also have to be picked up one by one. In essence, this system is beautiful as it is ugly. This is what separates this game from a lot of other crafting type games that provide inventory. Every move is calculated as forgetting something (such as a cart) may absolutely drive the player crazy. Even when something is bought the money and item cannot be carried at the same time. I loved this aspect of the game because it reminded me of working trades: don't make more trips than you need to. Same idea applies here and again, as much as players may hate this concept, it certainly a breath of fresh air because it requires the player to stay attentive and engaged at all times instead of mindlessly being able to quickly recover thanks to extra storage space. Building is very easy to do. What could potentially drive players crazy is accidently picking up the furniture/tools rather than the ore or produced materials. Luckily, it's easy to put the furniture/tool back in place. The village provides a decent amount of shops to check out and an easy to navigate village. Vehicles are available to the player to make transporting supplies easier. The player will have to manually load, one piece by one piece, even with vehicles. Vehicles do make life A LOT easier in Hydroneer!

The [b]visuals and graphics[/b] are well suited to the environment. The graphics resemble Fortnight, but have a little smoother details and rounded graphics. All basic and required animations are included and visible. Machines move about and the player can view materials going through machines, across conveyers, or into crushers. The output on some of the machines are quite funny as they launch out from the other side, and the player has to be ready with a bucket on the other side to catch the material. The terrain graphics are again smooth and don't have too many details, but in no way interfere with the game. Village ambiance and atmosphere was well designed and there is a day and night cycle included. The [b]sounds and music[/b] are mostly laid back and relaxed. There isn't anything over the top regarding the music scene and although it does suit the game well, don't expect any headbanging. A lot of sounds have been included and enhance the experience of play. Everything the player interacts with will make some sort of noise and informs the player with the sound that an action is completed. Both domains were done well, but I feel like a little more could've been added to further immerse the player into the game. Some missed potential here as a little more could've been done with atmospheric sounds. The village is nice to explore and look around, a little more noise would've made it a little livelier. NPC walking around doing their thing sort of helps.

Overall, I liked the game but I can see a lot of people being like "what the flipping flippers fridge firetruck fork fart did I just buy?". My immediate reaction was a little shock when I learned the character can only carry one thing at a time, but after learning the game a bit, planning my moves better, and discovering a little more useful tools around the map I was hooked. The game (and should say Dev) takes pride in not having to hand hold the player. Beyond the tutorial there isn't much help offered in the game, prompting the player to explore for themselves and discover what is possible. So, this is a difficult one to review. It has local split screen and has multiplayer online coop if one player uses Steam's Remote Play feature. Highly suggest players do their homework before purchasing, but would certainly recommend a purchase on sale. HUGE WARNING THOUGH - even to myself - the logic system has minimal instructions and can be very difficult to work with, unless you're good at basic programming.

Hydroneer: A Huge Disappointment After the 2.0 Release  (I am not the only one that feels this way)

I used to love Hydroneer—it was an amazing game with so much potential. But after the 2.0 release, the game has completely gone downhill. The dev's decision to rebuild the game broke everything. It’s now unplayable and ridiculously laggy. What was once a smooth, enjoyable experience has turned into a frustrating mess.

Before the rebuild, Hydroneer was one of the most enjoyable and satisfying mining and resource management games I’ve played. But the 2.0 release not only ruined the gameplay, it introduced new bugs and glitches that make it nearly impossible to enjoy. And don’t even get me started on the so-called “multiplayer” feature—nothing was delivered, and it was promised for so long.

The dev has gone from a one-man team with passion to a whole team, and it shows in the worst way possible. You’d think with all the millions of dollars made from the game, they’d be able to keep it playable and functional. But instead, it’s worse than ever. It’s such a shame because this game had so much potential, but the recent changes have ruined everything that made it great.

Save your money and avoid this game until they fix it. At this point, it’s hard to see Hydroneer ever recovering from this disaster.

After 42 hours in this game, I just can't play any more. I don't mind that the early game is tedious, but EVERYTHING about this game is tedious, and it doesn't seem to become less so. Even after purchasing the vehicles to allow better mining and smoothing of terrain, your projects only start to get bigger. The quests have an extremely slow ramp up, and you still get offered extremely low tier quests later on that seem to hold back more quests from appearing. There also doesn't seem to be much of a point to any of it. There's quests to unlock the stairs to the king, but if you just go to Volcadius, you meet him anyway, so it all seems pointless. Money is also extremely trivial after you get even a single mining machine set up. Crafting is boring, I was hoping it would be a little more specific and maybe you could unlock a wider variety of items, but you're limited to daggers, axes, swords, rings, amulets, and soup. There's also a bad fishing mechanic in the game that I barely touched.
Back to the tedium, even after installing some mods that allow for easier item management (no clipping on pallets) it's still a pain whenever you want to build anything. It would be amazing if you could put in an order with a store and they would drop pallets off at your claim instead of running back and forth in a store 100+ times to get pipes and conveyors.

We also have added in ‘backup’ saves to prevent total data loss. Try finding this backup, by opening up the game, pressing ‘continue’ on the main menu, then ticking the ‘Show Backup’ box. This will show a backup save file which hopefully won’t be corrupted.

Achei o jogo interessante, mas falta polir a jogabilidade que se torna confusa em muitos momentos, principalmente na questão de lidar com as ferramentas e na falta de um inventario. Então quando voce quer por exemplo comprar algo na loja, tem que pegar suas moedas na mão e carrega-las fisicamente até o local, complicando também a volta em que vai ter de trazer o troco e tudo o que comprou. O jogo também acaba ficando enjoativo e sem muito proposito a partir de um ponto onde voce já tem as RIGs de mineração prontas, elas trabalham sozinhas gerando uma quantidade enorme de dinheiro. O problema é que o jogador fica sem motivos para comprar os outros terrenos de mineração ou investir em ferramentas melhores, já que existem apenas quatro minérios e poucas opções de joias que podemos minerar. Seria interessante que tivéssemos minérios ou joias que fossem encontradas apenas nos terrenos mais avançados ou com as melhores ferramentas, assim o jogador teria um motivo para continuar investindo no jogo. Por fim posso dizer que o jogo é interessante, vou voltar a joga-lo no futuro aguardando algumas updates e também quero experimentar a DLC Volcalidus quando tiver a oportunidade

Good game for the cheap price tag, a definite buy on sale if you like tycoon-ish games. Though this really is a 'lite' game. 

The actual loop of gameplay is incredibly shadow with pretty abrupt dead-ends for most things. Money is incredibly easy to amass once you've made it past shovel and pan era and leaving piles of cash everywhere is common. 

Power crystals are essentially pointless, you smelt enough bars of shards in your first mine and even tiny ones last forever. In a 20 hour playthrough I never once had to replace a shard bar. Just make pressure pipes more expensive and scrub the shards or make the shards more useful.

Scratches a good itch of seeing mineral wealth go brrr, but not much to do with it. Making a cool deep T2 mine was engaging but then the fun ran out, doing T3 is the same process but just more expensive to tick a box.

Good fun for 20-ish hours if you like creating converyor machines, don't expect much strategy or effort like satisfactory or factorio. This is more a homage to old roblox tycoon worlds of the 201x's era.

The game rather well made, but fails to be all that interesting by the end. Especially grating is the final fishing quest of the base game, where you sit there, bored out of your mind, trying to catch the specific fish needed by the king's final guard. The fishing in this game is supremely uninteresting for it to be a mandatory part of completing the game.
I can understand hard games. I can understand soft games. But I will never understand why a developer would choose to make part of their game boring. There is no replay value here, unlike satsifactory or factorio. Having the equipment run off water is a novel and fun idea, but does not avail itself to building complexity as it does in better factory management games. 
The farming side of the game, likewise, is somewhat unique. But I find myself wishing I'd be playing stardew valley during the absolute slog that is the farming quest for the king's guard, or John Deere American Farmer (2006), which is a truely mid-tier game. The most fun I had, was creating a primitive repeating clock to water my plants, to reduce the lag of having that many water pipes watering my plants. 

Spend your time and money elsewhere. It's worth more than this game.

Es ist ein JA mit Einschränkungen, Ihr solltet daher bitte lesen was mich stört und unter welchen Umständen man es sich gönnen kann. 
Achtet am Besten auf ein Angebot, damit es möglichst günstig ist, nur so bekommt man da etwas für sein Geld, den es gibt Stör-Faktoren!!!

MEGA-Problem, hat man mal im Kreativ-Modus bzw. mit MODs gespielt kann es ein Riesen-Problem sein, ein Spiel mit Erfolgen zu starten, ich kann nur sagen, mir ist nicht gelungen, obwohl alle Mods deinstalliert  sind und Kreativ-Game nicht aktiv ist. Also kann ich NIE Erfolge erreichen, finde ich dreist! 

Es gibt einige Punkte die mich bei diesem Game echt stören:
Leider fehlen einige sinnvolle Bauteile wie z. b. eine Viertel-Wand, eine habe Hohe Wand (dreht man die halbe flache Wand, sieht man dies sehr deutlich. Es gibt nur Holztreppen gerade. Da wäre mehr gegangen.
- Im laufe der Zeit kann man sich mehre Fahrzeuge leisten, aber wenn man weit vom Fahrzeughändler weg ist, dort mit einem Fahrzeug hin fährt hat man das Problem, wie bitte soll man alleine 2 Fahrzeuge bewegen? Diese wurde aus Sicht von Single-Playern NIE durchdacht. 
- Ein weiter Punkt ist die "Helligkeit" in einem Gewächshaus, da gibt es die schönen Glaswände und Glasdächer doch trotz Glas wird es in Innenraum dunkel, es müsste / sollte heller sein, gerade wenn Pflanzen  wachsen sollen, was diese auch nur sehr sehr langsam tun, vielleicht weil es zu dunkel ist,
- Einiges was Technik angeht ist total schlecht erklärt und man blick nicht wirklich durch wozu einige bestimmte Teile sind. Angeblich soll es auch Teile geben die eine Art Auto-Repair-Funktion haben, doch dies habe ich nicht verstanden, konnte es nicht umsetzen. Wem Erfolge egal sind, kann hier mit einem MOD tricksen, dann geht nix mehr kaputt.
- Beim Graben per Hand muss man den umständlichen Weg gehen, alles erst in Eimer zu füllen, dann kann man diese Eimer ausleeren, leider gibt es nur einen kleinen Eimer. Alternativ kann man mit der Schaufel auch auf ein aktives Förderband klicken. Spart den Eimer, sind aber massig klicks.
 Der Abbau großer Materialmengen die man dann auch aktiv nutzen kann ist im Game nicht vorgesehen.
- Was auch nervig ist, ist der Transport von Bodenteilen, diese lassen sich nur super schlecht auf den LKW aufladen, doch sie müssen ja zum Ort wo man die Basis bauen soll, weil dies so nervig ist, habe ich in diesem Bereich die Cheat-Funktion fürs Bauen genutzt, den der Transport von vielen Teilen wäre einfach nur nervig, vor allem da sich Fahrzeuge sooooooo schlecht beladen lassen. 
Es gibt auch einen Mod mit dem man Bauteile erstellen kann, spart viel Zeit, nur gibt es halt keine Erfolge.

Das sind die Fakten die gegen dieses Spiel sprechen, es gibt jedoch auch einiges das schön gemacht ist. 
Einiges muss man halt auch erste mal richtig verstehen, hier fehlt eine gute Einarbeitung, bzw. man schaut sich Lets Play Videos an, um so einiges zu lernen.

Warum aus meinen NEIN nun es JA mit Einschränkungen wurde erklärt sich daher das es nun MODs gibt.
Hier gibt es praktische Mods die einem das Leben einfacher machen wie z. B.
- Unbeschränkt Treibstoff für die Autos
- Nichts geht mehr kaputt, macht das Leben so viel einfacher
- Teilauswahl über Menu-Taste, sehr praktisch, so bekommt man alles was man will, kein Transport, keine Ausaben dafür und dies ist gibt noch mehr Mods. 

Sonst kann ich sagen, einiges ist echt schön gemacht. Man braucht halt teils echt viele Bauteile. 


Wenn man eine TP-Rolle erwerben könnte zum Autohändler, wäre dies sinnvoll, dann wäre dieses Problem gelöst. Etwas bessere Erklärungen und mehr Licht durch die Glasteile und es wäre schon besser.
Doch in bezweifle leider das diese Probleme gelöst werden.

Was ich nicht verstanden habe, aus meiner Sicht schlecht erklärt ist, ist der Automatische Schmelzer wie man diesen optimal einstellt. Daher achtet bei Interesse auf ein Angebot, bei einem sehr günstigen Preis kann man einige schöne Stunden Spaß haben.

[h1]Automation Sim Lovers Beware: Tedium Can Spell Disaster[/h1]
[i]For what it's worth, my nearly-40 hour playtime with Hydroneer was over the span of quite a few years - before the Farming update and DLC - and mostly consisted of picking it up for 2-6 hours, inevitably burning out due to lack of QoL features, then trying again a few months later in the vain hope of an improved experience.[/i]

It was hard to compile my thoughts on Hydroneer for a long time, but after my latest attempt and becoming frustrated with how utterly anti-player the simple act of buying items is, I'm both putting this back on the shelf and unfortunately leaving a warning.

Hydroneer starts off as a pretty gruelling grind that sets the tone early. Drills don't come quickly, or easily - requiring quite a lot of starting cash that you need to manually sift and pan dirt (or engage in the "click to acquire" fishing minigame) for 1~2 hours - and once the first is acquired, the game largely becomes a waiting one as you struggle to get enough Iron to make more drills, as you can't directly buy any more.

This highlights the two largest problems I have with the experience as a whole: the tedium and the lack of quality-of-life features.


[b]Tedium[/b]

Subjective, but I've clicked with monotonous task-based games before without much gripe. The main point in making the tedious aspects of a game fun can come from a mixed bag of feedback, how you engage with mechanics, and how you're rewarded.
Hydroneer's earliest minutes highlight the main issue behind this: you're going to always be doing the same thing, you will always be at the same tech level once drills are unlocked, no matter what. Waiting for the numbers to climb up, ever so slothfully, so you can make that number climb a minuscule amount faster with yet another drill.

A grand weight of [i]300[/i] iron is required to get successive drills, which can easily eat up hours of your time while waiting for the first drill to chew out that amount. This tedium is barely broken up by the other ores/gems, as they ultimately fuel supplementary funds to (selectively useful) upgrades, ranging from lifegiving pipes, to the bane of my existence, conveyor belts.


[b]Lacking Quality-of-Life[/b]

On the note of conveyors, everything in Hydroneer is handled with physicality as priority, ultimately to the player's detriment after a few hours of play. There is no inventory, there is no HUD, you're expected to finagle items one at a time in your hands.

This isn't such an issue early on, when you only have a few items to work with, but a quick browse of the Discussions thread or Reddit will honestly highlight the bottleneck effect that I and others get once you're at the point of expanding your operations.

For conveyors to be so incredibly bulky, even with the use of pallets, to buy a simple setup [i]just[/i] to cut and sort gemstones should not take two full-round trips to accomplish. Why two trips? Because no matter your stacking skills, pallets do have an invisible limit to what they can hold, and you'll find yourself missing several pieces you've just bought from the shop, but couldn't see due to being blinded by their models while holding the pallet itself.

Just let us unlock something to have items shipped directly to the plot. It's a bafflingly easy fix to the biggest frustration of expanding.


[b]Conclusion[/b]

If you're into automation sims, or like the idea of an [i]extremely[/i] slow grind, and don't mind having large open spaces as the game rewards smaller setups, give it a shot. Two hours, provided you get the 300 iron for your second drill, will give you a taste of what the game's core is going to stay as.

I won't touch on the farming update aspect outside of my annoyance that another arbitrary and lackluster system took priority over making Hydroneer feel better to engage with, despite the tsunami of feedback Foulball have received. This stance is also reflected in the strange, paradoxical design choice of [i]"here's several immensely large play areas given to you, that lags horrifically on great rigs when you try set up operations to extract more than a sixth of it"[/i]. 

I get the point of sticking to visions, but when the vision compromises the gamefeel to the point of people begging you to fix it, to make it feel even moderately better, you're not going the right way.

A forethought: no blueprint mode especially hurts. You can't buy items in bulk, nor can you plan out to avoid successive trips (when the pallet decides to work).

Leider kann ich, nach "durchspielen" des Games (es hat kein wirkliches Ende) keine positive Bewertung abgeben.

Ja, das Grundprinzip ist weiterhin geil (ähnlich wie Satisfactory), aber letztlich haben mir folgende Punkte im Nachhinein die Freude genommen:

- die Performance geht bei Nutzung von Logikbauteilen massiv nach unten (nein, mein PC ist dafür nicht zu schwach, der lacht sich über die Anforderungen kaputt)

- Die Nebenquests stellen sich letztlich alles völlig überflüssig und nutzlos raus, da für den Fortschritt (neue Tiers, neues Equipment, neue Digging Sites usw.) absolut nicht relevant. Ja, der ein oder andere wird evtl. auf 2 Fahrzeuge stehen, die man mit speziellen Guilde Token erhalten kann, aber wirklich notwendig sind diese eben nicht und somit empfinde ich leider die Zeit, die ich unwissend in die Nebenquests geballert habe, als unnütz verlorene Zeit...

- "Freischalten" von Equipment ist, bis auf Bohrer-/Zerbröseler-/Druckverstärkerequipment (letzeres nie genutzt von mir) und einigen nicht wirklich notwendigen Tools, auch nicht vorhanden - man kann einfach alles kaufen und da man recht schnell viel Geld verdient, hat man alles Notwendige enorm schnell zur Verfügung und benötigt, genau genommen, nicht mal das max. Tier bei den genannten Gerätschaften.

Last but not least:

Den Rest gab mir der DLC, der letztlich ein Standalone Spiel ist.
Man nimmt exakt nichts mit in das neue Gebiet (keine money, kein Equipment, keine Tools), startet also bei exakt Null.
Es hätte genauso Hydroneer 2 sein können, aber dann müsste man sich ja nicht das "Originalspiel" vorher kaufen um den "DLC" spielen zu können ;-)
Es ist ein bisschen so, als ob man beim Elden Ring DLC mit seinem Charakter wieder bei Null starten müsste...

Wen all das nicht stört und auch auf Bauen, Buddeln und Fördern steht, der mag beherzt zugreifen!

This game is endless in the things you can do. If you are really technical you can spend forever trying to get your factory to the maximum efficiency. If you would rather build stuff and instead make your factory look nice to the people of hydroneer. Also if you like to mess around creative mode is the best way to do it. The shops are free, the tools are fun to play with and to make huge messes with. 

Along with this, the game is relatively bug free. On a normal play through, you would get no glitches. If you try to look for glitches through youtube, or on your on. You will eventually find some funny bugs here and there but nothing game breaking.

The only thing I don't like about this game is the start. The start is very slow and takes forever to get a drill. Even after that, the pipes and the other tools take a while too. 

This game still has a lot of potential of where it could go. At the time writing this there is only one DLC, there are many other islands that I could think of, just right off the top of my head.
Please don't let my critism discourage you from buying this game. It deserves more love than it is already getting.

"Hydroneer" to sandboxowa gra, w której wcielamy się w górnika, eksplorującego złoża złota i innych cennych surowców. Naszym zadaniem jest kopanie, topienie metali, produkcja biżuterii, broni oraz handel w celu zdobycia pieniędzy. Za zarobione środki możemy kupować nowe narzędzia, pojazdy i ulepszać swoje maszyny, co teoretycznie powinno czynić rozgrywkę coraz bardziej satysfakcjonującą.

Gra oferuje wsparcie języka polskiego, choć tłumaczenie nie jest idealne i momentami może utrudniać zrozumienie pewnych aspektów rozgrywki. Ponadto "Hydroneer" wspiera zapis w chmurze, co umożliwia łatwe przechowywanie postępów i grę na różnych urządzeniach.

Niestety, mimo ciekawego konceptu, "Hydroneer" na dzień dzisiejszy wydaje się niedopracowana. Sterowanie jest mało intuicyjne, co może być frustrujące i wymaga od gracza sporej cierpliwości. Niektóre mechaniki, które w teorii powinny dostarczać satysfakcji (np. kopanie czy tworzenie biżuterii), w praktyce stają się monotonne i nie angażują gracza na dłuższą metę. Brakuje tu dynamicznego rozwoju rozgrywki, co sprawia, że gra szybko staje się nudna i mało motywująca do dalszego eksplorowania.

This is a great game for people who are unemployed and want a very boring job that doesn't pay. There's nothing to do except mine. It takes about 20 clicks or key presses to get one unit of ore, which sells for very little. You have to pick up and sell everything one by one, meaning it takes like an hour and lots of carpal tunnel to buy even a few basic pieces of equipment. On top of this, the UI is the worst I've ever dealt with in any game. There's no 2D interface, the game relies on dropping things physically in the game world. It's easy to mess that up. For example, you have to drop a hot bar on an anvil in a specific location and have a limited time to do it. It's easy to drop in the wrong place, in fact I did it about 30% of the time. If you do so, it's easy to accidentally pick up the anvil rather than the bar. In either case you have to run back and heat the bar again. Very annoying.

On very rare occasions Hydroneers save files can be corrupted. This generally happens when someone closes the game while it is saving. We’ve added in measures to prevent this from corrupting but there are some outlying cases. 
We have also noticed that some anti-virus programs prevent Hydroneer from saving. Please list Hydroneer as an accepted program or consider disabling your anti-virus programs. (Windows Defender is fine, but other AV programs can have this issue)
We also have added in ‘backup’ saves to prevent total data loss. Try finding this backup, by opening up the game, pressing ‘continue’ on the main menu, then ticking the ‘Show Backup’ box. This will show a backup save file which hopefully won’t be corrupted.

If you’d like any more help with this or another issue, you can reach out to us by email: support@foulballhangover.com. If this has resolved your issue please consider updating your review. We’re a small team and reviews really help us out, thanks!

The gameplay loop in this game might be OK, but there are too many issues with it for me to recommend it. The game is, to put it bluntly, needlessly obnoxious. The interface is absolutely awful - the target cursor is rarely relevant - when you want to place something down/inside something else, you have to position the small circular *shadow* over where you want it to drop - it is nowhere near your cursor. Of the around 90 minutes spent in the game so far, at least 45 has been spent re-doing tasks because I missed a target.

The expected gameplay loop early on is:
* Get a shovel load of dirt and dump it in the basin.
* Fill a bucket with water and pour it in the basin.
* Use the brush to swish it around and expose ore/gems.
* Place 5-ish pieces of ore in a smelting pot and heat it over the fire.
* Pour the melted ore into a mold.
* Grab the mold while it's still hot, place it in the proper spot on an anvil, and hammer before it cools to craft the selected item.

The *actual* gameplay loop is as follows:
* Put a shovel load of dirt into the basin.
* Grab a bucket of water and pour it on the ground next to the basin.
* Try 2 or 3 more times until water actually lands in the bucket.
* Swish it around to reveal ore.
* Repeat to get enough ore to smelt.
* Drop a couple pieces of ore into the smelting pot with several landing on the ground outside. Search for the ones you dropped and put them back in the pot.
* Pick the pot up and try to place it on the smelting fire. Land it just enough on the edge that it rolls over, dumps the ore out, and falls off the fireplace. Collect the ore back into the pot and finally get it on the fire.
* Once the ore is melted, pour it into a mold, starting about a 10-second timer before the bar is too cold to work.
* Quickly drop the pot and grab the ore, then drop the ore on the opposite side of the anvil because the drop location is *so* far off from your target cursor. Pick it back up and finally after 4-5 tries get it into the spot to work it, at which point it is too cold to work.
* Put the bar back in the smelting pot, re-melt it, re-pour it, and try again to race the clock and get lucky enough to have the bar land where you need it.

Three fourths of your time in this game are spent fighting absolutely asinine controls for no good reason. They *could* make it so the cursor accurately targeted where you set stuff down, but instead chose to use a pointlessly obtuse shadow that you may not even notice, and definitely won't show up at all if you don't have light overhead, making it pointless to even think of working at night.

I absolutely do not recommend this game based  on the terrible controls alone.

It could be an interesting game if not every system purely relied on tedium.
You cannot handle more than one object at a time, mist is also an object, every item you might need needs to be bought at a high price, the actual mechanics are arcane and rely on trial and error, because the actual tutorial is borderline useless, leading to you sitting around with lots of useless BS you bought and didn'T figure out how to use well. Partial automation doesn't really work and just messes up already existing workflows. This game needs a very big QoL Upgrade.

I really wanted to like this game and I'd say most of the time I did. But eventually the issues overshadow any long term enjoyment. I lost all my money multiple times when it fell through an object which is annoying but isn't a deal breaker for me since it only happened a few times. But the final straw was losing my starter drill somehow. I think it flew up into the sky since there was another object attached to it. A buggy game with a lot of potential.

review:
Hydroneer is effectively a cartoony sim-lite, but lacks the charm or progression of most sims I've played. Your first couple hours will be hand washing dirt in a pan with very poor controls, trying to earn enough to set up simple automation. Once you've done that... you're effectively done. There's "higher tier" versions of the original equipment to buy, but it's literally just reskins with a faster output. There's some simple logic systems, but they're barely needed. There's other plots of land to buy than the starter plot, but they fundamentally gain you nothing other than more space to build the same stuff. 

Hydroneer is somehow radically less satisfying than even a standard farming sim, I think because there's very little clear progression (all the plots of land can be bought in the first few hours), and the mechanics barely change over time. Mixed with the lifelessness of the world and the poor visuals it's just not much of a game. I picked up the game and its DLC for $12, and even that feels like I overpaid. Minecraft over a decade ago had a better mining sim experience via mods... if you're itching for something like this, just go pick Minecraft up again.

Hydroneer is one of the coolest and most in-depth sandbox games ever. Hydroneer isn't for everyone. The game starts off pretty slow, with 2 hours of numbingly tedious gameplay to scrape together enough hydrocoins for a drill. The game embraces creativity a lot, and I sure got a hell of a lot of ideas when I got my hands on one of those drills. The hypnotizing clatter of the gold ore chunks falling into the pan and smelting the ores into a fine ingot is so satisfying. I can't get enough. The game is very confusing, it really doesn't tell you all that much and lets you explore on your own. With only a map in hand you are tasked to find the most efficient place to sell your fish. The map is quite big and it is easy to get lost, but I think it is just big enough to feel big but not big enough to feel overwhelming. Although the game is very grindy and tedious sometimes, I do find that the satisfaction of crafting your first automatic ore harvester is amazing. I haven't even messed with conveyer belts or all sorts of other automation methods yet and I've come up with so many clever ways to automate everything. The game lacks in story, but I doubt that's why you are here for. The game gives you goals for quests and that gives me the illusion of choice. I really enjoyed the process of finding a quest I liked and working towards that goal. The game is very relaxing and is really just a great comfort game. I don't really have any major complaints except the fact that the crouching animation was a bit too fast and that entering vehicles glitched out the camera a bit. Overall? A very solid indie game. You can let your creativity roam free and do whatever your heart desires. Oh and I forgot to mention, you can buy nukes in this game.
this game has a lot of grinding but it's awesome

Definitely give it a chance past the horrible intro/tutorial (lack thereof) What's there is a very good mining game.

There's logic chains so you can automate pretty much everything late game and it can be a lot of fun figuring this out with the physics gameplay.  I enjoyed the logic chaining a lot compared to Satisfactory, because everything is physical vs just imaginary on a belt.

review:
[h1] My Issue Is on the Multiplayer Aspect [/h1]

I can respect the grind as a single developer trying to create a game nowadays, especially with the oversaturation of games in the overall market. That being said, it might possibly be an overshadowed mistake; you need to talk about the multiplayer aspect of the game if the user-defined tags, and many people say it's multiplayer, but in fact it isn't. You need to understand "Remote Play" isn't actually multiplayer. That being said, I understand that the developer is actively trying to get multiplayer to work, but if you don't actively say there isn't multiplayer, people will be confused, like me.

I shouldn't need to go to the developer's YouTube channel, looking for this information on multiplayer and finding a video that was recorded 2 years ago.  It should be on the main Steam page illustrating (possibly through a video, picture, or text) that there isn't a true multiplayer, but it's active development. I hate to be that guy when it's a single developer, but you can put in the description or something that there isn't actually multiplayer and that there is only remote play. 

This game has potential, and I'm in no way saying the game is bad. But I bought it specifically to play with someone, only to find out you can't after purchasing, which is never good. It doesn't matter if you're an AAA developer or an Indie developer.

Edit: I am writing this for the slim chance that the developer reads this again.

I would revert my review if you do one thing, and I'm not expecting a developer to heed to my whims do to a single bad review, but if you do take my request seriously than I will revert my review.

You need to make the information about the lack of true multiplayer more readily available. Make it a picture or some text explaining that it's only "remote play"; why is it that any information on state or whereabouts for the multiplayer is 2 years old? In simpler terms, make it easier to find this information by updating the page. I shouldn't need to do a background check to find this information. I've returned my game and my friends game copy due to this simple mistake, but I would rebuy the game and revert my review if you fix this.

-The lack of inventory system and hotbar really hamper the game. Want to check your map? Go get your map. Want to switch tools? Climb above ground and grab one at a time. Imagine in minecraft if you are digging at the beach and get 200 sand blocks down and need a pickaxe. You need to climb all the way back to the surface to get it. You even have to carry money with you. It's easy to lose things because of this, and makes it hard to store items without the game chugging. I see the dev defending this in the comments, and I respect having a vision, but if everyone complains about the same thing, maybe you should consider having it as an option for those who want it, and keeping your vision as an option for those who don't, as a majority of the reviews, and even gameplay videos from those who love the game complain about this. It's supposed to be immersive, but it makes the game a chore to play, rather than fun. 
-Placing things are not accurate, and you often times accidentally grab the thing you're trying to use, like an anvil, rather than the tiny gem on top of it, and have to place the anvil again and then reorganize the things laying on top of it. This happens with controller and KB&M
-The optimization is really poor. In an automation game, this is really bad. The frame rate chugs on my 3060 and 3070 with so many things active, and the way the inventory is laid out, nothing despawns and things accumulate taking up resources really quickly, and even strong machines start to buckle quickly.
-NPCs and quest are useless. They hand you a parchment with a item and number on it, and if you hand them the wrong thing they throw it on the ground and say "That's not right!". Throwing tiny items makes them easy to lose, and it should be improved.
-Things are way to expensive to use for what you get with your money. If you're not cheating, it'll take you hours of tedious panning, and selling to get enough for basic pipes and a conveyor belt pieces, which won't really get you started. You have to either use creative mode, which kills any sense of progression, or go at a slow, tedious pace and have progression move at a snails pace.
-Navigating the roads is confusing without the map, which due to the inventory system you have to carry with you at all times in a truck bed, then get out to check it as everything looks the same texture wise.


This game could be great, but the lack of budging on the vision the dev has I feel is keeping it from that greatness. Once again, I respect having a vision, but if it's a very vocal complaint maybe your vision is not for everyone. Most negative reviews all have the same complaints, and I bought it anyway, but I see what they mean. Any excitement and urge to play the game is killed by the thoughts of how tedious it is. Any valid criticism is met with the dev replying that the game isn't for you and to return it, but that's a sad view in my opinion as it's just deflecting criticism rather than using it to grow and improve.

review:
The game badly needs a story mode or some kind of quest / tutorial to try and get you off of the ground and out of the early game faster.  Whatever might seem interesting from an automation standpoint is going to get erased in your first hour of shoveling dirt into a bucket.  This aint Factorio or Satsifactory.

The controls and "everything is an individual item" design is the real killer.  I can't remember the last time I played a game with controls and an environment this clunky.  When combined with no inventory and the fact that EVERYTHING must be interacted with in this extremely clunky manner, it just kills the experience.  Imagine trying to play an FPS-based crafting game, but the crosshair alternates between the middle of your screen when you need to pick something up, and somewhere vaguely to the bottom right when you need to drop something.  Now also imagine I just took hundreds of rocks and scattered them on the ground for you to pick up and put down  If you manage to tediously put all of the rocks in a basket, you get a few more points than if you didn't.

What's the reward?  Well more rocks of course.  That's the game.

If you were given a magnet / vacuum or any kind of tool in the first 10 minutes of the game that could avoid the tedium of picking up individual nuggets or dirt clods, or perhaps ANY kind of inventory, you might avoid at least some of the time-wasting effort of scraping up pebbles off the ground.  I vaguely recall from Youtube vids that such an item exists later in the game, but it's doubtful most people will get there if they can't so much as make it past the hurdle of being directed to a wiki to learn or know exactly how to progress from hand-digging and hand-sorting to even the most basic of automation.

Lol, I still can't fathom who thought it was a good idea (and then kept it in the game at release) to make picking things up use the crosshair, but placing things down use a completely different crosshair instead of just, you know, just dropping it from the middle of your POV.  I'm guessing a dev figured that holding the item in the middle of your screen might block your view, but then why not just hold it to the side until it's going to be placed in the middle?  It's so awkward and unintuitive that I can't imagine how people didn't complain of this in the years of early access.

Complete lack of tutorial, no toolbar/inventory system (that I know of) and just a generally difficult game to play for no apparent reason. Had to go to youtube for a tutorial on how to even find a shovel and then find out how to use it. A very good concept but for me, it's just unnecessarily hard to play.

review:
After trying this game, I cannot recommend it to most people that I know of. Nevertheless I feel this game is really good and that it scratches that aumation itch in a different and unique way.

First off, the controls are a HUGE turn off for me, the very awkward schema is unintuitive and you will be misclicking stuff a lot. Even after 4 hours, it still fell clunky a badly designed.

Secondly, you do not have an inventory, every tool, every resource and even your currency is an in game entity, with their own model and physics. On the plus side, this is handled surprisingly well: currency goes in a stack, resources and ores no clip among then, which allow you to store them in pans and containers, and your tools will stick to your vehicles, which ultimately results in way less jank than expected. 

Nevertheless, you can see why these systems are abstracted away: It's cumbersome and. in my opinion, don't add too much to the overall experience. You will be distracted by these mechanics instead of enjoying the game.

edit to reply to the dev:

1) First of all, thanks for responding,

2) Secondly apologies for my rant, it was really disheartening not to have the same experience as other folks for this game apparently

3) Third a few specific issues to speak more technically:

3.1) Issue: The tutorial is missing key instructions with gaps of knowledge for new players, just FYI. For example, from the "pick up the lantern" goes to "use the shovel",
Solution: here's a more straightforward example on how to fix this:
"Hello Hydroneer! See that lamp post? There's a couple of items there for you! Pick up the first one, then return for the other. You can use the shovel on the dirt - any part is fine! Scoop up some dirt then place it on the other bucket item you see by the river."

3.2) After selling items in the tutorial i was under the impression that you... you know, get the money? But apparently there is no inventory? or at least not at that point in the game? So when i was asked to buy something i had no idea where the money was? Until i saw that they were still in the bucket where you first sell the gems?... Sorry this is very counterintuitive. Couldnt you just.... u know, have the money like every other game?

3.3) When i did all of the above and was asked to buy more items (e.g. furnace, cast pots, etc.) i was asked to load them in the nearby cart. I could not load the items for the life of me. review: Very good game Minecraft in a way 👍🏻

This game is very pointless. It feels like it is missing half of the game loop.

You start the game panning by the river for materials. You grab a shovel to dig, drop dirt in a bucket, bucket to pan, add water to pan, use a brush to receive your rewards: Some iron ore, gold ore, and raw gems. No functional value to any of those, just sell them to the merchant. Then use that money to buy an automatic miner and some pipes to do the digging for you, then... Go play something else, because you've reached the end game here. 

You can smelt the ore into ingots, but it's still vendor trash. Slightly higher value vendor trash, but still vendor trash. Buy an anvil and forge that ingot into a dagger(or mix an ingot with a gem to make a ring!), and then march on over to the same vendor because nothing you can craft has any use. What's all this money for? Vanity, mostly. You can purchase another mining plot, set up another automatic miner, and get the same materials you already have. You can save up for the tier 2 or tier 3 miner to do the same thing but faster. But the set up will be identical, and you'll still be crafting daggers. 

Zero progression, zero goals, nothing to do but amass a useless pile of coins and marvel at your wasted time.

This is the first game in my extensive steam library I wish I could leave a neutral on. It's fun. There is about 6-8 hours of true 'content'. You progress your first mine with more and more automation in that time. Then you're done with all the automation. After that, it's just 'more'. It takes my tiny 3 miner base at the bottom of "tier 1" in the starter area about 30 minutes of pure idle (maintenance can be automated) to create enough wealth to buy virtually any item in the game. You can go much, much further, but it's just going deeper to set up higher level machines in the exact same order to produce the exact same materials to craft and sell the exact same items, at a higher value. There are quests, which give you a secondary currency you can use to work on a side activity of gardening, which just returns more of the same secondary currency, which you can ultimately use to buy fancier house building parts, which are all purely cosmetic. 

There is also a DLC to go to a second island, which is basically a new game in a volcano which makes water management slightly harder, and has two new materials, but otherwise you're going to put machines in pretty much the same order to produce the same materials to craft and sell the same items. 

So a chill/cozy game that might make you think occasionally, but is more of a 3d incremental game than anything else.

review:
Honestly, if I wasn't playing this because my son wanted to work on his machine, I would have quit 80 hours ago. It's been a slog from the first few minutes and it never gets better, but that boy is my world and he loves this game and it's coop (which is great btw)... so here we are.

Lets start with the obvious. This game is the brain child of a singular (assuming) very amateur developer. Not that this in of itself is a bad thing, but there is a severe lack of depth. You can smelt ores and create weapons... but you only ever create one of five items, and they are not useful for anything but selling... and the only point of smelting more ore is to create an item that sells a calculable amount more than the last thing you made. MORE ORE = SAME BUT HIGHER QUALITY ITEM = MORE DIGI-DOLLAR. It's simplistic and boring. What do you do after you have made some decent bank? ... well you create a machine that pumps out even more raw materials so you can do it all again. I ask you... why can't I take my beautiful sword worth 150K and smash some baddies with it? It's worthless. Time spent in this game feels more meaningless than most. Especially when doing the simple exercise of moving and placing items can take ages... which brings me to the next point of contention.

The control mechanics for placing items is fully autistic. Rotate three times and the item now fits in a space where it didn't fit, but should fit, but no longer works for your construction due to the direction it shoots out ores... Or perhaps you need to look at the location of your item placement from a different angle, sometimes that works too, like a sculptor peering into the depths of their creation for inspiration... somehow now from the left you can see "AH YES that does fit"... FFS unalive me now.

And the DLC... Well I haven't seen it. My kid doesn't want to go there because he would lose everything. Yes that is right, you cannot access the DLC without saying goodbye to all the hard work you put into your main game's bases. No ores, no items, nor hard earned and nary spent digi-dollars can be brought with you to the new volcanic isle. I almost wish I had started there (since I bought the dlc with the game...) because I can't fathom spending double digits in hours to create new systems to do the same exact thing I did on the main island (WITH EXTRA STEPS) for the exact same outcome reached on the mainland. Why would I do that?

What confused me is that the Dev (nascent as they are in their trade) decided to double down on what they had going on with the DLC instead of improving the base game. I am fully behind them (financially, obviously) and I understand the need for green... But this game is not done. It's shallow, it's clunky, and it is frustration without reason. That is the whole game.

Nice and fun in general, however, I have a few gripes.

- The picking up and dropping mechanics are extremely annoying. If you want to drop something from your hand into something, you need to position yourself so that thing is on the bottom right of your screen, indicated by a small circular shadow that's only visible in the daylight.

- Traveling from area to area is extremely tedious, unless you have the truck.

- Not really a gripe with the game, but just so you know the game feels kind of like a simulator as you generally follow the same process for digging and mining several times before you get anywhere.

- This is the biggest one I have of all. Many of the machines/equipment snap to a grid within your dig site, and all resources, as well as machines/equipment can be picked up with E, meaning if you accidentally point your screen next to a resource and try to pick it up while it is on something, you will end up picking up the thing its on instead of the resource, and unsnap it from the grid. The number of times I've had to keep moving my stuff around because of this is beyond me, and it's even driven me to quit a few times lol.

That being said, I still generally enjoy the game, and I am always curious to discover something new the more I play. So in the end, still a good game and recommended if you can get past the points above.

I finally played enough to give it a review. I would have quit playing and returned this game after 10 minutes if I could still leave a review. 

The programmer in me has just one thought: WTF. 

The gamer in me also has the same thought, but also, WTF. 

I spent the entire time repeating the same task over and over and now I have enough money to upgrade my shovel, which means filling my bucket takes 4 clicks instead of 8 maybe (I didn't actually try it). So you get to do the same exact thing, but with ~75% of the effort. The problem is that the process is beyond tedious and isn't fun, so making it 75% easier is like polishing a turd; it's still a turd. 

There is no inventory except what you hold in your hand. There's no map except when you hold one in your hand.

There's no info available in game. You start out with nothing and no idea what to do lol. Games that follow conventions can get away with this, but not this game.

Placing things inside another item (like the pan) requires standing near it and lining up so when you drop it, it falls in the item.  And of course it doesn't fall straight in front of you like you might expect, it falls off to the side. I did discover that you can click the bucket from a distance to fill it with the shovel, but that's the only thing I found that does that (WTF). You still have to line up your bucket to dump it into the pan. It defies nearly all gaming conventions for an ideology I can't even fathom.

It would be far more realistic and fun if just taking the pan and standing in water or putting it under a water source let you sift it; but no, you have to drop your bucket in water, then pick it up, then dump the water in the pan, then pick up a brush and then click the pan to sift it. WTF. And why can't I just fill the pan directly? You can place a single shovel of dirt in the pan, but it holds 4. If one shovel of dirt is in the pan, you can't empty a full bucket of dirt in the pan, you have to dump the pan out first. WTF.

I'm certain the only reason it has decent ratings is because anyone who doesn't like it can't bring themselves to play the game long enough to qualify for leaving a review. It's a similar phenomenon to games with demos. Can't leave a review by playing a demo and anyone who doesn't like it doesn't buy the game, so can't ever review it.

This game has a lot of potential, but I guess it's just not for me in it's current state.

Alright, buckle up because we're diving deep into the world of Hydroneer. This game, folks, let me tell you, it's like a digital gold rush meets engineering genius meets that feeling you get when you finally solve a puzzle after hours of head-scratching.

First off, Hydroneer ain't your run-of-the-mill game. No sir, it's a sandbox extravaganza where you, yes YOU, get to live out your wildest dreams of striking it rich in the mining biz. Think Minecraft meets the Discovery Channel's Gold Rush, but with a dash of mad scientist vibes thrown in for good measure.

The graphics? Oh man, they're like something out of a futuristic dream. Crisp, clean, and so realistic you can practically smell the dirt (in a good way). From the shimmering rivers to the majestic mountains, every pixel is a testament to the artistry of the developers.

And the gameplay? Don't even get me started. It's like they took the best parts of crafting games and resource management sims, threw them into a blender, and hit the jackpot. You start off with just a humble shovel and a dream, but before you know it, you're knee-deep in machinery, building your own mining empire from the ground up.

But it's not just about digging for gold (although that's pretty darn satisfying). Hydroneer lets you flex your engineering muscles too. You can build intricate contraptions, from conveyor belts to elaborate water systems, all designed to maximize your mining efficiency. It's like playing with virtual Legos, only way cooler.

And let's talk about the thrill of discovery. Every nugget you uncover feels like striking gold (pun intended). There's this rush that comes with uncovering hidden treasures, upgrading your equipment, and watching your bank account swell. It's addictive in the best possible way.

Now, I won't lie, Hydroneer isn't without its quirks. Sometimes the controls can be a bit wonky, and yeah, there's a bit of a learning curve when it comes to mastering all the tools at your disposal. But hey, isn't that part of the fun? Embracing the challenge, honing your skills, and ultimately, reaping the rewards.

In conclusion, if you're looking for a game that combines creativity, strategy, and that sweet, sweet rush of hitting paydirt, look no further than Hydroneer. It's like a virtual playground for aspiring minors and engineers alike, with enough depth to keep you coming back for more. So grab your pickaxe, fire up your imagination, and get ready to embark on the mining adventure of a lifetime. Hydroneer, my friends, is where the gold (virtual, of course) truly shines.

My Review Revision

I've come back and played another 17 hours because I got excited seeing the """"Optimization Update""""

I thought "oh boy! They finally fixed the problems with this game!"....

They did not.

Unfortunately, the game still doesn't do the most basic entity stacking optimizations you could expect. Filled up a bucket with about 8k iron, went to dump it into the forge. The game actually froze for 30 seconds.
This isn't some elaborate stress test I constructed. This is something the normal progression of the game asks you to do.

I genuinely don't understand how something this fundamental can still be missing from the game.

In a factory game, putting a million physics rigidbodies all running in realtime is the most caveman-esque solution I've ever seen.

In LITERALLY every single factory game I've ever played, entity stacking, physics pausing, item clumping, etc. are present.

This isn't like NASA level stuff I'm talking about, these're basic solutions to a problem you'd expect to encounter in a factory game.

I'm just so disappointed, because I genuinely want to love this game, but it just keeps stabbing me in the back...I guess I'll go reinstall satisfactory.

That's... a tough game to review, and my relationships with it could be only described as love-hate. I hate to love it.

It's a game about mining with automation, but mining is first and foremost. And all its problems arise from this. You dig the dirt, you clean it up to find something useful in it, get the resources, sell the resources or make something out of them and sell that for slightly higher price. However, almost everything is just a little bit more inconvenient than it absolutely has to be.

You dug the dirt, now you have the inconvenience of uneven ground until you buy a rake to fix that. You bought a rake - have fun raking every tile separately without ability to hold the button and just keep the elevation. And pray it won't change raking direction or elevation at the last moment before you click. Because it can, and it will, and suddenly you have a block of dirt where you don't want it or a hole where you don't want it. You buy a pickaxe and want to dig down - well, you can, but it's awfully slow, and you won't see anything underground. You take your trusty lamp with you, but can't hold a pickaxe... ok, time to go buy a helmet with a forehead lamp. You bought a helmet, equipped it with Q and mining got better, but you can't enter any vehicle while in that hat. You have to unequip it, because... it counts as a vehicle, of course. What else? Bought a machine to dig into the ground? Well, it can't keep the elevation either. It can't even keep itself flat. Bought a ground flattening machine? It does the job just fine, but can't flatten dirt when it's just a bit too high, so make sure to start from the highest place and whittle it down first. Belts could be only built on pipes, and you can't take out a pipe from a belt to replace it. You have to remove a belt segment first.

...oh, right, and the biggest inconvenience of them all. You have no inventory, and EVERY SINGLE ITEM IN THE GAME always exist in the world in some form. Probably the only exception I found so far are spanners to fix your machines. Yes, of course they break. Why would you think that automation present in the game will just work? Anyway, every single pipe, belt, floor, wall, or almost everything else have to be bought in a shop and brought to a dig-site, and you can't just buy "pipes" or "belts" and lay them down happily. Of course not. Not only you can't make them (even though you can make weapons and jewelry), but they exist in different types like straight pipe, bent pipe, T-junction pipe, X-ju... oh, right, there's no X-junction pipe for whatever asinine reason. Belts also exist in variants as straight, left turn, right turn, up belt, left filter belt, right filter belt. Bought a wrong one? Well, too bad, the best you can do is to put it aside and hope you'll need it later.

And so on, and so forth. I can list every single inconvenience for hours at this point. And yet, I love the game and I don't know why.

BTW, buy yourself a few extra carts asap. Carts and cars are the closest approximation of an inventory you'll have in this game, as well as a pan for small items. You can attach a cart to a car if you hop on top of a storage part of a car and unequip your cart (E) or enter driving mode (Q). When you visit a shop, just go there with a cart and drop everything you want to buy into it. This way, you won't have to move items one by one to the buy platform and then again to your car. Just don't forget to pay, or your ears will be assaulted with a loud scream as soon as you try to leave the shop with "stolen" goods. The more of them in a cart, the louder it will be.

And two more tips: always have a bucket of water in every car with inventory, and change drop target pointer color (displayed on the ground where the item you hold in your hands will drop) to white. You'll thank me later.

I spent about 30 mins playing the tutorial on this game.  To be honest I'm on the fence about it so far.

The Good
-The crafting system looks really deep and requires alot of planning ahead and figuring stuff out which I love
-Once you figure out the controls it plays pretty smoothly.  Default controls are a little weird (i.e. R is the default rotate key when placing things) but it looks like you can rebind them how you want.

The Meh
-Graphics are meh
-I noticed I was getting the odd stutter but it wasn't frequent
-Steep learning curve.  I'm cool with that, but I could see it being a huge turnoff for people.

The Bad
-Why the hell do you have a pointer to indicate where you are going to drop stuff but then it actually drops to the right of the pointer where the shadow of the object is?   That was incredibly frustrating to me.   Give me an option to disable the shadow and drop stuff where I'm actually looking at.

The Funny
-I probably spent half the time I was in the tutorial trying to figure out how to buy things.  I found it pretty funny after a while but I suspect it's a little frustrating for people.  (You have to drop your coins into the bucket and left-click the red button, which is counter-intuitive to most of the other controls).
-Took me a good 5 minutes to figure out how to use a shovel properly and it's one of the first tasks you have to do in the tutorial

I'm giving this a thumbs up right now because I can see the potential the game has, but I'd say it's about a 5/10 overall.   I'm gonna try playing more on the weekend now that I finished the tutorial.

My advice - take this game with a grain of salt.   Don't get angry or frustrated.  Just laugh at how silly the controls and gameplay is if you can't figure out it.   That's what I did and I found it pretty fun even if it was janky as hell.

review:
Short update 2026 - warning before you buy - 80% of positive reviews are botted, just look at all recent positive reviews that are coming from private accounts with random numbers in the end. It's been botted for years, if only dev's would invest those money and effort into a game over the years - maybe it would be playable, but seems like that is not happening anytime soon (spoiler - never).

[b] Don't get misled by positive reviews if you are looking for automation type of a game, because it's not. [/b]

I have about 40 hours in this game, probably 25 hours if not more I spent running back and forth to a shop buying pipes and repair kits. You have to physically grab every single piece of pipe or item from the store and walk with it to tractor (assuming you parked on sale point). Alternatively, you can get a wooden cart and just spam items on top of it and as soon as they will settle down in the cart they will lose collision, basically allowing you to slowly but surely stack hundreds of pipes onto the cart on the same spot. But the fact that you have to find the ways to cheese the purchase from store in order to save time is insane.

On the gameplay side, you technically don't have to progress further than tier 2, because on tier 2 you can mine corestone - end game resource. That's it... Game completed. You can also make a farm to grow crops from which you can create a soup, but there is no way to fully automate farming so you have to manually run like around constantly collecting and then planting everything one by one over and over again.

There are also quests in the game for two factions: miners and farmers, each will give you unique tokens helping you to progress into the end game. Mining is okay, but farming is so much grind to get anywhere that you probably will skip that unless you are part of 1% tryhard players (according to Steam achievements).

Buy this game if you want to mindlessly spend your time, but, if you are looking into sandbox with automation that actually feels rewarding with "visible" progression then I suggest to look elsewhere. There is nothing more pleasing in sandbox games with automation than to see you factory/farm or whatever grow before your eyes, first by you putting in lots of effort and then watching that effort pay off because everything is automated. This game makes you constantly work, check filters health, replant crops, etc. and you can never just stand and admire your beautiful creation that just "works".

There are mods in the game that can help you a little bit with annoyances, however, according to comments on each of them, they tend to break every other update so I did not installed them.

このゲームの購入を迷ったら、このゲームのグローバル実績を確認してみてください。
最も達成率の高い「My First Hydrocoin」の達成率が恐らく40%程度ではないでしょうか？
（本レビューを書いている2024年7月13日時点で、38.6%です）
この実績の達成条件は「初めて物を売却し、ゲーム内通貨を入手する」です。
たったそれだけのことすら半分以上のプレイヤーが達成できていない。そういうゲームです。
私は「ダートワンド」を入手するまでプレイしましたが、このゲームを他人に薦めることは無いと思います。

～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～～
以下、「買っちゃったけど返品するのも何だしプレイしてみよう」という殊勝な人向けのアドバイス。
①最初に「設定」→「ゲームプレイ」から「ターゲットカラーをドロップ」を変更してください。オススメは青か緑です。
本ゲームが上記のような初心者バイバイになっている最大の原因は物を置く場所の感覚が掴みづらいことにあると私は考えています。
実は物を置く場所（右手の手元）に影ができているのですが、これがデフォルトでは灰色で非常に認識しづらいです。
②カートをインベントリ代わりに活用しましょう。カートに乗せて動かなくなったアイテムは衝突判定が無くなります。物をたくさん買う時はカートに乗せてカートごと移動し会計しましょう。
③最初の拠点近くにあるトラックはQで乗れます。降りるときもQです。東側の街に買い物に行くときに活用してください。私はフォントのせいでQを2と勘違いして困っていました。
④Steamコミュニティハブに「Hydroneer 日本語ガイド」という素晴らしい知見がまとまっているので、是非参考にしてください。
最初の拠点をある程度自動化できるまでの辛抱です。頑張ってください。

Building and various other tasks in the game is extremely messy and difficult because there's no inventory system at all, not even a hot bar system. I've spent more time transporting and organising my build spaces than actually building or playing the game.

I get what the developers were going for with the appeal of manually transporting and placing blocks and items instead of an inventory, but it just doesn't work for me since I constantly misplace items.

The game doesn't allow you to place conveyors without a pipe already attached to them which ends up making bigger setups a little more tedious

Would be nice if say the construction hammer allowed you to store, remove, and place item's instead of the current build system where blocks constantly take up space, making you create a huge mess whenever you want to redesign an aspect of your factory.

There also needs to be more content within the game. There is not much of an objective or reason to expanding your base or production line other than for the sake of doing so once you get a certain point in the game.

EDIT: actually, I've come back and crystalized my thoughts. Original ramble at the bottom.

The game is miserable.
The premise is great! Mining and panning and eventual automation with some fun side things like farming. But every step you take feels like a slog. The core mechanic is clunky and weirdly unrewarding.

I understand that early game is meant to be slow. 'Manual labor' to get your ore nugs and all that. But even when i scrounged enough for my first water pumps and could pan four (!) whole piles of dirt at a time it was still clumsy. The pans don't fall straight on flat dirt. I have to constantly pick up and drop my tools. The money you make is too piddling.
I fished for an hour, just brainlessly, one hand on mouse other on my phone waiting for sound cues so i can scrounge a few hundred coins for the first machines. It was only at that point, like, what, three hours in, i could actually start engaging with one of the main game mechanics. And even then! I might as well not bother. I don't think i payed off the damn anvil with how little smithing actually adds to the crafted item's price.

After letting my single driller and washer run for another hour while as i, you guessed it, just kept fishing to have some actual spending money, i made some jewelry. Alright. i slowly dragged them to the stock market and got myself a WHOLE 4k coins. Incredible! You can't buy ♥♥♥♥ with that. To set up so much as a single conveyor square to even think about upping production i would need like 1k in belts alone, and the tedium of individually moving each block around. 

Ok. fine, I thought. I've slogged through the rough earlygame, i've given benefit of doubt, now it's time to actually… actually start playing the game? After five whole hours? 
That can't be right. There has to have been fun somewhere here?

I bought a quad because the walking speed is obnoxious and the map is empty. I packed my money and a 2k bar of gold i'm saving for the stock market on the back and drive around a bit. Look inside the mountain, whatever.
At this point i'm not too sure what even happened for my cart and quad to straight evaporate. From what i've been googling its a known issue. I don't know if i should rag on the devs for it or not. They've tried to fix it? But they've don't it in the dumbest way possible because i had my new quad and old cart next to each other so clearly something somewhere went horribly wrong with the respawning mechanic. (which i kept fiddling with for a good 20mins so don't say i give up easy)

Don't get me wrong. The bug (?) isn't the reason i'm throwing in the towel, it was just the last straw. Because my meager gains poofing wackily out of existence really drove the point home.
This is it.
The progression curve is a 90* angle. 
And I've already seen what the game is. Slow, monotonous (in a bad way), and tedious with every single click.
No step up the tech tree will change that.

There is none of the 'relaxing mundanity' of stuff like Shipbreaker or those powerwash games. 
The automation is piddling and locked soooooooo far up the cash tree its borderline unreachable. Nor is it even that effective or potentially creative. The world is empty and needlessly spaced, the main mechanic is waiting and awkwardly angling your cursor to drop things. The prices are completely unbalanced and in turn ruin any of the side things. (why would i build a cute house when i can buy an entire sorter for the price and have actual progress??) And the overall lack of any tutorialization or any kind of ingame manual at least doesn't help either.

It's just. I've suffered through bad mechanics for the juicy bits, ok? I was a WoW player once upon a time. But if you take out the miserable mechanics here, there's just not even a game left.

REFUND / DON'T BUY

I've actually had my eye on Hydroneer for a very long time, 4 years to be exact.  Ever since I saw "Lets Game it Out" trying to break it like he breaks every game it’s had my eye.  There was something about it that always gave me pause though.  Maybe it was the advertised price of the game vs my perceived value from the game play I’d witnessed.  That said, this year when I saw it discounted on the Steam Summer Sale I finally decided to break down and get it.  So, was I disappointed? 

Starting out I gotta say that I was fully expecting the game to be a bit of a grind.  That said, I didn’t realize how chaotic the beginning would be.  Placing a shovel full of dirt into a bucket, pouring water on it, and then having to scrub, just to get one little chunk of iron worth practically nothing… Well, it was painful.  I quickly found myself trying ANYTHING to get the system more streamlined.  Started out by realizing that if I shoveled up a few dirt balls I could then combine them and drop them in the bucket, with the goal of washing more dirt at one time.  Then I moved on to realizing that if I had a pipe dripping into the dirt bucket I wouldn’t have to gather water with a separate pail to do the same job.  On and on I found little ways here and there to streamline the gathering of resources.  So how long did it take?

Well, it’s 6 hours later and I’m writing this review.  In that 6 hours I got one drill up and running as well as one cleaner.  I also got a little conveyer belt to clean gemstones and then separate the power crystals, the gemstones, the iron, and the gold into separate buckets.  I’ve got an anvil and a hammer, with absolutely no idea how to use them.  Also have a crucible that seems to melt down metal into single bars.  Melt down a ton of iron chunks and you get a large bar.  Melt down one iron chunk and you get a small bar.  Doesn’t matter how much you put in the crucible, it always pours out one bar.  Makes for easy carrying, but haven’t really figured out how to properly measure a bar so you can actually craft anything with them.

I think that’s my only real complaint with Hydroneer.  There are some very helpful tooltips when you pick up items, but there’s no real tutorial.  I have to admit, my first 10 minutes in the game were extremely chaotic because I didn’t know what I was supposed to do.  I had the buckets and scrub brush, but it took me a while to find the shovel laying off to the side.  Graphics were also an issue when I started the game up.  For some reason the default setting for motion blur was 100%, which made any movements really crazy.  I dropped it down to 0% and everything was good.  That’s not really something I’d take off points for though.  It was a really easy to locate and change the setting.

I saw quite a few people complaining about the DLC, and I’m assuming those people paid full price for it when it first came out.  That said, I haven’t really gotten into the DLC but I really have to say that if it added as much content as they’re talking, it’s well worth it.  The new island is bigger, there are new ways of doing things, and it forces you to basically start over again so you’re not going to instantly hit the end-game.  This, in my eyes, makes the total price I paid of $19 well worth the expense.  In fact, upon reflection, this game might even be worth it’s full price.

So, getting back to the first question I posed.  Was I disappointed?  Well, no I wasn’t.  There is a lot of content in the game and something for everything.  Are you a machine builder?  They’ve got conveyers, logistics, it’s all in here.  Are you a farmer?  They’ve got crops, tractors, fields to buy and use for growing, pipes for watering.  Do you just want to casually fish?  You can do that too, which also includes the use of fishing traps.  There’s a full-blown, yet fairly basic, economy in the game that actually rewards you for cycling through the different possible items you can sell.  6 hours into the game and I can easily say it’s going to take me over double that to even get through the basic mining aspects of the game.  Let’s also factor in that this recommendation doesn’t even take into account that this game has multiplayer.  That’s right, bring your friends along because you’re fully capable of working together and sharing the rewards!

So what are you waiting for?  If you’re on the fence about buying Hydroneer then I’d say it’s the perfect time to take the plunge and, like me, see what you’ve been missing.

現在DLCを遊んでいる最中ですが、一言でいうとめちゃくちゃ面白い
根気と忍耐力を求められる単純な作業ゲーではありますが、はまる人にはとことんはまるゲームです
自分で考えて形にして完成したものをニヤニヤ眺めつつ無限拡張していく数字が大好きな工業風建築家におすすめです
行動に意味や理由を求めるタイプの人だと途中どころか序盤で嫌になってしまうかもしれないですね

【良い点】
・オブジェクトの設置数に単純な上限がないこと
　多くのゲームは採掘用の機械や配管などに設置できる上限数が存在しますが、このゲームは作れさえすれば好きなだけ使えます
・作業量が比較的多い
　飽きない限りやることがなくなることはありません
・いい感じに適当
　何事にも100%を求められることがなく、割と適当にやってもうまく完成させられます
・ビジュアルがいい
　結構ビジュアルに凝っていてアイテムの一つ一つがかわいいです

【悪い点】
・無駄に操作に癖が強い
　「なんでそういう設定なんだ！！」ってブチ切れることがままあります、うまく動かせると爽快感ですが操作に失敗するとストレスになりやすいです

I am having way too much fun with this game. 

Although i can 100% see why the pacing of this game would be a major downside to a lot of people (you aren't wrong for thinking that), I absolutely love it. The fact that you have no traditional inventory and everything is a physical object adds so much to the processes the game has; it simply wouldn't be the same if you weren't the one physically moving resources around and working with them. It can be a bit unruly at times (seriously, dropping a shovel in a cave shouldn't be that awkward), but it really isn't a deal breaker. I don't think I've ever used the term "Charmingly Janky" before, but i'll use it here.

It's dumb that this little indie darling has gripped me way more than any AAA game I've played recently. It just goes to show that a solid gameplay loop is the biggest thing when it comes to making a good game. If you don't mind the steady pace and give yourself the time to get used to the way the game plays, you'll have a good time here.

Oh, and don't miss the shovel lying next to the dig site sign. Took me an embarrassingly long time to track that down...
