When I first picked up  and played this game, it seemed like the inventory system and doing the most trivial things like picking up and placing items was as much of the challenge as growing your base.  I initially gave it an not recommended because of this.

I'm editing this review because I figured out what was wrong. During the tutorial they talk about a circle that its supposed to be used for aiming at the ground.  The problem there is a reticle that is also a circle.  Trying to use this to aim at where you will be dropping your items will not work and that was the cause of my frustration.  

The aiming "Dot" that is mentioned in the tutorial  is almost invisible because it is initially a very dark color and matches the color of the ground.  This why I didn't see it.

My advice is when you start this game, go into settings and change the color of the aiming dot to something brighter.  After I made that change, it made the game much more enjoyable.

Something else I didn't realize is that I own that little piece of land I start on. So now I can feel more leisurely about how I travel about in search of supplies. I was travelling like a nomad before, putting everything in my cart and pulling it around...now I understand that we own that truck in the village and that made such a difference.

Anyways, now that all that's out of the way, I find this game to be charming.  The way you have  to actually build stuff block, by block reminds me of playing with building-blocks as a kid.  Its the sim I play when I just want to relax for a little bit and pan for gold.  I haven't made too much progress yet as I'm still farming and gardening, but at least I now have a roof over my head after assembling a house.

This game is different. You will be weighing things and you will do things a bit more manually than most other sims of this type. I really do appreciate the more hands-on approach.

Early game is enjoyable and relaxing, process of discovering the game was honestly fun. Very glad they give you a truck right out of the gate, getting around is a bit annoying with the large map and things spread out but wasn't too bad once automation got running.

Mid-Late game is a bit of a slog however, lag spikes will cause resource chunks to freeze occasionally and would sometimes cause a pileup on the machines. The only clear indicator that this has happened is your game will start to chug and slow down, causing even more pileups. Had my game nearly crash twice until I figured it out, if you have multiple automation setups the lag from one of them will cause the other to back up as well. Got in the habit of hitting the "clear all resources" from the pause menu every time I noticed my game freezing up. 
Once I had gotten in the habit of just clearing resources every hour or so and moving all my mining automation to one plot it got a lot easier to manage.

Crops kinda suck, having to replant after every harvest and the only way to get into crop automation being the guild tokens from quests means it's a new slog to build up farming capacity; with a lot of aimless wandering around going "where the heck is that quest person." The quests tell you what town the giver is located but with nearly a dozen NPCs in bridgepour it can be annoying trying to find them.

Frankly I don't really see the point behind tier 3 automation. After only 60 hours I'm well over 14mil hydro coins and thats only because I stopped bothering to craft things out of gems/metals, and it doesn't really look like there's much else to buy. You need guild coins to buy T3 pipes and such but unless it starts kicking out guild coins there's really no point, You get more than enough money from the T2 setup to Build a mansion on every landplot in the game if you really wanted to and by the time you finished building the automated setup would have made you back the money you spent.

I'm starting to work on the Kings Quests but the huge amount of crop requirement is the only thing holding me up, so I'm at a situation where I'm just letting the mining operation run in the background while I meticulously try to split cut vegetables to get the absurd decimal point accuracy the denizens require.

The required accuracy of crafted goods is frankly obnoxious with the given system and honestly has killed a lot of the momentum of playing the game, if somebody says they want 45.2 cut tomato, 45.199 isn't enough , and 45.26 is too much. I've frankly gotten more glee out of throwing the contracts into the recycler and bunting the offending NPC into the ocean. 

Overall I do really recommend the game, but honesty only for the first 40 hours or so, I haven't bought the DLC but I'm a firm believer that I shouldn't have to spend extra money for a patch to make the base game complete. I'm probably just going to build a sizeable house on one of the plots I'm not using and call it quits.

Hydroneer is an interesting though finnicky game that lacks a solid direction. After playing 80 hours, I am a bit disappointed in the game as a whole but I enjoyed it overall anyway so it gets a thumbs up anyway. The game has a neat gameplay loop that I would describe as Factorio/Satisfactory lite. Dig for resources by hand, get some automation going, build up and optimize and rebuild and create your own little factory process.

However, Hydroneer's biggest problem is that it has no overarching goal to work toward. You set up automation to create vast amounts of resources but you don’t really need all that much to earn more money than you could ever spend. There is something you could kinda consider the 'main quest' to finish all unique fetch requests but that didn’t create a very satisfying ending and the reward was disappointing.

Actually, I take that back; its biggest problem is the poor optimization of its vast number of entities. It doesn't take much for the number of objects in the world to chew up framerate. The game has minimal UI so almost everything in the world is represented by an individual entity in the world. This causes plenty of problems when you want to buy 300 pipes, 200 conveyer belts, 200 foundation blocks and 100 logic wires and transport them all to your dig site. Or funnel the output a half dozen mining machines into a transport pan for sale a half hour later.

Oddly, there is a solution for this already present in the game; cut produce stacks into a single entity that you can then separate at will and items you buy come from a single object you can just pull an infinite amount out of. Stacking objects automatically into 'piles' the player can take from and allowing the player to pull large quantities of items into a single 'distribution' pile for purchase would save all the frames and reduce a lot of the irritation while not at all breaking any established immersion.

Vehicles have warthog levels of jank but are missing a lot of the 'fun' that comes with driving wild. Guild tokens are not very fun to acquire, imbalanced in their value and annoying to manage. And fishing is really boring while being borderline required to do for hundreds of casts.

There is a much longer list of things that are irritating or wrong, with more than one CTD too. But I still found the game interesting to play and optimize so it still gets a stamp of approval. If it’s a game that looks interesting to you too, it probably will be worth a purchase.

It is incredibly slow and clunky to get started in this game. 

Automation doesn't come into play until many hours into the game (even tier 1)

There doesn't seem to be anything to do in the first few hours but repeatedly shovel dirt into a pan, scrub it, and sell the ore (to a shop that is miles away). Eventually, after nearly a full hour, you can cobble together enough coins to get the 3 separate items required to turn ore into ingots, but even then, you are still just shovelling dirt into a pan, scrubbing it, melting it, pouring it out, then selling it to the shop that is miles away. 

automation doesn't come until you can scrounge together ~1000 coins, to buy the first machines, but given that it takes about half an hour to make 100 coins, you can tell it's going to be a LOOOOONG time before this supposed automation game actually lets you automate anything.

I love automation and logistics games, but this isn't one.

色々な動画を見ていて「とにかくめんどくさいけど面白そう」と思ってたところにセールが来たので購入。

初期の手掘り期間はあっという間に消化して自動化に入れるので、操作習熟期間とでも思えば OK。
インベントリが無いのは、面倒ではあるが意外と慣れる。
移動は面倒だが、慣れる。

人間って慣れの動物だなと思った。

坑道を手で掘っていくのとか、コンベアベルトを作っていくのとか、
とにかく何をするのも面倒なゲームなんだけど確実に前進しているのが感じられて止め時が見つからなくなる危険がある。
やってて本能的に楽しい感じ。

大きな問題点としては 2つ

1つ目は鉱石がコンベアライン上でスタックすることがある点
細かな誤差とかでライン外に落ちたり、ライン上で止まったりすることがあり、
運が悪いと詰まる。
詰まりが発生すると（下の問題で）割と最悪な状態になったりする。
一応、「できるだけ発生しないように」組むことは可能だけど 100% ではない。
メニューから未加工資源の全削除ができるのでなんとかならなくはない。

2つ目が（多くの人が指摘するように）致命的で、
ある程度大規模な自動採掘になると、鉱石同士の衝突判定とかの関係だろうけど、急に動作が重くなる。
コンベアから遠くに移動しても重いので、描画ではなく計算が重いのだと思う。
（その割に、CPU や GPU には余裕がある）
その為、「ゲーム内の時間の進みは一定だけど表示上コマ落ちが発生する（カクカクする）」のではなく、
「無限に重くなって最終的には動くこともできなくなる」ので注意。

うちだと、Tier 3 のドリル 14台を Tier 3 のパイプライン（結構長い）で流したら急激に重くなったので、
過去に使っていた Tier 1 と Tier 2 のドリル（計 16台）を止めた。
坑道の照明も消した。
少し重くなったまま。

鉱石がスタックしたりすると多分指数関数的に判定が増えて最悪なことになる。

ラインの長さと構成、PC の性能次第だと思うのでどこまでできるかは一概に言えないけど、
こういうゲームって「ドリル100台並べてやるぜー」とかをやりたいもんなのに、それは叶わぬ夢。

基本的には楽しいだけに、鉱石の衝突判定はちょっと見直してほしいと切に願う。

Hydroneer is close to being a great game, but I found a couple of design decisions that are frustrating for the player, and needless. The game has a fun game-loop and satisfying progression for an automation / sim game. The processing of ores is hands on and visceral and feels rewarding when you get to your next improvement. 

The game involves a LOT of 'dropping', but precision based dropping. Now that's not a bad thing, and lends to the visceral nature of the experience. The issue is the drop marker, is not the center cursor, but another cursor, situated in the bottom-right quadrant of your screen. You can change the colour of this marker and increase it's visibility, so that's not a problem. The issue is how poor this is ergonomically, as you spend most of your time with your eyes locked to the bottom corner of your screen as you are dropping or tipping items constantly. This is a pain and a poor experience. Changing the drop to be on the center cursor, if not completely physics accurate, would greatly improve the experience of this game. 

The second issue, also revolves around an extension of the precision dropping. Everything interactable is a physics object it seems, and you have one hand. The PC has no toolbelt or storage of any kind, so you just throw tools on the ground, but far enough away from your other tools so it will let you drop them. It extends to the money you get from selling items, you have to lug this around, back and forth, dropping it in buckets to use in shops, but if you have left over cash, you can't take your money and your new toy home, you have to do two trips or load them both into a vehicle. This gets worse when you buy a series of items in a single shop. Now you have to hand pick each item to buy and put it in the 'buy zone' then pick each item up individually and load the vehicle, then unload each item individually. It's just not very fun to do that and it's not what is exciting about this game. 

My final issue with the drop mechanics is when you drop containers such as crucibles, casting molds, pans or buckets, they will often bounce off flat ground and fall over, it's annoying to pick these back up when this happens and there's no reason it should (implement a soft fall for items you want to land flat). 

It's a shame, this game is fun and satisfying, but it's such a poor experience to play due to a couple of design choices. If they even just made dropping work directly on the cursor or implemented that as an option I would buy again in a heartbeat and enjoy this game. Someone give me a ping when they do

I have played Hydroneer for about 100 hours, and what makes me super frustrated is when I decided to scale up my operation, using the items and tools available to me, my game now crashes every time my gems go through sorting.

Everything in my operation is automated, and now when my gems feed off my belts in to sorters, then to compactors, the game will crash and post an error report. I have sent probably 100+ reports over the course of 3-4 months, some including specific details of what is happening, to no avail.

I notice the new DLC was launched, yet my problems still remain. No word back from the dev or team when the issue will be fixed. The only solution suggested right now is to DELETE all the loose materials, including every single gem I have that is not already in a compactor and restart my mining operation. I have done this before and the issue returns regardless. As fun as it sounds to beat my head against a wall on a game that has ENTIRELY physical objects/inventory to work around a well documented issue, I am going to pass on that.

I don't want to play creative, because I enjoy the achievements and strive to complete them. This crashing issue has completely ruined my experience, and destroyed my potentially great review for the game due to this being literally game-breaking. This is a very well documented issue, with many players reflecting the same problem. Yet, we aren't being heard, and that is more disheartening than the issue itself.

I give up Hydroneer. I tried, I really did. A single dev, or team of 2-3 can really struggle to manage bug issues and implement potential fixes in a timely manner. However, when you release a DLC pack without first addressing big known issues your players are experiencing, it is clear your priorities and focus as a person or small team is not in alignment with the needs of many of your community members. 

I cannot support that kind of practice and I will not purchase the new DLC until this issue is fixed. I sincerely hope my review will help light a fire of priority for the developer. [b]Be wary, if you are making a large scale operation, avoid cutting and sorting gems as the likelihood of your game crashing and eventually becoming unplayable is very high.[/b]

The "Clear all loose items" option is not a solution, it's a band-aid fix to a much bigger problem. For a 10gb game to crash on a gaming PC that can run 130gb+ AAA titles on ULTRA settings, this is unacceptable. Please for the love of God stop working on DLC and Hydroneer 2 and FIX THE PROBLEM WE HAVE CURRENTLY. Thank you.

一見自動化して大規模なラインを作るようなゲームに見えますが、どちらかというと作業ゲーに近く「不便を楽しむ」マインドがないと楽しめないと思います。

そのため前者のようなイメージで購入すると、序盤こそ技術の進歩に達成感を感じますが、中盤以降は呆れるほどゲームが不便すぎてプレイ意欲をそがれます。

具体例をいくつか挙げると、
・インベントリがないので持ち運ぶことができるのは一つのアイテムのみ。
・上記はリヤカーで解決するが、載せるのは結局一つ一つ手作業。
・自動化ラインを作るために大量のアイテムが必要なのに、まとめて購入は不可（商品を手に持つ⇒リヤカーに乗せる、を購入分だけ繰り返す必要がある）。
・普通ならUIに組み込まれる金銭やワールドマップすら「1アイテム」として持ち運びが必要。しかも通貨の種類が複数ある。
・採掘設備のアップグレードをしたい場合でも、ワンタッチでアップグレード！ではなく、古い設備を外す⇒新しい設備を全部設置しなおす必要がある。上記の通り一つ一つ手作業で。
・アイテムの設置はグリッド通りに配置できるのに、採掘はグリッド通り行ってくれない（熊手を使って手作業で整地することは一応可能）。綺麗に整地してラインを作ることができない。

といった具合です。

更に「王宮クエスト」というゲーム内の大目標になるクエストで必要になる農業要素は致命的で、「農業で楽をするための設備が整う頃には農業が必要なくなる」、という本末転倒具合になってます。

「MODでなんとかするか」と思っても、MODを導入すると実績が解除されないというペナルティがつくため、やりこみたいプレイヤーほど不便を強いられます。

最近追加されたDLCのレビューを見ても「本編をより苦行にした」というものが散見される当たり、不便さに関しての根本的な改善は見込めないでしょう（自分はDLC未プレイなのであくまで所感になります）。

ここまで書いておいてなんですが、他の自動化ゲームよりも牧歌的であり、不思議な魅力があるゲームであることは確かです。
前述の通り序盤にコンベアを導入したりして鉱石採掘の自動化ができたときは感動しました。
しかしそれ以降はほとんどがただの面倒くさい要素だった、という形です。

総括すると「序盤こそ自動化で発展させていくことや斬新なシステムの魅力にワクワクするが、中盤以降は不便さによる苦行が押し寄せてくるため、やりこみには向かないゲーム」といえると思います。

The developer has seen fit to publish a DLC and yet the core game still has extremely serious problems with the physics engine. Every game I've ever played of Hydroneer has ended when a system I created started behaving erratically, causing buildups of resources in unpredictable places that drag down the FPS and eventually crash the game. To be clear, it is not possible to build a stable system above a certain (small) scale in the game, every system with more than a dozen or so miners (any tier) will eventually fail as it enters and leaves render range repeatedly while the player plays the game. This is very, very much a known issue and has been for the game's literal entire existence, and is a problem for me specifically as I do not find the game to be very much fun prior to large-scale automation, meaning that the game is kind of a chore until just before it no longer functions at all.

Previously I gave no recommendation either way on the game, as I was confident the developer was working to fix it and eventually would succeed. Now not only has the developer released a DLC, but they've released a DLC with a map supposedly much larger than that of the main game, which will serve to exacerbate the issues we already have. This is not the behavior of a dev that intends to fix a problem. I no longer believe they're even trying. I cannot recommend anyone else play the game at all.

review:
Don't be fooled by the fact that this game is a Factorio-like. Hydroneer gives you the freedom to earn money in a variety of ways, gradually easing into the mining aspect if you're a slow learner like me.

The initial gameplay may seem tedious: Use a shovel to dig dirt, put that dirt in a bucket four times, empty that bucket into a pan, fill that pan with water, then use a scrub brush to wash the dirt away and reveal ores and precious gems.

The little bit of coin you get from this effort will allow you to purchase machines, water piping, and conveyor belts that can be used to automate the mining process. I'm not good at those types of layouts, though, so my first purchase was a fishing rod.

I earned a small fortune fishing, which gave me the financial security to start experimenting with the mining machines. At 22 hours, my mining operation is still modest but effective enough to get things done. But if I didn't care to mine at all, it would still be okay because fishing is a viable way to earn some coin.

If fishing and mining aren't your thing, then there's also farming. Plenty of people seem to want soup made of fresh vegetables, so you can turn any plot of land you purchase into a farming paradise. There is a large variety of crops available, though for the majority of them you'll have to earn farmer's guild tokens.

That's something to be aware of with this game. There's multiple currencies and while coin is gotten from selling anything, the other tokens are only acquired through completing villager quests. They can range from really simple to ridiculously complex, though the payout is greater when the quest requires more. Upgrades to your operations are obtained with tokens so you will eventually have to give mining a try. It's much better when you're too rich to care about expenses, though.

I have some personal frustrations with the game. Quests are on scrolls which are physical objects in the game world. You can post them to a bulletin board you can purchase with guild tokens, but the board only holds two at a time, and the scrolls are easy to misplace. Also, quest givers aren't static. They like to wander the admittedly small landscape, which can force you to hunt them down for a long time when trying to turn in a quest.

Honestly, the whole questing system could use some work though for now I've been able to successfully complete several orders. I also find the camera can be very frustrating once you're digging underground, especially with the massive mining machines. But other than that, I find the game to be extremely relaxing. It's something that's easily played while listening to a Podcast or video.

developer_response:
On very rare occasions Hydroneers save files can be corrupted. This generally happens when someone closes the game while it is saving. We’ve added in measures to prevent this from corrupting but there are some outlying cases. 
We have also noticed that some anti-virus programs prevent Hydroneer from saving. Please list Hydroneer as an accepted program or consider disabling your anti-virus programs. (Windows Defender is fine, but other AV programs can have this issue)
We also have added in ‘backup’ saves to prevent total data loss. Try finding this backup, by opening up the game, pressing ‘continue’ on the main menu, then ticking the ‘Show Backup’ box. This will show a backup save file which hopefully won’t be corrupted.

If you’d like any more help with this or another issue, you can reach out to us by email: support@foulballhangover.com. If this has resolved your issue please consider updating your review. We’re a small team and reviews really help us out, thanks!

I want to love this game, but I only like it.

This isn't a negative review, I just find something left to be desired in the mid-late game and hope the developers take this as constructive criticism!

Definitely scratches an itch and I love the unique quirky mechanics of the game, where I get lost is when I get to the point of, "I have 500,000 hydrocoins, why am I still doing this?"

I'd love to see more "difficulty points" to drive the motives in career mode:
-  Equipment maintenance or detrimental effects for being exposed to weather, I think this would give a sense of purpose to building.
-  Incremental upgrade points within each tier of equipment, things like "adamantanium drill heads" to upgrade a drill and improve its efficiency etc. I think this would add some longevity to the game by making the production speeds of the current equipment lower and working towards upgraded components.
- harvester processing, I've yet to build anything "game breaking" but I feel like a harvester easily managing my current busiest mine of 21 drills to be underwhelming... give me a reason to upgrade my processing capacity! 
- Make Lava hurt, I want to feel like I'm taming a dangerous creature in the name of production.

Quality of life:
- the road block I hit with every mine I've made is when I want to refine my factory and build something nice looking around it. I love the pick and pull aspect of the stores, but there's point where I'm loading 50 or more stone walls into the back of my truck each trip where I just decide it's not worth it... bulk order? prepackaged pallets? delivery for a premium price?

Mining sites:
The only mining site that has really inspired me is Ember Cradle, the Aquifer sounds like a unique challenge that I haven't dabbled with yet, but I think the unique terrain with the river running through the plot brings some design challenges that the other locations just don't offer.

If you've made it this far, here's my only genuine complaint.

Journey to Volcalidus requires a blue light filter to play, every where I look I'm blinded by ice, which is some realism I could live without.

Unfortunately, while this was the kind of game that looks like it is really made for me, I can't recommend it in the end.

I really like games where you dig, harvest resources, and creative automated processes; or games where you take things apart, or clean stuff up, etc. I like to put on music, or a podcast, and then just have at it. Unfortunately, I just found this game to be too boring and grindy, even with other things occupying my main attention. It is a personal gripe to have, I know, but that is why I can't give it a thumbs up.

Perhaps I should go into these reasons as to why I dislike the game a little further. I found it pretty annoying to sort and keep track of all your items and resources. I think something better should have been implemented. The different types of currencies, while good at helping to promote the use of other tools for other jobs, made the game progress super slow. You really want to get into farming? Well, it is going to take you a massive grind, like the very start of the game for mining, to get anywhere you want to be. Farm carrots by hand for a couple hours to get enough 'farming currency' the unlock better and faster ways of doing it. Regular currency just won't cut it here! Sometimes it felt to me like it was done just to add on and pad how many hours you would get out of the game; and not in a fun way.

You don't want your machines to break down and stop all your automated processes, understandable. Add on water filters to your pipes, each filter gives you 20% filtration. If you have five, that is 100% filtration and your machines won't take damage. Great! That means I don't need to worry about constantly going and buying repair kits to fix my machines... wait, the water filters take damage and need to be repaired? They literally break down and stop all of your machines from functioning? Well, that was a waste of my time and resources.

There is no centralised place to record your quests, you are just given a piece of paper with what you need to do and who to do it for. This becomes a problem in many ways. The first is that these people can move and walk around a very large area. The second is losing these papers (which again goes back up into my point about keeping track of items). If there was some kind of bookshelf, or a journal you could access from the menu to keep track of things, that would be great. The other problem is that there is no built in map in this game. There is a piece of paper you can pick up and hold, but it does not show where you, or the quest givers, are.

Then there are the achievements locked behind a DLC that probably should not have been a DLC. I dunno, in the end I just felt like the game was too disorganised, too boring, too grindy, and too annoying, in just too many different aspects for me. I wouldn't recommend this game, but if you do think the game looks interesting and you want to try it, get it on sale. Buyer be warned: it takes too long to get far enough into the game to know whether you don't like it or not, for you to be able to apply for a refund.

While fun to build stuff, the game is frustratingly designed with multiple non-exchangeable currencies to gate progress with grinding delivery tasks.

In the early game you can sell things to a shop for the first currency but after that progressing requires driving around the map to find people to make items for because they're the only source of the other currencies.

All of these other-currency trades are randomised and low value so you will have to do hundreds of them, each requiring driving to a person, finding what they want, driving back to your base, make it, drive back to the person to give them it then repeat. You spend far more of your time driving about between different coloured exclamation marks on a map you have to get out of your vehicle to view than doing anything else.

I like the building but parts of the game seem to not have been thought through. An example being the second tier of drill on the Volcalidus DLC (the Heavy Drill) is required to mine Corestone, but needs Corestone to build it. After several hours of trying things, reading the wiki and asking the Discord it seems the only way is to manually hand-mine  a low-random-chance-to-mine resource for tens of hours to progress from one automated mining tier to the next. Bizarre design choice with no documentation or guidance available anywhere to help (the official wiki hasn't been updated to cover the DLC released a month ago).

If you get stuck and want help then don't go to the Discord, i was told "it's better to try things and learn yourself" in response to simple questions like "What is required to make a Heavy Drill in the Volcalidus DLC?", nobody else would answer. Closest they would offer was a link to a rambling "FAQ megathread".

Would only recommend if you really like the building part and are willing to either put up with the rest of it or skip it by playing creative like all the content creators for this game do.

review:
My first comment was written after an hour of most frustrating controls and somewhat interestering gameplay. So i think it is fair to write some more after cooling down a bit.


The premise is quite promising. Various levels of automatisation, tools, logics etc.. nice gfx and finally no "survival" thrown into the mix.

Unfortunately I cant really see how this could work considering that the controls are... unique. Sure WASD, mouse and some keypresses more. Sounds perfectly normal especially with a crosshair... but there is a catch.. there is second crosshair.. a very unintuitive mix the use of left mouse button and E, building reminds me a damn lot on my years in cristallogrphy and HKL system of rotating and nudging stuff rather than more sane systems which might be used in every game but.. for a reason. 
Last but not least.. the crosshair situation.. 
It is unique to have a game that is, at the same time, a squint simulator. You have centerscreen crosshair and a topright offset one, almost invisible but quite important for interacting. maybe its my 30 years of gaming experience but if i see a crosshair i know where to aim, use, throw, do, walk, read etc.. i dont expect anything else.

This said.. i would have loved giving the game a second, a third or even a hundreds chance. Like i said, the premise was good... but it really was frustrating enough to file for a refund after only an hour of "gameplay". That never happened before and tells me: No, Not this time. 
During development someone must have had the idea to make the controls be exactly that. Other people must have said "thats a nice idea" or at least havent voiced any concearn. And while i like quite unique games i want to enjoy them. This is, literally by design, not possible in this case. 

I more friendly note to the devs:
Back in the days when there was the big "starship controls" war between Elite-players and WingCommander-players there were games that offered an option to switch between controls to either reflect the first or the latter. Noone was forced into unique and strange controls... and back when the second generation of FPS came out there was a way to swizch between arrow keys and wasd... something so familiar we still have this option in games to this day (rebind controls...).
Maybe, just maybe, you could open up yourself for the idea to add a switch for people to have either the squint mode or classic controls... 



- Previous comment -
This game might actually be fun... But the controls are just BS. If you like games that randomize the point you interact with, that feel as sluggish as pigeon snot in winter and simply wont do anything the way you intend to.. then yes. This is your game.

Note do the dev: If you have a crosshair like indicator for the player: Dont ♥♥♥♥ things up by having a SECOND almost invisible indicator for the point of interaction.

Transparency: I have just asked for a refund. Normally I'd give a game 20 chances if needed. Not this time. This intentional controls BS ruined it.

A very fun sandbox with a couple things holding it back for me.

Hydroneer is fun and creative, if you love mining resources/ farming / base building. Then this really is a good a game. It’s very satisfying when a plan comes together. There’s many ways to build upon your plots. 

But there a few issues I do have with the game. It seems like there aren’t very many elements to make your experience easier. It took me almost 3+ hours to dig out a hole for T2 drills. Which is fine. But if you don’t have a bunch of spare time. Then this game probably isn’t for you.

Also, you have to do everything one by one. If you’re planning a big build. You have to drag and drop every single resource one by one from a store. I wish there was a mass purchase option, just to smooth things out. Although there are some ways the tedium of doing so can be slightly mitigated (wagons).

All in all Hydroneer is a very satisfying and rewarding sandbox. The main issue I have with it is the amount of time the game requires for you to actually get to where your next goal is.

Not amused by this game and the new DLC.
After fiddling around with Tier 1 drills and getting an automated system up and running, I noticed a couple things that halted my progress.

1. THE GRIND. You don't get anywhere in this game after several hours of digging, mining, smelting, hauling, repeat. I'm several hours into my game because of this. I already know refunding the DLC and game won't work.

2. Useful tools and items locked away behind the higher progression tiers. I would have loved to discover the rake and expanded tool rack much sooner than I did. There's no way to 'recycle' items as soon as their bought in the DLC, possibly down into scrap like you could in the base game unless you opt for the nuclear option and sell the scrap left over.

3. I stopped getting any Corestone. I need a good amount of this ore to construct future machines. In order for my machine to even work properly, I creative-spawned in a 1-Weight ore to use as a sorter. Prior to automating it, I was getting Corestone by pan-mining on the surface.

4. Tier 2 drills did not perform as well as I was expecting. Probably because it was rather misleading that a Tier 1 drill model appeared when I built the Tier 2 shop.

5. A secondary currency in the DLC, Scout Guild Tokens (T), is REQUIRED to progress. After fully automating a system and generating more of the regular Guild Tokens (C) than you'd ever need, you need (T) to progress any further. The only way you get (T) is by running around the map to collect bones or do random side-quests for the NPCs that want 1.5 lb ores or 40 lb ingots. Once the system is automated, this becomes a major chore. Sure, you could give them ingots with weights higher than they asked for. I personally decided on giving everyone 50 lb ingots when they wanted 40, 45, etc. You're not paid anything additional if you do exceed their request, but handing a 5,000 lb ingot to a NPC that wanted a 50 lb seems incredibly wasteful.

6. Researching the Heavy Drill revealed to me the immensely painful quest you endure to get the better drill. I couldn't buy the blueprint without (T), nor could I even build it without Corestone. Should I manage to have build the damn drill, you need a large crane (4200T). In order to even get the crane, you buy a boat ticket (200C) to a tiny island where all the vehicles are. In order to even buy the boat ticket, you build the ticket office. This is just compounded every issue I started to have with the game, but there's more. Apparently the crane itself is a nightmare of complications as big of a lumbering and uncoordinated oaf that it is.

First and foremost: Thank you Max for granting me a key to this game (and the Volcalidus DLC) even though i am currently no longer streaming.

I promised the devs i'd leave a review when i was done with the game and i try to keep my promised, so without further ado...

I've noticed that this game is not entirely my cup of tea, i love making nicely optimized builds, but i don't feel the need to go "overkill"
I've seen plenty of builds that produce an insane amount of resources per second, but i don't see the use in doing this.
Nontheless, the game is a lot of fun to mess around with but it has a bunch of quirks that can get a bit annoying to some.

The normal gameplay is not for the lazy people, you want to make a build that does stuff for you? Get ready to do the work.
The better pipes (Tier 3) are only obtainable with Tokens, which are obtained by doing item requisitions, this can keep you busy for a while but if you want the best, you will need to work for it.

The first Tier 1 Drill and Harvester can be bought for hydrocoins (the game's "main" currency) but beyond that: you need the resources to make them yourself.

So as you can see, if you wanna build something big it will require a healthy amount of work on your own part (and this in my honest opinion is not a bad thing, it keeps you busy).

This however can make certain things a bit tedious to do and if you don't plan ahead and make a mistake those mistakes can be a bit costly, because you cannot sell the items back to recoup the costs of your mistakes.

That said, i've had plenty of fun with making an automated resources system which ended up working without any issues for hours on end, but i've heard people with bigger builds tend to run into issues where resources glitch out or start accumilating where they are not supposed to and it makes their games slow or unplayable.

I also ended up making an entire system to sort and store vegetables for me, which works almost flawless after a few revisions, the only thing i have to do is harvest the crops with the hydrocropper and hope that that vehicle doesn't glitch out and spray vegetables all over the place (which seems to happen every so often for some reason).

The only thing i REALLY miss about the game is the lack of a (small) story, i know these games are usually not made this way, but a guy can hope right?
What i mainly did was let the achievements guide my course of actions, i just looked at a few of them and started to work towards those goals, but a small story or list of objectives to guide players would not go amiss.

With this all said i now want to adress the only real issue i had with the game so far: Creative mode.
For me Creative mode should be super easy to use so you can quickly test things, but sadly Creative mode in Hydroneer is anything but fast...
Flying is done using a hat, Item duplication is also done with a hat and you cannot wear both at the same time, which makes things a bit more tedious then it needs to be.
Items and Resources cannot be spawned in without obtaining them yourself somehow, which means you make a setup to obtain them before you can mess around with them, which means more work.

As per usual i have a few suggestions for the devs pertaining this "problem" wether or not they wanna apply these or do anything with these is entirely up to them.
(it won't make me dislike the game if it never gets implemented, but it would make Creative a LOT easier to use.

My suggestions for this are as follows:
- Add an option to toggle Flight/Repeated Item Placement instead of having the player equip a helmet/hat for each of these things.
- A Shop/Item menu to select stuff from instead of having to walk/run/fly to each respectable shop for the items you're looking for would be a GODSEND.
I tend to use creative mode for quickly testing things, but in hydroneer there's no "quickly" testing things because i have to manually grab all the items 1 by 1 from a store.

All in all, the game is a lot of fun and i'm currently going through the DLC so i can give this a nice review as well.

~ General M-13

I think overall the game is quite good, especially at this price. It's a very hands on game much like Gold Rush where from beginning to end you will be doing a lot of work by yourself throughout most of the progression. However you can automate all of the process until going to the traders to make your money.
It can require some small baby sitting sometimes to avoid odd issues mostly caused by the physics system in some way. I have not had much issues at all in this late stage of development.

I won't go into the details of how the game is played you can understand that quite quickly browsing the guides and videos on here. I will focus more on the few things that do bother me.

First is inventory. The game is designed to be highly interactive and less gamey, therefore you can only carry one tool or object at one time, dropping it off and picking it up off the floor or shelf every time. Same for resources. I like that as it encourages being tidy and organized it's part of these things that make the game more immersive. There are some things that i feel could change though.
Absence of tool belt is intentional design but i think the player could use a single slot for big tools and maybe one for smaller tools. Allowing to carry the builders hammer, or the pickaxe while carrying some kind of building block or driving or pulling the cart. The small tool slot could carry something like the magnifying glass while carrying spanners to do a maintenance run. This is about streamlining some of the processes in a way that doesn't break the design of the game.
This ties in to an addition that could expand some of the games mechanics being a character "upgrade" shop. A sling for carrying a big tool on your back, the tool belt for holding a small tool. 
Some kind of resource pouch to carry multiple nuggets could be useful too. It could work like a regular bucket you fill and empty by hand but can be hidden and pulled out with a key. Ideal for cleaning up a spill or measuring precise weight before dumping it into a crucible. Not for carrying large quantities it would probably be limited to 100u or a number of nuggets. Other upgrades are possible of course like boots for running or jumping and whatever.

One part of the game that bothers me most actually is the building process and really the shopping process.
Each item you need for building is individually picked up from the shelf, purchased and then loaded in the truck or cart or whatever you're doing. This includes carrying your money. Building larger infrastructure in the mid/late game becomes too much busywork in my opinion because of this process. Building itself is rather simple.
There's a number of things i think could be done to improve this and make it less overwhelming so the player can focus on the fun part of the game.

Firstly, i think rich players should be able to pay premiums for delivery without resorting to modded shops. 
Maybe the player could buy a contract from a shopkeeper with a daily cost allowing him to take a catalog home, or browse one at the shop. Making a purchase and getting it delivered at a dig site on a delivery pad you purchase as furniture. This could also be tied to a specific quest or a type of reputation with a trader, or based on tokens instead of cash. Rich players shouldn't have to make numerous round trips to shops when building big mines. This is mostly a problem with pipes, conveyors and foundations which you may need a lot of. 
Another issue that pops up with this process is pre-planning. If you have so many trips to do and the purchase process is tedious, not being able to pre-plan your builds in a convenient way is a problem. Some new tools could help with that.
A catalog. Purchased at each store with the name of the store and location as a reminder, purchasable at each individual shops. Allows the player to browse items and check where they are available, check prices and the purpose of each item. 
A shopping list that could work in conjunction or merged in the catalog, allowing the player to make a list of purchases with cost breakdown.

The other part of planning is designing. A tool for planning where things go would go a long way. Something like a hammer and stakes for measuring lengths for pipes and belts or area surfaces. A spray paint marker or a tool that drops flags, models or whatever to mark spots for other items like drills. This would work well with the shopping list, allowing players to know right away how much they need to order and not end up short requiring extra trips, or overflowing with items that can't be store conveniently or sold off.

Charming, strange, game. Build a machine that makes you rich, using water and/or lava (DLC) to power it.

No combat, no health bar, no falling damage (yay!). This is not a survival game. More like a puzzle game.

There's no "win" condition. By the time you've figured out how it all fits together you're earning enough money to buy anything in the game. Then it's just about "how much is enough?".

But addictive, if you like that sort of thing. Which I clearly do.

[b] TL;DR - This one was a great core idea, executed so badly it's actually impressive. [/b]

So a while back, i somehow managed to get all the achievements in this game, despite it being so poorly cobbled together that it would literally crash on me every 10 minutes (and that's being generous, it was frequently more often than that. One time i didn't even make it past the main menu. Not to mention it being far from the sole issue, it was only the most glaring one). And by some incredible miracle, i didn't decide to give it a negative review. They so nearly got away with it. And then they had the astounding gall to decide this absolute dumpster fire deserved a DLC.

For me, the point in playing the DLC where i realised i should have given this game a negative review in the first place was after handing in all the bones, and not getting the achievement for doing so, and then somehow managing to get the bike that can randomly crash into thin air and lose all momentum, around Mot's island in under 1:11, only for that achievement not to work either. You'd think from that phrasing that's what happened today before i posted this review, right? Nope, today's issue was catastrophic physics failure #3628. The iron and gold ores were getting stuck instead of going down the funnel they were meant to, meaning they formed an ever thickening ball of ore chunks, which exploded into thousands of shards the moment i touched it, each with their own physics trajectory. I spent the next 5 minutes basically watching a powerpoint presentation of my entire base being covered in iron ore, at a framerate of 1 frame every 40 seconds.

It's a shame, because the core concept of this game is really fun. Do basic mining, get money, use that money to buy fancier and fancier automation tools, which improves production, which gets more money. Fantastic feedback loop my lizard brain appreciates. But instead of focusing on that, they spread themselves too thin working on extraneous nonsense that only serves to get in the way, and everything feels painfully undercooked as a result. 

The game relies heavily on physics, but the physics are wonky and unreliable. It has 4 different currencies at this point, but they're each their own flavour of horrifically unbalanced. It has driving, but the vehicles all control terribly and get stuck on any given object because it's in the same zip code, or if it doesn't have an object to get stuck on, it'll get caught on the ground itself. It uses intentionally clunky systems to do anything, but even the stuff that isn't meant to be clunky, is clunky. 

And arguably most painful of all, it's a Factorio style automation game, and half the time the placement system will refuse to acknowledge the one obvious logical spot. Smelters will refuse to go in the big obvious hole you dug for them, but they're fine with the space right next to it, half-buried in the ground. Stairs will insist they belong anywhere except the one spot that would make them a direct continuation from the stairs directly above or below them. You want to place a drill? What do you mean you want it in the spot that would connect it to the end of the pipes you've already set up, where it would also be facing the conveyor? [i] What are you, stupid? [/i]

It's just an abysmal mess. The game didn't need farming mechanics, or fishing, or driving between towns that are annoyingly far apart, or an equally broken DLC. It needed time and work smoothing out the core mechanics to make an end product that's cleanly functional, and resultantly stays enjoyable. It's a classic case of ambition massively outmatching talent, only in this case, they failed so hard as a result they made something where your primary experiences will be either seething with resentment, or laughing like a maniac because the game did something so stupid, it wrapped all the way around and became funny.

Overall, bad game, stop making more extraneous content for it and [i] try to actually fix what's already there, please, for the love of god![/i]

Once you get used to the controls (voxel / environment based), and turn off the default "maximum motion sickness" settings you have quite a fun little digging/automation sandbox. The cash you obtain is used for QoL stuff in the game which is interesting, but 100% worth the asking price. Gripped me much for than satisfactory did. Hours upon hours of content if you like to create systems a la DSP, but on a much more intricate scale.
gud

If you like to mine for gold yourself, or if you like to automate the process like a true engineer, if you like to dig holes to dig bigger holes to find gold and gems and iron and ore, melt it down, make it into jewelry and weapons, if you like to make huge farms and cook soups, or if you like to go fishing in 2 inches of water to somehow catch a shark, then hydroneer is for you. It has all the right types of silly jank you want from a sandbox game that, while definitely interesting and sometimes relatively serious, reminds you of its silly nature. It's the perfect game for those who call themselves Dwarves or Molemen, or tunnelers. And the devs are extremely hands on, and one even makes things in the workshop, if they can't be added into the base game. And if you don't wanna work for everything in the game, or just wanna test stuff out, there's even a creative mode!
9/10, would absolutely recommend, occasional bugs aside (which is to be expected)

Would definitely recommend mods. Trying to dig in base game is such a hassle other wise, especially if you want a mining rig underground. Even the mining excavator you unlock later can be a massive hassle to use. but otherwise the game is good. I just wish it was possible to dig out more than one spoonful of dirt at the time. Otherwise, this game is worth your money, just be wary of trying to mine underground... In the mining centered game.

Edit: You don't get any achievements if you use the workshop, so be wary of that!

review:
If you like very sandboxy and relaxing games - this one might be for you.
The mechanics are easy enough to learn (even if the 'E' to take things and mouseclick to use felt a bit counter-intuitive in the beginning).
The island you play in is cute and leaves a lot of room to build stuff. What I like is the 'no menu' approach. Any buying, crafting, building is done ingame. Want to buy stuff? Throw it on the marked area in the shop and throw your coins in the basket nearby. Push the button to pay. Smith stuff? click the anvil to choose recipe, throw resources on anvil hit it with hammer - boom - item.

A thing you should know - no menus means no inventory. You can hold one item at a time. But you can throw infinite items on a cart or vehicle (items in store don't have colission, so you can stack multiples). But building takes considerable more time if you have to move every object by hand, and if it's even from a nearby cart. Activation range is good, though, so it's more about planning and keeping order.

There's missions, like people want certain objects you can craft in exchange for coins - but there's no storyline at the moment (at least I didn't find any). There's obviously hidden artifacts you can display in a temple near the starting area, though.

All in all - nice, relaxing with a pretty neat building system, slower than, say Minecraft or Valheim, no combat (as of now) - just chill, listen to the soundtrack and get to dig and build.

review:
C'est bien la premiere fois que je met un Non pour un jeu que j'aime bien.
Mais la question est "Est ce que je recommande ?"

Hydroneer est un jeu d'automatisation sans inventaire. On a 2 mains et on peut porter un seul objet.
Donc mecaniquement, si on doit construire une usine de 1000 piece, il faut ramasser puis poser et donc appuyer 2000 fois sur le meme bouton en faisant un aller/retour au magasin a chaques fois.

C'est la tout le genie et l'horreur d'hydroneer. C'est tellement chiant a jouer que lors que l'on arrive a avoir un peu d'automatisation, c'est royal de soulagement.
Toutes les mecaniques initiales du jeu sont la dans cet objectif unique. 

On ajoute sur ca que c'est un jeu d'usine "Physique", les tapis font rouler les ressources, tout est sous forme de petit blob qui trainent et que l'on deplace a la pelle. C'est tres interessant !

Le soucis maintenant c'est qu'une fois automatisé ya plus rien a faire et c'est triste.

Ne vous fiez pas au screenshots, le jeu est tres vide, ya rien a faire a part pelleter et les cartes ne contiennent rien. 

Donc j'adore le systeme d'automatisation et de gestion des ressources, mais avant ca, on passe des heures de pelletage,  d'aller retour au magasin et de lutte contre la physique du jeu avant d'avoir 10minute de bonheur en voyant que ca marche.

Donc oui, good game !

Mais recommandation ? F*ck no !

This game is really well put together. A slow start with a pan and a brush and slowly build your system step by step. First some pipes to get water easier. Then your first drill and harvester into a pan. Then conveyors and sorters. Then more drills.

I always start playing thinking I'll do an hour then take a break, but there is always a little bit more to do so the hour flies by and I'm better off than when I started and have just a little bit more I want to do. It's so easy to come back to I can't tell you how many times I've restarted from scratch and enjoyed it every time.

One of my top games I always come back to, up there with Satisfactory and Evospace.
i love factory building games and even more when its simple

This game feels like an introduction to factory style games. It's super cozy, relaxed and very easy to get the hang of.
In other factory games I feel compelled to improve and optimise my setups to get the best outcomes, whereas here I feel no such pressure and I keep building because I enjoy it!

You'll start out with some basic tools, a cart, a truck and a patch of dirt, very quickly expanding from panning for gold to having a fully automated setup that repairs itself when things break.
There's a bit for everyone, mining, farming, fishing, building.

The systems here are not as complex as other games in the genre and that's okay, it's more inviting and easier to learn.

At just over 20 hours I feel as though I've completed most of the base gameplay loop, and I'd be happy with that but was given a free key to try out the DLC. So I'll give that a go and see what new things the DLC brings!
I've thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and would absolutely recommend it to people who enjoy factory style games, want something a little different or a more relaxed experience.

Hydroneer offre une expérience de minage engageante, où la progression technologique et la gestion des ressources offrent un réel plaisir de jeu. Le concept de montée technologique dans le jeu de base est bien conçu, apportant une dimension stratégique intéressante. La nouvelle carte incluse dans le DLC est particulièrement adaptée à l'utilisation de véhicules, enrichissant ainsi l'interaction avec le terrain grâce à des mécaniques innovantes comme l'utilisation d'un treuil et la nécessité de dégeler des pierres pour optimiser l'efficacité des machines.

Cependant, certains aspects du jeu nécessitent une attention particulière pour une meilleure expérience. Le développement de la pêche et de l'agriculture reste en retrait par rapport aux autres éléments du jeu, ce qui pourrait bénéficier d'une plus grande automatisation et de raffinements pour rendre ces activités plus attrayantes et moins répétitives. Ce manque d'optimisation dans l'agriculture a malheureusement nui à mon expérience globale.

Concernant le contenu additionnel, bien que le DLC propose des innovations intéressantes, la montée technologique semble moins aboutie que dans le jeu de base, particulièrement avec les restrictions rencontrées en début de partie et la récupération des minerais. De plus, la possibilité de créer des alliages pourrait ajouter une profondeur supplémentaire et offrir plus de variété et de personnalisation dans la progression technologique.

En termes de véhicules, la foreuse et la foreuse lance-flammes étaient moins satisfaisantes en raison de leur manque de précision pour le terrassement. Le rouleau compresseur, bien que plus lent, permet une finition plus soignée et satisfaisante.

En conclusion, Hydroneer est un jeu solide avec des aspects très réussis, mais il bénéficierait grandement d'une attention aux détails dans les secteurs moins développés. Malgré ces points, le jeu reste une recommandation positive pour ceux intéressés par une simulation complexe de minage et de gestion de ressources.

review:
While I enjoy games in this genre in general. Hydroneer does not hit the spot for me.
There are some  good ideas and interesting choices here but it does not come together in the end. I'll list my main complaints in order of significance.

--Clunky inventory--
While the idea of not having an inventory seems interesting it quickly becomes tedious. Having to run pick up a map to see where you want to go is not fun. Furthermore every single run to the store to buy supplies  is pure agony. In order to buy something you need to:
1. Put your coins in a bucket in the shop
2. pick out the items in a designated "buy zone" for them to register
3. Click the buy button next to the coin bucket for the transaction to go through and load them onto your vehicle.

Now imagine buying 400 different pipes, some platforms and logistics components to start a new build...
In the end it's what kept me from doing any bigger builds. Just didn't have it in me to stand around town loading supplies in my car for 10-15 minutes. The early game loop of mining dirt, putting it in a pan and brushing it is also very very clunky. Hated every second of it.


--Pacing problems--
Very boring early game loop, no money what-so-ever and BOOM! Unlimited coins and no real point in scaling production since you got unlimited money already and there are no unique resources in any of the dig sites. Late game is just running around to NPCs handing in radiant quests for another currency. Grindy, Boring, Pointless as you already have all the coins you'll ever need  and don't need to expand production.

Dead world
While the  art style is nice and some very cool and well designed locations in the world it feels hollow. There is nothing noteworthy to find outside the main towns and dig sites so exploring simply is not encouraged. Furthermore the copy pasted NPCs with no characteristics what so ever feel more like part of the scenery than characters. I feel like just a little personality to a few of the NPCs could have made a big difference here. 

While other automation games usually make me hyped to expand and build a new production line, the clunky inventory/shop system and the fact that there is NO point in expanding once you're past a a certain output just made me quit the game, rather than expand futher.

It's simply more production output for the sake of more production output, which is not interesting to me.

TL;DR: Hydroneer is a clunky, unpolished experience you can safely skip. If you want a game about factory automation, save up for Dyson Sphere Project, Satisfactory, or Factorio. This game is not worth it for any price point -- seriously, if you value your time at all, just play something else.

In this game, your character can only carry one tool at a time. To use a different tool, you need to drop your current one and pick up a new one. There is no inventory or hotbar. I can respect this from a game design perspective, but it is simply not fun to pan for metals over and over in order to get out of the early game. Ex: Pick up shovel, shovel dirt into bucket, dump bucket into pan, drop shovel, pick up bucket, fill bucket with water from river, empty bucket into pan, drop bucket, pickup brush, use brush on pan to "pan for metals". This will give your a paltry amount of metals. Expect to do this several times before you have enough to smelt something.

Once you're past the early game and you have the simplest possible miner + sorter + smelter chain setup, the automation challenge of the game is essentially over. That simple setup is enough to create anything you want in the game. You don't need to upgrade any of your machines, or setup sensors/automation, or move to a different mining site, or setup inter-mine logistics, etc.. From a "factory game" perspective, Hydroneer is extremely shallow.

The act of "mining" is also very shallow. The only material in the world is dirt. The mining machine just checks that there's dirt under it. If there is, the machine spits out ore. It doesn't actually remove the dirt underneath it, so it will keep working forever even if you just place it on the surface level.

I played this before the base building feature was introduced, so I can't comment on that -- but if it's anything like placing miners and conveyor belts, it's clunky and frustrating.

Finally, it's completely unacceptable that this game is receiving $10 DLC when the base game is in this state.

review:
这游戏之所以前期让人玩着很难受，完全是一些实用道具没有放在前期和玩家难以理解如何使用所导致的。


举个例子：
可以把游戏中的[b]矿[/b]理解成[b]豆子或小米[/b]。掉在地上后你需要一个一个的去捡起来。
我们现实中遇见这种情况肯定是厨房拿扫把来扫。可这款游戏呢？他把你的扫把(磁铁)藏在了离你家较远的另一个城镇里，而且价格对前期来说非常贵。

除此之外，游戏中有一个非常实用的手工分拣器，它的用法是：在A面接上管道使其运作，在机器顶部一个不起眼的小平台上放你需要分拣的矿物，把矿物从机器顶部倒进去，B面和C面会吐出分拣好的矿物。
看起来还好？那是因为我研究了半小时又去看了官方的wiki才搞明白它是这么用的。


上面这两点加在一起，就导致了绝大多数玩家前期跟个弱智一样一个一个的捡石头往桶里扔，扔歪了掉出来还得重新捡。好不容易装好了到熔炼时又得把不同的矿一个一个挑出来，玩的比吃屎还难受。


不过在解决了这两点后，游戏还是比较有意思的。

Also you have to carry your coins and map with you everywhere. there is no inventory space at all. which is quite irritating. there are no signs of that being implemented in the future unfortunately - at least implement a map on key stroke feature....

review:
This game has one of the clunkiest user-interfaces I've seen so far. There is no inventory or tool-belt. You can only carry one item at a time. Either an item or a tool. Not both. This ends up in a lot of running around for not much gain.

Now, maybe that's something that's fixed by in-game craftable upgrades. But that shouldn't be necessary. A minimum of "quality-of-life" features are needed to reduce the grindiness.

Even [i[if[/i] some of those upgrades can be crafted, the rest of the UI dashes all hope of it becoming fun. Take "trading items" for example: To sell you need to drop them off on a specific place (carrying everything one-by-one), then walking over to a button and presing the button. This drops coins which you have to pick up [i]and hold in your hand[/i] so you can't carry anything else while carrying money.

To buy items you need to pick up items (one by one again) and move them to a designated "shopping-cart" area. Then go pick up your money (again, remember that you have to carry that in hand) and drop it into a bucket and  press the buy button. The remaming coins stay in the bucket so you have to move those around again if you need them at another shop.

After trading, all items need to be carried around again one-by-one.

And if this wasn't enough already, then get this: To drop items into a bucket (f.ex. for buying/selling) you have to carefully aim. Your character simply let's the fall wherever the virtual hand is located. So, somewhat off-center right on the screen. There is a small "shadow-circle" that helps. But it's not always well visible. So there are moments where you drop the coins to the side of the bucket which won't count.

It reminds me of "Astroneer" (different developer) which also tried to integrate the UI into the game-world. This resulted in similar frustration. And while I thought that "Astroneer" had a bad UI, "Hydroneer" is objectively worse. If only for nothing "snapping" properly. At least [i]that[/i] worked well in Astroneer.

In any case, if you care about good user-interfaces and sensible quality-of-life features then don't touch this game with a ten-foot-pole.

review: STONKS HERE WE GO!

I know this game has some dedicated fans who really enjoy it, but my thirty minutes with it were some of the most frustrating I've ever had. I open up my new world and immediately have no idea what to do, because there is zero tutorial or guidance of any kind. After roaming around for a bit, I give up and go look online. Turns out, I missed the shovel that was leaning next to my spawn point that I was apparently supposed to notice. So I grab that and head to the dirt area where I start trying to dig around. 

For some reason, I can't scoop dirt directly into the pan. Instead, I have to scoop it into the identical bucket and then pour the bucket into the pan - but after a few failed attempts where I pour my dirt out on the ground next to the pan instead, I realize the bucket pours things not where your cursor is, but where a very small and almost transparent circle off to the side is. review:
To all the people whining about this game, you're objectively wrong - I wrote you a starter guide below.
This game is addictive. It adds unique logic, mining and factory mechanics which all provide a fresh experience for such games. While there isn't a storyline, there are NPC fetch questions which allow you to earn extra money or tokens to improve your experience in different ways than just with money.

To those whining about the DLC not being free - you'd rather complain on a tiny indie game, yet you're still the type to pay £70 for the latest CoD game where most of the gameplay is DLC. Oh no, I guess I have to play game I bought without the (entirely optional yet still f***ing cheap) DLC...
There's many people who can't deal with being allowed to do your own thing and not stuck in a tutorial - there's a wiki - please RTFM.
I've bought this yesterday, and have already played 16 hours.

So, without further ado, here's my list of starter tips and tricks:

0) Revise The Keybindings
If you are familiar with Minecraft and similar keybindings, you'll find the controls a bit weird as you pick-up and drop items with the same key in this game.
Also, do not use the same key for vehicles & items - it'll prevent you from using helmets as you'll keep removing them when trying to put down a tool.
Fun Fact: There is a "Wiki" keybinding, which will open the wiki page for any item you are currently looking at, provided you didn't lock it with a construction hammer.

1) Dig deep, but not too steep
The walls of the dig sites are sometimes too steep to walk or even jump up, so try to leave some way of getting back out.
Worst case scenario, there's an "Unstuck" button in the pause menu which does work while driving.

2) Containers & Inventory Madness
When you place an item in a container, whether it's a bucket, pan, vehicle, etc... it becomes "pinned" to the container and no-longer collides with other items (excluding quad-bike storage). This allows you to stack what is essentially an infinitely-countable number of items in the same spot.
So, while there is no conventional inventory system, you can still transport almost anything using the already-provided vehicles.
Note: Containers stored in containers, such as a pan stored in Hydrotruck, will continue to hold their contents, but can only be filled if taken out of any surrounding containers - otherwise items will be stored in the outer-most container.

3) The cart is more useful than it seems
The cart allows you to maneuver larger items just by walking. However, while pulling the cart, you can fit through spaces that are too small for it - collision doesn't occur while pulling the cart.

3.5) Cart Mining Method
Fill buckets with dirt, then empty the bucket directly into a cart once full.
This will allow you to continuously dig chunks of dirt in the mine, rather than having to resurface just to dump one chunk. Using the cart not only ensures the chunks stay put, but allows you to easily get the chunks back to the surface for cleaning.

4) Free Refills
By placing a pipe to continuously drip water over a pan, you can just insert a chunk, scrub it, then repeat without needing to refill the water in the pan, allowing you to batch-process a lot of dirt very quickly.

5) Emergency Fuel Stop
The buckets and pans can hold a small amount of water, which will allow you to quickly give your vehicle just enough fuel to get somewhere to refuel, or at least closer to a body of water so you can refill your buckets.

6) Don't forget your wallet!
You'll need to bring your coins with you to your purchases. My personal recommendation is to have a pan in your truck or on the quad which acts as a wallet. You can take the pan out and place it directly in the baskets for purchases, and your change will automatically be stored back in the pan, so it does really act like a multi-currency wallet when used like that.

7) Unstuck Warp
If you time it well enough, you can press "Unstuck" and be teleported to the nearest recall point. As an example, pressing "Unstuck" when anywhere around Bridgepour will place you directly in the centre of bridgepour. This allows you to skip some of the driving if you're feeling so inclined. However, you'll soon realise that some places are better than others for performing this trick as sometimes you lose progress, rather than gaining it.

FN) If you appreciated this list at all, please feel free to upvote this as I entirely want to spite the person who whined about having to transport foundations because they didn't try and use the free cart which is literally shown in images in the same building you were trying to put foundations.

Fun Bottom Fact) Lanterns will entinguish when touching water... unless you re-light them as they're being extinguished, which tricks the game into keeping them lit underwater.

We’ve added in measures to prevent this from corrupting but there are some outlying cases. We also have added in ‘backup’ saves to prevent total data loss. Try finding this backup, by opening up the game, pressing ‘continue’ on the main menu, then ticking the ‘Show Backup’ box. This will show a backup save file which hopefully won’t be corrupted.

It's light hearted, laid back and creative. You can go as simple or complex as you choose or just go fishing. It's all up to you. 

Anyone that gives this game a down vote simply does not like fun.

A new DLC is about to roll out. Hell, it's about time to write a review for this game. Got over 666 hours played in it as well, that should count for something, right?
Well, not really. You see, my experience with the game is unlikely to directly translate into your own. All I can do is share a bit of mine, and hope that I don't mislead you.
"From so simple a beginning..." - First of all, this is a chill game, that doesn't pressure you into doing anything with incessant tool-tips and tutorials everywhere. You get a bucket, a shovel, a pan, a truck and a cart. That's it - now go make your fortune. There's no hand-holding (and that makes our lives over on the game's Discord more interesting, more on that later). Everything takes time to do in this game. There is no inventory system. You just have to find efficient ways to move the stuff you need around - be it construction materials, consumables, equipment, even currency - to and from the shops. There are a couple of speed-run tactics, but, as a new player, expect to spend some hours, maybe on multiple saves, before you understand how to properly build your base of operation to do what you want it to do. 
"...endless forms most beautiful have been, and are being, evolved." - There's hardly a consensus about what the end-game is. You shovel dirt to get resources, expand the hole you just made deeper to get better resources, to get better equipment to mine more efficiently, to get resources to fulfill quests, to get better quests, to unlock even better equipment, to mine even more resources, until you don't really need those resources anymore - but, in the end, it's just so satisfying to just watch your builds in action. Maybe you want to produce 1 million resources weight per hour. Maybe you want to be able to press just a couple of buttons and have all the mats needed for your quests ready for you, by using logic. Or maybe you want to create logic builds that play freaking "You sunk my battleship" within the game - that have nothing to do with mining. Or you just want to farm and make better and better soups for the villagers. Or chill with fishing and get the best rod, and then (why not) create a bridge out of fish. Or build a castle with the available construction materials, complete with a throne and crazy expensive items dotted around. Or search for relics and other secrets around the map. You do not HAVE to do any of this stuff. The game is a sandbox, and your imagination is the limit to what silly contraptions you can build.
Besides mining, logic, fishing, farming. building and decorating, one of the most important features of this game must be its Discord server. It is filled with passionate people that are always willing to help you out, and share some of their crazier builds or ideas. There are also a lot of mods that can help with some aspects of the game you might not enjoy (e.g. the lack of an inventory, the relatively long time it takes to dig out a site, and many more). The game can be customized extensively.
All I can say is, if you try this game out, I hope you make it your own, and enjoy the process. I'll be ready to hop into a new save on the DLC in a couple of hours, starting again from scratch, for the n-th time. For me, this is the best part. For you, it might be something else entirely, and that is fine. Peace.

I'm on the fence about this one. on the one hand, i have spent a lot of time with it and i'll probably spend a lot more, but on the other hand, it's ridiculously flawed.

you can only carry one item at a time, which makes everything super tedious. that's the major pain point. If the Dev gave you an inventory and the ability to stack items, I feel like 90% of the  negative reviews would become positive. half your time in this game is spent manually loading stuff into your truck, one by one. then you take it to your mine and unload it, one by one, so that you can access it all. then if you want to automate your mines, you have to lug each individual piece of pipe and each individual piece the conveyor belt down into your mine, one by one. it's so utterly obnoxious. 

 but they probably won't do that, mostly because the base game is severely lacking in actual content, so if they removed the tedium the game would probably only last about 5 hours instead of 50.
that said, the DLC releases tommorow and it sounds like it's got a lot more content, so maybe it'll change my mind


EDIT TO ADD:
so i've played the DLC now, and honestly, after another 35 hours i'm done with this game. don't get me wrong the dlc adds a lot of content and does give you a better progression curve,  
but it doesn't fix my core issue with the game which is that it does not respect your time and makes basic interactions extremely tedious. also, for some reason, this dlc just completely removes the farming mechanic. I get that it wasn't the best mechanic in the world and could have been a bit better integrated into the core loop, but removing it outright seems a bit silly. 

The big hauler is kind of interesting, and i do like the forge mark mechanic in theory, but in practice i don't think randomisation is the way to go here, because by the time you have a perfect, fully optimised set of drills and other equipment, there's not much to really do.
Also, I like the stuff with building up the new town in theory, but in practice it just amounts to paying a toll (first in money, then in resources) to access most of the shops, and i think it needs a way for you to actually put your stamp on it, instead of just the ability to chose which of 4 plots of land the 4 shops get to sit in. 

the problem is that the world feels way too static. you can only build stuff on a far away plots of land and you don't really have much reason to build yourself a house besides aesthetics.  

I think the solution to both of these problems would be to give the player the ability to actually, literally build up a town like new glade. The house building stuff exists in the game already, maybe just give it a bit more of a purpose so that you can literally build up a town as you like it. it would solve the issues around the endgame, because it would give the player a creative outlet to funnel all of their resources into.  (it would also give you a reason to get more into farming, since you could make the player responsible for feeding the villagers in order to draw more of them in maybe, or hell, maybe even adding some basic survival mechanics to help the progression curve along?). 
I also strongly feel like we should have the ability to craft tools and other bits and pieces for ourselves instead of buying them, without having to travel to the heart of a volcano and use a giant forge. 

however, I've officially quit the game after getting sick of running around trying to fix my production lines. there seems to be a bug if you get your production going too fast, which causes the game to lag and the ore gets stuck going over the edge of a line. (note: i have an RTX 4090 and and a Ryzen 9 7950X3D, along with 64gbs of DDR5 RAM.  some of the absolute best hardware on the market, but i had constant issues with lag when i was near my production lines, not to mention multiple crashes, especially when trying to unclog my production lines) 
i tried everything to get my lines unclogged and working again, i used the option to remove all ore a few times, but they just got stuck again, i used the magnet on a stick to unclog em but they'd just spray everywhere, cause the game to lag or crash, and create a huge mess. I used centralisers and mergers, but ore still kept getting caught. 
my lines had been working fine until i added more drills, which is what leads me to believe the issue was caused by lag. for the record, i had 7 drills in total. that absolutely should not be enough to cause that many issues. 



Overall, i think there are definitely a lot of people who could have fun with this game, and on some level i was one of them for a while, but i just couldn't handle the jank and the tedium. I definitely respect the low price tag, and the game has some pretty cool and interesting mechanics, so i'll probably check out the dev's next game and i'd definitely be keen for a sequel, but i'm definitely done with this one and i probably wouldn't recommend it to anyone who hasn't already played Factorio, Satisfactory, or any of the other big automation games out there to death already. it just doesn't have enough content and what's there is just a bit too buggy, finicky and boring to really justify spending your time on.

explosives could be much more cost effective.
