Hydroneer( 하이드로니어 )는 수압과 물을 주축으로 한 세계에서
채굴, 농사 혹은 낚시와 같은 수단으로 돈을 버는 게임입니다.
입니다.. 만.
공장 게임을 생각하고 온 이들 뿐만 아니라, 대다수에게 불편하다고 여겨질만한 진행 곡선을 가지고 있습니다.

1. 다른 게임에서 찾기 쉬운 게임 기능인 캐릭터 인벤토리가 없습니다.
따라서 플레이어는 "한 번에 하나의" 아이템만을 옮길 수 있으며.
이로 인해서 운반을 보조해줄 다른 수단을 찾아야합니다.

이와 관련된 조언이 있다면 첫 번째로 차량 뒷 공간에 수레를 끌고 들어가서 집어 넣을 수 있습니다.
두 번째로 큰 양동이는 별의 별 아이템을 우겨넣을 수 있습니다. 수레는 차량처럼 무한하게 물건을 겹칠 수 있으므로
상점에서 구매하는 자리에 수레를 두고 그 수레에 아이템을 겹처서 넣은 다음 한번에 결제할 수 있습니다.

2. 플레이어가 들러야 하는 상점"들"이 넓은 지역에 분산되어 있습니다.
초반에 필요한 잡동사니들은 가까운 거리에 있으나, 자동화에 있어서 중요한 컨베이어 벨트
생산량을 늘리기 위한 기계들과 더 나은 제련 시설등등이 차량을 이용하지 않고서는 꽤 먼 거리에 있고.
이용한다고 해도, mk 2 차량을 사기 이전까지엔 이동하는데에 많은 시간을 소모하는 것 같습니다.
초반을 넘긴 이후에도 상당히 먼 곳에 상점들이 위치한 까닭에 게임 진행 대부분을 이동하는데 할애하는 기분이 듭니다.

3. 정말 필요한 내용들이 튜토리얼에서 제공되지 않습니다.
예를 들어 채굴기의 경우 "~ 사용하는 경우 주기적으로 피해를 입는다."라고 작성되어 있어서
정제된 물을 투입하는 경우 손상을 입지 않는 수확기와 다른 느낌으로 서술되어 있지만
그와 달리 채굴기가 수확기처럼 동일한 구조인 상황이라 정제된 물을 넣어서 손상을 예방할 수 있습니다.

[quote=Sandball]... (중략). 더 이상 번역에 참여하지 않게 되었습니다. 개발자 분께서 따로 고용하셔서 쓴다고 하네요. 따라서 번역 수정이 이제 쉽게 되진 않을 것 같습니다.[/quote]

한글 번역에 기여하신 Sandball님의 말을 인용해본다면, 개발자가 따로 고용해서 진행하는 듯 한데
그럼에도 불구하고 번역이 많이 빈약합니다. 예를 들어 한글 대신 영어로 출력되는 부분이 굉장히 많습니다.

게임을 시작하면 필요한 도구가 삽, 양동이, 큰 양동이( 명칭이 기억나지 않네요 ), 붓 정도가 있는데.
삽과 렌턴이 가로등에 따로 있고, 강에는 양동이들과 붓이 따로 있어서 이걸 한 번에 못 찾으면 게임 진행이 막히는
이상한 부분도 있습니다. 저는 게임 개발자가 너무나도 영리해서, 게임에서 따로 튜토리얼을 진행하지 않은 경우
삽을 생성하지 않는 줄 알았습니다.

4. 최적화가 이상합니다.
특히 자동 저장부분에 무슨 일이 벌어진건지, 종종 게임이 멈췄다가
저장 과정이 끝나면 다시 돌아오는 편입니다. 평가 작성 시간 기준으로 플레이 시간은 19시간이며.
이 많은 시간들 조차도 처음 헛짓거리를 많이 했기 때문에 게임을 많이 진행한 것도 아닌데다,
개발자가 경고하는 거대한 공장이 있는 것도 아닌데 왜 그런진 모르겠네요.

그래도 다음에 있을 업데이트에서는 몇몇 최적화 문제가 해결될 것으로 보여서 다행입니다.

장점이 아예 없는 게임은 아닌데, 상당히 불편한 진행 곡선으로 인해서
중도 이탈이 많은 것으로 생각됩니다. 일단 초반 진입 장벽이 매우 상당한 상황에서
스팀 리모트 플레이같은 유사 협동 플레이보다는 제대로 된 coop 멀티 플레이나,
무작위 지형을 사용하는 멀티 플레이가 나오던지 해야할 것 같습니다.

I really want to like this game, but it ultimately falls short of greatness and becomes boring and repetitive due to a major flaw: the harvesters.

The problem with harvesters in this game, which give infinite resources, is that they turn the game from what it should be, a strip mining sim (ala Gold Rush: The Game) with fantasy elements and more automation, into an inferior version of Factorio and the like with just physicality to differentiate itself. The physicality itself eventually turns against the game when you have to pour resources into a crucible or other bucket and the game starts chugging like Thomas the Tank Engine climbing up Mt. Everest. It's kind of ironic that. at the beginning, the game encourages you to not waste pay dirt, only to tell you a little while later to use a pickaxe to destroy most of it on each patch just to place harvesters on rich patches of dirt in order to get a never ending stream of rare resources. It makes everything, from gold to gems and other rare resources, seem worthless and mostly pointless. The quests given out by NPCs that walk around the map don't alleviate the problem and are themselves also tedious.

Honestly the base idea is kind of neat but it's so lacking in features and the QOL is literally non existant, I'd even go as far as saying the developers insisted on anti-QOL to drag out the lack of content in the game. Once you've played it for an hour or two you've actually basically experienced the entire game, there's very little else, every thing else is a shallow gimmick including most of what you see in the trailer (vehicles, "quests", everything else). Might even be a passable game with multiplayer, but alas, only splitscreen (in 2024?) is available. Don't be fooled by the positive reviews, this game is pretty terrible despite being in development for half a decade, and the global achievement stats indicate about as much.

I was hoping for a relaxing game with gradual progression and some basic & satisfying refining content. It's actually the exact opposite, the direction the developer has chosen to take is so completely contradictory to the basis of the game; you can literally only hold 1 item at any one time, which is so completely unrelaxing & unenjoyable, and progression is a facade in this game.

Want to drop your shovel but your tiny brush is on the ground next to you? Can't do that, game plays annoying sound. Turn slightly, still can't drop shovel because...??? Turn slightly again, lets me drop the shovel. Try to drop brush, game won't let you & plays annoying sound because your shovel is next to you, not impeding your brush.

They could have made a really satisfying, relaxing game but it feels like this game is made to frustrate you and be unenjoyable. I imagine the developers have taken this direction because of how content-poor the game is, so they flood your time with micromanaging and messing around with poor controls.

I bought a mining helmet with a light on it; not only does the light not illuminate even a meter in front of you, but for some reason the game uses the same button for "drop" to equip/unequip your helmet. Why? You get used to the hotkey to drop your items (which you have to do literally several times a second because you can only hold 1 thing at a time) and then you buy a helmet/get vehicle and now the only hotkey for those is the same as dropping your items.

Have helmet on -> try to drop item -> drops helmet -> try to re-equip helmet with Q -> drops item in hand -> Q AGAIN to equip helmet -> have to pick back up item and move it again because you've moved to pick your helmet back up. Repeat every single time you have to pick up and item (which is 90% of the game). So very, very unsatisfying. 

You also can't choose where to drop stuff in relation to your character, and the drop location is locked to be kind of in front of you but off to the right? Again, why? It's just stupid and tedious, so instead of looking somewhere and being able to drop your singular equipped item, you have to turn and drop it to the side, it's so needlessly annoying and unsatisfying. Very unintuitive, especially when you pick up items from directly in front of you.

The lighting is also horrible, the lanterns illuminate nothing and nor does the mining helmet. Night time (which serves practically no purpose) lasts too long and you can't see almost anything. For a game with no enemies/challenge, why would you make nighttime so annoying? What purpose does not being able to see at night serve in a PvNothing game?

There's no real progression either, you just grind tedious processes for small amount of ores/gems (there's a total of 4 ores and 4 gems in the entire game...) to then grind more tedious processes to make any of the 2 jewelries/3 items to sell. Every process is tedious, from mining, to refining, to making the items to sell, to transporting the items, to building, everything is pointlessly tedious.

Honestly has cool bones, but there's absolutely zero direction or path to take. No story, or small achievements to work towards without already having the full breadth of knowledge of the game.

Not to mention this game is absolutely masochistic if you ever, ever happen to have ores miss a pan. There's no way to get hundreds of ore on the ground neatly into a pan for transport, you will quite literally have to spend 10-30 minutes spamming "E" while having a bucket PERFECTLY placed with your position PERFECTLY between to place anything on the ground, one-by-one, into the bucket. There is no other way to do this on any type of scale. This is absolutely terrible, terrible game design.

Oh, but wait! There's a magnet on a stick! Surely that will pull the ores and let you place a bunch into a container (pan), right? Haha, you wish! It keeps the ores far too spread to place into the tiny pan, and what's worse, is once you get it near the pan... Any ores inside it now get vacuumed out! Hope you enjoy starting the cleanup over, prepare your replacement "E" key!

Absolutely cannot recommend this game until a bit more thought and respect is given to tasks like this. It's in a really bad spot due to this oversight.

review:
English / Deutsch
---

Hopelessly overrated. Can it be fun - yes.

Would I recommend it to anyone? No! You play a idiotic old man who can only use one arm, has an aversion to any kind of bag and thinks backpacks are the work of the devil.
While with Factorio, Satifactory and the like you carry entire factories around with you, here you get the complete opposite. The game is designed to bully you from start to finish.
If you have the masochistic need to pick up hundreds of objects one by one with the mouse and carry them around, then Hydroneer is the right choice for you. The quick change of day and the dark start of it are the icing on the cake.
The only carrot on the hook: You bought an ore rich piece of land by lugging buckets... no, sorting sieves full of coins, into the middle of nowhere. 

The stupid residents have lured you in to drive you crazy. At some point the Stockholm syndrome mercifully sets in and you convince yourself that you have achieved something. Until then, suffering is the order of the day.


Good reviews or not, as far as I can see less than 10% of buyers have seriously touched the game.

- - -

Hoffnungslos überbewertet. Kann es Spaß machen - ja.

Würde ich es jemanden empfehlen? Grundgütiger, nein! Man spielt einen grenzdebilen, alten Mann, der nur einen Arm benutzen kann, eine Abneigung gegen jede Art von Tasche hat und Rucksäcke für Teufelswerk hält.
Während man bei Factorio, Satifactory und dergleichen ganze Fabrikanlagen mit sich herumschleppt, bekommt man hier das krasse Gegenteil serviert. Das Spiel ist darauf aus einen von vorn bis hinten zu schikanieren. Einzige Karotte am Angelhaken: Man hat günstig ein überaus ertragreiches Stück Land erstanden, indem man Eimer... nein, Sortiersiebe voller Münzen irgendwo ins Nirgendwo geschleppt hat. 

Die strunzdummen Bewohner haben einen angelockt, um einen in den Wahnsinn zu treiben. Irgendwann stellt sich dann gnädig das Stockholm-Syndrom ein und man redet sich ein, man habe sich etwas erarbeitet. Bis dahin ist Leiden angesagt.

Wenn man das masochistische Bedürfnis hat hunderte Objekte einzeln mit der Maus aufzupicken und durch die Gegend zu tragen, dann ist man bei Hydroneer richtig. Der schnelle Tageswechsel und der dunkle Tagesbeginn sind das I-Tüpfelchen.

Gute Rezensionen hin oder her, soweit ich sehe haben unter 10% der Käufer das Spiel ernsthaft angefasst.

Imagine you're happy with your tier 2 automation set up. It was somewhat temporary but now you're ready to break into tier 3 so you want to straighten your base up. You've been mining down in a cool looking dwarven ruin but your stuff is just laying all over the cave floor and it looks like you're some kind of dwarven hobo. You want some foundations at least so your floor is level. You can't build them, you can only buy them. You head out of the ruin, up 6 flights of stairs, down a couple of walkways, another flight of stairs, an elevator and now you can get to your car. You go to the store on the other side of the map that sells foundations. You can't buy the foundations because you forgot your money in your dwarf hobo cave. There's no inventory, no wallet, you have to literally carry a pile of coins which prevents you from carrying anything else. Back in the car, back across the map, down the elevator, down the stairs, across the walkway, down more stairs, pick up your coins, up the flights of stairs, across the walkway, up the stairs, up the elevator, in the car, across the map. You can buy about 5 foundations at a time because you have to physically put them on a purchase platform and more than that doesn't fit. You hit buy, it doesnt work. You forgot to put your physical coins in the purchasing bucket so you run to your car, pick up your coins, put them in the bucket. Now you have to load those foundations into your car, tediously. After 10 rounds of this you have 50 foundations, not enough but you're about to rage quit so you take what you have. You drive across the map back to your dwarven ruin. You now have to load, 1 at at time, every foundation you purchased into this conveyor belt that will transport the items to your base. It's tedious and takes way too long but it's better than running each block down 1 at a time. Now you need more pipes and conveyor belts. Buying these will be the same as buying foundations, tedious. Luckily there is a store in the dwarven ruin conveniently located 6 flights of stairs above the only place you can use and build with those items. You go load up the purchasing platforms 3 conveyors that will fit for that purchase, you're already dreading this because you'll have to run each conveyor down 1 at a time or use a pallet and carry 4 at 1/4 the walking speed. You hit buy. Doesn't work, you forgot your coins at the store that sells foundations.

先讲结论：游戏资质尚可，但是频繁发生的恶性bug、糟糕的优化以及在特定情况下十分反人类的交互体验使得这款游戏成为了名副其实的会员制“美食”。
而且还有就是使用模组禁用成就这一点十分的蠢，说白了就是教玩家怎么玩游戏，既然你要搞创意工坊和模组社区就不要限制玩家使用模组，现在搞得四不像，纯傻逼。
自动化之前的交互十分的繁琐，并且即便自动化之后也摆脱不了烦人的检修和排查，游戏内容看着多但是重复度其实很高。
自动存档很好但是没法及时读档，基本上断绝了SL大法的可能性，让人不是很理解，一个单机游戏搞这么多针对玩家减负的行为是想干嘛，我是来娱乐的不是来上班的。
自动化流水线说起来也没什么好说的，深度很低，适合轻量玩家，但是自动化前期十分折磨，尤其是搭配上这游戏答辩一般的优化，更是让人两眼一黑（说到这就不得不提我好不容易抽到了一块炫金块结果回家收拾产线的时候因为优化太辣鸡导致游戏卡死使得我不仅前功尽弃还损失了整整一下午的时间因为我tm自动保存关了）
自动化也只是做了一半，很多事情到最后还是得玩家亲自动手才行。
钓鱼系统算是有点意思但意思不多，没办法把战利品展示起来，只能卖了或者做成汤然后卖了，就让人挺不爽的，尤其是现在改版后钓鱼的收益被大砍，卖鱼更没意义了，就不能加个鱼类展示架之类的东西或者让主角自己能吃点啥吗？有自动化种田但是只能拿来做菜卖钱，那到后面这农业自动化有屁用啊，收入都溢出了也不差这点了。
原价是不推荐买的，打折可以考虑入手。
我骂完估计也会继续玩下去，当然前提是这勾八游戏别再给我整这出了，赶紧把优化想办法再整整吧，我真的受不了每次卖完东西回家搭产线收东西的时候都会帧数直奔两三帧了。

오늘 겜켜니 세이브파일이 날아갔다.
-----------------------------------------------------------

이게임이 왜 망했는지 알 것 같다.
개발된 콘텐츠가 많지 않으니 노가다로 플탐을 늘려놨다.
상식적인 과정보다 일부러 불편하게 여러번 행동하도록 만들어논게 티난다.
Hydroneer라매. 3시간동안 시설은 커녕 삽질이랑 양동이솔질만 하다 끝났다.
다른 자동화게임이라면 놀면서 해도 일주일 안에 종료될 만한 콘텐츠양을 빡세게 몇 달해야 할 분량으로 늘려논 듯 하다.
분량을 쓸 데 없이 늘려놨으면 멀티라도 지원해주던가 수동으로 템팔러 마을 다녀야하는 게임에서 분할화면으로 멀티를 하라고? 

매긍인데 왜 망했다고 하냐고?
평가들은 보면 100시간 이상한 사람이 많지 않다.
두자리수 플탐 비중도 같은 장르 게임들에 비해 매우 적다.

출시가 4년 지난 공장겜이 100시간 미만이라면 정말 콘텐츠가 없다는거다.
공장겜은 특유의 이거하려면 저거구해야지가 있어서 수천시간 수만시간 어마무시한 플탐을 잡아먹는데 이건 그냥 뭐 하나를 하려 해도 꾹 참고 해야된다.
돌나무만 캘 수 있으면 재밌어하는 내겐 이거도 재미가 아예 없는건 아니다.
다만 게임을 하는 3시간 내내 성취감이라곤 개나줘버린 '고의적 불편함'에 욕을 박고 싶다.
게임이 즐거워서 빠져들게 해야지, '암튼 버티면 재밌어져요!' 라고 하면 굳이 같은 장르의 다른 재밌는 게임들을 두고 이걸 해야하나 싶다.

그냥 잠시 스쳐지나가며 좋게 평가하지만 그만큼 플레이를 다하지 않고 라이브러리에 짱박는 게임이란 거다.

I found this game in the store a few months ago, tried it and hated the way it played. Recently decided to give it another try. For me it was hard to play with a keyboard, once I switched to a controller, it was WAY better (I know, BLASPHEMY!).
The game is simple enough, mine, smelt, either sell or complete the tasks from NPC's and use the money to upgrade your gear. The cartoon world isn't big but isn't small either, the graphics are the cartoonist style that seems popular these days. The game starts very slow and can be a boring grind but after you start automating, it gets so much better and more fun to craft and upgrade. 
There are some downsides. The biggest example is one I ran into, where it was hard to know what to do or how to do it. a great example was figuring out how to make more mining machines. There are also different currencies (normal, lantern and apple) that can be confusing at the start for what does what and how to get each type. There are also slight annoyances when you get big enough, for example, you might need 10+ conveyors which you have to buy one at a time and load into the truck/pallet one at a time. It can be a bit annoying as you cant buy in bulk.
Overall, I still highly recommend this game, (as of writing this) I have poured 20+ hours in and still cant wait for more. If you like crafting, mining and building this game is definitely worth playing. Just make sure to keep YouTube tutorials handy.

review:
This game has been in my library for 2.5 years now, played it a bit, left it alone, played it again, left it alone again and now picked it up once more. And yes, I am on the verge on abandoning it once more. Why? Because once things are up and running, there is nothing more to do and it has been like this for that time.
As mentioned in other reviews, the start takes a bit of time, but after that, the curve of production shoots up to the moon and all challenge, and thus meaning, is lost. Yes you can move your whole production line somewhere else, dig deeper, faster. You can add logic. You can blow stuff up. Or retire a farmer feeding the people. But the question is: Why? Only if you really like this game to be an optimisation job without a purpose. There is no incentive. No greater goal, nothing. You do not have to build a house, don't have to eat, have no need for more than 50.000 coins.
In a game like Stardew Valley you at have to possibillity to feel part of the community. And in games like Factorio, Dyson Sphere Program or Satisfactory there is a need to build and optimise. This game does not have that. It is flat after the first tedious hours which you could have spend playing better games.

A game's worst crime is that it's... fine.
As in, it does what it says on the tin, but not much else.
It gives you a sense of steady progression in the early and mid game, which is what I love most, but I feel like the bugs, and various construction systems are clunky and not well optimized. I also feel as though the promise of true co-op was broken as the weird split-screen co-op experience is lackluster.
I got to the point where the main limiting factor of my success is that my machines produce far more ingots and gems than I can ever sort through and process on my own. I'm also to the point where everyone wants me to do Agricultural goods and it's like... no, I won't blow thousands of coins on starting a whole new business venture because nobody in the town knows how to fish or farm themselves lol It's ridiculous.
The game at first made me feel like I'm a part of a cozy little village of people, but now I'm shanghai'd into abandoning my 20 hour business venture in order to satisfy these mooks in order to earn some dumb trader coins so I can buy better equipment to break through the progression wall I hit. 3 hours of my play time was wasting time starting a dumb farm in order to progress, and 1 hours was spent doing farm work. It wasn't even enough coins to break through the wall, and so I needed to keep doing it... No thanks. I thought manually panning for resources was tedious...
Also there's DLC coming out when the game still feels incomplete and in Early Access. Granted, the base game is only 15 bucks and it's almost always on sale. It's just a bunch of small tedious parts added up to me not touching the game since June of last year. Satisfactory, Factorio, Techtonica, and plenty of other games akin to this exist which all have working multiplayer and have infinite depth (Literal depth for Techtonica) which all are around the same price or are often also on sale.
If you're thinking of buying this game, don't expect it to be like the games I mentioned, and maybe wait to see how the DLC fares.

Icehelm's interior is the worst culprit of this. The scale of it is neat design-wise, but the walk in and out of it are nightmarishly long to put it nicely. The walk is at least >1-min long, and that's without even carrying a pallet, which stops you from sprinting. And then at the entrance, the elevator is the bane of my existence. Rather than staying where it last was used, it is always in motion, moving up, waiting a few seconds, moving down, waiting, over and over. The elevator is also really slow, and I might just be an unlucky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but I swear, that elevator, always leaves just when I get there. And then I'm left just standing there. Waiting. For. The. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Elevator. All things considered, good game! It can seem a little tedious at first, but as soon as you get even a little bit of automation, it feels very rewarding. Manually purchasing and placing things can be a little tedious occasionally, but it feels more satisfying when you finish things because of it. So, my final verdict: A few annoying aspects, but not enough to ruin the otherwise great experience, especially at a very low price.

This is a bad game. More specifically, every version past 2.0 is bad.
If you want to play this game, play it with the beta branches on 1.7 or below. I personally prefer 1.7.
Why is this game bad?
-The developers changed the entire "feel" of the game by adding people and giving more life to the world. Normally this is good. However, the weird style of the NPCs makes the game feel... off. Whenever you walk next to them, they suddenly shout at you.
-The developers lied about multiplayer. Now, technically I'm lying here, but what do you think of by multiplayer? Online play? Perhaps servers? Nope. You get split-screen coop advertised as if it's across seas pingless frictionless play. The devs routinely try to excuse this.
-This game is so ungodly buggy. Four years after full release, whenever I vaguely hit a rock, my car goes flying across the map. Hell, just look at Let's Game It Out. One of his videos showed him literally breaking the game by putting an item on a cart. They do no QA testing.
-Instead of releasing good updates and fixing bugs, the developers decided to release a weird DLC. I won't give an opinion on the actual DLC considering I'm not going to waste my money on it, but it's safe to say the game needed to have updates on the mainland before a whole new DLC.

I bought this game in 2020, before update 1.4. The developers have changed a lot of things. The game doesn't feel like how it was before. Instead of buying machines, you now have to craft them. You now have to spend twenty minutes getting enough iron to make an entire machine, then you have to drive to Icehelm... and then buy a whole new blueprint so that you can build the thing. You can no longer buy these things. Which is a terrible decision. It changed how the entire game works, and not in a good way.

I no longer like this game in its current state. 1.7 is what I play. If you want to buy it because you like all of the new features, sure. Just know that this game is not what it used to be.

I have enjoyed this game quite a lot - Currently at about 46 hours at the time of this review,
and there are a lot of pros about the game but a few major cons that I didn't much like (but, they might not bother other people)

Pros:
1) The feel of the game is fun, having to do the different jobs is what sim games are about, and this fits that role brilliantly, especially for the early game, you really start with just the bare basics and salvage a pittance to buy your first drill and things and it feels quite rewarding (though, that does quickly die off, admittedly)

2) Planning your build and how you want to set everything up is very fun, it gets the mind working and it is also really cool seeing your planning come to fruition, and planning is also key because of how long-winded it is to buy and transport the parts you want - But remembering the parts you need, taking pressure into account, planning how things will be sorted into their respective items along the way, adding logics with wires, etc. Having all these options available to consider when building an auto-mining thing is fun, and if you do it all right first time round as you envision it, and it works perfectly, I must admit is very rewarding and feels like a 3D schematic that's come to life - Its awesome

3) Having the different vehicles, different patches of land and higher tiers of drills to aim for is also a nice factor to add to the game as you can try different ideas in different areas and work on better ways to make your build more efficient, while yielding results the whole time - There are also more vehicles than I first thought too, with more being found as options to buy in other towns (some with tokens, others with coins) - It would make hardcore grinders have something to show that really shows they have spent hours on the game

4) The very start might feel like a monotonous grind, but actually, it is quite charming to have to pan for different resources and pick up the individual pieces and pop them in a crucible to melt - Making your first weapon is satisfying too. You can make hundreds of swords or daggers from very minute amounts of metal, but they sell for sell (obviously), but having the freedom to mix and match resources when crafting as well as using different amounts of resources is a good touch to the game and if you wanted an RP kind of game, I would wager that it would be more fun with friends

5) Stockpiling resources and forging weapons to sell is quite a fun mechanic, which is charmingly basic and simple to understand - Its also fun to see the highest value item you can make will be (my current record is 1.7 mil, which would have been more, but i was curious and wanted to know so i built it sooner, instead of waiting longer)

6) The furniture and housing parts are a nice touch to the game, it gives you something else to do and each town has different parts available too, so you can mix and match styles in any way you see fit, then pick one of the plots of land that you have, take all the pieces you have loaded into your truck and start building your own homestead

Cons:
1) After some time, the game does feel quite grindy, once you have a good automated system in place, you are basically golden on the money front - I only have about 4 x Tier 2 drills (which remain inactive most of the time) and I already have over 3 Million Hydrocoins, So, now there isn't much I really *want* to do - The game has other currencies in the form of tokens which are earned for different guilds by completing villager requests (the results of which can be used to buy things to make the respective guild requirements easier, like sprinklers for gardening, etc), but the game by no means requires any of them, so you can forgo the extra effort and pain as the results aren't *that* amazing.
It basically makes it so, the only "reason" you need better drills and would want to dig deeper is to get the two better materials, "Cloutium" and "Corestone" to make T2 and T3 respectively, but you don't *need* them... you can do everything with T1 things, the T2 drills also have a different orientation, so you cannot simply substitute your currently build with the new tier drill, it requires an entire rework of your build, which I thought was pretty sucky, tbh

2) Farming is something that is so SO slow, the plants themselves grown quite well, but the game is linked to a grid system, so that things line up nicely (which isn't the issue), however, when a pipe is connected to a water source and is not connected to anything the other end, it trickles a single drop out repeatedly, this drop can be used to irrigate 1 plant hole (Which, when digging, are NOT bound to the same grid system), So, having to have LOADS of pipes to get a large yield of crops is a nightmare, and while the sprinkler solves this issue (i would imagine), each one is very expensive in tokens and would require hours upon hours of growing a plant, waiting for it to grow, destroying the crop, replanting one, waiting, and so on, just to get enough crops to make 1 soup to get 88 tokens, when a sprinkler costs over 2000... And seeing as the only *real* reward from a large plant harvest (after you dont need tokens for maximising efficiency) is just getting more Hydrocoins, you might as well completely forgo that side of the game and favour the mining

3) While novel at first, having to load up a car with each and every single piece of equipment takes a very long time, and there are pallets which somewhat make this easier (and trucks can hold endless stuff as the pieces merge through one another when in that area), it still takes forever to load up the truck with things, especially with pipes (which you always need loads of) or building pieces - I like the feel of going into a shop, picking up the item and placing in the "buy zone" and paying for it, that's a nice touch, but having to pick up, drop, buy, pick up, move to truck, place in truck, and so on, PER ITEM takes an ungodly amount of time

4) I have over 50 drills mining chunks of dirt for processing, and production is great, however, the amount of items that are on the belts (as each lump counts as an item) makes the frames take a serious hit, I have a nice Laptop that can run many games with ease, but the frame rate drops massively to the point where I had to isolate a whole 27 drill segment of my build just to make sure the game ran smoother, which for an autonomy game is annoying

5) Lastly, (and this is just a personal gripe), For some reason, it ALWAYS seems to be night time - You can sleep and make it day time, but night comes around every 15mins, which, in a grind game, (and a game that takes FOREVER to shop en masse for things), isn't much good, because 15mins goes REALLY quickly, without even noticing - But, when night falls, the darkness just makes it next to impossible to see on the land patches, and requires you to sleep (or use an annoying mining helmet for a small circle of light) - Like i said, its a personal gripe, but I've had to resort to shopping in the dark so that by the time i get back it should be light (which it rarely is and still requires a sleep) - I just find it annoying, and as "Sleep" and other survival factors aren't actual mechanics, it wouldn't be out of place to maybe put the option to take the day/night cycle off

Overall, though, I would definitely say that the pros outweigh the cons - Just view the game as a casual play and don't look towards the "End Goal" and the games is so much more fun - The more you try and aim for something, the further and further away it seems, despite steady progress.
So, i will probably still play the game after this review, and I would certainly recommend it too.
If you use the £1 per hour of play system, i have got about 4x my money's worth from this game (purchased at £12.79)
But, If you aren't happy spending that, when it goes on offer, *then* buy it, because it is a well made game and is very fun

My list of problems:
- You can only carry one object at a time.  Need to run a 100 object length of pipe?  You have to manually grab each piece and place it one at a time.  The only way around some of this is to use something big enough to load items.  Metal bars into pans, pipes into a truck, then carry/drive that container object around.  And items like a conveyor belt wont fit in a pan
- Even your money is physical item, and not a stat, and requires carrying it around into buckets to push buttons to buy stuff with it.
- Expanding is a pain, especially if you want to reuse stuff.  You have to manually take it apart, one by one, then rebuild one by one.
- Starting out is very slow.  Use shovel to dig dirt, put dirt in a pan, get water into pan (with bucket or dump pan in water), use brush on pan, pick ore out of pan, put it somewhere to sell, repeat until you can afford to automate
- Your starting plot can earn enough Hydrocoins in a few hours with 4 digging units to buy nearly everything you could want with Hydrocoins
- Automation units degrade over time, and need repaired with the flimsiest wrenches in the world (single use each!)  Eventually you need water filters to protect any and all drills and grinders, BUT, now the water filters will each break over time, and more often than the working machines!
- You can fish or farm as well now (since I last played), but they're both going to have a lot of manual one by one interactions
- You can't even buy a watering can for farming until you've proven yourself you can grow a plant and feed someone tomato soup.

I feel if you want to play this game like a sane person, and try to do it like a factory game, you're playing it for the wrong reason, as every other well known factory game does a way better of job of this. This is painful, but if [I]Hydroneer[/I] intends to continue in the spirit it's shown me so far, it's a no. Having just rage quit, I don't intend to put any more of my afternoon into it.

This is a game so overtly designed to be as fussy and needlessly slow as possible to stretch out its playtime and it is far too slow to get even remotely going. 

This in itself would not be so bad were it not for the fact that the interface and physics add yet more to the already-frustrating slowness of the gameplay loop - one which becomes tedious rapidly.

That loop seems simple enough: dig four loads of earth... except for no discernible reason these need to first go via a bucket before being put in a pan. This pan then needs submerging in water. Cue furiously scrabbling round after it as it invariably ricochets off the riverbed. Pan wrangled, it's time to brush the dirt out for some meagre nuggets, assuming you can get it to drop on its backside as any real-world pan full of dirt and water would? This one? Upside down, obviously.

The fun doesn't end there. Despite there being both target and drop reticles, these feel oddly imprecise. I was stunned to learn the game [I]wasn't[/I] designed for VR, because it sure as hell feels like it (in all the wrong ways). 

Wait till I tell you that there's no inventory and you can only ever hold one item at a time - of [I]anything[/I]. Lucky enough to not fall asleep with boredom after digging up, panning and filtering twenty nuggets? Enjoy loading them one at a time into your smelter. Sorry, into the crucible that you then have to put into your smelter, because this game likes extra steps. You could try putting them all in a pan and upending it, but half off them will just ding off the sides and bounce off the ground in all directions.

Even as you start to unlock the next gameplay elements of crafting, this is again ridiculously fussy, with conditions needing to be just so and actually against the clock. Even better, when trying to fish ingots out of your furnace, the button for picking them up and [I]picking up the whole damn furnace[/I] is the same.

Have a guess what I spent about 75% of my time doing while trying to aim at a glowing hot ingot in the middle of a similarly-coloured blizzard of particle effects.

This game teases so much promise so early but is absolutely ruined by its poor interface, infuriating physics and deliberately slowed pace. You want to be able to come in of an evening, spend an hour or so getting a gameplay loop going and then get on with your life. This game takes 3 hours to get even remotely started.

There are several interesting mechanics in this game. The game is polished, it's enjoyable for some time, but there is a problem with late game content. What is exactly doesn't feel right:
1. No rewarding end game goals.
2. No way to seamlessly migrate from your factory on the starting field to the extended one.
Because of these 2 factors together, you don't have a strong motivation to leave your starting land plot to build something big on another plot.

To elaborate (1). What might be a reason for you to build a big factory? More resources, more money - but what you will buy with these resources? To clear quests? It doesn't feel rewarding. To create expensive items? For what? Could building a huge factory be a goal by itself? Might be, but not for anyone.

About (2). You have to deliver every part from the shop to your land plot. Even with wooden pallets, it's a lot of manual labor and feels too grindy. There is a problem with game flow, when you deliver many parts to your plot to understand that you forgot something and you have to return to the shop. Also, imagine placing 100 pipes on a pallet one by one, and it is only one part type.

1 could be fixed by introducing well designed end game goals. For example, some meta-game might be introduced, so you can produce items on a larger scale to make a difference for a whole kingdom.
2nd could be fixed by introducing part orders, when you just write a number how many parts of this type do you need, and they are delivered to the desired plot, for some extra money maybe.

As said earlier, the game still enjoyable to some extent, but because of these 2 factors, I feel that it misses some of its potential.

Примечание к обзору по поводу патча:
Наконец-то можно нормально закупаться, ведь предметы физически влезают в телегу, и игра не проседает буквально до 1 фпс, когда загружаешь кучу предметов в грузовик и начинаешь ехать;
Вроде как не придётся корячиться как одержимый, чтобы разместить предмет стройки.

То есть перед выходом длс разрабы решили игру сделать просто играбельной, а на релизе - нет. Вот и думайте, надо ли оно вам.

Я оценил достоинства игры, но "опухоль раннего доступа" убивает моё желание продолжать игру по следующим причинам:
1) Производительность. Забудьте про мегазаводы, ибо они буквально не оставят следа от вашего фпс, как и попытка перевезти хотя бы сотню конвейеров от магазина до базы, т.к. игра, судя по производительности в статике, пытается рассчитать для них отключенную физику, как только они приводятся в движение телегой или грузовиком.
2) Постоянная беготня туда-сюда, т.к. всё необходимое продаётся где-то там, будь добр, под каждую деталь отдельную телегу заведи, чтобы эти десятки деталей одного типа сложить друг в друга в магазине, затем в кузов грузовика телегу, и не забудь про производительность. Если 3 вида труб штук по 30 ещё можно перевезти с падением фпс, то конвейеры придётся везти исключительно штук по 30 только одного вида, иначе игра станет буквально неиграбельной, выдавая по 1 фпс раз в 5 секунд. А теперь прикинь, сколько ходок туда-обратно тебе понадобится для твоего мегазавода.
3) Моды. У них до установки нет превью, а в придачу скудное описание нечитабельным шрифтом.
4) Убогая система строительства. Во-первых, объекты не привязываются друг к другу, а только к пространству, из-за чего для их установки буквально приходится искать какие-то упоротые ракурсы. Во-вторых, неинтуитивное вращение объекта по трём осям кнопками. В-третьих, никакой масштабируемости - каждая деталь устанавливается по отдельности, никаких тебе чертежей и строительства в ряд, что в совокупности даже строительство простейшего механизма или объекта декора затягивает на долгие нудные часы. Столь же неудобен и демонтаж каждой детали по одной с последующим складыванием каждой в свою телегу.
5) Расположение входа/выхода на ряде построек, а также отсутствие востребованных разновидностей форм труб и логических кабелей, делает схемы местами сложнее и больше.
6) Странное управление - объекты при отпускании сбрасываются не по центру экрана, телега поворачивается крайне медленно.
7) Неудобная закупка. Нужно тебе 10 деталей - берёшь 10 раз по одной, медленно и точно перемещаешь каждую в телегу, которая по ширине уже большинства деталей, так что те из неё вываливаются, если их складывать неаккуратно. Нужно 100 - повторяешь этот процесс 100 раз. Неописуемое удовольствие.
8) Прогрессия. Её практически нет. В игре контента на одно строительство простой добывающей базы. Дальше только неинтересное повторение того же самого в совокупности с крайне неудобным строительством и закупкой.
9) Производство и экономика. I've recently picked up this game again, after letting it rest for a long time. I bought the game the day after it released for around 7 euro's. It was a fun game but buggy. I remember losing nuggets and tools through the world floor, items being so bouncy with collision issues that they got catapulted out of the world, never to be found again and more.
The common bugs I found are gone now. The free updates and a dedicated dev team made sure of that. Could there still be bugs? Sure, every game has them. Even AAA games, which have usually more bugs and glitches than indie games.

This game is a really fun game that you can pick up when you feel like it. Casual mining, exploring a world, getting money to improve your setup and build your house or whatever you want. It is a sandbox mining game. 
If you dislike grinding, it is probably not the game for you. So think before you buy. Watch some gameplay video's and read up on the game. I dislike grinding in a lot of games but this one is just fun.

review:
Was soll ich sagen? Als erstes: ich habe nichts gegen DLC's. Aber für ein sich immer noch änderndes Spiel.. für ein halbfertiges Spiel, ein DLC dazukaufen? Ernsthaft?? Was soll das? Ich verweise mal frech auf Valheim, in dem ich schon über 1400h verbracht habe. Ohne das ich dort für irgendetwas zusätzlich zahlen mußte. In Hydroneer habe ich inzwischen 212h verbracht und lange darauf gewartet das das Spiel mehr Überarbeitung und Inhalte bekommt. Das jetzt ein DLC zum bezahlen kommt, das 6x größer ist als Hydroneer und das Hydroneer 
mal so einfach in "Basis Spiel" umbenannt wird, empfinde ich als Schlag ins Gesicht. Sämtlicher Fokus der Devs lag in den letzten Monaten nur auf dem anstehenden DLC. Die paar Änderungen für das "Basis Spiel" waren/sind wohl nötig, damit das DLC läuft. Aber eigentlich liest und hört sich das DLC wie ein eigenständiges Spiel an und nicht wie ein DLC. Man bedenke das man ja keine Items vom "Basis Spiel" ins neue DLC mitnehmen kann. Warum? Ganz einfach, sie haben die typische MMO Variante des RNG übernommen. Ja, wir craften jetzt Items mit zufälligen Stats. Die mal Gut und mal Schlecht sind. Im Großem und Ganzen könnten sie das DLC nun zu Hydroneer machen und das "Basis Spiel" als kleines DLC umändern und Neukäufer würden nichts bemerken.

MEIN FAZIT: 
EA Spiele werde ich weiterhin meiden (ja Max auch du hast nun dein Teil dazu beigetragen), 
mein Vertrauen in Foulball Hangover ist angeknackst und ich werde die Weiterentwicklung von Hydroneer erstmal nur verfolgen und nichts Weiteres kaufen.

______________________________________________________________

What can I say? First of all: I have nothing against DLC's. But for a game that is still changing... 
for a half-finished game, buying DLC? Seriously? What's the point? I'll cheekily refer you to Valheim, in which I have already spent over 1400 hours. Without having to pay extra for anything there. I've now spent 212 hours in Hydroneer and waited a long time for the game to get more rework and content. That now a DLC comes to pay that is 6x bigger than Hydroneer and that Hydroneer is simply renamed "base game" is a slap in the face. The entire focus of the devs  over the last few months has been on the upcoming DLC. The few changes for the "base game" were/are  probably necessary for the DLC to run. But the DLC actually reads 
and sounds like a stand-alone game and not like a DLC. Remember that you can't take any items from the "base game" into the new DLC. Why is that? Quite simply, they have adopted the typical MMO variant of the RNG. Yes, we now craft items with randomised stats. Which are sometimes good and sometimes bad. On the whole, they could now turn the DLC into Hydroneer and change the "base game" to a small DLC and new buyers wouldn't notice.

MY CONCLUSION: 
I will continue to avoid EA games (yes Max you have now done your bit too), 
my trust in Foulball Hangover has been shaken, and I will only follow the further development of Hydroneer for the time being and not buy anything else.

I enjoy this game in small spans. I would say any time I feel the desire to play, I do so for maybe 1-2 hours for about a week before I get bored. This game's 'progression' is a bit shallow where it really only offer's the same options for production, but 'faster'. At some point they did add some interesting new items and features, but those are more for 'fun' than they are for expanding the options you have.

My biggest gripe is that this game would be SOOOOOO much better with good multiplayer (I'll explain more in a bit), as this would take away from the weird, awkward loneliness that creeps up as you repetitively do the same thing, as well as make it more interesting with the couple plots of purchasable land. This is probably the biggest miss that keeps me from booting the game back up.

For anyone looking at this game seeing the [Shared/Split Screen Co-op] tag, this game does not have traditional multiplayer. It has local split screen co-op only. You may ask then how you are meant to play with your friends online. Well, the developers rely on Steams 'Share Play' feature. For those who don't know how this works, essentially one of you is actually playing the game on your computer, and another is invited to play the game through a sort of 'shared screen' format. You will see both of your screens, like back when we played the campaign in Halo. You will have to annoyingly configure control setup, meaning if you both with to play Keyboard and Mouse, one of you will need to change all of your keybinds, or you will both be controlling the same character (This means the 'best' way is for one controller player, and one KBM player). And then there is the latency issue. If both players have good internet, aren't too far from one another, and the host has consistent upload speeds, then this is not an issue. However, in almost every case I've experienced where I have tried this with a friend, the connection and lag is too much to enjoy the game.

TLDR:
The game is 'fun'. Technically speaking the gameplay has enough content to warrant it's price point. Personally, I cannot recommend a logistics, sandbox game that does not have complex logistics and/or good multiplayer.

This game is a lot of faffing about for not a lot of progress.

Start of the game has you manually panning for resources for about an hour or two. Alright, a slow start, whatever. Then you get your first automation and you start to set things up and you are earning some decent coin, but you start running into the faffing problems.

You can only carry one item at a time. The game is all about placing pipes, conveyor belts, foundations, etc. A basic sorting build is about 20 items. You have to manually pick them up at a store, load them onto your car one by one, then unload them and place them at the correct space. In something with similar amount of leaning on realism and pipework, that would've been 5 minutes of work. In this, it's a half an hour job. And that's the simplest most basic setup for automation.

Want to move to a new plot and build something bigger? Hope you have hours saved up because you will be manually placing one foundation at a time. Want to dig some nice looking mine with straight walls and floors? Nope, you mine in round-ish clumps, you are basically sculpting with an ice cream scoop. Good thing foundations and wall can cover everything up oh wait that's an hour to just cover up your mess...

Want to do some cool crafting with all the ores you've picked up? Great, you can make a dagger out of the iron, and if you're feeling fancy you'll spit that one bar into two and make an axe. If you are pro, you will split it into three parts and make a sword! It's not much harder, you're not using extra resources, and the result yields you more money so why isn't that some kind of default...

Oh, and hope you don't miss-click and dump a bucket of ore on the floor instead of going into a furnace. If you don't have a magnet wand to pick things up you will spend some good time fixing your mistake one nugget at a time...

All in all, I want to like this game, and it's come a long way since I originally bought it when ti first released (by giving you more convenient access to basic automation soon after the game starts). But we need some kind of inventory system to lower the tedium.

I put about 18 hours into Hydroneer and had a genuinely good time with it.

The early and mid game are satisfying in the best “factory brain” way: you go from manual mucking around to a real automated pipeline, and it feels great when the whole chain finally clicks. I ended up with auto-drilling/auto-mining, centralized filtration for easy maintenance, automated sorting for iron and gold, gem polishing, and a clean output flow into a cart for quick selling. Watching that system run smoothly is exactly the kind of payoff I wanted.

That said, once the automation loop is stable, Hydroneer becomes much more self-directed. If you love building bigger and prettier factories just because you can, there’s plenty to tinker with. But compared to Satisfactory or Factorio, it didn’t give me the same clear “big end goal” to build toward, so I don’t feel the urge to sink hundreds of hours into it.

Overall it is a fun, satisfying automation sandbox with a great sense of progression to your first “real” factory. I’m glad I played it, and I’ll happily recommend it to anyone who wants a lighter, more relaxed factory builder, even if it didn’t hook me long-term the way the genre’s heavy hitters do.

Fun in theory, but there are too many design decisions that make it incredibly frustrating in practice. For example:
-You have a cursor, but it doesn't correlate to where you're placing objects; for *that,* you have to refer to your *second* cursor, which is actually a shadow effect and is therefore really hard to see on certain surfaces.
-Your machines break down. A lot. This doesn't add anything fun, it just means you have to buy a single-use(!) wrench and click at them sometimes. It's a time tax, in a genre whose whole appeal is making assembly lines and letting them run without intervention from you.
-In the early game you'll be panning for ores manually. The pan can hold several shovel loads of dirt--but only if you put that dirt in the bucket first and empty the bucket into the pan. If you try to fill the pan with your shovel directly? Then it only holds a single scoop of dirt. *Why.*
-You can only carry one item at a time. So for example, if you want to do some fishing, you can't carry your fishing rod and bucket at the same time; hope you enjoy loading everything you own onto a slow-moving wheelbarrow or vehicle, because that's what you'll be doing in situations like this.
-Likewise, your various currencies exist as objects in the world instead of just being tied to your character. So if you want to run to town and buy a single item, well, hope you brought your vehicle with you, otherwise you'll be leaving your cash at whatever store you were shopping at. And if you end up with multiple piles of coins and want to combine them, you can't do that while the coins are in a cart or pan or whatever; you have to drop the piles on the ground--good luck aiming with that wonky shadow-cursor by the way--and then pick them back up.

On that note, the thing that finally made me give up on this game for now: when items are added to a container, like a vehicle or pan or whatever, they cease being physics objects. There are good reasons for this, it makes hauling large loads of items easier, and I imagine it helps performance a ton. However, it also creates situations like the coin-stacking bit mentioned above--and more frustratingly, it makes using crucibles an absolute pain in the backside. If you accidentally add ores to a crucible when it's not *quite* hot enough, does it auto-melt the nuggets when it gets to the right temperature? Of course not, the nuggets aren't in the physics anymore, so they just sit there in the crucible like they would in a pan. But unlike in a pan, you can't tip the crucible over and empty them out; the only thing you can pour out of a crucible is liquified metal. So if you accidentally drop a whole pan full of nuggets in a crucible that's not at the melting point yet, you now have to pick each of them out one by one and drop them back in the crucible. And because of the "your cursor matters for picking things up but not for putting them down" design decision, you have to point at a single nugget, pick it up, then turn like forty-five degrees to the left to drop it into the crucible. Over and over again, potentially dozens of times.

And yeah, sure, you could use a magnet on a stick to pick up all the nuggets at once instead, but that's slow and tedious, not particularly accurate since, again, the actual pile of stuff isn't where your cursor is, and more to the point: instead of using a wonky in-game item to circumvent a frustrating design choice, the frustrating design choice just shouldn't be in the game to begin with.

This is not the fun kind of jank, this is just refusing to take cues from the last thirty years' worth of video games. This game is updated pretty regularly, so maybe some of these frustrating choices will be ironed out eventually and I will probably reinstall in a year to see what's changed, but I really doubt they're going do anything as major as adding an inventory system or changing how cursors work at this stage in development.

I actually like the game itself; the gameplay loop and progression seems quite balanced, it's relaxing game for people who likes mining and increasing production, without any stressing elements or threats.

I can't recommend it though, because the pain points are just too many and way too severe.

* Tutorial is helpful, but not enough. There is not any description anywhere on how things work, so you will be spending a lot of time searching internet for answers, and stumble across spoilers.

* While trying to figure out the game, my computer crashes three times. It have never crashed once since I bought it. It's a gaming desktop computer, the type that launches all new triple AAA on high quality, never have to check system requirements. Casing is hot enough to fry eggs. Reduce video settings twice to see if it helps, it still crashes. Removed side panel, running with open casing, and that's the only way the game will run for me. What are you doing with the GPU??? It's an RTX 3080, should be more than enough...

* Gameplay is far from polished and non-fun elements are shoved in your face. You spend more time on these non-fun elements than on any game progression. For example, there is no inventory. You can only carry one item at a time, forcing you to drag a wagon around everywhere. Pulling the wagon reduces your speed, so you will often opt to still run with one item to semi-close locations instead of taking the wagon/vehicle... just to realize to grabbed the wrong thing by mistake, or any other arbitrary reason forces you to run back and forth again to change items. "Should have just walked slowly with the whole wagon instead". The "immersion" with this design choice is far, far, far, from making up for the non-fun pain that it adds.

* You actually do get a vehicle that you can drive with to locations further away. All fun and convenient until you run out of water the first time (it uses water as fuel), and you realize that the only way for you to refuel it is to WALK all the way back to your base, pick up a bucket, then WALK all the way back to the vehicle again, misclick when pouring the water so you have to WALK to the closest river you can find and fill up the bucket again.

* You could actually just buy a bucket in the closest (still not close) village instead of running all the way back to the base, buckets are cheap. Oh, forgot that there's no inventory and your coins are also back at your base...

* Other than that, driving the vehicle is smooth, other than OH, THE ONLY AVAILABLE MAP IS A SEPARATE IN-GAME ITEM. At least I thought of bringing the map with me. Lucky me, the navigation is now as simple as PARKING YOUR VEHICLE, GET OUT OF THE VEHICLE AND GO TO THE TRUNK, LOOK AT THE MAP, TRY TO REMEMBER THE TURNS, PUT THE MAP BACK IN THE TRUNK, ENTER THE VEHICLE, DRIVE AGAIN. Next crossroad you see a tower, "wonder what that is", LET'S CHECK THE MAP... OH GOD WHY

* All quests I found wanted items of particular weight. Only problem is that there is no scale anywhere, or so it seems. Visiting all villages and all stores, nothing (also get to experience vehicle running out of water far from home, yay), gave up and searched on internet if there is any scale anywhere. Turns out that there is only one store in one particular village (not really walking distance from starting base) that has a scale to sell. All this pain just to figure out how to complete a quest.

* Finally, got the items of correct weight to complete quests. Only problem is that quest givers don't accept the items I bring. Tried four quests with different items in different locations, none worked. Then realized that the scale that I bought had snapped below ground, with the weight display not visible. I was watching the price display, interpreting that as weight. Nice to spend hours trying to figure that out.

* Finally got my drill in place, starting to produce enough materials to craft some more advanced items on the anvil. PAIN. Sometimes works, sometimes not, never know why. Seems I need to put the bars exactly right? Seems like I need to be faster so that the bars are still hot? Seems like some combinations of materials doesn't work? Seems like there is some minimum size of bars? I don't know, there is no feedback, no message, nothing. It just doesn't work and never tell my why. Repeat enough times and it does work. Clueless.

* FINE, I'll just craft simple items that do work on the first try so that I can farm some money for a harvester and extra drill, let me get some production going. Moving back and forth, getting into the flow. Umm... feeling dizzy.... want to puke... am I motion sick? Looking it up online again, apparently there are many reports on motion sickness with this game. Last straw.



I'm five hours into the game, experience is nothing but pain, even though I think the game is fun in the moments that I actually get to play it. It's just that there is pain everywhere and if I am to struggle through the pain to get to the good parts, then I want to do it without motion sickness on top of it all. Plus I am a bit afraid that it will fry my GPU.

It was lovely, but the new updates really screwed it. It's a lot more complicated, and not in a fun puzzle type complicated way, more of a annoying complicated. If you buy it (which i recommend you do), go to properties, then betas, and select the 1.7 option, it's the most updated update prior to 2.0. The older versions are a touch buggier and have less QoL but it's worth it as the new updates make it less of a sandbox. Having to make machines is really tedious and annoying, and it takes away from the beauty of simply throwing things together and hoping you make more money than you lose. I really wish they add a classic mode that combines the style of the game prior to 2.0 and the bug fixes and QoL that the new updates have. Nonetheless it is a fun game before 2.0, and i can not recommend it more, but a game about goofy machines and mining doesnt really need all the fancy bells and whistles of farming and quests. Also in the process of the 2.0 update they really got rid of a lot of features, i mean the gem compactor is gone, replaced with a logic gem press that requires logic and only compresses cut gems which makes the gem compression process more tedious. In short, I would really appreciate a gamemode combining the game before 2.0 and QoL after 2.0, but because you can revert updates it is a really good game that i love with all my heart, i recommend it to anyone who loves simulation games, sandbox games, and stuff like that.

I really enjoy this game, but I will note a few glaring issues in it's current state. Not accounting for bugs which like all new games, will be removed over time. 

The thing this game lacks, is the WOW factor that keeps you coming back. to clarify, there are things to do, but little reason to do them, once you have an initial set-up the game becomes a money printing machine where your only progression is in the time taken to achieve those things.

The progression in the beginning is quite slow and the manual process gets very tedious very quickly. on the other hand however, once you get fully automated the game again becomes fairly tedious so there is only that bit in the middle where you are "improving" your factory that really feels engaging and fun.

The world is big but not too big so you get a range of locations to explore and exploit but you seem to spend an unnecessary amount of time ferrying things to and from your factory which makes the game feel even more tedious.

Not a game breaker for many here but the multiplayer being locked to local only seems weird, any game involving construction is asking to be shared with others, we all want to show our build to someone, so open it up to true online multiplayer functionality to get that experience.

What the game needs, IMO, is purpose. It needs a reason to buy an additional plot of land, such as locally specific resources, a reason to improve the factory, more than just desire, like time constraints on some of the construction requests. a tangible and Incorporated progression system, currently there are three guilds with independent currency which seems disjointed, maybe use a simple reputation system to lock items for progression but segregated commerce doesn't feel like the way it should work. finally, a reason to want to play, after only nearly 50 hours of in game time, i started to run out of things to do, this shouldn't be something gimmicky like another faction with independent coins but something progressive.
this game seems to be an interesting blend of factory and farming sim but in my honest opinion, it needs to decide on what it's long term aim is going to be. 

it is for the reasons above that i cannot with honesty leave a thumbs up, I would not in my experience value this game at the amount it is currently priced at (£12.79 GBP) although it is a fun game, there simply isn't enough to keep me coming back right now, but i hope that this will change with future updates.

特に、スープを届けた際の器の回収とトークンの回収を別々で行う必要がある所など、不必要なストレス箇所が多めです。（器をぶん投げて返してくる所と、食べ物以外のクエストでも食べ物を食べた時の感想を言う仕様？もイライラ）

This game is almost good. It has a fun build mechanic and requirements making factory building fun. But it suffers hard in 3 major areas:

1. When you leave your dig site and come back, there's a 90% chance your machine got clogged up somehow. It appears to happen consistently when using sorters, but other machines suffer from it as well. It's not something you can build around, as it's simply "a sorter has a 5% chance to not process the material and leave it in the way". When this happens to 5 minerals, suddenly nothing is processed. 
2. They slow you down via quests, which give you unique currency instead of money. While this can be a good approach to extend the life of the game, picking up and turning in the quests is miserably slow. When you see a quest that's not worth your time, too bad. It's permanent until you complete it.
3. The biggest limiting factor is how your character can only pick up 1 thing at a time and do 1 thing at a time. Imagine Factorio, where you had to craft all your conveyor belts at 1 location, and then run them over one by one to place them. A pallet helps minimally. This can be fun to start but please make some sort of "butler" robot that you can request things to be built and it'll build them. It can cost 1 million dollars. Or 10 million. But something to strive for to ease the manual suffering.

某Gold Rushによく似たシステムで砂から金属のナゲットを集めて、インゴットや商品を作って売って稼ぐゲームです。

某ゲームと違って砂金から簡単にインゴットまで作れるし、商品となるアクセサリーや剣をインゴットの簡単な組み合わせで作れるので直感的で楽しく、単純なシステムなのに奥深さがあります。

採掘場は地形を変更できるため高低差のある自分だけの採掘現場を作ることができます。

チュートリアルで砂金の取り方など教えてくれるので進め方で悩むことはないです。

ゲーム内の店には自動採掘機やベルトコンベア、炉がありますので、インゴット作成までの工程を自動化できます。
最終的には工場ライン作りに没頭することができるでしょう。
回路パーツがあるため、簡単な回路を作って自動的に修理や仕分けを行わせることもできます。

別ルートで農業要素まで用意されており、コンバインや種植機などで大規模農業を楽しむことができる。

バグについては改善されたのか、自分がプレイしてる最中は特に発生しませんでした。
ゲームの重さについては超巨大な自動化ラインは作っていませんが重くはなりませんでした。

バグも治ったし、分かりやすいシステムや自動化ラインも手軽に作れて非常に面白いのでお勧めです！

と言いたいところだったが、、、、

次に紹介する欠点のでせいで良い所のすべてを台無しにしている。

　　このゲームには【インベントリ】がない・・・

　　【インベントリ】が無い！

　　もう１度言う【インベントリ】が無い！！！

プレイヤーのインベントリが無いせいで自動化ラインを改良する時に外したパイプや、ベルトコンベアなどの大量のアイテムに採掘場が埋め尽くされるのである。

採掘は地下深くにするほど良い金属が産出されるので、狭いところに作ったラインを解体し、荷物を大量にぶちまけて自分が埋もれない様に気を付けながら、地上まで部品を搬出する方法まで編み出す羽目になるのである。

初期地点の自動化でもインゴット４種類作ろうと思ったら結構大きなラインになり、使用されるパーツもどんなに効率的にしてもかなりの数になる。
また、パイプ部品にはTierがあるので上位Tierに交換すると下位のパイプは倉庫のこやしになるのだが、アイテムボックス等は無いので捨てるための倉庫も物理的に用意する必要がある。

この作業に大半のプレイ時間が割かれるのである。ふざけてんの！？

また、アイテムは基本的にお金で購入するのだが、買い出しする際も店から採掘場までアイテムを物理的に運ばねばならない。
幸い最初からトラック１台を支給されており、複数のアイテムを同時に運べるパレットを購入できるので少しは楽になると思うだろうがそうはいかない。
パレットに載るのは精々アイテムが１０個位までだし、トラックもパレット１個分だけの荷台しかないのだ。
（一応パレット同士は重ねられるので無限に荷物を運べるが、置く前にアイテム同士は重なってはいけないので絶妙な調整を毎回しないといけない）

おまけに道路は狭くてやたら勾配がきつく、採掘場から店までウネウネと回り道させられるのでストレスが半端ない。

自動ラインを作るには大量のパーツを買って運搬を繰り返すことになり、強烈な虚無感に苛まれる。

review: This game made me hit the sturdy
mining.

Shovel dirt into bucket. Dump bucket into pan. Put water in pan. Scrub dirt. Shovel dirt into bucket. Dump bucket into pan. Put water in pan. Scrub dirt. Shovel dirt into bucket. Dump bucket into pan. Put water in pan. Scrub dirt. 

It's a super fun, light hearted, mining/automation game. The beginning stages, while slow going, are relaxing. Later stages with automation and sorting systems are equally as satisfying. This game is as simple or as complex as you want it to be. I personally have enjoyed doing both the early game numerous times, and giant automated mining complexes multiple times. 

Updates are also done fairly often for this game and have been pretty meaningful over the period that this game has been available. A lot of quality of life improvements, performance improvements, and gameplay changes since I first started in early access. 

If you like slower paced automation games I would recommend.

Honestly, This isn't usually the type of game I play. It isn't dynamic, there's no survival aspect, nothing that adds a sense of urgency to the game. It's well and truly a sandbox game. However, that's not to say that the game lacks anything in any of those departments. There's a sense of realism, albeit not entirely, that Makes the game somewhat charming. There's no fast way to do anything, which I think is wonderful. You're forced to take things slow and be methodical about the processes you use, whether it be manually mining ores and gems to clean and refine, or creating massive foundries to automate the work for you. The lack of an inventory adds to the realism, making it so you can't just load yourself down with countless materials and machinery, expediting a process that doesn't really have an end goal. In short, if you have the patience to just relax and allow yourself to be carried by the pace the game sets for you, this is a wonderfully perfect game to wind down with and just chill for a few hours. Enjoy the greater feeling of accomplishment when you accomplish something, no matter how long it took, and remember that there is nothing pressing in this game. Have fun, wind down, and enjoy.

review: really good and fun game  10/10

Having played Hydroneer for more than 80 hours, I can give a solid opinion on the game. I've played probably every factory-style game there is extensively over the last 20 years.

Positives:

-Nice graphics and a good color palette.
- Runs well if you stick to basic mining setups.
- Can be fun to begin with building your mining and drilling operation.
- The open world is pleasant, not too big, not too small.
-Good for people who just like to build stuff and see how it works, a sandbox for messing around with no necessary aim, just to build better systems and bases. Those who don't care for the story or any meaningful objectives.
-Better with mods; if you're into modding, then you will be happy to know these improve the base game significantly.

Negatives:

- No inventory; you have to pick up and drag everything around one by one like real life. But unlike real-life backpacks and logical ways to carry tools don't exist for some bizarre reason. You have a useless cart and a tractor that are difficult to load items onto; that's it. This becomes a serious pain in the butt and is a great example of why an inventory is revolutionary to video games. This game mechanic means everything takes 50% longer than it really should, a nice cheap way to inflate the gameplay time. Lugging large drills and machinery around from one corner of the map to the next is just awful.
- Grinding repetitive gameplay.
-Picking up and dropping items is very poor, you have a poor marker displayed where things will land. No logical way to just place an item down gently, all items are thrown like you are controlling an angry Neanderthal man. 
-No proper map or UI; the in-game map is a ridiculous joke.
-Severe lag when you get to mid-game; the game limits what you can build as it cannot handle a few items on conveyor belts without having a nervous breakdown. This makes the game ultimately pointless if you are restricted to small builds but lots of plots and lands to build on that cannot be used.
-No real objectives or goals in the game; your job is just to build and mine and have stacks of money you can't buy anything useful with. You have tasks from citizens to build daggers, swords, or cook foods, etc., that are basic and repetitive, and that's about it; no story, no competition from other miners. Nothing!
-There are only 6 resources: Iron, Gold, cloutmium, corestone, shards, and gen stones. No option to make or manufacture other ore or metals; that's all you get, which is a very small amount compared to other factory games and gets boring fast.
-The playable character seems to find it impossible to put items down, and you have to do a little jump and then press the drop button before he is willing to let go; he constantly makes an 'umm, umm umm' noise to tell you he cannot understand how to let go of an item. This gets very annoying after a while. Perhaps having a playable character that has an IQ below 40 isn't advisable!
-The need to use pipes everywhere becomes a chore; I know it's the base of the game being 'hydroneer,' but it feels unnecessary that every part needs a pipe running through it.
-Limited machines and variety; you have a drill, pipes, grinder, and conveyor belts. You have three tiers of these items, which are a chore to reach.
- The item snapping is very poor; the game should automatically detect which way to place something, but you have to manually rotate each and every piece.
-'Logic,' which was added in later updates, isn't particularly necessary, and you only need to use a fraction of it.
- Poor tools; no proper terraforming options. The pickaxe and shovel, etc., are just awful to use and take huge amounts of time to dig. You can't select terraforming sizes or anything; a huge negative.
- Vehicles are useless; awful controls and diggers and terrain levelling vehicles are frustrating and a waste of time.
- No true automation; things break and need repairing no matter what, even when using logic auto fixers, which need restocking with tool bags (which is a huge pain).
-Farming that has been added to the game is interesting but really just the same as mining and just as irritating.

All in all, I would rate this game a 5.5 out of 10. Mildly interesting, but gameplay gets boring, the mechanics are frustrating, and it has a lot of bugs and lag that ultimately make the game unplayable after mid-game. Probably the worst factory-style game I've played in several years.

Rating: ★★★★☆

"Hydroneer" is a delightful sandbox simulation game that allows players to dive headfirst into the world of small-scale mining and entrepreneurial ventures. Developed and published by Foulball Hangover, this game offers a unique and relaxing experience that lets you build your mining empire from the ground up.

The premise of "Hydroneer" is relatively simple: you start with a small patch of land, a few basic tools, and a dream of striking it rich in the world of mining. The game's open-world sandbox environment provides you with the freedom to dig, mine, and explore to your heart's content. As you gather resources like gold, gems, and precious metals, you can refine them and turn a profit to expand your operations.

One of the game's most notable features is its impressive physics system, which adds a layer of realism to your mining endeavors. Using various tools and machinery, you can dig, excavate, and transport materials in a way that feels satisfyingly tactile. The sense of progression in "Hydroneer" is incredibly rewarding, as you gradually upgrade your equipment and expand your operations to tackle more challenging mining sites.

The game's visual style is charming, with a bright and colorful aesthetic that contrasts nicely with the gritty world of mining. The world is filled with interesting locations to explore, from picturesque valleys to underground caves. The day-night cycle and weather effects also add to the immersion, making each mining expedition feel unique.

While "Hydroneer" offers a relaxing and enjoyable experience, it's not without its challenges. Managing resources and optimizing your mining process can be complex, and the game doesn't hold your hand. It encourages experimentation and learning from your mistakes, which can be both rewarding and frustrating at times.

Multiplayer mode is another highlight of "Hydroneer." Playing with friends can turn mining into a cooperative and enjoyable experience, as you work together to tackle larger mining operations and share the rewards.

In summary, "Hydroneer" is a hidden gem in the world of sandbox simulation games. It offers a refreshing take on the mining genre, combining a relaxing atmosphere with satisfying gameplay mechanics. While it can be a bit daunting for newcomers, the sense of accomplishment and the joy of building your mining empire make it a worthwhile investment of your time. If you have a penchant for entrepreneurship and don't mind getting your hands dirty, "Hydroneer" is well worth exploring.

I generally enjoy factory style games, but this one is very "grindy". I learned to play with a lot of trial and error, but looking back I wish I had read the guides in the Steam community section to get started. Aside from a tutorial, there isn't much help to get you started. If the beginning experience were changed, I think I could change my recommendation.

This game is really fun, but there 2 things that really stick out as a problem. As expected of a game of this type, it's a grindy resource management game that allows you to build creative, yet basic factories which at the late game allows you to fully automate and provides new tools for your mine/farm to make you're job much easier. it doesn't hold your hand and let you explore and learn how to play at your own pace however, here comes the problem, there's no real payoff to your work and while it's fun to build and try to maximize your profits, there's little to no incentives available to do so, especially with the lack of a story or other overarching challenge system. outside of just a lack of incentive, the grind is incredibly real, it provides a real problem as the controls are clunky and you have specific rules you have to follow when transporting materials, even worse you can't carry more than one item, and the physics of the game with an off-center drop marker make it challenging to progress without spending hours just getting materials in and out of buckets with each tiny piece of the ore having to be moved 1 by 1. I would not suggest the game to most people, however those who like the grind and don't need a major pay-off to enjoy themselves, then this game is still a really fun game. in the end, I will have to put a thumbs down, but I have to say, I will likely play more of it waiting for some updates or messing around with workshop items.

I give up. I've put several hours into Hydroneer but I cannot stomach investing any more time.

This is a survival / crafting / open world game. You dig, you buy + sell, you build. It's exactly the sort of game that I spend most of my time with. However, it is critically flawed: there is no inventory. You can hold just one thing at a time. The developers have provided carts + trucks that you can use to move items in bulk, but they're clumsy and slow. 

The core mechanics of the game are good, but the lack of an inventory system dooms players to wasting a non-trivial portion of their in-game time on tedious / pointless make-work exercises. I _like_ digging + building. I do not like picking up 30 pipe pieces at the store, one at a time, dropping them into a cart, and then unloading them, one at a time, at my dig site. I'm only a few hours in; I've set up a tier-1 auto-digger. I've read online that the time wasted on clumsy handling of items only increases as players progress in the game.

It's a real shame, but the 80% fun of the game is inseparable from a miserable 20% that devolves directly from the lack of an inventory system.

Thumbs down.

Title: Hydroneer - A Tranquil Sandbox Gem for Budding Prospectors

Hydroneer, developed by Foulball Hangover, is a unique and relaxing sandbox game that invites players to immerse themselves in the world of small-scale gold mining. As someone who has spent hours panning for gold and crafting intricate machinery, I'm excited to share my review of this charming indie title.

Gameplay (4.5/5):
Hydroneer's gameplay centers around the art of gold mining, offering a serene and surprisingly addictive experience. You begin as a humble prospector with basic tools like a shovel and a gold pan, but as you dig deeper into the earth and uncover the precious metal, you can expand your operations with increasingly complex machinery.

The game's progression system is well-balanced. It encourages you to start small, learning the ropes of prospecting, before gradually advancing to more efficient and automated methods. The satisfaction of discovering a valuable nugget or a rich deposit of gold is immensely rewarding.

Graphics and Sound (4/5):
Hydroneer adopts a minimalist yet visually pleasing art style. The environments are colorful and serene, with clear water bodies reflecting the surroundings beautifully. The physics-based interactions, such as digging and water flow, are well-executed and add to the immersion.

While the game's sound design is functional, the soothing music and ambient sounds contribute to the relaxing atmosphere. The gentle sound of running water and the hum of your machines create a tranquil backdrop as you work on your mining endeavors.

Crafting and Machinery (4/5):
One of Hydroneer's strengths is the crafting and machinery aspect. As you progress, you can design and build intricate contraptions using a variety of components. From water pumps and sluice boxes to conveyor belts and heavy machinery, the options for customizing your mining operation are extensive. Experimentation is encouraged, and watching your creations come to life is immensely satisfying.

The crafting system is intuitive, with a straightforward interface that allows you to assemble and disassemble components easily. The sense of creativity and problem-solving it offers is a highlight of the game.

Community and Modding (5/5):
Hydroneer benefits from an active and creative modding community. Players have developed a wide range of mods, adding new content, machinery, and even additional gameplay elements. This extends the game's longevity and provides a platform for players to share their creative mining setups.

Conclusion (4.5/5):
Hydroneer is a delightful and relaxing sandbox game that offers a unique take on the world of gold mining. Its serene atmosphere, satisfying progression, and extensive crafting possibilities make it an excellent choice for those seeking a tranquil and creatively engaging gaming experience. Whether you're a fan of simulation games or simply looking for a game to unwind with, Hydroneer shines as a gem in the world of indie gaming.
