Before 2.0 I thought this was just a janky sandbox, great for funny videos but not something I want to mess with. The newest updates changed pretty much everything as I understand it.

I've had fun with it but it feels a little shallow for a 2.0 release. There is only 1 production chain so do yourself a favor and figure out as much as you can by yourself, only get help if you are stuck. Because that 1 production chain is pretty much the entire game.

I see little reason to make mines all over the map, there is no benefit to it. It's faster and easier to make money by making an easily expandable layout and just keep adding on to it. When you figure out how to do it you have beaten the game.

Sure you can play around making cute little houses or try to figure out the terrible logic parts only to create a monstrosity and realize there is almost no benefit to it besides repairing. In the grand scheme of the game everything is priced super cheap so once you have the (semi) automation setup and figure out the mining mechanics there is no more challenge and nothing to work toward. Tier 2 mining and any future tiers will not change that much as the end game is still the same, non-existent.

It's a fine sandbox, if you are into that you will love this game, for the price it's an absolute steal. If you want another Satisfactory keep looking.

I look forward to the planned updates and see promise for a deeper experience.

Farming Update:
The farming mechanic itself is an interesting addition but it feels out of place in a game that was previously just about mining. It can be fun but it's still pretty shallow. Some of the best parts you buy with tokens are useless because by the time you can afford them you want to be done with farming (sprinklers, harvesting vehicle). The NPC's do bring some life to the previously dead world but only a tiny bit. The soup making quests are not fun at all, pure grind.

Tier 3, Prospecting, and Achievements Update:
I started a new game for this to get the full experience. In the end prospecting is completely useless. Ore veins are not useful, just building more drilling machines is way more efficient. I was able to complete all achievements (except farming tokens because the quests are bugged) using only 6 tier 1 drills and 6 tier 2 drills. TL;DR version:  
It's good fun if you like mining and fishing.  But there are no enemies, no story, no NPC's.  Has creative mode as an option, and I think multiplayer too but I haven't tried that mode.  If you hate digging and fishing, you will hate this game.  And it is a little bit glitchy sometimes but not too awful.

The version for people who like to read the encyclopedia for fun: 
Would you like to spend an hour digging a hole and panning for gold, then spend three hours fishing for profit, then spend 200 hours digging BIGGER holes, automating your mining operation with machines, pipes, and conveyor belts, and then forging weapons and jewelry for profit?  If that sounds like fun, then you will probably enjoy this game.  Most of your time will be spent in underground cavers that you dig yourself, then you have to find a way to cram all your pipes, belts, and machinery in there (either down in the hole or on the ground above).  But the longer your pipelines go, the lower the pressure gets... So it's sort of like a 3-D logistics puzzle.

There is no story in this game, it's just you alone on a small island with a few mining sites and tool shops.  There are no enemies to fight.  No secrets hidden in obscure corners of the map (except a handful of "relics" that you dig up but as far as I know they serve no purpose other than bragging rights).  Just pick up a fishing pole and catch fish, or pick up a shovel and pickaxe and do some mining.  

There is multiplayer.  But I haven't tried that mode yet.

There is a creative mode where you can steal everything from the tool shops, and you can get a magic wand that lets you clone or delete items instantly, and you can get a hat that lets you FLY at high speeds.  Or you can play in normal mode without those benefits.  Your choice.
If that does NOT sound fun to you, well then go do something else with your time.

Also, the game still has a few weird glitches.  Sometimes these produce funny results.  Sometimes they're just frustratingly annoying, or annoyingly frustrating.  But for the most part it works well as long as you don't do anything stupid ("stupid" = load 50 pieces of ore into a pan and then try to lift the pan... your graphics card will have a stroke, fps drop to zero, game will crash.  "stupid" = load too many things on one side of the truck bed, the truck will shoot into the air and start spinning out of control as it leaves the atmosphere.  LOL.  Not kidding.)

When you try to drop your shovel (which you need to do when you want to switch to the brush so you can clean the panned items) it's hit or miss whether you can actually drop it if you're underground because of space...only so many times can you hear the "nope" grunt before you annoyedly ragequit and request a refund (I think I've only ever requested a refund twice, and have 1000s of games...so that says a lot about this half-assed eye candy with little real gameplay).  The fact that you need to switch from shovel to brush 1000000000s of times and this annoying grunt happens 50% of the time, that just adds to the annoyance.

Don't get me started on the driving dynamics if you dare to use a tractor to go anywhere...(shudder)

Also don't get me started on navigation...they give you a map (that you have to carry) and you have to LEARN where the hell you are or get lost for eternity.

Coming from games like 7D2D, Satisfactory, Minecraft and the like, I saw potential in this game...sorely disappointed, though one day the sole coder may pull his head out of the sand and do away with "immersion" settings that just make games like this more boring and LESS immersive!

I did request a refund, but as I had more than 8 hours of gameplay logged they denied the request...for the record, 7 hours of that was me watching YT videos or reading websites that gave advice on what to do that usually turned out to be wholly inaccurate and left me no better off than I was before.

So no, I do NOT recommend this game...don't make my mistake, go play a game written by a competent coder rather than an Unreal Kiddie who has access to assets.

At the time of writing this (May 18, 2022), this game is in early access.  There are bugs, known and unknown, that are being worked on.  Features are still being added, removed, and modified.

That being said, this is a fun game that has a lot of potential and is fairly different from a lot of other games out there.  With all that, there's a fair amount of grind to get started and once past the early play, a lot of automation can be implemented.  With the automation, funds start coming faster, which also allows for further automation and upgrades.  There are a number of people posting vids on You Tube, so there's a lot of examples of said automation and the expandability.

[b]UPDATE June 22:[/b]
NOTE:  First off, there is an expected patch due out shortly (v2.0.6) that will fix a number of the bugs in this game, so expect that any early issues encountered may already be fixed or are expected to be fixed in this patch.

This is a fun game that is under continued and active development.  The Dev are actively involved in addressing issues that people experience and have created some MOD's that apply a "bandaid" to address critical issues that cannot be addressed faster.  It's a fun game that can get a little grind-y, but figuring out solutions is half the fun.

In this game, one starts are with a Property to mine, a map of the surrounding territory and nearby towns, and basic mining tools (a basic Shovel, a Bucket, a Pan, a Brush, and a Lantern).  The start of the game, one uses the Shovel to scoop a chunk of Dirt into a Pan, scoop water with the Bucket and pour it into the Pan, and use the Brush to clean the Dirt revealing a Nugget of Ore (Gold, Iron, Cloutium, a Shard, or an unpolished Gem of one of four types).  One then repeats this a bunch of times and can then take the resultant Nuggets to the Jeweler and sell them.  Wash, rinse, repeat a bunch of times and one can fairly quickly earn enough to start upgrading.

Initial upgrades include buying a Harvester, a basic (T1) Miner, and some Pipes (all devices are powered by water pressure delivered through Pipes).  This is the initial stage of automation.  The Miner replaces most of the actions with the Shovel, Bucket, and Pan, and the Harvester replaces the Brush activity.  This all speeds up the process but also brings complications and moves to the next level of complexity.  One can then purchase Conveyors from the next town over and start building out Mining automation to increase the rate of getting necessary Ores and eventually working up to more complex Mining automation until the process pretty much runs itself.  As one advances, there are additional mining plots that can be purchased near the adjoining towns and more powerful equipment can be built that can Mine larger chunks of Dirt that result in larger Nuggets being Harvested.

Logic automation can also be applied to ensure larger Gems are produced from the smaller Polished Gems that come of the Conveyor system, with Logic automation ensuring those larger Gems are ready to be turned into Jewelry (Rings or Necklaces) or weapons (Daggers, Swords, or Battle Axes).  This is a game that builds as it goes, but there are some fairly stiff System Requirement that need to be met for the game to even run.  Beyond that, the better the System Requirement are met or exceeded, the better the game will perform over time, as the mine develops (see NOTE at the beginning).  There are new features yet to come, opportunities within the game that will continue to be developed, and bug fixes on their way.

Look, the game idea is great. Most things work well and are well implemented. But for the love of all that is holy, if you're going to make a game with no GUI you have to optimize it so a lot of physical objects on screen or in a truck or in a bucket etc. doesn't tank the frames or cause major lag. 

I have a little under 10 hrs of game play at this point. I am no where near endgame, I don't even have a serious factory yet. So far I've experienced lag that lasted several seconds where I thought the game crashed when I dumped ore from a pan into a crucible. I had my frames hit less than 10/second because I had stuff in the back of my truck, which is the replacement for storage when moving around, since no GUI. The truck would bob up and down randomly and was extremely hard to steer. I normally run at 120fps max settings. I can only imagine how bad it gets for weaker PCs.

This game feels unfinished as it is. "2.0" just came out, implying the game is not just officially finished, but on a second more polished version. It's not. This is a Beta version.

To top it all off, there's no guidance at all. NONE. I only know what the game is even about because I watched a streamer play it and that got me more interested in it. I started knowing the basics and hit the ground running. If you have any questions there is only google. There's no in-game tutorial, or story, or progression explanation at all.

All in all, I've enjoyed the 10ish hours I've put in, it is and was enjoyable. The game needs serious work. I would not recommend this unfinished version to any but the most patient players.

Alright 1 hour in and I already have a lot to say

The Good:

-Unique concept

-Great graphics

-Constantly evolving

-Great Dev/Devs (not sure which applies) who apparently support the community very well (Great work!)

-Very relaxing to play

-Satisfactory level of details when it comes to producing a resource

Now the gripes, of which for now there are many

The Bad:

-Tedium sets in quick, the controls are not snappy enough to allow fluid switching of items or unloading of resources from buckets and such so early game is extremely tedious, it doesn't need to be dumb down, just refined 

-Weird control choices like how when unloading dirt from a bucket or dropping resources they don't drop at your feet but at a weird angle to the right of your body indicated by a small circle overlay, its near impossible to get used to

-Physics break extremely easy, they need fixing, newest patch notes say flying cars are fixed yet somehow my truck still just took to the skies and the only way to fix it floating above me was to hard reset the game as using the menu option to reset the car just relaunched it!

-Game needs a better introduction than "watch this YouTube video", when I buy a game I don't want to spend the first half hour researching how to play it online, that needs to change

-More content is needed, I am an hour in and the map already feels incredibly small, I feel like after another 3-4 hours I am going to be bored out of my mind trying to find things to do, games like satisfactory succeed because the object is more than just "make money" its to explore, thrive and survive. 

I hear the game has farming mechanics being thought about for the future, that is a perfect solution, give us a homestead where we spend our hard earned cash on crops, make it so they can fail or we can fail at managing the farm and lose money, make it tough but rewarding because this game is a gem in the rough, it is crying for more content that feeds back into its awesome economy!

Maybe let us open our own stores in the future like a bank or blacksmith, maybe even a jewellers but for that we would need npc so that a pipe dream for now!

Tldr:
Should you buy it? Yes, you will run out of content after a few hours and most likely get bored but the Devs are kind to their community and passionate, launching constant massive updates and the price they're asking for is very, very reasonable.I have no doubt this could be the next Valheim given enough time!

This game can be summarized in 2 words "Unnecessary tedium".

The game offers a whole hour of content before you experience the entirety of its gameplay loop because it all boils down to: get resources, turn them into refined materials, sell them rinse and repeat.
Now, hold on a second, if you think 1 hour is a short amount of time, that's not the best part!
It would take even less!

The reason it takes 1 hour to do the basic 5 steps this game revolves around, is because the game is so painfully riddled with unnecessary tedious operations and they go as follow:

-There is no wallet, you have to constantly juggle around with your money.
-You have no way of picking up with multiple resources at once.
-You have not hotbar so you have to juggle with EVERYTHING this game has, one thing at a time, which slows down the game to a crawl and makes everything a pain to deal with.
-Placing down items on the ground is done with a retarded side dot that is extremely unreliable.
-Machines are broken, they clog and break so oftern you have to babysit them regardless of your setup, sometimes even logic stuff stops working and makes it impossible for automation to be set up, which by the way, automation is the entirety of the "endgame", there are artifacts but are few and unrewarding.
-Building  is painful, items don't place where you want them to and often will work unreliably.
-Digging is terribly slow and flattening ground seems extremely random since you cannot set if you want to lower or raise manually the ground also extremely unreliable.
-The truck is uncontrollable and it will lag the game out if you load too much stuff on it and will also randomly fly away or behave in a weird way depending on where you placed the cargo.
-You can only buy 1 item at a time and the process is slow, tedious and just unenjoyable, pick up item, move it into the buy zone, pick them up again and load them into the truck RINSE AND REPEAT FOR EVERY SINGLE ITEM YOU HAVE TO BUY. (sometimes you can simplify this step by putting the truck directly on the buy area but not every shop has enough space to allow the truck inside)
-You cannot drop stuff on top of eachother outside of the truck, if the items or ground/wall hitboxes collide with your held item you cannot drop it, you'll hear the frustrating grunt of your cuck of a character more times than you'd like to and after 30h I really cannot hear that sound anymore.

This was a pretty rad experience, it was awesome to see some new mechanics challenging the way we traditionally interact with these sorts of games. Things like having no inventory, your mine is much smaller scale to something like Satisfactory but it's so much more personal when you had to lug every single piece from the shop, store it around your site and get it into position. The carts, pallets and vehicles where a fun way to approach an in-game inventory that wasn't just an infinite bag of holding. The world is very charming. I only wish there was more things to do, early game was a fun grind but I very quickly realised there was no real objective for me to be doing. Once money was no longer a problem I was just kinda standing there thinking... now what?
Still a worth while experience for the price and I'm happy to support the devs, I'm looking forward to seeing where the game goes!

While this game has potential, in its current state I can only describe it as frustrating.

The game starts you off with a shovel, a pan, a bucket, and a brush. You pick up the shovel, click on some dirt to dig it up, click on the pan to put the dirt in the pan. You then drop the shovel, pick up the bucket, go to the river, drop the bucket in the river, pick the bucket back up, go over to your pan, drop the water into the pan, drop the bucket, pick up the brush, and click on the pan. Congratulations you have now produced a nugget that is worth about 5C, the games currency. Repeat until you have enough value to buy something interesting.

But first you have to sell it, so you pick up your pan, walk to the jewellers, put the pan on the table, press a button, and take the coins that you are given, put them in your pan, and walk back to your base.
Overall this is not a very interesting gameplay loop, but you don’t need to do too much of it. The problem is its emblematic of every single thing you do in the game.

Once you get to about 100C you can buy a water pump and some pipes, so you no longer need to fill your bucket. To do this you need to go to the store, grab the items you want to buy individually and put them on the buy pad, put your stack of coins in the coin basket, press a button, individually take each item you bought and load it into your cart, bring the cart back to your base, and then put together your dripping pipe.

Once you get about 600C you can buy a drill which will dig up the dirt for you so all you have to do is use the brush on your pan once every second or so, and once you get another 500C you can get a machine which will convert dirt into ore automatically.

Now you are in the end game. Because all the harvesting is done automatically, money is no longer really an issue. Another 2000C will let you set up a sorting system, and another 5000C after that will allow you to automatically forge bars. At this point you will have seen everything that the game has to offer. Yes you can buy a new plot of land and make more drills/better drills to create even more wealth, but that’s really all that’s left. 

To test how much content there is, I did a bit of a speed run. It took me 10 minutes to automate water, another 20 to automate digging, and another 15 after that to automate processing. It took another 20ish minutes to move the entire system into a hole to increase drop rates, and another half an hour of just waiting to get a sorting system in place.

That’s not to say that the game is bad, there is something very satisfying about building everything up from nothing and I hope development continues. However at this point there is just not enough content, and what little there is is more frustrating then fun.

This is by far and without a shadow of a doubt the MOST frustrating game I've ever tried to play! The snapping mechanics for placing items like blocks, pipes and machines is infuriating bad. Then, for a fraction of a second, it snaps to where you want to put it but you miss the 1/1000 of a second opportunity to place the item, and then never be able to get the piece to snap there again.

Why does the sorter have to expel the resource chunks like a blunderbuss? It is easier to just sort the chunks manually.

However, the game WILL NOT let you place these items on ground that has been leveled using the rake. However, it is happy to let you place these items below ground level somehow, anywhere that hasn't been raked. 
In summary, run! Run away!...and don't look back!

This game has great potential, but some fatal flaws for me.

Shopping for factory components is incredibly tedious, especially if your base of operations isn't near a store supplying what you need. In the default starting area, the moment you need conveyor belts, you need to drive your truck with its questionable handling a good ways down lumpy dirt roads and a narrow bridge to the nearest town that sells them.

The buying process itself is a further exercise in tedium, involving grabbing each item one at a time (they don't stack), placing them on the buying platform, placing your coins in the bucket, hitting purchase, and then moving each item one at a time, including your remaining coins, into your truck. You could load a cart on and off your truck, but placing things on it is awkward and error prone.

Speaking of awkward and error prone, each usable item has two targeting reticles that appear no matter what the item is. Which one is used when you left-click to use the item? You have to memorize it for each item, because each one is different. Nothing on the screen gives you a hint, so if you forget, you just spilled all your ore from your pan onto the side of the crucible, instead of the middle. Now the ore which fell to the ground rather than into the crucible? You may have guessed it: you need to grab each one, one at a time, and place it in the crucible, simply because you forgot which reticle will be used when you dump the pan. I have done this multiple times.

The day/night cycle is a real drag. At night it's impossible to see without setting up lighting, which involves another shopping trip and all the associated ceremony. You can use a bed to skip to morning, but at least in the starting area, the ground is still quite dark for a while. Imagine you just spilled your ore and are going through the ordeal detailed above, and also it's dark out.

I know the developer has a vision for a minimalist UI with no inventory, no backpack, and not even a pocket for your currency. But I really think *some* compromise there would *vastly* improve this game. If not, why not fully commit and force the player to carry coins one at a time too, given that they're the only items that stack (sometimes, as long as you drop them on top of each other just right).

I really wanted to like it, and I considered using the F7 mod which basically gives you a creative menu to spawn in items without going to the store. But then I'd have no reason to make money selling products from my factory, which to me is the whole point of not playing in creative mode in the first place: you want some level of scarcity to direct you and provide a sense of forward progress. If I can just buy anything from the start, I could just build an optimal factory and call it done.

Je pense que c'est le second jeu Steam qui m'a fait demander une refund, le premier étant Rust, qui est une alpha d'un BR expérimental à l'accès vendu 40€. 
Hydroneer souffre du même problème. Le jeu n'est pas fini. Ce qui me pousse à faire ce refund est l'annonce d'une 2.0 sur un jeu manifestement en Alpha, et donc qu'il ne faut pas s'attendre à une refonte fondamentale du jeu. 

L'UI n'est pas mauvaise, elle est simplement absente. Je ne sais pas si c'est un choix voulu, mais c'est extrêmement difficile de s'approprier un jeu de minage sans UI; Imaginez commencer Factorio sans UI...

Les contrôles sont plus que basiques, on dirait Subnautica sur terre si vous avez dejà essayé, rien que les déplacements sont laborieux, mais alors les interactions avec l'environnement sont désespérantes (Hitboxes mal réglées, impossible de viser correctement, système de vente/achat compliqué pour pas grand chose). J'ai peut-être raté la partie fun de passer 5 minutes à déposer des bouts de terre dans un seau? 

Sauf erreur de ma part, le monde est vide de PNJ alors qu'il est sous-entendu qu'il y ait de l'activité (Bijoutier, stock exchange, etc...). Peut-être que le jeu est fait pour du multijoueur ? 

La patte graphique est a la fois un point fort et faible du jeu; Le low-poly est une tendance pour faire des graphismes a prix discount mais la direction artistique est intéressante. Ce qui rend d'autant plus frustrant l'utilisation des low-poly, car le jeu pourrait être magnifique avec de vrais efforts.

Mention honorable pour le développeur seul, dommage que le jeu n'a pas reçu autant de polish qu'Undertale ou Kenshi par exemple.

I can't play games unless the mouse is inverted.

The game (like many others) has an option to "invert the mouse movement".

Unfortunately, the invert-mouse option ONLY affects the player character (PC).  But the game also have vehicles.

The mouse is NOT inverted when in a vehicle.

That means, if you need an inverted mouse setting; in this game, you then have to become proficient at BOTH ways of using the mouse - inverted as you need it when on foot, and non-inverted when in a vehicle.

Players that don't need an inverted mouse aren't "forced" to get used to both ways - they get to have everything non-inverted.

I can't get used to non-inverted gameplay, AND I definitely cannot get used to having it both ways.

It's much worse than not using the inverted option at all.  If I could get used to non-inverted, I would. But I cannot.

The game might be wonderful. I don't know. I can't play it as it is.

So.. this review serves as a warning to others like me that need the mouse inverted - and that would find things even worse if the game forced both ways upon them.

If ever I see they have fixed that issue, I may then take another look.  Until then - off the list.

Honestly, this game is so good that it doesn't really need a positive review.
Buy it. Play it. Break your PC with it's physics engine, make a functioning computer with the logic system or just chill and build! it's tons of fun for the whole family! (going into that a bit more later).

The whole game revolves around it's extremely advanced physics engine: objects are always existent in the world, you fill buckets and pans with tons of nuggets and you can always see the individual nuggets, loading up a truck or pallet is done by [i]literally throwing[/i] it onto the truck etc.

not having an inventory in a sandbox style game is truly interesting! it's a tight rope to walk on, but hydroneers has managed to pull ti off flawlessly! even the crafting system is highly immersive and extremely fun! i could literally spend hours just crafting weapons and jewelery! (even through the controls take a bit getting used to: Q is for entering and exiting vehicles mostly, E is the main pickup / dropoff key and left click uses your items. this is a bit hard for some people to understand at first though.)

the entire logistics system and physics engine even allows for emergent gameplay! for example when i played with my friend together, we needed an unholy amount of pipes, so we went to the pipes store, and put each and every pipe manually onto the purchasing terminal, then purchased them, and then loaded it up into the wooden cart, and after a short jaunt into the truck. a truly tedious task!

well, my friend came up with the idea to put the pipes into the cart first! of course i immediately thought that it wouldn'T be possible, but he loaded up a few pipes into the cart (which is easier since once in the cart they don't have a hitbox anymore, meaning you can just spam-pickup and drop them into the cart really fast), then pulled the cart into the purchase zone and lo and behold - we could buy them and be on our merry way with them!!
we were so proud of him for figuring that out by ourselves!

a bit later i then had another idea: i held the cart and jumped onto the loading deck of the truck, and he started driving, and [i]the cart was being dragged behind like a trailer![/i] this made transporting tons of stuff infinitely easier!
and the game does not tell you stuff like this - it's up to the player to find these things out and use them!

there must be tons more hidden deep in the game's physics engine, since none of this seems hard coded!

speaking of my friend, this game (kinda) has multiplayer!
surely, it's via steam's split screen functionality, but trust me! it's not a bad thing! input lag may be a thing, but it's definitely easily manageable, and besides, it's not like this is a first person shooter where you need millisecond-reflexes. it's a calm game where you can take your time with everything.

it's also infinitely less buggy than a proper multiplayer  would be, as everything runs on the host's machine, and mods easily work aswell!

you see, with the sheer amount of physics going on, having porper internet multiplayer would either fry your router with the sheer amount of necessary information that has to be transmitted, or your game would instantly crash every other second due to desync issues, so this is truly the best way for now.

you can even play it at home with a friend or family member together, since it's split screen! so now your son / cousin / nephew / other innocent and / or (maybe) younger family member can be used as free voluntary forced labour for your gold mines!
you can even customize your avatar, a feature they didn't [i]have[/i] to add, but they did nonetheless, since the dev cares! i mean, he spent over 3 years and more than 100,000$ trying to get normal multiplayer to work, and in the end apologised profusely in a video for not being able to get it to work, so cut the guy some slack, please!

also, with version 2.0 out now, more stuff is on the way, and it shouldn't take too long for more new updates to hit! so buy it while it's still a bit cheap, learn everythign the game has to offer for now, since there's more coming in the near future!

I originally bought this game a year or so ago. I got frustrated by the controls and unconventional approach to player inventory as well as not really 'getting' what the game was supposed to be. I quickly refunded.

Then 2.0 came out. I started to see it appear in videos, and on the steam homepage, and for once I decided to do a bit more research on the game before finally deciding to give it a second chance. And I'm so glad I did. This is not the same game it was and in nearly every way this is an enormous improvement over what the game was.

This is a game that defines grind, and yet everything you do also feels incredibly rewarding because of how much planning and work goes into even the smallest accomplishments. There's nothing quite like the feeling of putting together a fully automated system and watching it run, finding the places it could be improved and making adjustments to refine your design, then sitting back and watching as all the resources pour in.

My biggest gripe right now would be that after a while money becomes a little bit pointless because of how easy it becomes to obtain. My suggestion would be to dramatically increase the prices for more advanced machinery and house building items. A few more resources to work with and unique processes would also help expand on the gameplay and encourage you to need to continue to design and build more and more complex automation (perhaps have additional resources added in each tier of dirt?).

If you're the sort of person who enjoys minecraft and other sandbox games, then definitely give this game a chance.

I love this game a lot, and it's just as I expected.

While it lacks in NPCs, the game is immersive in the sense that you actually feel like you're making a small mining operation.

Though I do have a few problems to point out. The only goal to the game is the goal you give yourself... and although that's just fine for some players, there could still be some goal set by the game. But alas, I feel a lot of games revolving around the tycoon theme usually have a rather bittersweet goal. Put simply, there is no reason why the player is making an automated mining operation other than the fact that's just what we're there for.

Despite the fact that the game has left early access, it still very much [i] is [/i] in early access. It may start off without a single glitch for any player, but it glitches more frequently as time goes on and seems to be boosted by some actions (i.e. driving, buying items, selling items (this one's infrequent), etc.). For example, I bought a bunch of conveyor belts and the left-turn conveyor had a interaction box 3 times its visible size until I reloaded the game. Pans have lost their proper hitbox and now register as rectangular prisms that can't hold items. While reloading the game fixes the problem, it only does it briefly in the end. And those were just my most recent problems after having just got off of the game.

I'll probably change my review when these problems are fixed, but for now I'll just have to stop playing it for a while.

I couldn't recommend Hydroneer pre 2.0 but with the more stable dirt physics and the (albeit compromised) multiplayer it's a thumbs up!

Beware, the game is glitchy, there's no real goal, there's not a huge amount of direction and money quickly becomes basically meaningless... But it's just fun to play, especially with a friend. There's just enough jank and interesting interactions to keep the game fresh as you play. It'll bring even the most powerhouse machine to their knees with mountains of dirt and gold, but it lets you do it and that's the great part.

Pre 2.0 I had fun with the game, but it was misery to get automation to work without hours and hours of tweaks. In post 2.0 I've found is so much easier to throw together my automation and let it run. 
Dirt doesn't clump anymore on belts which is the biggest change for me. It used to be a nightmare to manage splitting dirt and it would get caught on every pixel within a KM of the belt. But now it plays nicely, so much more enjoyable!

Multiplayer is played on a local splitscreen and played through Steam Remote Play Together. I've been playing it across two monitors and streaming to my brother. It's been fine for us, we both have good internet connections and he has a 4k monitor big enough to ignore my half of the screen. But if you didn't have this setup, it would be awful to play I think. If nothing else one player is forced to use the controller and although it's entirely playable, it's not great.
However, it works, it's easy enough to setup and play. It's brought the two of us hours and hours of fun (only I need the game too which is nice!) 

Overall... It's a one man project. It's only £7. And it's worth every penny. Support Max because he seems like a chill dude and this game is a passion project. It's janky, but very fun janky. We still laugh every time the car decides to return to heaven and I hope it never changes!

Hydroneer is a game about bad controls and crashes. In theory, it's a fun engineering/automation game, but I've spent 80% of my time in the game working around the baffling lack of inventory and restarting the game after crashes. The input system is one of the worst I've ever encountered, and I've played hundreds of hours of Dwarf Fortress. The fact that a game can have so much promise but have such abysmal execution is disheartening.

- Physics crashes happen pretty often, especially if you're dealing with about more than 10 objects at a time. Keep in mind the game is *fundamentally built around small chunks of dirt and ore*. The game became unplayable for me at the earliest stages of automation.
- The truck is nearly undrivable because the turning rate appears to be proportional to the truck's speed. Yes, I get that that's how actual vehicles control, but most real-world vehicles aren't controlled with a keyboard.
- Lack of any kind of inventory means you have to individually collect every single ore or object you want to move or transport. Shopping alone becomes a 10 minute chore. The shopping starts off as "quirky" and rapidly becomes a barrier to progression as you spend mulitple minutes individually picking up every pipe you want to purchase. As soon as you get the magnet stick to start moving many pieces of ore or dirt, then you get crashes.
- You will rapidly come to hate the "HUH?" sound effect that occurs any time the game doesn't want you to put an object down. Because of the lack of inventory, switching tools means you have to drop your current one, find where you put the next one, then pick it up. If you're facing uphill, the game will refuse to allow you to drop your existing tool because that would produce collision with the ground.
- Figuring out how to stack items in the cart or truck is nearly impossible until the collision detection completely gives up and you clip into your stack of tools and get to drop items in a Katamari-style blob. When this collision detection works it's infuriating and when it doesn't (which is often) it just looks bad but lets you at least play the game.
- The entire early-game with putting dirt into a bucket and then scrubbing it appears to have zero benefit at all. The game allows you to smelt individual pieces of ore into bars and then construct jewelry or weapons, then sell those constructed items. Keep in mind that the controls make placing the individual bars onto the anvil to construct these items more tedious than most people would do once or twice, and once you DO create these things, you are rewarded with... the sum value of the ores you put in. Zero value to the labor. Why even have these mechanics in the game if there's no value? And yes, the "stock market" gives you a few percent increase in sales if you get lucky with the items you're selling, but again the effort required to make these items is at no point worth it.
- The game doesn't make it clear that multiple ores can be used to smelt a single ingot because the ingot size increases only very slowly with its weight. The first time I attempted to make an ingot out of 2 ores, I got an ingot that was an identical size to an ingot made out of a single ore and had assumed that the game had simply eaten the second ingot. I didn't realize you could make larger ingots until watching a playthrough online.
- There are two tools available to purchase in the shop that are critical to playing the game: the scales which show the weight of the ingots you cast, and the construction hammer which keeps you from accidentally picking up critical infrastructure when you're trying to clean up the 500 pieces of ore that spewed everywhere because the magnet stick malfunctioned again. Both of these items *work around fundamental flaws in how the game works*. These should not be "optional upgrades". These should be obsoleted by making the game not infuriating in the first place. You should be able to estimate the weight of an ingot by looking at it, just as you can determine how much money you have in your stack without an extra tool. The placement system honestly just needs to be reworked; the fact that there's a tool you can buy to attempt to make it slightly easier is an indication that the system is fundamentally bad.

Overall I may continue to play this game, especially since hopefully some of the crashes post-2.0 will get fixed soon. Unfortunately things like the lack of inventory make me think that the designers of this game have a concept in mind that... honestly, I'm just not interested in playing compared to modern games that are actually fun instead of tedious.

I can recommend this game, but, not for everyone. Not for the casual player. You got to adjust your expectations for how finished or bugfree the game is.
This game has so much potential, but is quite buggy and lacks focus and polish. The game wants to do it all. Mining, farming (up-comming in 2.1), fishing, exploration, housebuilding and decorating, management, etc. However it kinda falls flat, due to not having the polish to support it.

There is no real tutorial, you gotta figure everything out yourself. The main developer tries to help the player by having their youtube channel with a tutorial linked in the actual menu. This feels like a temporary solution rather than what the game actually needs. 
There are very few context clues, and since the game has a rather small playerbase, there is not a lot of knowledge out there if you aren't much into watching lengthy youtube-tutorials. 

The game badly needs an in-game book-type object containing a encyclopedia with knowledge of the game. A lot of games like this, have that. Also in-game context clues could also help the game. An example of this could be NPC's talking about another town, and what great things they purchased there. Things that can give the player some clue of where to explore. Currently the game gives you a map that is slightly incorrect in regards to some locations. (Probably due to the 2.0 update.)

There are some awful bugs that don't belong in a game that is not in early access or beta. Vehicle physics are horribly bugged, leaving them almost unuseable, forcing you to travel far on foot or risk your hard-earned goods. The vehicles shoot off into space. They have, from what i've been able to research, tried to fix this many times, with little success. They even rewrote most of the code in the game, and still were unable to fix this particular problem.  

There are still bugs with being able to place objects underground and out of sight.
There are a lot of bugs with putting items into buckets, and then when you lift the bucket, the item falls out rendering the bucket useless.

The development of the game lacks a bit focus and polish. There are very in-depth systems around vehicles, which also brings bugs. There is very in-depth management systems with pipes and factory elements, which sorely lack explanation, there is very in-depth crafting and ore / gem weight system, that again needs explanation, as a new player is left with no knowledge of this at all.

The game is almost entirely without UI, and this both works for, and against the game. I would love to have a physical backpack in-game i could store smaller things in, like hammers, tools, etc, as there is no inventory system.

The game world feels empty, as it is. There are no NPC's. (That i've encountered yet.) but apparently, they are working on this. 

Because of the above, the game feels like it should still be in early access, and not on a 2.0 release, as it currently is a bit misleading as to what the player can expect in regards to polish. But dispite all this, i can still recommend it. Because the core gameplay is _FUN_ with a capital F.

The game has huge potential, and the devs are very clearly ambitious, very motivated, and passionate and they bring in their community in the development of the game. They clearly care a lot of both the community and the game. For me, this game IS fun, and is worth it. If you don't mind unpolished gems, this is certainly one i can recommend.

This is a game with loads of potential ruined by its aggravating interface and a horrible NPE. I've spent 45 minutes trying to do the most basic things and getting more and more frustrated. I mined some ore, then went to sell it. I spent a good 20 minutes trying to find the jewellery store at a place called Bastion Keep. Turns out I went to the wrong castle (none of the locations are named so I had no idea it was the wrong keep) and by the time I figured out where to go it got dark. I then spent several more minutes trying to actually sell my stuff, turns out I was pressing "e" rather than LMB because the interface is arbitrary. 

Stumbling back to my mine, I had to find all my stuff in the dark using a crap lantern. You can't pick up anything else if you're carrying the lantern so I was stumbling in the dark trying to find things. Oh, and the "drop" recticle (which is different from the "pick up" recticle, something which adds nothing to the game except to make it more annoying) is BLACK and so you can't see where you're putting things in the dark.  I couldn't buy a bed to wait until daylight because I didn't have enough money, so my options were to drive myself mad trying to see black interface in pitch blackness or literally stand there until dawn. After 3 failed attempts to put my paltry $74 in a bucket in the dark, I quit.

In all, in 45 minutes of gameplay I had to look at two video tutorials, 3 wiki articles and 2 Reddit posts just to do the basic things in the game (and yes I watched the dev's tutorial video). Maybe I'm stupid, but I was able to grasp Factorio in 10 minutes and create a ludicrous factory within an hour, so it's not that I can't grasp complex games if the learning curve is at least logical. I love the idea of this game but the interface throws so many roadblocks between you and fun that it's not worth the effort imo. I'll give it another 30 minutes when I'm feeling more patient but this is probably a refund for me. What a shame.

I got about 8 hours of very high enjoyment out of this game, which for the price is really good.  In that way I can definitely recommend it if you like building and automation games.  It was very fun for me going from panning for gold to building up an automated setup over the course of those hours.  But I think I'm done with it at this point.  Why?

1.) The controls are needlessly futsy.  When you put your buckets down, they're *constantly* flipping upside down so you can't fill them up.  It's very finnicky to drop items precisely where you want - and the precision is necessary or some of your ore will fall to the ground for you to individually collect.  Where to place your pans to catch the output of harvesters and sorters is trial and error - and when you error you might  be collecting 30+ pieces of ore individually by hand ONE AT A TIME and depositing them each into the pan using the imprecise drop mechanic.      

2.) The building system is needlessly futsy.  It is a struggle to place foundations and items where you want - particularly at the HEIGHT you want.   

3.) The lack of an inventory adds tedium and limits the scope of what you can do.  For instance, to build even a very basic foundation, you have to carry each block individually from the store or load just a few onto your truck or wagon.  Then you place them individually (using the aforementioned futsy building placement system) .  So even to make a 4x4 foundation (which is quite small in this game), you'll be going to the store many times.   So building anything sizable / cool would take many many trips just to accommodate the lack of an inventory.  Heck, even your gold is a separate item that you have to carry like everything else by hand or in a bucket/pan.  Spill a bunch of ore?  You need to pick it up ONE AT A TIME and individually drop each into a pan. 

4.) The whole world isn't diggable/buildable.  There are a small number of plots that are somewhat limited in size that you can build and dig in.  Only these plots have the voxel soil that can be dug into.  So there's no element of "prospecting" - any soil you can dig will yield all the resources (with better yields the deeper you go) . I think it would be a lot neater if you could build / mine the entire world but had to find specific lodes of ores / gems.  So essentially there are zero exploration elements. 

5.) Unlike manual mining, your automatic drills don't seem to deform the terrain.  They'll just give you a steady output forever.  Meaning there's no need to adapt your build over time or naturally open up the mine/go deeper as you work.        

6.) General user unfriendliness.  The game links you to a very short youtube tutorial on how to get started.  Otherwise there is no in-game tutorial or story to help guide you at all (contrast with Satisfactory or Factorio which both give you just a bit of direction so that you know have a goal to work towards).  Not much in the way of in-game explanations either - so it can be mysterious how certain items work or what they do unless you look them up out of game.  

7,)  Very limited crafting.  You can only craft daggers, axes, swords, rings, and necklaces and the only purpose is to sell those for money.  You cannot equip or otherwise use them.  You can't craft anything you'd actually want to use (like better tools, building parts, etc).  That's really frustrating as that could limit the trips to the store due to the lack of inventory.    

That said, I did indeed enjoy my 8 hours with the game.  It is a budget title developed by one guy, and I think he's done a great job.  Just don't expect the next Satisfactory.

Let me start by saying I rarely leave reviews but I really need to in this case. This game is GOOD. So the first question is going to be why the negative review?

It is because it has a ways to go to polish itself up and the first thing it could do is really improve the super early game QOL. Unless you just have a dying passion for rinse and repeat activites then you will be very frustrated at this game. I love games with a good grind. But this grind is different and frankly it is not that it is long it is that it is frustrating. 

If the developer happens to read this please.. for the love of all that is holy on this earth... make your mouse pointer put stuff where it is aiming. I understand the shadow drop system and how to get stuff onto the anvil etc. but it is beyond tedious. If I am aiming a hot iron bar at the anvil that is where I want it to go. Not having to look for a shadow on the anvil and still having a center aim location on my screen would be a vast improvement. 

This will be the first few hours of your gameplay:

Dig 3 scoops of dirt into a bucket
Pick bucket up
Go to washbin and hover bucket shadow over the washbin. (Note: if you try just using the middle icon on the screen you will dumb your dirt on the ground. Have to drop the bucket and pick the dirt up and repeat.
Pick washbin up and drop it in the water. Pick it back up.
Drop washbin on the ground and then pick up the brush.
Use brush on washbin. Congrats you have made JUST the ore. 
Sell ore to buy anvil and hammer. also preferably stone grinder.

Rinse and repeat all of those tasks and watch the youtube video to learn how to make stuff on the anvil. Do not miss putting anything in the cauldron and for sure do not miss pouring your melted ore into the bar maker (forget the name). Because once again none of these go off of the dot on the center of the screen. They all cast a shadow you have to hover right over the item you are trying to hit. 

This game has IMMENSE potential. When I first saw it and read the description I was very excitied. I believe with time the developer can get there for sure and make this an amazing crafting/building game.

Une pépite d'or à ne pas manquer !
Hydroneer est un jeu incroyablement relaxant et addictif qui vous permet de laisser libre cours à votre créativité. L'objectif principal est de creuser, miner et construire votre propre empire. Que vous passiez des heures à optimiser vos machines minières ou à construire des systèmes complexes, le jeu offre une liberté d'action remarquable.

Les points forts du jeu sont sans conteste sa simplicité d'accès et son potentiel de progression illimité. On prend vite le coup de main, et on est rapidement absorbé par l'envie d'agrandir sa production et de débloquer de nouvelles technologies. C'est un vrai bonheur de voir son installation grandir et devenir de plus en plus efficace.

De plus, le jeu est constamment mis à jour par les développeurs, ce qui ajoute régulièrement du nouveau contenu et des améliorations. La communauté est également très active et propose de nombreuses idées.

En bref, si vous cherchez un jeu bac à sable qui combine la satisfaction de la construction, l'exploration et une ambiance apaisante, ne cherchez plus : Hydroneer est fait pour vous. C'est un excellent moyen de se détendre et de s'amuser pendant des heures.

BLUF - 4.5 out 5 would recommend.  Has a couple mechanics that are... different but not game breaking. ( like many of the negative reviews show) Decent Physics and a game where you really need to think and just let the time melt away and try to start hauling in that cheddar.


So if you are past the the bottom line up front... here is some more info in case you are still on the fence.  

This game is unique... from the Dev being active and responsive from what i have seen,  to what you are able to do.  And how fast this game is able to pull you in and start having the time melt away.   don't think its as near as a time sink as Factorio or Satisfactory but ... that is not a bad thing.   

There is no tutorial but lets be real.  you cant figure something out 99% of you are going to YouTube to find and answer anyways.   oh and the dev made a small video on the basics of the game that is on youtube and able to access it from in the game.. whaaaaaa??? its like he knew... 

Some of the mechanics are a bit weird and take some getting use to.. one of them is that E is use for everything... or 99% of everything. not bad at first but again this is where the game is not a 5 out 5.  but at the same time dont really have any suggestions on how to make that part better.  soo really its me just trying to complain with out having anything to add to fix it.  

another complaint.  pick up and drop (done with the pressing of E)  again the dev has items in the game to help this.   one of the the parts that is unique is an offset drop box.  you pick up what it is that you are looking at center screen.   when you drop it .  it does not just fall in front of you.  it drops slightly to your right.  some people hate this.  just look at the negative reviews and they will point this out.   again not game breaking.  just a devs unique way of doing basically the same thing but different.  

Another item is physics.   some of the negative reviews are about parts flying away and other game breaking items.   

***From my experience and even trying to break the game*** I have had nothing crazy go on except some FPS drop.  or stacked too many objects and triggered a glitch with the colliders.  and i got stuck once.  ***game has an unstuck feature*** and poof back on the road.   ***

Object placement can be semi tricky due to 3D grid style placement.  but again not game breaking.  Maybe a bit more challenging when you are building a multi level design but if you are just on flat surface... easy peasy .    

This game will apply physics to objects while you are moving around or looking around.  Soooo if you have an item in your hand and you are trying to hurry and you twisting side to side and dont allow your character to stop before you release your item... yeah.. well you are now doing basically trying to play Frisbee with that item.  

All in all.  for 9.99 *at the time of the review on sale for 6.99 USD... This game is awesome.   beautiful art and textures.  nothing really feels out of place.   makes you think about the game and what you need to do next.   keeps you engaged.   great game from what seems to be a great Dev.   and again in my opinion.  Games like these are rare.   and with how much I have enjoyed it.. I am surprised this is not a 19.99 or 29.99 USD price tag.  Have seen and played way worse games for around that price tag and have not even had half the quality or game play that this game brings for 9.99.

This is possibly the most frustrating game i've ever played.

It immediately and clearly has the potential to be amazing, but is absolutely kneecapped by it's movement and interaction system.
It's entirely too easy to grab something without meaning to, and despite being on a grid system, the machines you can place down don't "just work" in that they'll spray materials everywhere instead of depositing them right where they should.

It's like one of those "most unsatisfying" compilation videos, where something enjoyable *almost* happens but never does.

Honestly, you spend more time fighting the mechanics than playing the game.
You can use a sorting machine to sort ores out, but the ores will eventually just... not go through? They clog up on the grate and turn into a big pile that takes forever to sort through, or just goes everywhere when you inevitably accidentally pick up the sorter underneath.

Even later in the game, conveyor belts don't quite work right either. Again, you can use sorting conveyor belts to split out different ores, but i keep finding bits of iron at the very end of the line even though everything is perfectly aligned. There's no reason for it, it's just a buggy, frustrating game.

I'm also finding out that there is little or no information on how to progress.
The developer took down the fan wiki for some reason and put up his own, but there's basically no information there. No images, no explanations, nothing.

And in-game, all you get are pictograms. Images of objects that you may or may not recognize, roughly depicting... something? Maybe the dev is an ancient egyptian, and it makes sense to him. We've developed an alphabet since his day though, so maybe he should bring on someone who knows how to use it.

And now, after playing for a fair amount of time and getting basic automation done, i'm getting continuous crashes.
Maybe it has something to do with dirt clumps? I can't tell. The crash log tells me nothing.

Don't get this game unless it's at a deep, deep discount.

update jan 2, 2023:

decided to give the game another go, since there'd been a major update and a few patches.
another six hours. in which very little was accomplished, a great deal of time was spent fighting the clunky gameplay, and i've renewed my resolve to not come back to this game anytime soon.

last patch notes tells me vehicles were reworked! but nothing about how. i [b]do[/b] know that vehicle steering is still tied to framerate, against all rationality, so if you have your framerate fixed at 30 fps (which the game lets you do in the settings ui, and there are many rational reasons for a player to choose to do so), steering is misery (and this isn't just the trucks; carts are vehicles too). also controller turning is also tied to framerate. good luck with that if you don't have rock solid fps.

gameflow is still a trainwreck. no inventory, no ability to move things in bulk in any kind of rational manner aside from small pans of tiny objects. need a bunch of building supplies? yeah, tedious manual labor. need to rework your layout? more tedious manual labor. want to get a nice smooth span of dirt? play the rake gambling game, there's no way to get it to work consistently in vanilla (and i couldn't bring myself to start messing around seriously with mods to find out if it can be fixed properly that way).

for that matter i couldn't even bring myself to get as far as doing crops, because i was so miserable just trying to get to basic automation going; i'm now convinced the hand sorters are a malicious trap, since the belt versions aren't much more expensive and are substantially less frustrating. [i]less[/i], mind you. all automation in this game is still misery.

pretty much everything from the previous version of my review still stands (the objectives might be stretched out by farming, maybe, but i didn't get there and i doubt it addresses the fundamental issues), so i've left the rest unaltered.

original may 12, 2022 review:
it's a cute game, with a fairly clear premise, with a dedicated dev team. there's just not enough to it, and there are enough user experience flaws that even at the current sale price ($7 usd) i can't in good conscience recommend it.

content-wise, there's six dig sites, each with different vistas, there's a few shopping areas, and a little bit of explorable territory that has no gameplay impact. unfortunately, unless you are into hunting hidden items, you can easily see most of what the game has to offer without ever crossing into 'tier 2' equipment. after you get through a little of the obligatory hand mining, the tier 1 harvester (you only need one, bought by the starter plot) and some tier 1 drills (you can buy one with the harvester) will easily produce quite a lot of money, and while it will keep you busy for a while buying more automation framework (conveyor belts, pipes, repair tools, better pipes, automation for repair, etc), there hits a point with just tier 1 machinery where you are producing money faster than you can spend it. once you hit this threshold -- i did with just six tier 1 drills in a second digsite -- there is little actual pressure to continue on to tier 2 equipment unless you just really want to see bigger numbers.

to be clear: you don't earn money faster than you can find things you want to buy, but faster than [i]you are capable of actually spending it[/i]. this gets into the user experience flaws: you have to buy things one at a time, moreover, the process for purchasing things is especially laborious due to the dev's choice to avoid anything menu-like. pick up item, put it in purchase area, repeat, until you have as many things as you want to buy (or can fit into the purchase area, if you aren't using a cart), then you put money into the pay bin, hit a button... and then you have to get the stuff back home. usually by loading it into a truck. at which point you have to laboriously unload it, optionally staging it somewhere before you start building things.

there is no way for this to move more quickly. there are no reasonable ways of packaging objects for ease of movement or storage. you cannot buy things in bulk. everything is, by design, exceedingly laborious.

and all of this is without getting into the persistent issues: hydroneer 2.0 did function as an effective rewrite of the game's logic, which greatly improved the physics stability, but there are still a large number of issues with regards to arbitrary framerate issues (in truth [b]simulation rate[/b] issues, but simulation rate and framerate are tragically linked) which result in effectively punishing the player for trying to buy too many things at once. especially since while the game is at a low frame/simulation rate, physics for the vehicles get increasingly dodgy, to the point where they can rapidly become undriveable. while i'd like to think these problems could be solved, the fact the developer didn't think solving these problems warranted more time before shipping the update is unfortunate.

i'll probably check the game out again in the next major update, and maybe i'll flip my recommendation around at that point, but right now i just don't see the game as worth it for most players.

and as for my current playtime of 73.9 hours as of this writing: only 37.1 hours are from the 2.0 update, the previous were from my failed attempts at getting automation going because the pre-2.0 physics were unbearable. it *has* improved markedly. it could improve more. but the game still isn't there just yet.

So… I’ve played **219 hours** of Hydroneer.

That’s not “I tried it for a weekend” hours.
That’s **“I could’ve learned a new language but instead I became a professional dirt investor”** hours.

And yes… my review is still **Positive**.

Hydroneer is the kind of game where you start with a tiny mine and a dream… and end up with a giant industrial operation that looks like someone let a beaver loose inside a factory.
And the best part?

I’ve restarted **countless times**.

Not because the game forced me.
Not because it bugged out.
Because every few weeks my brain goes:

> “Okay but what if… I rebuild EVERYTHING… better.”

And suddenly I’m demolishing a working mine like a man possessed, fueled only by ambition and 3% sanity.

Gameplay

Mine dirt → wash dirt → filter dirt → extract shiny rocks → craft jewelry → sell it → buy better machines → repeat.

It’s basically **a satisfying loop of:
DIG → PROFIT → OVERBUILD → REGRET → REBUILD**.

Pros

✅ **Addictive as hell**
“Just one more run” doesn’t exist. You will blink and it will be next Tuesday.

✅ **Factory/automation heaven**
If you like Factorio or Satisfactory, Hydroneer will hit you with that sweet **automation dopamine**.

✅ **Tons of content added**
This game has grown a LOT. More stuff to build, explore, mess with, and turn into a chaotic mining empire.

✅ **Restarting is part of the fun**
New map? Restart. New idea? Restart. I placed one pipe wrong?
RESTART.

 Cons

❌ **Still no real inventory system**
You don’t “carry items”.

You *become one with the items*.
You juggle your tools like a medieval clown while whispering “please don’t fall in the water” like a prayer.

But honestly?
That’s part of the charm now. Inventory would be too modern. Too civilized.
Hydroneer wants you to live like a true miner:

**hands full, pockets empty, dreams huge.**

Final Verdict

Hydroneer is still one of those rare games that makes you feel like an engineering genius… even while your entire mine is held together by **hope**, **ramps**, and **pipes clipping through reality**.

After **219 hours**, I can confirm:

Hydroneer isn’t a game.
It’s a lifestyle.
A dirt-based religion.

⭐ Recommended if you enjoy:
Automation, rebuilding, mining, production chains, and ruining your own perfectly functional setup because you thought of a cooler design at 2am.

I thought I would hate this game but it was on sale and something inside my brain made me give it a try. I started playing it and found out you can only ever hold one item at a time not counting buckets and similar vessels; I REALLY hated it now and wanted to quit and refund but something in my brain made me keep playing. I started digging down with the shovel deeper and deeper, filling my bucket over and over again with dirt and hauling it back to the pan full of water to brush away the dirt to find minerals and gems, wash, rinse, and repeat and at first I was thinking how tedious this was but eventually something weird started happening. I couldn't stop playing. I continued on like this over and over again, occasionally stopping to bring the treasures up to the store to sell for money to buy better equipment. Soon I had a more proper deep mine shaft thanks to the pickax - deeper yields better treasures. I had lighting so I could see what I was doing in the dark. I encountered weird bugs like having my truck jump into the sky and float away because I used the miner's helmet light near it and yet I felt compelled to keep playing through it. Eventually I started playing with pipes, valves, and the hand sorter; the kind of stuff that puts the Hydro in the title and as frustrating as setting up the hand sorter can be due to it's propensity to fling sorted minerals and gems out at a hundred miles an hour, getting it to work felt like an accomplishment and I realized I was hooked. I was looking forward to seeing how I could improve on my machine. I found out about drills and harvesters, conveyors, and funnels and after some hours of gathering up the funds to buy everything, and a lot of tinkering I slowly put together a larger, more complicated, more automated machine for digging up and sorting through all the various minerals and gems for me separating them out first into individual pans and eventually directly into smelters. This would allow me to easily cast bars to craft into jewelry and weapons to sell for more money to buy better equipment to build an even bigger, faster machine (still figuring this one out). Now I have designs on building a shack, then a house, just because I can and it's a challenge since you can only carrying one thing at a time and your truck and cart can only hold so much so there is a lot of back and forth to gather building materials and machine parts. All of that is part of the charm of the game. I found my mind racing to figure out how to make improvements to my contraptions. I found myself playing for hours straight forgoing all the other games I might have played during this time. I was hooked. I can't wait to see what the devs of this awesome, highly addictive, physics based contraption playground have in store for us. There is a literal mud mountain of value in the full price and even more while it's on sale and the devs are very active and responsive to the community and have definite plans for improvement so I highly recommend you just give it a try.

Fun game that feels like it's in early development. Uses lite-gui and avoids traditional paradigms around inventory, crafting and earning resources and is refreshing in that respect. 

Building anything takes a while due to need to physically move each object one at a time across the game world. Mass transport exists but is still very limited and each individual item added to a truck or hand cart must be interacted with manually one by one. Need 40 pipes? Drive to town, sell a necklace for endless money, buy all the pipes, load them into the truck, drive home, unload them... find out you need an L pipe? Time to run back to town again.

20 hours and I have a base setup with essentially limitless resources capable of obtaining end game everything... in the starting area. 

Higher level areas exist but just give more, better, faster. Fishing mini game exists but who wants to fish? 

Hidden items exist according to the internet if you mine out areas until you get them.

Lots of fancy logic exists but is completely unnecessary due to lack of things to do with funds. Early game is exceptionally grindy but gives way to somewhat automated gameplay fairly quickly at which point the gameplay loop is static.

Worth the 10 bucks as a relaxing diversion as-is.

Okay, Do I like this game? Yes
Am I happy with the game? No
Do I want to be happy with the game? Yes
Will this game eventually get to a enjoyable state? Hopefully.

I don't think the game is done as it sits. If you're just going to play in the beginning area and mess around a little, then go for it. You'll have a great time. 

If you're trying to play the game how you did in the previous version, you're going to have a bad time. Running any sort of mass mining operation will give you a decent amount of FPS loss. 

I'm struggling to see where the optimization was put in. The dirt chunks are smaller and there are less of them, but I'm still having massive lag if I load my truck up with items. I tested the minimum amount I could put in the truck before fps dropped. 10 building walls, 3 window frames, 2 doors, and 4 flooring pieces. I went from 150 fps down to 15 fps. I'm running a i7 12700k, 64gb of ram and a 3080ti. Why am I having issues with minimal playtime on each session? These are the frame rates I would have on the previous version with a massive mining rig running for over an hour. Why would this be happening? Because the game isn't optimized. 

I want this game to be good, I really do. I just don't know if it can happen at this moment. Whether its technology limitations that are keeping the game from being 100% or if it's just a developer issue, who knows.

At the end of the day, its a 10$ game, you're going to get your money's worth out of it, but you're going to want more from the game. At this point, it's just not there.

Make no mistake this maybe the most misleading title currently on Steam. This is not version 2.0, this is not version 1.0 this is more like version EA .2. There are no NPCs, there is no inventory, the basic equipment does not work as expected, simple QoL is absent, etc. Here is my 5 hr experience:

1. Took me a while to find the shovel since it was sitting beside a sign where it blended in like camouflage.

6. As you have no inventory, the money you receive is not in single pieces, but what I would describe as a welded together coins.

Since 2.0 release the game is pretty broken.  I expect a slow stream of updates to address the many issue but this could take months or even more than a year.  At the moment the game is IMO not playable.  The main issues are from pallets of supplies that cost small fortunes or even complete vehicles loaded with supplies simply rubber banding out of the universe.  Flying off into space or glitching under the map.  10 mins into the game i put down my shovel, most basic mining tool and it glitched into the ground.  I barely had enough money to waste it all buying another shovel.  When in late game building massive machine networks some parts simply refuse to be placed in open areas for absolutely no reason.  Sadly due to the complexity of the machines this can mean having to shift the entire machine one way or the other,  hundreds of components, just because one single part wont place for no reason.  Then even if you do that you probably run into the same problem with another part.  Its ridiculous waste of time just to be stopped by simple bugs refusing to let you use game mechanics to achieve your goals.

The multiplayer they just added is similar to console multiplayer with split screen.  At the moment it even requires one of the players to use a console controller.  My wife and I bought the game on pc so we could play multiplayer and yet it still is not possible unless I drop even more money on a controller, and am willing to play with a controller, which I am not, and to play in split screen, which I am not.

I wish we could get refunds but they strung us along with promises of multiplayer and the 2.0 update making everything better until its too late to return the game.  I certainly can't recommend it in its current condition.  I strongly recommend NO ONE get this game with the intention of multiplayer until you are completely clear what that means in this game.  You will be disappointed.

The most important aspect for games nowadays is not the production value for a game, it's not the graphics, functionality, etc. It's how much developers personally invest in their game by catering to the community rather than to the profitability of it. Hydroneer is a great example of a development team who are here to achieve an ultimate goal for themselves and the community. With the new 2.0 update that released recently, they had to basically rebuild the game from the ground up to accommodate HUGE changes to the game. FOR FREE! Hardly any developers nowadays would put forth this kind of effort (My only other example is No Man's Sky). The gameplay is simple, yet it pushes your creativity for creating efficient automation which can be a great challenge. If multiplayer was full on multiplayer, and not split screen remote play, I would certainly buy this for all of my friends. Well worth it and excited to see the future of the game.

1.5 HOUR SNAP JUDGMENT REVIEW

I want to like this game as it is similar to others I love like Satisfactory, Planet Crafter, Factorio, Dyson Sphere Program, etc, but currently the frustration outweighs the fun.  First of all, the game provides almost no guidance on how to play or what to do other than making more money.  However, it was still oddly compelling trying to make more and more efficient operations.  But the frustration of having to manually manipulate every single item in the game world and frequently missing the pan or smelting pot or losing an expensive piece of equipment to the void underground made me just want to play a more polished game.  I wish I could give a NEUTRAL review because I like to support solo developers (I can't imagine the work it takes to make a game) but I just didn't enjoy it, sorry.

PROS

+ Process of mining, refining, crafting, and selling seems relatively realistic and compelling
+ Automation and logic tools leads to more fun, efficient operations
+ Lots of ways to customize your base with decorations, lighting, structures, and vehicles
+ Interesting (but lifeless) world
+ Good music and graphics

CONS

- Absolutely no guidance except for link to brief YouTube tutorial video
- Absolutely no goal presented other than making more money
- Manipulating items is awful (Think manual item moving in Skyrim)
- Manipulating items is awful (No inventory - must handle one thing at a time)
- Manipulating items is awful (Equipment frequently flips over or gets lost under the ground)
- No UI leads to confusion and frustrating item and money management

1 get gold, make money ( now idea how much is needed  ) , 
2 get an unknown amount of iron out of the ground, make it into bars of an unknown size   
3  Find a store ( not found yet, map is quite large and you can get lost easily ) that sells miniatures ( =blueprints ) of the item you want, and be sure you have your money and materials with you / in your truck as theres no inventory ( to less iron or money - drive back,.. )

While initially fun, after a couple of hours physics become a huge deterrent which is a huge problem for a game whose "inventory," storage, and purchasing is physics-oriented. 

Trucks have a tendency to grip more to the skybox than the ground with a stopping distance of a city block; recalling the vehicle is nostalgic of portal 2, as the velocity only rebounds towards the sky with increasing fervor. 

Carts have a cool feature where sometime after version 2.0 nowhere is a valid place to drop it, soft locking your game; god forbid the automatic backup decided to save then.

All in all, this game is probably worth the sale price, but what was an initially fun experience became a psychotic break in mistrusting anything that moves, saving frequently and making backups around every corner only to be punished in the fifteen minutes you forget to. Only because of how janky the physics are can I not recommend this game.

Game was very fun and promising early stages, as a solo game, but they decided to promise "mutliplayer support".

They failed to provide an enjoyable mutliplayer experience (split screen, unable to get to far form the "player one", and with some controls issues) wasting ressources that could be used to properly add real content.

Then, they just added a new zone, not very meaningfull, with no reals aditions to the game, and it was a DLC (basicaly same price than the base game). So you should pay twice for a full experience.

Few time after that (one year and some minor patches for bugfixing), they claimed "game is finished, let's make a new crowdfunding session for a new game".

That's very greedy, and not totally honest.

At this time, the game is repetitive (not any replayability) and there is very few content (2-3 hours at best, with some hours of unactive wait between, just for the machines to make you money.

Ps : I was a follower of the project since the begining, even if i was delighted early on, i can say today i'm simply honest.
