Game is fundamentally broken on both a technical and a design level.
I will break it into two sections Bugs and design decisions.

The Bugs:
Vehicles taking off into space with their entire cargo.
Buying helmets causing the entire map to unload.
Tools falling through the world and burying themselves.
Lamps that act like dynamite when placed, playing the explosion noise and destroying dirt.
Mysterious dead spots on the map that pipes simply cant ever be placed on.
Vehicles that accelerate infinitely.
Picking up a bucket of more than 5 gems melts a 3080 with 32gb of ram to the point it struggles to run at 5fps.

Nonsensical design choices:
In 1.7 You simply bought a drill from the town for 735 coins and brought it back to town and used it.
In 2.0 you must drive  to the corner of the map with a bucket of iron and a bucket of cloudium, buy a miniature replica of a drill, then drive to the opposite end of the map, place the miniature replica on a scale, place the iron and cloudium bars in a smelter, then pull a lever. The game will then spawn a drill, which you must carry the entire way back.  You must do this for every drill you want to make. And in the end game, you will sometimes want to make 40+ drills at once.

In 1.7 a pipe cost 25 coins, and reduced water pressure by 5% for each section.
In 2.0 a T1 pipe costs 25 coins and reduces water pressure by 3% for each section.
The T2 pipe costs 280 coins and reduces water pressure lost from 3%...to 2% per section.
A T1 pressure tank which gives 25% pressure still costs 60 coins... That's 6375 coins that can be negated by a single pipe section add-on that costs 60 coins...

Items such as guide rails, conveyor covers, sorting machines and digging tractors were simply deleted from the game, without rhyme or reason.

Final verdict: 
Sad to have to say the game has become completely unplayable and the developer has utterly destroyed all the promise the game held.

What can I say about Hydroneer... it's a game that I didn't expect and that I discovered quite by chance and surprisingly for a farming game I was pleasantly surprised!

without being a gamer from the start, I experienced before 2.0 and after 2.0 and you have to admit that it's a joyful mess!

Having only a "tutorial" in the form of a Youtube video, the game already lacked a lot of clarity, but the recent modifications have succeeded in disturbing a lot of people who already had their little habits in the game!

The devices are less accessible than before since you now have to buy models that can be used on the great dwarven forge to be able to craft them (besides I STRONGLY hope that the sorter is part of his crafts because the new mini red sorter is a NIGHTMARE to use without putting it everywhere!) in itself it is not a problem but explain it a little better than with a panel above the two used machines at the start!

the new way of driving vehicles is still just as... dangerous! the slightest bump, the slightest obstacle is a potential risk of take-off (besides the lanterns along the road are more annoying than anything else)... I'm waiting to see what will happen to the mined vehicles that " coming soon"

Collision bugs are more present than ever... and THAT's a BIG problem! the number of shovels, pickaxes, pallets, buckets or even minerals that I lost after they have flown away I don't know where or they got glitch in the ground is maddening and unbearable!

I give a lot of bad points for a game that I recommend, right? xD
Honestly the game is nice, especially for its price... you just have to get the hang of it, understand what the game wants and above all know what you can or cannot do in order to avoid the collision bugs that are , for me, the most frustrating!

PS: THE MINI RED SORTER IS CRACKY!

My real issue with this game is that it does an awful job educating players how to play. Even digging around online is something of a pain. It looks like it will be simple once I figure it out but it is a real painful chore to even know what to look for to access the info.
Good game design incorporates teaching game mechanics into the gameplay so you learn as you go. Ok game design builds in a wiki that explains how stuff works. This game does neither which drags down the experience.

-Edit
Gave it a bit more time and figured out how stuff works. Even understanding it now its just frustrating. The hard part about this game is understanding how to play it and the poor functionality of playing it. Some examples:

Drive to town to get some stuff and the truck dies out of nowhere. Search online and learn you have to add water. Great.. Now your stranded running across the map for a bucket because you had no warning or indication that mechanic existed.

Try to put something in your truck? Huge pain for no reason. The functionality is coded into the game to add items to containers. Like putting dirt in a bucket. But this is a HUGE pain for everything else.
Try to dump your bucket full of gold into the smelting thingy and physics sometimes just blows up scattering hundreds of tiny pieces everywhere. Then you get to spend forever picking them up one by one. Soooo fun
Try to just put down your shovel in the mine you dug and the game sometimes just says no over and over.

Its stuff like that killing the experience at every turn. Its not enjoyable to struggle to do the most basic functions and there is no skill in it. Its just frustrating.

Aside from enjoying this game immensely, and now being able to enjoy it alongside my child, the 2.0 release happening at the same time as LEGO The Skywalker Saga has made me think:

Hydroneer's tiny dev team may have not been able to deliver "full" multiplayer, but they have been honest and upfront about this and keep in constant contact with their players. review: det var mcäldigt braigt

This game is as relaxing and sanitizing your hands by cutting them off.

I expected the controls to be clunky, but this is a lot to take in. I could have dealt with this, the bad frame rate (even with a new save) and bugs (did not even play one hour and encountered multiple), but the interaction UI made me do a refund. 

You click in the middle of your screen to interact with something and with some items you interact with the spot in the middle. When dropping something or interacting with other items (but of course not all of them), you have another point of reference in the bottom right of your screen. The idea behind this is kind of cute: this is where you would drop things from your right hand. Well, ok. But why does the rest of everything interact with the middle of the screen, even when holding the current item in my right hand? Does my arm stretch forward while shoveling or does its weight change? As soon as I dop the item, it drops dead straight down, but you guessed it - from where my right hand would be. It seems my character can bend the rules of gravity, but only with objects he is currently holding. That is probably also the reason why I can only hold one single item at a time. Of course there are expections to this rule as well: It seems my newly created character had so much bottled up power that it made the shovel I dropped to my feet (on a flat ground) fly several hundred meters away from me (1 meter = around 20 hamburgers for people not familar with the metric system). 

Truly, it is just a god simulator. 10/10.

Version 2.0.....

  Yea going into this I was excited and have been waiting for a long time for V2.0 and oh man.... Not much changed. I was expecting basically a whole new game but it feels like the same game with multiplayer and a few quality of changes. Also now crafting required to advance in the game? I guess its ok. I love the game but it still feels like the year it took to add these things in was just a waste of time and money. I played the V1 and 1.7. They were good and was possibly was my favorite management game. But now it is just the same game with minor improvements. I watched all the update videos, which only added hype, and thought "wow we are getting a whole new game with all these new improvements". I still like the game and plan to keep playing it, but the only major change is the progression system. Which, again, is just a crafting system. I never made a house on any plot of land because I felt that it was just a wast of time and resources. That system has been slightly improved. I might just build a house just to test the mechs of the game, but I have doubts. The new thousands of new items, yea, locked behind a crafting system. No map to navigate. Insult to injury, It takes awhile to just get the the crafting area. Why was it not built more accessible and close by? Some changes make since but some also do not. 
  You want to know how all this new stuff works? No? Correct answer!!! There is still no easily accessible tutorial. When you add all new for mechs that make me have to relearn the game, why? It would be nice to just have a integrated book that shows you all items, parts, places, ect. by just pressing 'B' on the keyboard. But they could not have bothered to add that.
  Do I sound mad? GOOD!  They ruined a game that was already difficult to play and now much more difficult to play or even impossible.
  Decorations look like hot garbage! The crafting area looks like a bunch of orange glowing rods stuck around with a moving skin put on them to help make a sorry excuse for lava. I did not even blink and the decorations. NOTHING CHANGED. Everything still looks the same. Better FPS, YES. But better FPS means nothing if you put so much time into making new areas and decorations if they don't remotely LOOK GOOD. Nothing about this games strikes me that they even blinked at the idea of making the world look good. 
  The work is still bland. Why do you call it V2.0 if there is no change to the world? Walked around and the world still looks the same. I would love to have seen animals like birds, fish, rabbits, deer, ect. roaming the area. NOPE! Just a lifeless game with a lifeless world full of nothing. Lots of space filled with all you can't see. ARE YOU SERIOUS!, ALL THEY DID TO THE WORLD WAS SLIGHTLY IMPROVE THE AMBIENT AUDIO. This is a sorry excuse for not adding adding actual animals to the world making their own sounds an noises.
  Mining has not changed at all. Maybe a gas powered hand drill or something cool. NOPE, nothing changed there either. WOOP DEE DOO! They made the vehicles easier to drive. Literally just a 10sec game development quality of life improvement.
  Yes, it is a $10 game, but when the devs make a big deal with all that they are changing and adding, you would expect something close to it. This is just a sorry excuse for a game that WILL NEVER be anything but a poor indie game with nothing except being known for crappy game mechs and dev team.

  DO NOT BUY
  All in all, i am very disappointed. Time, hype, and money has been wasted on a lost cause.

I purchased this game while it was still young, since then there has been a few updates so i thought to come back to it. At its core this is a unreal engine game, the physics are janky at the best of times and game breaking at others, especially when using vehicles of any sort. The terrain destruction is a good idea thats been executed well, but due to the poor physics using some of the mid game strats like the excavator turns the terrain into an in-navigable mess most of the time. starting off the game is a grind, but quickly picks up its pace after you get even the most basic of automation going. Be wary if you have a weak computer, i have a rig with an RTX 3070 FTW and a Ryzen 9 3900X yet i still average ~45 FPS when there is a lot of objects on screen. Im excited to see where development takes this game, but i truly hope to see some of the more core issues fixed first. If you can look past these relatively small gripes its a very fun game that is both satisfying and addicting to play for 30 minutes or 8 hours.

I originally played Hydroneer about a year ago. It was very clunky and too difficult for me to enjoy myself. Knowing the dev was active and this was early access I decided to shelve the game and come back to it for a second shot down the road. Reading the current reviews I was very excited to give this another go around.

This is still a game not worth purchasing short of supporting the development. I applaud those who persevere and slog thru this grind-fest. I really think the underlying game play loop would be enjoyable but there are too many hurdles at this time (about a year after my first attempt, mind you (acknowledging there is a single dev)).

A feature I personally think of more as a gimmick is there are no inventory based items, everything is a real world object. You cannot carry more than one object at a time. If you're holding an item and want to pick up another, you'll need to drop your existing item. Seemingly obvious, it gets more cumbersome than you'd think. Make sure you drop it in an area you'll remember it exists. Make sure the surface is flat. Make sure you're not pointed at another object. Remember to click to pour but 'Q' to drop. Sometimes 'E' will drop. After mining 6 rocks, you must pick each one up individually, place on the cart, carry to the store, pick up one at a time, place on the table one at a time. Collect your payout, collect your other payouts (one at a time), cart them to the next store, place one at a time in the purchase bucket. This might be endearing for some users, it feels unnecessarily time consuming for me. The game does compensate for this some by allowing fair pickup distances. All objects are 'dropped' from a standing height. This works 90% of the time just fine. On occasion, when dropped, the object will assume the spirit of a bouncy ball and make a break for it. Most of the time, it just flops off the table and can easily be picked up. Easily, meaning move your avatar, move the pail, move the cart, angle your body for line of sight and pick it up to attempt dropping it again.

It's my understanding a lot of this frustrating grind is alleviated with automation, I didn't reach that point (admittedly less than an hour). Given all this, I was still enjoying the progression well enough to keep playing.

HOWEVER- this last round of mining resulted in a bouncy ball effect on my latest coinage haul. I lost about a third of my wealth with a random bug. I rage quit out. Maybe I'll try it again in the future when it's more stable.

This game is truly enjoyable. Cathartic to the core, you start out shoveling dirt into buckets and adding water to brush and pan away the dirt for resources. By the time you've hit 10-15 hours you'll have an automatic harvester, maybe a conveyor system, maybe several fishing poles, perhaps an excavator, maybe thousands of coins in the bank and maybe several properties. And there's more to do from there.

You start out in a little area with two sites you can dig on either side of a creek. You can spend time fishing or buy a fish trap to make a little money as you dig and pan. There are currently 3 other dig sites you can purchase, soon to be a 4th in the next update I believe. The resources get better and bigger the deeper you dig. I was amazed once I bought an excavator and the Aquafier property to find there are huge nuggets of gold and iron along with huge gems to be dug up from the lower depths of the property. 

By the time I've bought a second site, I had a full conveyor system where 3 automatic drills harvested dirt, sent the dirt up a conveyor belt and into a harvester. I had that dump into a pan for a while until I recently upgraded again with 3 separators to put gold, cloutium and iron ore into their own pans while gems and shards go into a pan together. Eventually I play to add a 4th separator for shards or gems.

Not long after that I began excavating and discarding the dirt from the excavator into an extra truck I bought. I would do that 3 or 4 times then take all the dirt clumps and throw them onto my conveyor at the other site and was earning massive amounts of money. I have tens of thousands of coins now after building up my harvesting and mining into a fairly efficient system and I have so much more optimizing and expanding I can do.

And that's roughly half of the game's items and half of the sites. There's still much left to do and it's all so relaxing and enjoyable. The music is nice, I love the visuals and the feeling of building up to a well oiled machine is so satisfying. 

The game does have some issues with it's repetitive nature, but that's something that genuinely only pops up in bursts and then when you've run out of things to do. So far, I find myself wanting to play the game regardless of my mining being optimized enough to not really require any more optimization. And the only other issue is the performance of the game can really tank after a bit of playing thanks to the physics system for the dirt. As you mine and amass ores and loose dirt, the game can really struggle. I don't know if it's GPU or CPU but the physics definitely hurt the performance over time. At the start of a one hour play session you'll have 60fps solid but by the half hour mark, if you've been mining, you'll have stutters down into the 20-30fps or lower at times. That's with my rig, at least, which is probably high-middle end for gaming.

The developer(s) are working hard to release new content too with a big new update on the way. I believe it was a one man show that has expanded to include several people now working on the game. I am so excited to see what the game has in the future, I know multiplayer is coming as well as a new dig site and new items and a totally reworked driving system. 

The game is a good price, it's fun, unique and has active developers who clearly love and care about their game. It really is worth the money if you're interested.

Pretty ok game !

Main issues i have with it: the game expects A LOT of tedious, often repetitive stuff from you before you get enough money for automation, both in mining and farming (farming being the worst imo).

Something that's both its strength and its weakness: the lack of (almost) any UI and inventory. It makes the game feel very unique, but this means that you can only carry one thing at a time, which can get really annoying and means you'll do A LOT of trips back and forth. Thankfully, there are ways to carry multiple things, but they slow you down quite a lot (both the cart and the pallet). Other than that, you can use the car to quickly carry a lot of stuff (the first car is free, which is great).

The fact that you can only carry one thing at a time means that doing large constructions is a drag. I wish you could do stuff like buy in bulk. Having to buy 50 wooden floors manually is not fun at all, even with the help of cars and pallets, which sucks because there are some cool decor pieces i want to have fun with, maybe build houses or a greenhouse, but i really can't be bothered to do it.

You COULD use creative mode in order to quickly duplicate items, but you can still only carry one thing at a time. Also, enabling creative mode (or any mods, even UI/quality of life mods) completely disables your steam achievements on that file, which is a shame tbh.

Also, if your game starts tanking, PLEASE use the clear raw resources button. Stuff gets stuck mid-air or on conveyor belts for no reason from time to time, and it clogs FAST.

Overall, a fun enough game to relax and spend some hours in, but i do think it's missing some quality of life features to get rid of some of the tedium. I don't think it's for everyone, you need A LOT of patience !

It was worth the 10 bucks for sure and it was fun for a while but for me it's a pretty short lived game.  Once I got an automated production line up with a few drills, I really lost steam and got bored quickly.  Money instantly became a non-issue, and the tedium of having to manipulate one item at a time very quickly outweighed my desire to build a fancy automated factory.  Read on for more but TLDR:  It's a good game and fun for a while, but unless you just really love building complicated factories, it will get old fast.  But you know .. it's 10 bucks, I played for 24 hours.  Can't really complain.  

So I have tons of money and the only thing I can do with it buy more stuff, so I can build bigger and make more money, so I can buy more stuff.  But I can already buy anything I want ... ?  I mean I can run my rig for 20 minutes and then build a sword and 4 necklaces that will sell for like $300K, which would be enough to build a whole new factory twice the size.  Everything is electric and automated up to the smelters (the electric versions of which are definitely not worth the effort to set up).  What is left to do?  Build a bigger rig, which will required hundreds of pieces, each of which I have to pick up from the table, put on the pad, pick up and put in the truck, then pick up and put on the ground, and then pick up and put in it's final place.  That tedium is real.  The pallets help a little, but not much.

Now you've assembled all this machinery to produce bars and gems ... and no matter how much ore or gems you make, or how fancy your rig is, the outcome that will make the most money is always going to be making a sword and 4 necklaces.  With a hammer and anvil.  Which I have to put in a cart or truck one at a time and drive to the jeweller to sell manually .. one at a time.  Sure I get more and more money for each of those objects, but it just feels kind of anti-climactic when I can't then buy anything I couldn't before.

Last thing - the beginning can be a bit rocky.  It's really easy to get stuck in a loop with a shovel, pans and a brush wondering how you're ever going to get enough money to automate anything.  A little more guidance at the beginning would be helpful, as it was nearly enough to make me bail after a couple of hours.

review:
After having played this for some time now, I am giving it a weak recommend. Here are my thoughts:

In Hydroneer you are with no context dropped into a world where you can dig up dirt, which you can turn into resources such as iron and gold. These resources can then be crafted into items that you can sell for money, and it is with money that you buy stuff for your digsite.

Note that there are no skills or tech tree or anything like that in this game. The only resource in the game is money and what you can buy with it. There are also (at the moment) no NPCs or quests in the game. Neither are there achievements or really any end game content. The entire map is unlocked for you from the very start, so there are no road blocks in the game either. This makes the game more into a sandbox game than a typical crafting game, in my opinion.

On the whole I think Hydroneer is a game that you can kill a few hours with, but after about 20 hours (maybe less) into the game you realize that there really isn't anything left to do. The most expensive things cost about 20 000 coins, and at that point you can easily have 100 000 coins or much much more. And since the only point in the game is to make money, but there really isn't anything left for you to buy, the game feels kinda over. Even for completionist there are no hard to reach achievements or anything. 

The game is made in Unreal Engine and has inherited a lot of the quirks from its physics engine. When items clip into each other they tend to fly either at super high speeds. This means that your wagon with all your gold could suddenly fly away off the map. The game also allows you to place items into the ground, where it is impossible for you to reach them afterwards, so they are practically lost forever.

Another thing I don't quite get is the workbench. You can get new blueprints by handing in previously crafter items you have made, but the problems is that the items you unlock are really useless. Why would I want to craft pipes or toolboxes when I can buy them cheaply in the stores?? In particular pipes are super cheap, so there is literally no reason to craft them from the rare resource cloutium. SO reaching the end of this crafting chain leaves you feel empty since there was no point. The only good thing you get is the recipee for Blunderbuss, but since cloutium makes up so little of the resources you get from dirt it's really not very good.

The final tier is the logic system, but after having read guides and tested it out I don't see the point of it. It only helps marginally with automation. If it allowed for automatic item crafting and selling without manually having to go to town it would have been interesting, but no...

The world is quite expansive with buildings and things to see here and there. But there is no real point in exploring anything except the cities and dig sites. I think there are some collectibles hidden away if you want to hunt for them.

I think this game feels more like an early access concept demo than a complete game. For its price it's just barely worth it. I think the game has some charm to it though, so maybe 2.0 will be better.

I know this is a small Indy title and i kind of enjoyed my time with it. But still, before you buy some information for you to consider (as of march 2022). 
This is in no way a full release, it feels like an early access. The basic game loop of building a small mining operation with limited automation is there and its kind of fun. BUT.
The building system is very clunky.
The physics simulation is constantly on the verge of breaking and needs some serious work and optimization.
There seem to be some memory leaks and other bugs. The game goes from 130 fps to 25 fps and need to be restarted from time to time.
The world is totally dead and static. There is no reason to expand beyond you first plot of land, you have nothing to spend the money on anyway. There is no progression system and no replay value after you explored the already very limited building options.
Conclusion, if you want to support Indy developers buy the game. Otherwise come back in one year after a couple of updates. There are better options out there for your 5 or 10 bucks, especially during steam sales.

Hey! Sometimes keybindings can bug out and need to be hard reset. To do this.

- Close the game
- Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
- Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER.
%localappdata%\Mining\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor
- Delete the 'input.ini' file and relaunch the game.

This game is awesome! 
I have been playing for a few years and I have seen it grow and blossom.
The best part is, it is still evolving!
There are a couple of bugs in the game that are being worked out.
Max is the creator of this game and I have to say his vision has been spot on.
Currently it is only available as a single player. That is about to change very soon.
The graphics and music are very well done and it is a pleasure to play.

You start off with no money and very basic equipment.
You get a shovel, bucket, pan, brush, cart and a lantern in the beginning.
You start off by digging and selling your resources.
Soon you start to upgrade and expand.
Eventually you are buying new mining sites and automated equipment.
You can build a production line and start bringing in tons of Gold, Iron etc.
You can start making Jewelry and Swords etc to sell for profit.
You can learn blueprints to make your own stuff. 
You will find rare artifacts on your sites that can be used to unlock a secret area.
You can build and decorate your own houses.
You can fish for fun or profit.
There is so much to do and all of it is fun!

Boring grind fest. So I will place here a recipe for huckleberry pancakes instead.

Huckleberry pancakes.

1 3/4 cups all purpose white flour
4 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1 1/2 cups of buttermilk
5 tablespoon butter, melted
2 large eggs
1/2 cup Huckleberries
In medium bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, set aside. In small bowl combine buttermilk, butter and eggs. Add buttermilk mixture to the flour mixture, combine until mixed do not over mix (I prefer to use a whisk it does the best job). Fry at 400 degrees. Pour about 1/4 cup of batter on the griddle and sprinkle with the huckleberries.

Cook on first side about 3 minutes until bubbles appear along the edge of the pancake. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more and golden brown. Serve with a big pat of butter, and some pure maple syrup ( get the real stuff it is worth it).

First of all its a cute game, with interesting mechanics, and me and the kiddo had some fun on the first couple hours, but when you get to a stage that you start automating the process, it starts to become somewhat of a hassle. I'm a firm believer of getting paid for a job, but when I pay for a game, I don't want it to be a job.

Let me explain our gripe, first couple hours you'll get the hang of it and you won't notice the grind, but as soon you start to scale up your operation, it really becomes a job, since the game has no inventory (not an issue for me; kinda of a refreshing idea/Interesting game design decision), but the fact that you can only hold one item (be it a tool, ore, or anything for that matter) at all times, makes for example purchasing items in bulk a p.i.t.a.

Since you'll have to get each item individually, carry it over to the purchase area, deposit the item, then rinse and repeat until you get the quantity you desire. Then, after paying you have to repeat the same ordeal to load up the vehicle (there are tractors, carts and a excavator in-game), get to your destination and repeat the whole process again to unload. This just eats a major part of your time, and you haven't even started to build whatever you had in mind. Now do this for everytime you want to expand and you'll get to a point as we did and just notice that you spend more time in logistics then building your setup.

But, don't let this small detail discourage you, me and the kid enjoyed it for the 5h we've played, but that detail has worn us out of the pleasure with the game, since it started to become a chore instead of "fun". IMHO, I think that this mechanic needs some further adjustments. 

Putting the cons aside, let's get to the pro's. GFX are lovely, the devs have created an lovely ambiance (and the variety of locations), game performance is great also, the remaining mechanics are fleshed out (bar our gripe previously stated), in the end it's a fun game if you don't mind with the grindy aspect later on into it.

So, don't be discouraged by our "negative" review, its just that it's a reflection of our experience and I think possible buyers need to be aware of what they'll face later on in-game. Your experience may be completely different, but this is our review/experience.

TL;DR: If you like the mechanics, go for it. for the price it has, it was worth it.

[b]Review[/b]
This is one of those games that is hard to give a solid thumbs up or down on, I have a feeling most folks will either love it or hate it. 

You dig dirt, that’s it…but Sam says it’s fun. 

Ok, there is a bit more to it than that, you dig dirt, wash the dirt to collect metals, sell the metals to buy equipment to upgrade so you can dig dirt faster, sell those metals to buy equipment to dig - am I getting repetitive? Yeah, that’s the game.

There is fishing and netting in the game so you can sell the fish, which allows you to buy more equipment to dig dirt faster.

While the game is an open sandbox, it is not that big, and some of the design decisions make the game tedious at times. Once I started playing and got past my initial frustrations with the lack of an inventory or continuously dropping stuff because the UI was not intuitive I found myself continuing to play the game long past what was needed to write an initial review.

Any game that does that might be worth your time. For US$9.99 it has already given me hours of sometimes frustrating and tedious gameplay, and given the current state of games, this is already a plus. If you are on the fence, check out a few videos of the gameplay to see if it is something you might enjoy. I will say, however, my younger kids enjoy the game.

Well that’s about it, thanks for reading!

if you like factory building games you should DEFINITELY check this game out, a real quirky take on the factory genre, and while it probably won't draw you in for hours at a time (unless you really get into it) it's a good one you can play for a bit and then come back to

cons:
-the early game is very slow
-there is no tutorial to speak off, you get dumped into the world with some starting tools (most of your help is gonna come from Youtube which the game does link you to a video from the main menu)
-building large scale can be tedious since every item has to be physically bought and carried to your site although there are trucks and carts and pallats to help with that (this might be a pro because of the realism and immersion)

pros:
-the game is definitely unique and new, every item in the game from the map to even your money has a physical form
-the game is simple in the beginning and gradually gets more and more complex depending how far you want to invest in it, the power and logic update really adds a whole new layer to the game i haven't figured out completely yet
-building your first simple automation is very satisfying, then you gradually expand it and make it more efficient
-unlike a lot of other factory games there are some decorative building pieces to really "pretty up" your factory by making it look more like a factory instead of a bunch of machines and convey belts in a dirt field, can also just build a nice house to relax in while your factory makes goods to sell for you

It is a lot more than I expected from a game that only cost $10. There are bugs, sure, but I have not run into any that have really broken the game, or even made it crash.

Trucks do go flying if you hit rocks... but this can be avoided by not hitting the rocks. I, personally, recommend hitting the rocks. It is hilarious, nothing falls out of the truck, and you often land closer to where you were going anyways.

If you notice your FPS going down, stop your machines. One of them is leaking nuggets or dirt. Clean up the mess, or clear the excess with the buttons in the menu, give the machine a better design, and try again. This is the fun/challenge of the contraptions. You're going to have to work on them a bit to get truly "set and forget" functionality.

The developer is still working on the game as well, with major updates planned, and multiplayer in the works. I thought split screen multiplayer was great for Minecraft, and I think it will work very well with this game too.

At first I thought Hydroneer is a little boy's dream come true. If you ever watched those dudes in Alaska digging out dirt to find gold, you know what I mean. If you were expecting a mine-manager-type game, or a semi-realistic mining operation that you can be a boss of, this game isn't it. In fact it is very far from that.

Hydroneer it is not like PC Builder, House Flipper, Gas Station, or any other simulator out there. It is also not like any resource-managing games like Satisfactory, Factorio or ShapeIO. Hydroneer created a new type of simulator: a pick-and-drop simulator. In addition, it does not have any goals, it does not have any innovative systems, no quests, no narrative, no progress bars, no skill trees, no upgrades, no NPCs - anything that can be seen in the above-mentioned games. It doesn't even have a tutorial. It's in a very early stage of development and it does not offer much content. You decide for yourself how long it takes for you to buy the next thing, and how long until you will reach the point of boredom. 

As seen in the trailer, you pick one of the many various items, click with it here or there, and then drop it in a random spot. This is one of the key features that is talked about in the in-game tutorial video (which actually redirects you to YouTube): the lack of inventory. You can only carry one item at any given moment, and in order to be able to use another item you have to drop it. This results in managing the space around you, having to deal with frustrating physics and forced positions of items that just keep on getting in the way of things. While this feature is at first interesting and original, it gets annoying really fast, but with time it dies down (with "automation" you pick up fewer things).

As the name of the game suggest, water is important and it's a key component of your mining camp. It ain't hard to learn  or master how it works, but without understanding it you might end up with bottlenecks later on. The game also has electricity, which I didn't get a chance to play. Those enjoying logic gates will for sure find it fun. The style of the game is very pleasant to your eye, the world is small but enough for the current state of the game. With nearly 15hrs of playing (5hrs afk), I still didn't need to and was not interesting in buying new land. Buying newer vehicles seemed like a waste of money and I was more interested in tools. It took me a long though enjoyable 10 hours of playing to be able to purchase more decent tools and equipment, including conveyor belts and splitters. Unfortunately, not being able to use those effectively and finding them extremely buggy resulted in frustration and disappointment. Having these was just a nail in the coffin. Not being able to make much use of those and progress further, I decided to leave the game until future updates. 

For it's current price, I could have recommended the game. However, I would suggest waiting some time until the game gets more content, newer and playable features, better systems, tutorial, inventory, and many fixes to physics and current content. Definitely have it on your wishlist. 

TLDR:
- Hydroneer is pick-and-drop simulator, far from games like Factorio, House Flipper
- Water is important, hence the game, be sure to understand it and use it
- No inventory is a poor "feature", gets annoying fast
- Great visuals, small but cozy map, interesting setting (RPG, fishing)
- You set your speed of progress, goals and joy from achieving them (game doesn't offer any)
- Many physics bugs, unforgettable buggy conveyors and splitters (nail in a coffin for me)
- Not recommending yet, but have your tabs open

Ps. Giving people hope, calling an update "MULTIPLAYER update", and the very next second saying "ha, not really" is very low and poor move. Dear developer, get yourself a Community Manager.

Fantastic game! It has its bugs like any game but no game breaking bugs unlike you would find from a huge triple A title (looking at you battlefield 2042). Bugs include occasional flight via angry machinery/vehicles. Frame rate depletion via backup on the conveyors. These really are the main 2 things and while they are bugs they can be sorted very easily. If you find your truck is fighting the forces of good and fighting its ascent into the heavens just use the unstuck vehicle tool whilst in the truck and hop out as soon as it snaps back on the ground. Usually caused by items clipping with the wheels. The dirt backing up on the conveyor usually can get fixed by adding a dirt shredder or pickaxing the larger chunks and then picking up and dropping them. These are the 2 bugs I have encountered that have posed some form of action on my part to get around. That being said these bugs are so few and far between within the current game that I more or less look forward to having them as they are quite entertaining. Especially the flying trucks, those are a hoot.
Onward to the actual gameplay, the digging mechanic is fantastic, the UI takes a second to get used to with picking up and dropping dirt (when using the shovel and pail) but after maybe 3 minutes of time you can have it down pat. The building aspect of the game is nice, a good mix of snapping and free placing depending on the item (Even going to be better in 2.0, review written at update 1.7). The automation is per-near infinitely expansive depending on your PC, The introduction of the logic and power system was HUGE for automation. You start out with a shovel and a pail making 1k coins an hour doing everything manually and by hour 10 with a decent drill and refining set up you could be making over 50k every 5 minutes with only 1 flip of a switch of effort. there is a crafting mechanic in the game currently with a relatively small progression system but again 2.0 will expand on that vastly.

I do advise following the developer on youtube, twitter, or discord for more in-depth info on what is going on in the game present and future.

Overall this game is worth more than the $10 price tag at the time of this review. It is a single Dev team and he is very responsive and welcoming of ideas or suggestions and is constantly making improvements to the game.

Uff, where to start? Gems like these are so rare nowadays and I'm so thankful to the developer for bringing a rare quality to the table: innovation! 

This game is so rewarding, so addictive, I love it. It's about creating, trying out possible paths, using all your creativity to get to that sweet $$$ faster. 

You're basically a miner, having at the start only a bucket, shovel and a brush. Getting that first nuggets is hard work, but then you advance. Better shovel, a few buckets. Then you start adding flowing water and pipes, then conveyor belts, and and and.... 

Slight downside is that I can see that the game is not that optimized, but from what I gather the dev is working on it. I really hope for multiplayer, this would be a blast with a buddy. But even without, give this game a try, you won't regret it.

I was a bit hesitant to get this game because from everything I've seen on the game... it's one of those games that feels like it should be early access and I'm sure you may have seen those reviews too. That being said, offically early access or not, the game gets constant major updates from the dev and it's obviously just going to get bigger and better so try to not let that impose too much on your decision to buy.

That being said! I will admit there isn't a ton here at the moment. Well I mean... there is.... but there isn't.... It's weird.

I already have a good amount of hours in this game but I couldn't really say I've done a lot. I've just stayed on the little beginning plot of land working on making a tiny little conveyor system with a couple of miners. I am aware that there are quite a few things to do. There is a building mechanic to the game where you can build on specific plots of land that you can purchase. You can build some pretty cool machines. There is a calming game loop here. It's just that... I don't know how to put my finger on it but for me it seems like it takes way too long to accomplish anything and it does get boring at a point for me. I think of part of why it takes so long to get anything done is just cause it feels like I got stuck in the beginning phase of hand digging and hand washing for a bit too long. The building is also a bit lackluster for me as there's not much you can do with decorating a house once you HAVE built it. Also, once you make even a small decently efficient machine... you kinda have enough money to buy just about anything in the game. So the game feels like it loses a REASON to make money way too easily.

I feel like I have to be in a certain mind space for the game to really be fun for me.

Also... just... I have to agree with Josh from Let's Game It Out.... the sound that water dripping makes.... is by far the most grating sound effect I've ever heard in my life. So like.... I could have had water auto dripping in a bucket to speed up the whole doing things by hand phase... but I couldn't because leaving the water dripping into a bucket to speed things up... made me want to uninstall the game.

I will say one of the most fun parts of the game is just leaving a machine running for a bit while you run around doing other things or crafting items for sale and kinda... uh... forgetting about it? Then you get back, pick up a bucket to smelt the ores inside.... and then BAM frames are gone XD. Then you get the satisfaction of burning the bad frames away as you dump just a block of ore into a smelter. Very satisfying.

Now all of that being said I've seen people having a TON of fun in this game and get really immersed and really involved. I'm just not one of those people, but like I said I do still enjoy it. So even if you are like me and find yourself getting bored... it's still a relaxing game to play with a decent game play loop you can fall into. Especially if you are the min maxing type of player in these kind of games I think you'll have a good time with it and it's worth the $10 price tag.

The only true major disappointment of this game for me is the fact that water powered cars aren't a thing in real life.

Stundenlang am Klondike River sitzen und mit seiner Goldwaschpfanne die ausgegrabene Erde waschen.
Und die Spannung, wie bei einem Rubbel-los, was sich am Ende in der Pfanne findet.
Jedes Nugget, jedes Stück Metall oder Edelsteine von Hand in Eimer sortieren, in die nächste Stadt tragen und verkaufen.
Klingt das interessant?! Ja?! Dann kauft euch das Spiel.

Nach 31 Stunden Spielzeit, habe ich immer noch Spaß daran.
Sicher habe ich auch meine erste Maschine am laufen, daran angeschlossen ist meine Sortieranlage.
Aber nach der dritten Reparatur der Wasserfilteranlage, benutze ich im Moment nur noch die Sortieranlage.

Wenn die Maschinen einmal am Laufen sind, entfällt der Aspekt des Grabens mit Spaten und Waschen völlig.
Die Nuggets, Metalle und Edelsteine purzeln dann im Sekundentakt vom Förderband.
Man muss dann nur noch die Maschine mit Wartung am laufen halten.
Aus diesem Grund habe ich die Maschinen abgeschaltet und mich noch nicht weiter damit befasst.

Der Verkaufspreis steigt mit dem Arbeitsaufwand der in die Fertigung eingeflossen ist.
Ein 1 kg Goldbarren bringt mehr Geld ein, als 1 kg Nuggets usw
Um Geld zu verdienen, kann man Waffen oder Schmuckstücke anfertigen und verkaufen.

Die Mechanik im Spiel funktioniert gut und die Grafik ist nett anzusehen. Graben kann man im Spiel aber nur an bestimmten kleinen Bereichen. Schön wäre es gewesen, wenn man überall graben könnte.
Momentan kann ich nur die Kollisionsabfrage bemängeln. Der Truck bleibt mit 20 km/h an einem Stein hängen, und fliegt mit 30 fachem Salto durch die Luft. Oder man nimmt ein Nugget aus einem Haufen und die restlichen Nuggets fliegen wie bei einer Explosion meilenweit davon.

Update: Nachdem ich die beiden Starter Claims von Hand leer gebuddelt hatte, ist mir beim Kauf der anderen Claims und deren Grösse die Lust vergangen weiter die Schaufel zu benutzen. x-D
Also, Ram Drills, Harvester, Sortieranlage und Smelter mit Förderbändern verbunden und die Produktion läuft (bei regelmäßiger Wartung) endlos.
Schaufel, Bürste, Waschpfanne und Eimer liegen nun Nutzlos am Boden.
Und mir stellt sich die Frage nach dem Ziel des Spiels!?

I would like to shed some light on the situation here and provide some explanation as to why this user was banned from the Hydroneer Steam Discussions forum.

Historically, from our experience the steam discussions are generally directed further away from constructive criticism and more towards toxic behaviour from its users in comparison to discord or reddit. It will not be an uncommon week for myself or another team member to ban multiple users for harassment, toxicity, or other general bad behaviour.

For this reasons, we have a lot tighter moderation in the steam discussion compared to reddit/discord to try and combat this (outlined in the pinned rules post)

For this particular instance (on Christmas day, no less) the user posted many times with un-related and completely negative comments which are not constructive and will eventually spiral into arguments. This happened twice within the first hour of play, functionally erasing the time spent.

The double reticle system is interesting, but that's the best thing that can be said about it. It doesn't offer any benefit and should have been scrapped for a more traditional single centered placement system.

The game could be fun eventually, but many of the poor design choices seem to have been made for the purpose of only being different rather than functional.

Gra Hydroneer, to prosty sandbox z dużym potencjałem. Początki bywają mozolne: wiadro, szczotka i łopata co dość szybko się nudzi. Po kilku godzinach dopieszczania techniki kop-szczotkuj-SEGREGUJ odkryłem kowadło, co spotęgowało potrzebę rozdzielania wykopanych bryłek. Co do tej selekcji... czynność która zajęła mi 60% gameplay'u. Bugi polegające na kolizji rud z samym wiadrem, nie zawsze gra "ogarniała", że kruszec wpadł do miski, co powodowało odpalenie katapulty przy podniesieniu naczynia i kolejne szukanie towaru. Nie mówiąc już o moim pierwszym pojeździe z wiertłem. Do tej pory nie ogarniam jak mam nim kopać, żeby nie ugrzęznąć, albo nie wzbić się w powietrze. Maszyny do automatyki też miewają swoje kaprysy, posłużę się przykładem rozbrylacza, wszystko idzie gładko do momentu kiedy chcesz podnieść bryłkę z ziemi. Jakimś sposobem bryłki wchodzą w siebie i podniesienie jednej powoduje wyrzut reszty w atmosfere. 
Sam koncept i założenia są ja najbardziej na plus. Po automatyzacji Bugi aż tak nie kolą w oczy, gra zmienia swoje oblicze drastycznie. Po kilku godzinach z narzędzi ręcznych używałem jedynie kilofa (aby odkopać pojazd...). 
Gra warta uwagi, do pogrania maksymalnie 30 godzin w obecnym stanie. Twórców upraszam o zmianę polityki, zamiast stawiać znak zakazu używania koparki na początkowym poletku, zróbcie tak aby maszyny nie zamieniały się w helikoptery.

review:
TLDR; The game seems under-developed, but I like it. 7/10

Keep in mind this is all my opinion, you can say what you want about it but I don't really care.

To be honest, this is a great game in concept, although the execution is somewhat lacking. Most of the things in the game function albeit somewhat poorly due to an either rushed due date or just straight up negligence on the part of testing the game before updating the game. The physics engine isn't very good leading to some problems with a couple items being in the exact same place and when bothered they basically fly away from each other. Vehicles in the game fly away for almost no reason for being hit with a tiny sign. And things just don't work sometimes. Another thing I would like to mention is the fact that there is no actual icon for the game and instead being replaced with the unity logo in the task bar, and the actual executable file is called "mining.exe" instead of "Hydroneer.exe" or something, making the game seem somewhat shady as if it was using your computer as a bitcoin miner in the process of running the game. Some of the models are literally just what seems to be some pre-made unity asset recolored or with something added on. And overall just seems like someones passion project that didn't fully come to life, but had most of the basic principles put into it. This game seems like one of those games you would find an "Early Access" label on it, but it doesn't so I feel like the game should be a lot better than it actually is. In my opinion the game could use a lot of refining and could use a few changes that make the game easier to play or run even. Other than all that I just mentioned the game is fun. You get to pan for ores, and then when you move on you can automate the process and start making tons of money within seconds (although I haven't reached that point myself) and just upgrade throughout which I really like. If I could rate this game out of 10 I would give it a 7 because I really do enjoy the game, but it could use a little TLC, but once it does I will most definitely raise my rating. I know they will be updating the game pretty soon, updating the unity engine version, adding QoL stuff, and more, so I know that this review will (hopefully) be outdated very soon.

Edit- Grammar and Wording
Edit- I just checked what they're doing with 2.0 and I just found out that they said there will be a lot of balancing, optimization, changing physics engines, and lots more which makes me really happy to see, since the game as it is doesn't seem amazing. I really hope this update comes very soon, and I can't wait until it does.
Edit- Added Edits notes
Edit- I realize that this game is created by one person and I wrote this before realizing such, but I'm too lazy to change the entire thing so just take all that I say with a small grain of salt

Here's a review that will get lost in the deep dark.

So, here's what I think...
Hydroneer is a perfect game to pass some time. The price to time played ratio is pretty good. (at least for me)
The game as it is (as of December 2021) was really fun. The start is fairly simple and it's easy to learn. The progression is great because right when I wanted to give up grinding, I was able to progress more and get back into it. The grinding isn't long or hard. It's fairly easy once you know what you're doing. However, late game using logic and power is very confusing. There is no clear instruction on what to be doing. Now i'm not talking about a step-by-step manual. I'm just talking about the rules and small things that each item works with. For example, powered pumps have to have a powered water pump in order to work properly. Sure, you can go on YouTube and watch a video on how do it. But that's no fun for me. I like to figure things out, but not all of it. I prefer a hint or some clue on how things work, then going from there.

Moving on, the graphics and overall visual of the game is great. I love the steampunk but also cartoon-ish vibe. The overall aesthetics of the landscape, the markets, and the equipment are great. Kudos to the visual design team!

So what about the actual game play?
The game play is great, the idea of pan mining to automation is great. You start of with a pan, shovel, brush, and a bucket. The process of getting gems is very simple and self explanatory. Then turning in the mined gems to a collector for money. Using the money you get allows you to upgrade tools, build a base, and start automating. (or at least semi-automation)

Overall, this an awesome game for 10 bucks. I'm really hyped to 2.0 and i'm overall happy with my purchase. Keep going developers you're doing great!

So the terminal end is where you need a pipe, but that means you can't put a crusible or enough underneath the end to catch the materials, as they'll land on the pipe.  Dirt gets stuck on conveyers no matter how many fences you put up.  This is one of those games where it has novelty at first but after awhile you're just fighting the game engine rather than playing the game.

[h1]Интересный эксперимент с унылейшим результатом.[/h1]
Эксперимент заключается в том, что это игра без графического интерфейса и такого “пережитка условностей”, как инвентарь. Вы можете нести вещи в руке и только по 1 за раз. А это значит, что когда вам понадобится что-то продать или купить X вещей, то вам либо придётся бегать до города туда-сюда Х раз, либо приезжать на машине и сначала каждую вещь тащить и укладывать в машину, а потом по одной их вытягивать. По началу это вроде ок и даже чуть прикольно, но когда дело доходит до большой конструкции, даже думать не хочется о поездке в магазин. И не дай бог словить баг с рассыпанной кучей камней - вы будете их подбирать и переносить в ведро по одному 10 минут. Да, я понял идею с вёдрами, тележками, палетами, но всё это неудобно. Вместо решения задач, ты занимаешься бесконечной беготнёй, перетягиванием и тасканием. Я бы понял, если бы это была игра для VR, заточенная на таскание всего в реальных руках. Хотя, в таком случае, это было бы ещё хуже, т.к. отваливаться будет уже не палец на мышке, а вся рука.
Вторая часть эксперимента - это добыча ресурсов. Вторая оригинальная, но жуткая механика. Первые десятки минут выглядят так: берём лопату, кликаем в землю, кликаем в ведро, повторяем 4 раза, бросаем лопату (вы ещё и выкинуть её сможете не в любом месте), поднимаем ведро, подходим к миске, целимся и высыпаем из него землю, бросаем ведро, берём миску, идём к воде, бросаем миску в воду, достаём из воды, бросаем опять, находим щётку, кликаем в миску, что-то делаем с получившейся намытой рудой (бежим продавать или кидаем в переплавку) и повторяем-повторяем-повторяем. Почувствуй себя рабом на плантации! Можно найти какие-то хитрости, типа поставить кран, чтоб вода сама капала в миску. Или уже насобирав много ресурсов, построить конвейер для доставки земли. Но общая геморойность процесса уже на лицо.
Ну и главное разочарование - это не смотря, на названия Hydro, т.е. “вода”, вся водность игры заключается в том, что (кроме вышеописанного размачивания грязи в речке) нужно протянуть от речки трубу, которая запитывает всю технику. Никакой вам динамики жидкости, запруд, плотин, водяных мельниц или ещё какой-нибудь реальной игры с водой, которую можно было ожидать от игры с таким названием, тут нет.

Единственный плюс игры - это её цена. Можно дёшево посмотреть на занятный дизайнерский эксперимент, но играть в это больно и нудно. Если хотите игру про конвейеры и добычу ресурсов, в стиме куча значительно более адекватных вариантов.

Я знаю, что автор игры - одиночка и старается, как может и мне не хотелось его огорчать, но процент положительных отзывов здесь неадекватен, а мне жаль потраченного времени.

I wanted to like this game.  I was really looking forward to a voyage...  well..  a [i]staycation[/i] of engineering and discovery.  What I got was a lesson about why I should probably avoid anything that resembles a job simulator in the future.

I'll start with aggravation, and move on to disappointment in a minute.

Most games would not take the term "drop" quite so literally.  I'm not sure what the QoL benefit of a physics-based interaction system is supposed to be.  It certainly does add a frission of excitement when you eyeball the trajectory of your ore bucket incorrectly and pour a hundred nuggets against the side of a crucible, scattering them all over the floor.  Directly transferring stacks would be nice, but that would require at least a primitive inventory system.  Hydroneer does not have one, not even for money.  You can carry precisely one item (and 'wear' a helmet) at a time.  You are going to be running back and forth [i]a lot.[/i]  I mean, you could use the cart to move a few items at a time, but it's a pain to load and a pain to move.

Sometimes you will be unable to drop an object in a particular location [i]because reasons.[/i]  When this happens (and it's going to happen a lot) you will be rewarded with a Tim Allen style cave man upgrunt.  [i]This absolutely never gets old.  Ever.[/i]  The clattering of tools and items as you swap them around to sift through literal tonnes of dirt one shovelful at a time is similarly refreshing, creating a pleasantly jarring auditory backdrop to the angry grinding of your wrist and finger joints and the low throbbing drone of your fatigue-paralyzed parietal lobe.

But the reward is worth it, right?

Leonardo DiCaprio Laughing.JPG

There's no content.  [b]There is no content.[/b]  There's just more ways and places for you to do the same thing.  I mean, there's fishing, but you know why you go fishing?  It's so you can buy more equipment, so you can do the same thing [i]forever.[/i]  But there's a very limited quantity of modifiable terrain to mine out, so once that's all gone...  I guess it's game over?  You win/lose?  No, because there's a device which (as far as I can tell) makes more dirt so that you can keep on playing until the heat death of the universe.

I've played worse games, no question.  But this entire experience leans exclusively on an investment trap to keep you playing even when you're so very, very done with it.  Whatever dollar value you may place on Hydroneer, you will never get your wasted time back.

Hydroneer is one of those games which, on the surface, should actually be fun, and easy to play.  However the problem is, that while sure, it CAN be fun in spurts... it's more frustrating than anything.  What's more, it's as if the developer simply doesn't either have a clue how to fix the issues that players have... or has become so invested with his own goal for the end game that he simply ignores the issues.  

The number one issue this game has, is tied to its physics calculations. Which, if you know anything about the game itself, or what it claims to be, is a MAJOR problem. A problem which isn't really being addressed. The developer regularly posts streams about how he's making entirely new sections of the game... and yet never touches on the problems with physics.

It doesn't matter where you look, as a player you will inevitably run into physics issues with this game.  From things you just dropped being thrown off across the map due to the weird physics calculations; to vehicles like the mining truck simply being useless due to an inability to drive up a simple ramp.

Stop and think about that part people. A mining truck CAN NOT drive up a player placed ramp.  Now the truck doesn't just stop and sit there. Oh no, it will suddenly be punted into the air. If you're lucky, it comes back down in a place you can use it. Most of the time though this thing goes flying through the air and leaves you dizzy and frustrated.  All because the developer can't be bothered to go "oh, you know what, instead of doing this whole new expansion, let's sit down and put some serious time and work into fixing these physics issues." 

I want to like this game... really I do. However I can't. I've over 100 hours in it, and were it not so frustrating seeing my hard work just get exploded across the map because of some bad physics calculations; I like would have far more.

2.0 Update is out... now where to start.  It's... broken.  There seems to be a bug where, randomly, the game will decide to just completely wipe your save. So all the work you've done, regardless of how many hours you put into the game, just poof, it's like you never touched the thing. Also, all your tools, money, and everything is gone, forcing you to start over and completely forget that save.

Compound that with tools like the 'hand sorter' that either yeets things over the pans you put down, or just decides to lag out and spill everything on the ground,  a curious, if not mind numbingly annoying decision to make players go on a hunt to figure out where the previously easy to find, and equally easy to use stock markets locations,  and an overall inflation of prices of the various better tools... and I'm starting to wonder why I even bother with the game.  Realistically speaking, were it even possible at this point, I'd request a refund, because I really don't want to bother with the headache of dealing with a game that's so buggy, and so very poorly thought out.  Buyer beware.  The game is NOT worth the price that's being asked.

I will say this, remember the mining truck? Well they fixed its ability to go up, or down a ramp.  And by fixed, I mean completely removed it from the game.  Which unless you particularly like using various expensive mining drills, or having to move a load of dirt by hand... makes the game so tedious that it's just not worth bothering with.  It's as if the developers looked at the game and said "Well we can't fix this, so eh, scrap it."  They claim to have 'more coming'... but given how they said "We'll have multiplayer" and then gave users a janky kind of split screen... something that games stopped doing in the 90's... well I don't hold out much hope of them actually fulfilling their promises.

That's probably what angers me the most.  The developers promise, promise, promise... and never really deliver.  It's like they expect you, the purchaser, to be dumb enough to accept whatever junk they throw at a wall in the hopes that something... anything... sticks.  Sadly, there's a lot of people out there who do just that, which in turn leads to things like that janky, failure of a multi player.  It's not hard to do multiplayer in unity. Other games have done full on multi player, and didn't have to default to split screen.  So what was the difference here?  

In the end, this "major update" is little more than "Added 2 new areas to mine, removed useful mining vehicles,  moved/hid sell points, and jacked the prices on machines up enough to make the grind even worse."  It's not an update, but little better than a 'content patch'.

Edit 2.

Oh it only gets worse. I mean seriously. The developer can't seem to figure out what he wants to actually do. Now a game that is marketed as a mining game... is delving into FARMING?  Come on Dev, pick something and stick with it!

The more these non-updates come out, that keep changing whatever direction the game is going in, the more I start to think that the game is just some kind of scam aimed at milking users for all the cash he can.  Always changing the direction of the game when popularity starts falling of.

Run, don't walk, RUN from this one as fast as you can. It's not worth it.

Edit:  So, here's a new 'update' to this review. Something you should seriously consider prior to even looking at the game.

Whatever you do, you must only say good things about the game in the discussions... else you'll get banned. Now, sure, I know that banning any dissenting comments, or even users from a Steam Discussion is directly against Valve's own rules for developers.... but based off my own recent experience where I dared answer a question honestly about whether or not the game, in its current state, is even worth buying with an unequivocal no... I have now been banned from the discussions. I do plan on contacting Valve in regards to this behavior though.

I do not regret the purchase, at the low sale price, but at 8 hours across two sessions, I've reached the point at which I can see my future with the game, and it is... The same, minus the generic logic-gate fiddling every sandbox building game seems to add for those who enjoy getting a little technical.

I went from a bad shovel to a slightly better shovel, I ran a short pipe network down my hole in the ground so I could rinse for larger gold and gems at the site of deeper digging (although 'deep' here means very little - you can only dig in predefined locations that are essentially a trough the size and depth of a small swimming pool)...

I assembled one of each item on the anvil, sold them for money enough to buy everything I could need from the initial shop.

I can reliably make quite a lot of money and could, feasibly, with a little work buy all of the incrementally better things, or set up a row of conveyors, or compress gems, or drive a slightly different truck, or pull a slightly different cart. If I wanted to crawl my way over to a new dig site or the distant town where you can buy more advanced and expensive gadgets that feel like solutions lacking a problem - you'd invest 10x as much time earning the money and arranging these items as they could ever possibly save for you, as the game lacks the complexity or resource variety of challenge to make them relevant.

There's no sense of any overarching goal or meaning, there's no implied mystery, no discovery, no motivation other than small, steady profits. The idea of being a prospector, a miner, a trader of finely crafted jewellery or weapons is *exciting*, but there's no exploration, no gamble, no surprises here at all. It feels more like a themepark about that concept, in which children can dig in the little pit to find the pre-placed fake gems then pay at the gift shop to keep them.

I knew I was buying a game without any sort of pressures (.. other than in the pipes, o ho ho ho.. ) for survival, without tension or challenge - but I didn't anticipate that the game would lack any sense of discovery or meaningful progression/achievement.

I will be forever shuffling buckets around and clicking far too many times to achieve basic interactions, which becomes genuinely uncomfortable on the hands after a while.

I had a nice few hours, but I already feel like Hydroneer has nothing more to offer, no lure or hook to keep me going.

Also had some major performance drops (easily fixed by restarting the game every hour or two, resuming perfect framerates), some physics glitches, some valuable objects flying 200ft into the treeline because I clicked three pixels off and moved something it was leaning on, and some serious bugs with the key rebinding.

I'd say Hydroneer is a nice toy for an evening or two, but only those who really want the ultimate in formulaic crafting-tasks will want to keep going for very long, as the game lacks depth, sense of purpose, variety or any of the excitement you might expect from prospecting and mining. You can't dig deep, you can't choose where you dig, you can't strike it rich or get lucky or find trouble. 

A cute, but very shallow game. In a literal sense.

A pipe is a tubular section or hollow cylinder, usually but not necessarily of circular cross-section, used mainly to convey substances which can flow — liquids and gases (fluids), slurries, powders and masses of small solids. It can also be used for structural applications; hollow pipe is far stiffer per unit weight than solid members.

In common usage the words pipe and tube are usually interchangeable, but in industry and engineering, the terms are uniquely defined. Depending on the applicable standard to which it is manufactured, pipe is generally specified by a nominal diameter with a constant outside diameter (OD) and a schedule that defines the thickness. Tube is most often specified by the OD and wall thickness, but may be specified by any two of OD, inside diameter (ID), and wall thickness. Pipe is generally manufactured to one of several international and national industrial standards.[1] While similar standards exist for specific industry application tubing, tube is often made to custom sizes and a broader range of diameters and tolerances. Many industrial and government standards exist for the production of pipe and tubing. The term "tube" is also commonly applied to non-cylindrical sections, i.e., square or rectangular tubing. In general, "pipe" is the more common term in most of the world, whereas "tube" is more widely used in the United States.

Both "pipe" and "tube" imply a level of rigidity and permanence, whereas a hose (or hosepipe) is usually portable and flexible. Pipe assemblies are almost always constructed with the use of fittings such as elbows, tees, and so on, while tube may be formed or bent into custom configurations. For materials that are inflexible, cannot be formed, or where construction is governed by codes or standards, tube assemblies are also constructed with the use of tube fittings.

Usually games that have minimal interfaces/HUDs are due to lazy developers or just someone looking for a quick buck.  Hydroneer is the first game I've played with absolutely no HUD (which also means no inventory) but it feels right.  Yeah, you'll do a lot of running around, but you'll soon adapt to using buckets, pallets, and vehicles to move goods around instead of some magical unlimited inventory.

It starts off very slow and a bit repetitive, but getting used to the mechanics is essential.  After a couple hours you can afford to build some pipes that can fill up 6+ pans at one time, greatly streamlining the process.  Do that for another couple hours and you can afford your first plot of land and some machinery.  Start digging, because the deeper you go, the more money you make.

The game is extremely addicting once you "get it", and I almost refunded it, then I played 30 hours in the span of 5 days.  Now the endgame is pretty lacking - once you go 4 goliaths/D.A.V.I.D.s, you make more money than you can spend.  I feel like that's where the real early access begins since there's not much point in getting bigger.

Games that are even slightly similar (Dyson Sphere Program, Satisfactory, Factorio, etc.) you always had bigger and better things to work towards - Hydroneer is lacking in that progression.  But this is after 30 hours of very addictive gameplay.

So I highly recommend it; for ten bucks, 30 hours is a good price and the developer is very active, so there's a bright future for it as well.

I love this game, but there are a few issues that kind of irk me a bit. 
Firstly, the vehicles are SO unwieldy. I wish there was a vehicle that responded better to turning than the hydrotrucks (original and mk.2) do. 
Secondly, if you're like me and prefer to hoard your shards in the beginning, hopefully you have a good computer because those things will TANK your framerate. It's unfortunate that I have to turn off "save raw resources", reload my game, and then have to collect the shards all over again just so that my eyes don't explode from the game running like a potato. 
Third, can y'all find a way to stop carts from yeeting themselves into oblivion? I learned the hard way that carts and pallets don't mix, and lost over 15k in coins because my cart decided that it didn't want to see my face anymore.
Lastly, I wish there was a "get up" button when the use the regular bed/cot thing. I don't know if it's just me, but if I don't time when I click to get up, the day/night cycle just keeps going by and I have to bring the game out of fullscreen, wait a bit, and then bring it back just for the game to respond. 
I'm well aware that this game doesn't have all the kinks worked out yet and that the devs are working their butts off to make that happen. Below are some of the things that aren't glitches or things that annoy me in the game, but are things I'd appreciate if they were added.
1. The "land for sale" sign crossing out the names of the properties when you buy them.
2. Maybe make the other properties a little more flat so that the excavator can work a little more efficiently instead of bouncing all over the place.
3. More ores/gems/things to craft. It'd help when beginning a new game to have a little more variety in what you can do.
4. Improved goliath drills. It'd be nice if goliath drills didn't break so easily, especially if you're like me and prefer to only go into bridgepour to buy things for your mine.
5. Some context or a guidebook for the logic/power side of things. I haven't even TOUCHED that aspect of the game yet because I don't wanna look up a tutorial for it.
6. A bank to store your coins. It's a little annoying to have to carry your coins around with you everywhere, especially if you want to set some aside for something (ie. new equipment) and leave the rest for buying other things like the materials for a house. 
Overall, I'd give this game a 7/10.

review:
I really love this game and the only reason I don't have more hours is that I'm waiting for the 2.0 update.

If you like games like Satisfactory and Astroneer, but are open to playing something slightly more grounded, then you'll probably enjoy this.

Pros (for me, these are subjective):
- I like the lack of inventory. It's too silly in other factory games that you can carry an entire cargo ship's worth of stuff in your inventory. In Hydroneer, you can only carry one thing at a time, meaning you have to be a bit smarter about moving things around. This takes some getting used to but ultimately I enjoyed the challenge it creates.
- I like that all the dirt, ores, stones etc are actually just loose objects in the world and can fall off conveyors or miss their outputs. It takes a bit more effort to make a "perfect" factory in Hydroneer, which leads to enjoyably trying to diagnose issues and optimise your layout to fix them. Other factory games have 100% perfect conveyance.
- There's quite a lot of different parts you can use to automate your setup. It's fun because the different drills have different constraints, so not every automation setup is necessarily the same.
- I found the game relaxing to play. There's no time constraints, and it's hard to make mistakes that you can't undo. The biggest mistake you can make that I can think of is overinvesting in parts that you don't need, but that's hard to do by accident. 

Cons:
- The game doesn't tell you what to do at all. This can be OK sometimes if there's still a fairly obvious path to follow (looking at you, Astroneer), but in Hydroneer, I had NO idea where to even start. I recommend watching LetsGameItOut's YouTube video on Hydroneer as he gives some early tips. Hybridsteel's YouTube channel is also helpful if you want more in depth help. Consider also joining the official slack workspace, the community managers are extremely helpful if you have questions.
- The balancing is not quite right. Early game can be a bit arduous (you're gonna fill a LOT of buckets with dirt and scrub them), which is fine, I like a bit of a grind. But once you automate a bit more of the process, you'll very suddenly be sitting on more money than you know what to do with. There are lots of parts to buy, so the natural next step is to build a better setup with higher output. Then you'll have even mooore money than you'll ever need. I think some of the motivation here has to come from within in terms of pushing yourself to build better setups. I would just say that the upside to every setup giving you more money than you need is that there's no particular pressure to build a particular setup - just do what sounds fun to you.

Anyway I would highly recommend this to fans of the genre! I'm really looking forward to playing the 2.0 version when that is ready. I don't usually write steam reviews but I think this game deserves more positive attention. There's a lot of really whiny reviews here complaining about bugs (it's an indie game with complex physics guys! Be reasonable) or feature incompleteness. I was still able to get more than my money's worth out of this and that's without the big update that is incoming.

Hey! This issue is actually related to a broken mod someone created, not the devs fault :(
Here's how to fix your issue:

Sometimes mods can break Hydroneer. Please follow both sets of instructions to ensure all mods are removed.
Steam Workshop Mods
• Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
• Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER and delete the contents:
%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1106840
NOTE: Sometimes the Steam Workshop folder isn't there for Hydroneer. If the folder cannot be found, then you do not need to worry about this step, please continue.
Manually Installed (Legacy) Mods
• Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
• Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER and delete the contents:
%localappdata%\Mining\Saved\Paks

If this has helped you please consider changing your review, it really helps us out!
