Josh from Let's Game It Out convinced me to buy this game. For ten bucks, I've had a great deal of fun with it.

Pros: The game has a LOT of promise. Water-powered machinery is a novel idea, IMO. The art style is also pretty distinct, and everything has a sort of rough and rustic feel to it that I am fond of. If the devs keep at it like they said they have, then I could see this game becoming something akin to a steampunk version of Satisfactory.

Cons: To start off with, the lack of content at the moment. There's no NPCs, and the world feels very lonely as a result. You can get to the current endgame fairly quickly, and I managed to get there in about a week of playing off and on. The game also has weird performance issues that appear over time, with framerate DROPS that vanish when I exit out to the menu and reload. I have an Intel i9 and an RTX 2080, so I can say with confidence that its not my hardware. My guess is that it pertains to some memory leak happening in the background that remains unpatched.

With all that said, and if you have a spare ten bucks, Hydroneer is a fun little automation toy for a weekend or three, if that's your jam.

I'm honestly torn about leaving a negative comment, because I have actually enjoyed playing this game... it's just that there are more negatives than positives for me in this game as it is.

It's very grind-y in the beginning, which I love, but then it's also very easy - almost too easy - to set yourself up with an automated mining place and making big bucks for no real reason. I mean there's nothing to really spend your money on besides expanding your automatic mining "factory" but even then it just makes your game lag more than it's worth.

I really do love smelting my ores and weighing them to see how much they're worth - I almost feel compulsive about having to make weapons or jewelry that are worth more than my last! .. but after a while it feels really pointless because it's basically the only thing I do in this game since everything is already running on it's own. I usually end up playing on my phone with this game going in the background on my computer.. and that's not really cool. 

It also needs some readjustments for snapping things to place - some times it feels like I've spent most of my time in this game trying to get my pipes in the right place. It is incredibly frustrating sometimes, especially when you haven't hammered something into place and accidentally pick it up again (lmao)
Collision is also crazy in this game - things will fly and bounce away into nothingness very frequently. 
I'm also experiencing some of the worst lag ever recently - out of nowhere - when I start my machines up. Like it's so bad I can't do anything!
All in all, I will probably come back to see how this game is doing in a near future, and will hopefully be able to leave a more positive comment on here! I very much love the concept of this game and I don't regret spending money on it!
I hate pressing the "no" on wheter or not I recommend this game, because I know there are people who have better patience than I do with the things I find negative in the game. I do recommend people to at least try the game out - but for the purpose of my comment I'll tick the "no" for now.

First and foremost: worth every penny of the $10 regular price. If it's ever on sale, absolutely give it a try. But even if it's not, I don't regret paying $10 for this game.

On with the Monty.

Imagine coming in from an hour-long snowball fight, during which you had no gloves, and sitting down to play Super Mario Bros 2 on the original NES. Playing Hydroneer feels like that. You can't feel your fingers, but your brain still thinks it knows the right amount of "thrust" to send in order to tap the A button to jump. Unfortunately, the feedback that triggers your brain to "stop" doesn't get sent back from the thumb, so about every eighth button-press results in your thumb popping out straight, and the controller flying out of your hand.

Don't get me wrong: I understand this is a one-man dev job. HUGE props. You're in the middle of creating a masterpiece here, on-par with Satisfactory or Factorio (no sarcasm or exaggeration intended: I fully expect Hydroneer will be as good as both those games). The ideas and mechanics here are just SO easy to fall in love with. In my opinion, this game should be going for $10 as Early Access, then rising to $25 at 1.0. But that ship has sailed, so I won't go on about it.

Having said all that, I have two very specific criticisms, both of which relate to one third of the game's control scheme (dropping stuff), and are pretty much game-breaking.

1: "precise drop" plain doesn't work. About every fifth time I "hold e" to "drop precisely," the game interprets the initial tap as a "press and release," and executes "just drop it."

It seems to me (and I have zero experience with developing with Unreal Engine) that the simplest way to fix that would be to create separate key bindings. So while (for example) "tap e" may mean "just drop it," "hold f" could mean "place it precisely."

If it could instead be simplified to the degree of "tap e" means "just drop it," unless an in-world object is highlighted, in which case "tap e" would mean "drop it on/in the highlighted object," that would be even better. But I see the unusual control scheme as one of this game's strengths, so maybe separate bindings for "just drop it" and "place it carefully" would be just perfect.

2: When the "place precisely" operation does work, it does this thing where the object being placed rotates according to the camera's orientation, rather than orienting with gravity. This makes it really difficult to (for example) drop the bucket so I can later drop other things into it. Not impossible, but challenging.

In closing, I just want to re-iterate: for a one-man dev team, this is really impressive. I know it's "only" an Unreal Engine "mod," but to be perfectly candid, all that matters is the finished product. Hydroneer is going to be a genre-defining game when it's finished. I personally wish the dev had gone the early access route, but there's still enough buzz around YouTube (Let's Game It Out, amiright?) that I'm sure Hydroneer will be a success.

I have enjoyed myself while playing this relaxing game. At first, I didn't realize that the gold and iron bars you craft in the game just store a value and can have an endless worth. I first tried only smelting 5 ores into a bar, then did 10. I played for a good 10 hours before realizing that I don't need to smelt more than one bar of each type and that I could just keep smelting the bars together. The cauldrons are limitless and will never fully fill up, this breaks immersion alittle for me and I would have liked to be forced to create multiple cauldrons than just 1 per resource. 

The game does allow for some decent complexity when creating an automatic system of mining, but I feel that once you get to a certain point, mining just becomes pointless because of the amount of money you rack in. There is definitely a point in time where you can't dig enough because you need the money to upgrade automation efforts and then suddenly you have all the money in the world but nothing to spend it on. I would have loved to have achievements in game so that I had something to work towards like obtaining a million coins or such. I found myself mostly watching my machines work at the end and enjoying the sounds of them knowing I did most of this from my own brush and wash pan. Having more craftables would be amazing.  

All in all. I'd give this game a 8/10.

They all have horrible fps, talk about it regularly, and constantly shut down their machines to do clean up because of it.  3. Lo adquirí en las ofertas de verano, luego de jugar varias horas, creo que es momento de dar una opinión, una respuesta rápida, es que POR AHORA NO se puede recomendar, en la próxima actualización (2.0) muy probablemente SI. 

Pro:
- Su precio (y más en oferta).
- La idea del juego.
- La cantidad de contenido que tiene el juego.
- Detalles como por ejemplo el hecho de poder pesar los lingotes, inspeccionar con la lupa...
- Se pueden sacar muchas horas (muchísimas) en este juego (siempre tengas en cuenta las cosas malas y/o las arreglen).

Contra:
- No hay ningún tipo de tutorial ingame, es decir, que si quieres un tutorial, el juego te deja un vídeo y su wiki. Para entender muchas de las cosas lo he descubierto gracias a mirar vídeos/gameplays...
- La optimización... Cuando ya estás avanzando en el juego y tienes 4 maquinas para intentar automatizar, el juego por extraña razón va de 5 a 30 fps como mucho (que ojo, importante, tampoco utiliza todos los recursos del PC al menos en mi caso).
- Bugs... Tiene bugs, bugs, que bueno, no pasan mucho, pero entre que los fps te caen en picado y de golpe ves como la tierra o algún objeto se va volando a saber a que zona... Llegas a un punto que te acabas cansando... Como también cuando tienes todo automatizado y que los crisoles, por extraña razón, no fundan el hierro o el oro...

Posibles cosas a mejorar:
- Un tutorial ingame es necesario para este juego, cuando empiezas la partida (y que sea opcional, claro) y probablemente también para la automatización con las máquinas.
- Los controles creo que se pueden mejorar, al principio cuesta mucho acostumbrarse.
- La construcción, está bien, pero se puede mejorar mucho la verdad (como por ejemplo, tener objetos/maquinas en el aire, como que volando)
- El mapa, creo que se puede trabajar mejor y poderle dar mayor uso.
- El mismo sonido que hace cuando sueltas cualquier objeto al suelo, sinceramente, cansa mucho este sonido.
- La conducción.

En conclusión, la idea del juego está muy bien, es más, el juego también lo está y hay que tener en cuenta que cuesta menos de 10€ y con oferta todavía es más barato, pero tener que jugar a 5-30 fps por la mala optimización o perder objetos/lingotes (que se van volando por un bug) que te cuesta su rato conseguir... Para mi opinión, lo mejor que se puede hacer ahora es esperar a la actualización 2.0 que en teoría se optimizará el juego, habrá multijugador, nuevas zonas...

[Updated July 2024. This review is mostly unchanged, but I have removed two issues that have been rectified.]

This no is one of those "maybe" nos that would have been a maybe if Steam had an option for maybe. I really want to like Hydroneer, but I'm just not able to.

There are several nice things to say about Hydroneer. I like the premise, where you are mining for minerals in the ground to grow your economy and build your empire. The graphics are quaint and appealing enough, and the world is clearly made with love. However, there are many aspects where Hydroneer falls short.

First of all, there are the fundamental problems. The most fundamental are the grindiness of the game and the lack of direction. I like slow burn games, but it may not be for everyone. And what's the point of doing this? Stardew Valley at least gives you an excuse for a direction and a purpose for what you are doing.

Perhaps the biggest problem is that it is hard to know what things do, and you are punished for experimenting. There is no way to sell back things you buy but realize you don't need. That is a big problem when you may have spent a long time grinding to be able to afford that item you just wasted your money on. The tool-tips only give a vague idea of what something does rather than all the specifics, and the official wiki often just mirrors the in-game tool-tips.

Another fundamental issue is the inventory-less design. I get the choice, but simple doesn't mean easy. Often this simpleness comes with a cost for the player in terms of frustration. Why can't I pick up something with my other hand? And since a pallet is meant to be the solution to this, why does it cost 450 money?! The inventory-less design would be fine if you had an "off-hand slot" and/or the possibility to put money in your own pocket (in a non-corrupt way).

Second, there are many quality of life issues that quite simply should have been taken care of. Auto-rotate pipes when placing them into a configuration that makes sense. Help buckets land the right way. Don't make items fly all over the place.

To sum up: Hydroneer isn't a [i]bad[/i] game, and you may get some enjoyable playtime out of it. However, it's not for everyone and it's sadly not for me.

I can't recommend it for the reasons i am about to list. The reason I've played for 48 hours was mostly building a massive building only to find out most of it was pointless and it realistically could have been a third of the size, due to the lack of anything to do with all that space. Hauling resources back to my dig/build site was one of the most tedious things I've ever done. Get your first automated miner--> grinder--> sorter--> smelter and from then on you are pretty much printing money and never need to add anything more to your machinery. There are not many decorations, hardly enough to decorate a single room without spamming the same thing over and over. And ultimately there is a lack of endgame content. Finding all the relics and unlocking the secret was kind of a huge letdown for the time and effort spent. And ultimately there wasn't much cool logic tech to play with, at least nothing even remotely useful other than the auto repair system.

Yeah, life is a journey and not a destination, but while the grind was fun and there are some cool things to play with (Nukes were actually surprisingly cool, watching all your machinery working is pleasing to see chunks of ore passing through) There was not enough to continue playing, or justify doing anything more.

If there were a multitude more decorations, a need to continue running your machinery or improving it, more pieces to that machinery, and a better end game goal to work towards, then i could justify playing it or recommending it... as is i would recommend you just play Minecraft or something else for the mining, and either Factorio or Satisfactory for the automation. These games have set high standards, and while the simplicity of Hydroneer is a nice change of pace you can't compete with what those other games offer.

Hey Mrfanaticfox
Thanks for your review. I have some good news, we have exactly what you're looking for (as well as some MAJOR optimizations coming in the next update) 

We're currently testing an experimental potato-mode for Hydroneer. This makes the GPU use less processing power, the CPU usage will remain the same.
What is Potato mode?!
This makes the GPU use less processing power, the CPU usage will remain the same.
- This will improve FPS for low-end machines with the exchange for worse graphics.
- This version will mainly benefit people with fast CPU and slow GPU.
- This does NOT make drills/conveyors easier to run.
- This isn't the optimisations for 2.0, those will be a lot better without the loss of visuals.
Sounds great! How do I get it?
Potato Mode is an opt-in 'beta' for Hydroneer on Steam.
- Open Steam, go to your library.
- Right click Hydroneer and click 'Properties'.
- Now click 'Beta' on the left menu.
- Enter givemefpspls in the access code box and click 'Check Code'.
- You should now have access to the potato-mode branch, if it isn't already selected, select it in the list just above where you typed the code in.
- Now you should see Hydroneer [potato-mode] in your Steam library.

Hey! Have you previously installed mods? 
Sometimes mods can break Hydroneer. Please follow both sets of instructions to ensure all mods are removed.
Steam Workshop Mods
• Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
• Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER and delete the contents:
%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1106840
NOTE: Sometimes the Steam Workshop folder isn't there for Hydroneer. If the folder cannot be found, then you do not need to worry about this step, please continue.
Manually Installed (Legacy) Mods
• Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
• Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER and delete the contents:
%localappdata%\Mining\Saved\Paks

For the price, it scratches that dwarven itch well enough. It's janky, and has the occasional killer bug, but overall it's quite playable. The no-inventory mechanic is unusual, but fits in with the overall gameplay easy enough once you get used to it. It does seem a little unbalanced in some ways - digging deeper only gets you more of the same resources, so it's entirely possible to amass considerable Hydrocoins just using basic gear and patience. I made ~350,000 coins in my 20 hours of muddling about with a half-dozen rams and some crafting - more than enough to propel me into end-game territory. A few gripes include no tools to level land out, and the janky physics. 
I'd give it a solid 6.5/10.

This game is so weird. It was interesting at first to try to get the machines to work together, but it doesn't at all work how you'd think it should. The dirt clumps and "dirt economy" or whatever, is bizarre; from the frustrating clumping behavior of the dirt clumps, to their movement on the equipment, the way the drills don't actually work the plot, then dirt creation devices, it just doesn't make any sense. 

The hydraulic pressure, of all things, is calculated in an odd and annoying way. The awkward connections and routing of each machine's inputs, outputs and plumbing forces complexity. The machines are messy, materials do not reliably pass into and out of them, materials fall through parts and collect unseen beneath them, many parts like funnels don't really fit or work together, it's all very strangely designed. My truck and items glitch out. Even when clean of rubble, the performance is stuttering, very poor optimization.

I'm told that there's fresh manpower on this project to build an update, but I remain skeptical. 
I can't recommend it without many significant improvements.

Don't expect a lot from this game.

The game as it exists now is worth a few dollars and I had a fun time playing it, but I'm probably going to wait and come back later. 

There are a few issues, which I'll get to, but my main complaint is the feeling of progression. The big draw in industry games like Factorio is that you are constantly moving forward; unlocking new materials, making new machines, optimizing previous areas, growing and growing forever. With Hydroneer, I felt like I'd seen all the content in the first area. Once I had a system that worked well, I had more than enough money to buy whatever I wanted, and didn't feel compelled whatsoever to buy new plots or investigate new ways to increase production. Right when the steamroller starts moving, it has nowhere to go. There are only a handful of materials and they aren't needed for upgrades or anything, so I just felt like I was done. 

There are other problems. The game is poorly optimized and it's way too easy to bring things to a crawl just playing normally. How water pressure works is poorly explained and also doesn't respond how you expect trying to do something like add another intake pipe. The inventory system is bad in that it doesn't exist, you can hold one item at a time otherwise you have to use a vehicle or a cart.  Even money is a physical object, which is just a pain to deal with. Because of this you have to use vehicles to haul stuff, which MIGHT feel immersive if they didn't have among the worst handling of any video game I've ever played. Additionally, vehicles are prone to exploding into the air and spiraling out of control doing simple things like ascending a small incline, and they'll also come to an instant stop if you clip even a pixel of something with collision. 

Aside from vehicles,  controls in general also aren't the best. Some actions use E and some use a left click, and it's easy to confuse the 2 and make terrible errors that dump resources everywhere which is not fun to try and clean up. To make collecting those small items easier there is a magnet, but it doesn't discriminate and you'll end up with a big mass that's pulled dirt off your production line along with every other resource and then you have to deal with that. 

The game world also feels empty. You go to towns to buy and sell things but there aren't any NPCs. You put your money in a bucket and hit a button and then you can take the item. Just using a more traditional shop structure with an NPC would do a lot to make the world feel more alive. 

All this said, the game is fun. The core mechanics of digging, selling ore, slowly buying better equipment until you have a smoothly running extremely productive machine is very good. Using pipes that occupy space, and only having limited connection options for them, make building your operation like a puzzle. It's a great, unique experience unlike other games in this genre I've played. 

I think this game has a lot of room to be something really special, and in it's current state it's worth a few dollars. You could probably spend a decent amount of time with it if you aren't as addicted to incremental progression as I am. I'll definitely be keeping my eye on it in the future to see where it goes.

Immediate early game is painfully tedious - forced tp repeatedly perform the manual action of shovelling dirt to wash, which you will do exactly NEVER after the first hour or two of the game. It's THAT bad. This part exists solely to push towards automation while forcing past a refund window to get into the actual game.
Early game consists of buying two basic machines and waiting for them to make enough to build a proper setup.
Late game consists of building a singular setup, then removing and rebuilding that exact same setup twice more further underground each time.
Latest game (bar DLC) consists of running around the map going to NPCs to hand them their specific wanted item for a set value reward - a pair of separate currencies required for the better items (as opposed to being able to provide larger items for extra rewards, like the entire previous time you've been playing, these come in smaller set amounts)
The lack of an inventory system and graphical issues greatly demerit the game as well.
Especially when to get a functional inventory you either need to A: drive around in a truck, which doesn't help at shops or around your base.
B: carry around a cart or pallet, which are slightly better for shops, but actively SLOW your movement (and obscure your vision, in the case of a loaded pallet).
Even the nostalgia of seeing let's game it out play the game doesn't override how much I disliked this. The man has incredible patience.

I'm cool with games with upgrade systems, but not when the "system" is "tediously rebuild your entire base the exact way it was multiple times, doing so one item by one item".

If you're looking for a game to just kill time with, it's a fun game.

Pros:
-You can buy land, build a house, and build a literal gold mine

-Great time killer

-Very linear on how it works so, it's easy to understand


Cons:
-Sort of a heavy hitter on the FPS side of things, don't underestimate this small game in terms of PC power. I can normally run MOST games on "Ultra" and never have an issue. However, this is a bit of a doozy if there is to much going on in one location. *Note: One thing I did find out that if have a lot of "non-placed or locked in" things in one area it can drastically reduce your fps on that reason alone, so if you're going to buy a lot of things at once, make sure when you unload them to "left-click them in place"

-The smelters... Ah, the smelters. This is probably my 2nd biggest complaint about this game... Smelters can't handle a lot of ore going into them at once, the "smelt-speed" is not instant, as there is a "small delay" to the point that if you have A LOT of ore going in at once, it'll only smelt some of it. To that end, the left over will just hover AS ORE in your smelter and over time turn into A LOT of ore un-smelted inside your smelter.
(You'll have to see it for yourself, if you don't understand what I mean)

-The buying system. This is my biggest complaint about this game. The buy system is INSANELY BAD for the amount of buying you have to do in this game. You'll see a lot of people complaining about the game not having an "inventory or stash box" but for me, not being able to buy multiple things at once or hell even have the "buy pallet" have a *no collision mode would be preferable to what it is now.. You literally have to pick up one item at a time, move it to the buy pallet, and then buy up to the point where you run out of space, then move those things you just paid for onto a truck. It's a tedious system for how much you literally have to buy for how far the stores are from your plot of land.
*Collision and Non Collision are exactly that. Collision is where you can only buy a certain amount, within the space given... As things will collide with each other. Non Collision(as far as I know the bed of trucks are the only place that have a non collision zone. Hydroneer is a medieval building game crossed with steampunk, to put it lightly. Your objective is to dig for iron, gold, gems, shards and cloutium to turn into jewelry, weapons and other sellables and make money out of it. This money is then spent on buying tools, machinery, vehicles, building materials, etc. to expand your operations.

[h1]Full Review[/h1]

You start off with nothing but a basic shovel, a brush and some pans for dirt and water: the classic gold digging method. You have to constantly shovel dirt in your pan, add water and scrub for the goodies. This is no way to make some good coin! So what do you do? You forge your found iron and gold into a sword and a ring and sell them at the jeweler in town. You bring a visit to the local equipment shop and buy a couple of pipes. You then install these pipes at the river so that you no longer have to scoop water into your pan: you can just put it under a tap. This allows you to scrub for resources much more quickly. 

Let this form of progress set the tone for the game: you constantly expand your operations with new machinery and improved logistics that make your base a little better each time, turning manual labour into machine works, allowing you to focus on more things. The equipment and machinery available is moderately rich in variety, such as automatic drills, conveyor belts, pipe systems, housing items, power and Logic (the game's electronics). Especially the latter, the power and Logic system, albeit simple, has quite an arrangement of powerful options that can both improve your current setup as well as build impressive new setups.

What's interesting about this game is that there's no inventory system. Everything (absolutely everything) has to be carried from A to B manually. Of course, you do have logistic tools to help you out in that such as tractors, pallets and carts, but you still have to load those by hand. This is both a breath of fresh air and a curse. It makes building your base and transporting more items to it feel more rewarding but at a certain point in time, especially when you have serious cash to flash, it can become tedious and feel like wasted time.

On items, because of the nature of the game, collision is an issue. Items that touch the world or other items in a weird way have the tendency to be shot away at high speed, glitch through objects or in other ways disappear. I've had several items fly away and I haven't yet found them back. This is especially frustrating when it happens to a valuable item (small tip: be careful with crafting battleaxes!).

One of the more major shortcomings of this game I find, is the exponential increase in your wealth. You start off incredibly poor, struggling even for basic items and equipment and having to do a lot of manual labour, and then suddenly the switch flips and you're a millionaire with a completely automatic digging, refining, sorting and smelting process to boot. After reaching that point of wealth (which comes sooner than you realize), the motivation to keep improving my base began to wane. You could argue that if you simply like the game, you'd keep building regardless of that, but for me personally I want to feel like what I do is worth it in the form of a reward, e.g. a really expensive piece of machinery or something else to look forward to, to [b]build[/b] towards.

The game's optimization has some issues when it comes to how long the game is running. It normally runs pretty smooth but every half hour till an hour, I find myself reloading the save because the FPS dropped to something like 30-40 FPS while I have a pretty powerful PC (that is with graphics set to low and resource saving to off). It's a mild nuisance.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]

For an eight euro game, this is a little gem, good for a couple dozen hours, if not more. The devs are active, their Discord server is helpful, mods are supported and more content is coming, multiplayer included! The game's content/price ratio is very good and the future looks promising. It has some flaws, but they're not game-breaking and will most likely be ironed out in the future.

If you like building games, especially in the style of Factorio and Satisfactory, this game will most likely strike your interests.

Hydroneer is a sandbox mining game, a very impressive effort for a single indie dev. It feels rough around the edges, but can be quite immersive and relaxing. You start out with a shovel and a pan, then move up to building an automated system all running on hydro power. It's worth trying if you like those kinds of games, although you'll need to be a bit forgiving. It's a very slow start and there's no inventory system, including for money - which means you have to pick up and move everything by hand, and you can't carry your money and the thing you just bought at the same time. If you do put a few hours into it, it's satisfying to see automation coming together, but there's no end game.

[b]Pros[/b]
- Relaxing background music
- Satisfying mining, once you get the hang of it
- Landscaping system
- Robust 3D building system (minus the bug mentioned below)
- Conveyor/automated mining systems
- The minimalist interface is annoying, but it is immersive and unusual

[b]Cons[/b]
- Going to town to buy things is tedious. Especially given that you have to pick up each item drop it in the cart, pay for it, pick it up, drop it in the truck, drive home, pick it up, carry the item and place them all individually.
- I was hoping to discover that there were multiple kinds of ores (other than just iron and gold), or new things you could create and sell. Unfortunately it looks like everything you find in the first digging area is everything in the game. New shops don't open, no new items to build.
- I really get the feeling that it should be made for VR - it would be perfect with the whole "no inventory" system and simplistic art style. Unfortunately not.
- Even once I got flat concrete surfaces, items often fall over instead of standing upright when you drop them
- No in-game tutorial or intro. There's a 3 minute video - but other than that you're entirely on your own
- No achievements, which might have given some goals for what to do
- It's kinda weird that everything in the game looks medieval, but you start with a modern day diesel truck. It would have been better to stick with just the wooden cart
- The towns feel really empty with no people in them. Buildings are closed. Who am I selling this stuff to? Even if there were just NPC models that didn't talk, it'd help make it feel more alive
- No inventory system at all. It's a nice idea in principle, and it does add a sense of immersion, but it becomes annoying really quickly. For example, you have no pockets so you have to carry your coin stack in your hands. You also can't pick up more than one object at a time.
- I built a water pipe system, and no water came out the end. I removed and re-built each piece one by one, then it worked. Makes me think the underlying systems are rather buggy
Multiplayer pls

I find it difficult to describe Hydroneer, despite the simple gameplay itself. The goal of the game, as such is to dig and as far as i can tell, this is its only purpose.

You start with a shovel and a bucket, and all there is to do is to dig in order to dig. There doesn’t seem to be a goal, other than to dig more, get more money, buy better equipment and to keep digging. And this is why I struggle to describe Hydroneer, because it has no right to be as fun as it is.

There is no purpose or goal, other than to keep digging, unearthing dirt, washing the gold nuggets from the dirt, melting it into an ingot and selling it… eventually automating your process with machines.

Also quite positive is the dedication of the Dev to this title. They didn’t just abandon the game and it feels like its very much in active development.

So if you are looking for a casual game, in which your goal is to dig gold and gemstones out of the depth of the earth… then give this game a try.

The control scheme took a bit getting used to at first, but it works very well once you do. Even without a sale, the game’s price of admission is well worth it.

I'm torn on this game. I'd almost recommend it but ultimately no.

The good:
Art style is great
day/night cycle is nicely implemented
the pipework system is nice, automation works quite well

The bad:
bad snapping when placing things, specifically pipes and boxes
grindy with no real 'point' or end goal to work toward
terrain deformation is very jagged, no way to smooth things out
physics have a tendency to freak out (ore/gem explosions, flipping truck = rocket ship)
no real 'atmosphere', a handful of NPCs or little easter eggs would really brighten the world


The review:
After about 8 hours or so (probably a lot earlier) you can end up with a very simple drill/harvester/sorter/smelter combo. It'll churn out gold bars worth 10k after a short time, not to mention the iron and gems produced. Upkeep costs are tiny so there's no fear of things burning out before you turn a profit...

And that's the crux of the problem, getting cash is easy. So after a relatively short time you have a steady income and nothing to do with it. You're spitting out iron and gold bars and crafting them... but why? If you like the automation side of things then you can go balls to the wall and get stuck in with the conveyor systems and logic based items... 

but ultimately there's nothing to actually 'do' with the coins you make, it's grinding for it's own sake... essentially it's 'creative mode' but with extra steps

The snapping and object placement is a nightmare, all items can be picked up with a single keystroke, including the floor you're standing on. Locking stuff in place with a hammer that you have to remember the location of (when you inevitably put it down somewhere and forget about it) is a nightmare... worse still when you want to unlock an item for a 'quick' layout change.

Performance issues start becoming a thing when there's lots of loot items nearby, including in buckets/pans. If you accidentally dump a pan full of loot on the floor, physics goes nuts and makes some of it explode; flying 15 feet away.


That said, the initial grind from panning to basic automation is quite fun and digging underground like a mole feels pretty good.

Great game as is and well worth the price, but still being updated with content and optimization. Really easy to get into and  try new things. It has a "more than one way to skin a cat" kind of gameplay approaches. Nice helpful community too. Pretty casual game, not much learning curve, but can be a bit slow to start out for beginners. Once you make a rig that spits out plenty of ore the challenge turns from making money planning a build, hauling the inventory to a plot, and problem solving.

The no inventory minimal UI theme of this game is what I think is the coolest part. Every piece of inventory exists in the world, there's no backpack or menu system, just pick up a part, place it where you need it. It creates the challenge and forces you to plan, even when you basically have infinite money.

Terrible controls.   Insanely buggy.  You also get the (pleasure) of figuring out how anything in the game works on your own.

Placement of any item is incredible bad, the first time I went to place my crucible, it placed it underground....

Wish I didn't impulse buy and forget I had this in my library, it would have been an instant refund.

1. Хорошая и минималистичная графика, не режет глаза.
2. Очень интересный симулятор строительства карьеров и т.п.
3. Не спешный и позволяет много "подумать".

1. При большом количестве частиц (в данном случае минералов, вещей) начинаются лютейшие "фризы", и ФПС с 60 просто падает до 15-25.

5. Отсутствие коопа (надеюсь временно).

review:
First off, I would like to say that as this game is in an incredibly unpopular segment, some bugs are expected. That being said, the game is damn near unplayable. I have never written a game review but this pushed me miles past livid and I wanted it to be known how awful this is. 
1. The physics are horrific. If you accidentally graze a sign in a vehicle, it will literally send you and your vehicle spinning into orbit and it can take upwards of a minute to get back onto the ground. 
2. Starting off is quite the grind. It takes almost 5 hours of fishing to build a basic semi-automated mining setup.
3. Related to number two, once you start your automated process, after 5 hours you could have a million dollars. Then where is the motive to play once you can buy literally everything in the game?
4. The lack of optimization is genuinely impressive. I have a fairly beefy computer with a ryzen 7 and GTX 1070 but it brings it to its absolute knees forcing me to restart the game every 30 min. According to task manager, it uses a maximum of 8 percent of my CPU and maybe 30 percent of my GPU. 

I accidentally left the game open for 10 hours so I can't return it anymore but I find it hard to believe that this game has good reviews at all. I don't even know if this would be acceptable in an early access game, let alone a fully released one. 
I'll definitely come back once the bugs are sorted, but in this state, it will remain in my recycling bin until further notice.

I played this game about 6 months ago, and this is my review from the changes that have occurred.

This game has a lot of promise. I love automation type games, such as factorio and satsfactory. When coming across hydroneer, I was very pleased.
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend someone this game at this point in time for a few reasons.

Lag/bugs: This game has many bugs, from flying cars to crashes, lost items, corrupted saves, etc.
Inventory: This game lacks a basic inventory system, which is not fun when dealing with even small quantities of resources. To move things around is time consuming, buggy, and extremely annoying. I really have a hard time overlooking this feature that is so desperately needed.

Overall, this game has a fantastic base. However before I want to see multiplayer, or any other feature, I want to see the refinement of the basic functions of the game because many of them are not intuitive and actually really detract from this game-play experience. I'm excited to see where the game goes, but until the very fundamentals of the game are polished, I don't recommend anyone to play this game. Don't get me wrong, the games fun. It just isn't there yet, or anywhere close.

A nice aspect I found in the game is once you get the basic flow of the process of the game, there's no set way to get things done. Each property after the beginning one is a chunk of land you can do whatever you want to it. It's the definition of repetitive! Lots and lots of repeating stuff when you're building/working/maintaining. Personally, I like to run ram drills while excavating. I find the whole thing quite rewarding.

Two crappy things about the game, (and they're kinda really crappy): 

1) There is ZERO in-game instruction. The learning curve is so harsh, I could easily see people throwing this game off immediately. You virtually HAVE to watch videos. The game does almost nothing to help you figure it out. At least there is a link from the start menu about video tutorials. USE IT!!!   :D

2) Physics/mechanics/collision bugs. There's a few particular ones that are present that, (I have to believe), are a work in progress. Reading the community on the game, you'll read about "explosions" of piles of things, items getting stuck in other things, (that one isn't real bad now, I guess), and the sickening barrel rolls your vehicle goes into when it hits some (unknown) particle that you couldn't see and you end up across the map up-side-down.... yeah, that one is annoying.

The dev team seems very responsive to the community posts and the game is really young. I hope it has a long life span. So much potential and a real fun game. Very happy.

Moc nerozumím tomu..proč magnet na tyčce přitahuje i zlato, peníze a krystaly? Ale ok, pořád lepší, než všechny vytěžený rudy..přehazovat do kyblíků/pece ručně. (jak jsme to bez toho sakra mohli hrát?)

Při natěžení většího množství rudy, padají fps na úroveň powerpointové prezentace. U hry, která je o těžení velkého množství rudy. OK.

Grafika je....no nějaká tam je.

Hlína. Zabugovaná šílenost.

Hudbu jsem nepouštěl, jsem doma sám a bojím se.

Naprosto depresivní mrtvo. Ani jeden človíček. Ani jedno zvířátko :-(

KLADY
=====
Rybaření. Do začátku slušný příjem. Později naprosto postrádá smysl. (ale ok, koneckonců..to není hlavní zájem hry)

Vzhledové změny velikosti cihel. Ovšem do určitého počtu. Čím více rudy smeltíš, tím víc váží, ale vzhledově se již nemění. 

Craftění a vyrábění šperků, zbraní.

Nápad. Nenašel jsem podobnou hru..možná Goldrush, kde to ale není tak pěkně "osobní", maličké, kjůt. 

Zlaté cihly. No tak. Blejskavý obrovský zlatý cihly. To chceš.

Grafika. Já vím, že už ji mám v záporech jo, ale vzhledem k podstatě hry..to vlastně úplně stačí.

Postup. Je možné kompletně vše zautomatizovat, ačkoliv hra absolutně k ničemu nenutí, nechává hráči naprosto volné ruce. Což je dnes velmi málo vidět.

Vlastně by to byla skvělá jednohubka a věřím, že jednoho dne i bude.

TL;DR - Good game, worth the buy, but with some annoying bugs and lag that might ruin the end game experience.

For the most part, I like this game. I found that is a good time sink. Do I recommend the game? Yes, I do. The price is low, the fun is, well, good and the bugs are few for the price. It is not a perfect game, but the topic (a gold digger in a gold rush?) is quite refreshing. So, my review in general can be divided in three parts:

[b]The good:[/b]
[list]
[*] The ratio of time spent/money spent is good. 
[*] It is a refreshing sandbox game with an interesting idea.
[*] The challenge is to discover what to do with what you have.
[/list]

For a game to be worth the money spent has to bring me joy for at least the same hour rate that a movie does. That is, if a movie ticket worth 10 bucks and I had fun for 2 hours, that is a 5$/Hr. This game already surpassed this and I enjoyed my time with it. This alone is worth the game. Furthermore, this is a refreshing idea that I found interesting (kind of a gold digger in the old west). There is also no pressure to get something done so you can take your time to plan and enjoy the game at your leisure. There are no enemies nor competition that can make you fail. You may ask, why is this a good thing? Well, because you have time to think and tinker with the mechanics in a relax and calm way. You can always make self challenges to increase the fun or just enjoy the ride.

[b]The bad:[/b]
[list]
[*] Funny and frustrating bugs that can ruin a hour or two of work.
[*] You will need a beefy PC to run this thing smoothly.
[*] There is not much to do with the gold that you acquire and, if your computer is not that beefy, you can't expand too much.
[*] There is no point to having different items to produce when, in reality, you'll do the best over, and over, and over.
[/list]

The first time you see your truck flying to space in a spiral and make fun of the game with "because video games" meme is quite an amusing experience. But when this manages to "steal" your money (or the new drill that you buy with all your hard earned cash) it might be frustrating. But this is just an annoyance that comes once in a blue moon, especially when you discover how to avoid this quite early. What is not funny is the lag once a small operation of drills is running. But things goes worse after you automatice your gold earning endeavour. There is not much to do when you can't expand too much because of lag and, even if you do, there is nothing to use the gold you earn. I guess you can say that the enjoyment is planning and working  your plan. But, here is where this gets a bit of a problem when you realice that there is no point in a plan that says: melt that gold to make that big sword and necklace and earn tons of cash. There is no [b] interesting [/b] market. Yes, you can go and see if they are buying your equipment for more that in the main shop, but it is way better to just sell it in the shop and return fast to your production without losing too much time.

[b]The wish list:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fix bugs and reduce lag to enjoy a better experience with the ability to do more. 
[*] Metallurgy and graded products.
[*] An actual changing market that you can use to your advantage.
[*] Quests.
[/list]

My wish list just a way to say "hey, this is what I'd like to have to make this game a bit better and worth a replay". First, optimisation; if the game runs better you can do more with your gold and expand much more. This just prolong the end game. However, there is no point in having more resources when you cannot experiment with them. As far as I know, there are no grades in the items that you make. You just made the heaviest and useless sword in the world and sell it for a lot of cash. A grade system where the item you make have different values and different processes can add a lot to the game. Tie that with metallurgy and you have a nice combination that allows you to explore and enjoy the crafting system once you are not worried by resources. 

Finally, the best way to add a bit of variety is to add a market that is worth something. I mean, yeah, there is a "market" that goes up and low, but, I did not find it rewarding enough to bother myself with it. I found that is way easier to just sell it at the main store that check the market since it was a bit far away. The fastest that I can sell my items the quicker I can make a more items and sell more. Imagine a system that says "Hey, there is going to be a war soon" and, thus you know that the prices of the swords are going to be up for a while. If you couple with a quest system that says, we need 12 knifes of at least X weight, we will buy it for 50% more money. This would make making knifes a better investment.

To close, this a nice game that is worth the money and the time. It is not the best experience in the world and needs more things to do, but as is, is worth the money. There are some annoying bugs but you can work around, but the lag is worse than the bugs for the endgame. There is a lot of room for improvement, specially in the crafting and selling part of the game.

Pros:
- You can additionally to dig also fish (possibly also mine - have not explored that part yet)
- There are different metals and stones
- in the earlier days of your "industrialization" you have to especially keep an eye on your machines and possible add these stones to some parts of the machinery in order for them to work - adding another element you have to keep your eyes open for
- Despite the graphics look somewhat blocky, it falls good in with the game
- There are stock markets where you can also sell your items
- It is fun to try to build the ideal mining industry

Cons:
- When you sleep, the machinery does not work at increased speed - the times goes as it otherwise would when you were awake, which makes little point in sleeping
- It becomes quite tedious to transport parts to your mining areas - because you do in time need a lot of parts, and there is only so much space on the tractors (there is principally no-clip when you stack it directly on the tractor, but it still takes a lot of work)
- The pallets do though, have clipping with the tractors - or a interference zone - so you have to place the pallets somewhat accurately
- The same interference zones are in the shops, not only with the pallets but everything, and this can become quite irritating, as the shop where you buy the drills is pretty small
- There are some physics issues with the vehicles, where a slight bump into something might send the vehicle forever spinning in the sky
- Especially the excavator is prone to be airborne
- The excavator is sh*te. The digging is horrible, it only shoots out "pellets" of dirt (and not that much on a full load) and despite you can lower or raise the shovel-mechanism, it quickly becomes too much work, and you cannot go to the deepest parts of the fields and dig away is now above you
- Even though it seems fun in the start, and you can start it over a couple of times, eventually it becomes rinse and repeat - you have done it all before, and you know where it is heading, and there is nothing new to it


Conclusion:
It is a fun game, and you can definitely spend some hours with it. But with the bugs in the machines, it can really kill the enjoyment of the game. Besides, as mentioned, it does become rinse and repeat. I do not know if it will add a new element of fun, when they add multiplayer. Ultimately, I like this game. I have a long list of gripes with it, but it has definitely been a fun experience and the reasonable price helps me forgive its jankiness.

You drop in with little preamble. The game says, "Here's a plot of dirt. Get digging!" and you do, and it is good. Right away, I could tell that this game is about efficiency. How can I make the process of getting the ores and gems out of this dirt faster? It seems like there are a lot of fun tools to work towards. Early on, the game runs well and I didn't run into many bugs, and none of them were all that troublesome.

Then I entered mid-game, and made baby's first drill rig, and that was the first real sign of danger. It wasn't working right. The drill was refusing to operate in some places, leaving behind shallow holes. I read online that some people were able to trick it into working, but others had simply stopped using the drill (Goliath) in favor of other techniques. This bug combined with the annoyance of having to restructure my piping every relocation caused me to abandon the drill as well.

Still, I was able to speed up the shovel and bucket method with conveyors and such, so that I was able to make decent cashflow. I had my sights on moving on to a new plot and putting the digging vehicle to work. Now, there are many little things that I will not mention because I'm long-winded as is, but the vehicle functionality in this game deserved a mention, as anything from carts to trucks tend to become airborne when they contact other objects in the game. That said, trying to use the digging vehicle on the plot of land was a mess.

Drive the digger over bumpy terrain; suddenly spinning through the air. Try to approach a conveyor system to offload dirt; get launched to the moon. This is what broke my opinion of the game overall. I kept getting excited to be making progress, but it seems like all the more complex tools are buggy and extremely frustrating to use. This is neglecting all the periodical bugs like the time I dropped a palette on top of my cart and the whole thing vibed itself into the sky and refused to come down- forcing me to reload. They're not usually too painful, but it does seem sloppy!

There are also some weird things about the game mechanically. At the forefront for me, the ores and gems all have weight which influence how much value the thing you craft will have. However, rather than having a more complicated pricing scheme which would allow the player to find a sweetspot between value per pound and the amount of time spent smithing, the developer chose to make the selling price scale linearly with the weight of the object. Furthermore, you can add as much material as you want to any item and so it is most time-efficient to just dump all the ore you have into a single item and sell it. Who in their right mind is trying to swing around a 500 lbs sword? 

Despite all this, I still recommend the game because it is fun, and it is affordable. I spent about 30 hours in three days time (Snowed in) learning the ins and outs of the game, and I have no regrets- but this game could use some serious polish. I don't see how a multiplayer release will make the game any better, personally. It would reduce the tedium of some of the more laborious activities, but it won't fix what's broken.

[h1]Edited Review (25th Oct 2023 @ 205h)[/h1]
Over two years have passed and since then there have been a few updates and achievements that I wanted to unlock, which is why I started this game again. Unfortunately, the developers still haven't fixed the blocking resources; the only way to remove them is a button in the pause menu that deletes all unprocessed resources. It's not as bad as it was at the time of my original review, but it still happens regularly.
Since there is no inventory, all items have to be transported by cars (or carts in the early game). But if you put a not particularly large amount of items on the loading area, the game starts to lag when you drive. Buying the items one by one is already a farce, and unfortunately so is transporting them, even if you ignore the physics errors when driving at low FPS.

Another problem is money. As soon as a halfway large setup has been built, money problems no longer exist, you don't know where to put all the resources, since once the setup is in place, only the filters need to be repaired every now and then (or the spanners need to be refilled once the repair has been automated). With the last updates, two other currencies were introduced in addition to the normal money. You only get these through quests, which NPCs give you. I assume that this was to curb this abstruse overflow of money by reducing the amount of money that the player can earn in a certain amount of time, because the quests don't spawn very quickly and only give limited money. Unfortunately, this makes the whole game even slower than it already is, since important items for the farming aspect can only be bought with this new currency. Especially the prices for farming equipment are completely idiotic. A single sprinkler (to water plants) costs almost as much as a vehicle that can harvest and sow plants. Additionally, nothing can be automated to obtain these new currencies except for gathering large amounts of the basic resources. You always have to pick up the quest, create the random item and bring it back to get a marginal amount of money. 

All in all, I can only say that the game is a real pain without mods. Unfortunately, mods lead to Steam Achievements no longer being unlocked, which is why you have to go through the whole thing at least once if you want to get the Achievements. In principle, I would say that the most useful feature in the future would be an inventory system, and I'm not sure I'd bother playing the game again without one. I also stand by my conclusion from the original review: the early game is fun, but the mid to late game is unpolished. Unfortunately, my hopes that this game would be better were not fulfilled, which is why I changed my review from a "would recommend" to a "would not recommend".

It's not even that the game is bad, but the mechanics break it.

[h1]Old Review (16th Feb 2021 @ 35h)[/h1]
So the first few hours are really fun, from digging by hand to getting the first automated rigs. However, there are a few things that fall apart when your rigs get bigger and the amount of goods you get exceeds some amount.

I just have 35 rams that dig on the surface, all dirt gets processed, the goods get filtered and smelted. All works without a problem until the smelting part. Ores get stuck at the side of the conveyor belts, at the exit of the sorter, the melting plants, the logic smelting plants and even in the funnels. If you do not catch that immediatly thousands of ores will be blocked because of that one stuck ore and any attempt to remove that blockade will either drop your FPS way below 1, crash the game or spread all the ores over the whole island as the physics just 'explode' the ores when touching one of them.
So I am sitting there on the "South Hope" field and can not even use all of the 35 rams (which is nothing compared to the size of the field ) as 1 blocked ore can already destroy everything. All of these rams would easily fit on the first field so I do not really see the reason to buy a bigger field except to dig lower and get bigger ores.
Maybe it would already be enough to join the ores like the dirt does at the moment and to not cap the ore size but to do it like the bars which do not grow in size after some point but get heavier. That would reduce the problems caused by the stuck ores (as that would stay 1 ore but bigger and way heavier) and might even reduce lag when handling ores by hand if anything happens. Keep in mind that bigger ores are already a thing when mining deeper so it would only make sense to be able to join smaller ores.
Another point of trouble is the magnet. While it does help a lot collecting all of the ores that flew over the whole island even after dropping all the ores it keeps lagging until i do not hold the magnet in my hand anymore. When I pick it back up the lag returns though. Same thing happens with the world save, after some time the game gets laggy which can be fixed by quiting to the game menu and loading the world again. 
Another thing that annoyed me is that you need to check your filter every now and then which is okay, but in my opinion it happens way too often and with the basic filters the water damages your machines if unfiltered water gets in some machines. Especially since you need five of them in early game but only one powered filter later on. The powered filters stops the water flow if the filter breaks so it gets better in the 'mid' game (there is some automatic repairing logic in late game) but it could be better.
Also the money should be no item that you literally need to carry around. While I understand the reason it just makes everything so much slower, a money system outside of physical items would be way better (but is fairly subjective so I understand if there are people prefering the current money method).
All in all it is a fun game but the mid to late game seems unpolished, the bugs I encountered are game breaking and should not exist in a full release. Maybe the developers thought one would get the better drill fairly early and instead of going on a large scale with small ores one would go smaller scale with big ores in the lower parts of the fields.

Those are the problems I encountered apart from some minor physics shenanigans and apart from those I really enjoyed the game. It is fun and has an awesome setting which kinda reminds me of minecraft in a more realistic and 'advanced' world than minecraft itself. So while this review might sound negative I want to stress that I really enjoyed this game and want to see what happens with it in the future. I would rate it with a 6.5-7.5/10 in its current state but it can clearly get way more than that in the future.

I can not in good faith recommend this game anymore. What i thought were glitches were actually apparently features. There are a lot of problems that I think really ruin the experience that I just can't get behind. My main gripes are as follows:

- picking up and dropping items is just tedious. Everything always drops to the right of your cursor. There IS an indicator for where stuff will drop but its barely visible and this is also just a completely unnecessary complication. Why have it? Why not have the ability to disable it? It's just irritating. It is also entirely too easy to accidentally pick up a part of your automation system, completely breaking it and forcing you to move around a bunch of floating entities just to fix it.

- There is no inventory system. You can pick up and hold exactly one item. While this adds difficulty, it also adds unnecessary tedium. I'm not saying you should be able to hold a lot. But like... a tool belt that can hold tools for you so you aren't CONSTANTLY going back and forth for no reason would be nice.

- The fuel system for vehicles is never adequately explained and there is no indicator as far as I can tell for how much fuel is left. I know you use water but beyond that, all it says is "vehicle is refueled at the water tank". Considering the vehicle is the only thing making mass purchases (which are often necessary) from being a complete mess, this is pretty a glaring oversight.

- The Dev's rarely respond beyond a simple, nothing-burger statement when people bring up these issues as far as I can tell. 

Since the game is far enough along to have paid DLC, I would have expected these issues to have been resolved already.

I wont say the game isn't interesting but these frustrations are part of core gameplay elements so you can't avoid experiencing them. Particularly my first gripe. That one prevents the game from being entertaining since it is EXTREMELY frustrating to deal with.

Hey, sometimes mods can break Hydroneer, to fix this you need to delete your Pak folder and clear your steam workshop folder.

- Go into C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\1106840 and clear out that folder.

- Open the Run prompt by holding the WINDOWS key and pressing R.
- Type the line below into the box (or copy/paste) then hit ENTER and delete it's contents.
%localappdata%\Mining\Saved\Paks

This game is an automation game, starts simply but at the rate new things are added to the game your factories just get more and more complex.  Still in EA, and definitely buggy here and there but mostly very playable and enjoyable.  

What are you doing in game?  Mining.  First by hand, and using a brush and pan to screen for goodies.  But you look in the store and see pipes, hmmm....maybe I can use one to auto-fill my brush pan?  So you do that.  Cool.  Then you buy a crucible and start melting stuff down into bars, making more money.  Cool.  What's the anvil for? Nonostante le mie sole 44 ore di gioco, mi sento perfettamente in grado di metterci la faccia, consigliandovi l'acquisto :)
Hydroneer è un titolo davvero originale, " nella più totale libertà " assumeremo il ruolo di un aspirante magnate minerario. Fin da subito e senza ulteriori filmati o spiegazioni si viene proiettati in un piccolo paese pieno di luce e "terra" :) con a disposizione un setaccio, una pala, un pennello ed una lanterna. Di fronte a noi scorge un fiume, preceduto da due lotti di terreno rimovibile. Lì ha inizio la nostra scalata verso la ricchezza!
Nelle prime fasi di gioco " a mio parere eccitanti e appaganti " dovremo faticare un bel pò, inizialmente otterremo i minerali nella maniera più rudimentale, ma oltremodo piacevole. Potremo anche acquistare l'occorrente per fonderli e poi rivenderli ad un prezzo maggiore, oppure "lavorarli" per ottenere armi e gioielli. Nelle fasi successive invece potremo già vantare di equipaggiamento migliore e più efficace nella raccolta di questi.  
Senza dilungarmi più di tanto, rovinandovi cosi il resto dei contenuti vi anticipo che non mancheranno i mezzi di lavoro, cosi come la possibilità di raccogliere i minerali "automaticamente" grazie all'utilizzo di macchinari e di tutto ciò che permette il loro funzionamento.
Inoltre è presente un sistema di "quotazioni" nei vari borghi del paese, dove ogni giorno varieranno i prezzi di vendita, in modo di avere la possibilità di vendere un oggetto nel valore più alto possibile, auentando cosi i nostri profitti in maniera considerevole.
Di contro invece pecca vistosamente la giocabilità, se guidi un mezzo ed entri a contatto con ostacoli o qualsiasi altra cosa hai a tiro, 8 volte su 10 avviene un Glithc, ma niente paura, poichè premendo il tasto ESC ci sarà l'opzione "sbloccami" andando avanti cosi però diventa alquanto alientante. Per quanto riguarda altri bug, personalmente nient'altro di rilevante. Anzi... trovo che sia uno tra i giochi più stabili, nonostante la complessità e la quantità degli oggetti da me utilizzati il gioco non è mai crashato.
Detto ciò....Per chi ama il genere deve assolutamente acquistarlo. Per me è stata e continuerà ad essere una bellissima esperienza. Inoltre Hydroneer vanta di uno sviluppatore serio e laborioso! egli si impegna ad ascoltare e rispondere a tutti i commenti e segnalazioni, rilasciando frequentemente aggiornamenti sempre più precisi e risolutivi.

This game needs some serious polish. No in-game tutorial to be seen, the video tutorial that is linked in the game still misses critical information, two different cursors to aim with that are both present at times that they are not relevant, clumsy object placement and buggy physics (nugget explosions... why?) that both make completing simple tasks frustrating, and an early-game loop that takes too many cycles to progress out of for how tedious it is. The early game is an absolute usability nightmare, and really needs some "fresh eyes" passes. Your first cycle of digging, rinsing, scrubbing, and selling is painfully confusing, and your tenth is terribly boring, which is made worse by the fact that by that point, you've got a sense of just how little each lump of resources moves you forward.

If the pacing is intended to be this slow, then the tutorial and basic interactions need to receive some attention to reduce the frustration of learning the game. Slow progression is fine on it's own, but the bugs, counter-intuitive UI, and clumsy interactions make the beginning of the game too frustrating to crawl through while trying to trial-and-error your way to your first little bit of money.

In its current state, I could not recommend this game as it is listed as a "full release".

The good:
*It has the building niche that some people are looking for
*Great concept and love digging
*Pretty game with a steady day/night cycle
*Grid system is great when trying to plan and develop layouts

The bad:

*Controls feel clunky

*When crafting on the anvil, sometimes objects created fly off into the nether

*Once you play for about 5 hours, you can pretty much have bought the reactor and everything to create a base leaving nothing else to do

review:
Features:
- Unique world interaction system, which coupled with the lack of inventory, forces you to think ahead and plan your base/crafting areas properly
- Machines that run on water rather than fuel! The pipe systems are simple, yet offer a complex scope for operating machines and automated systems.
- Advanced logic gates and powered reactors. I have not yet reached this stage in the game, but having looked at the parts available it is certainly possible to fully automate an entire mining, refining, and smithing process
- A beautiful house building system. My god, the housing pieces that are available so far are varied and fit the aesthetic well. I have high hopes for the building content at full release of this game.
- A relaxing, yet dynamic art style, with grand vistas and well-built towns.

Current gripes:
- The building/placing objects system is still a bit clunky, and the way certain objects interact with each other can be frustrating (notably, piles of ore/dirt being picked up by hand causes them to explode and send objects everywhere!)
- There doesn't seem to be too much to do with Shards, other than power machines, given how frequently they are mined. I find I have a large excess in storage, as machines do not use up the shards very quickly at all. I imagine there is a planned use for them in future releases that would solve this problem, though :)
- Frame lag when a lot of objects are in view - again something I should imagine will be solved throughout early access!

Overall:
A great work in progress that promises to be a truly engaging and unique crafting game. Well worth investing in the future of, particularly at it's current reduced price!

Want to buy tools and equipment? you have to take it to the checkout, hand over the cash and carry it home or load it into a truck. The development has been consistent and new features are constantly being added. The community is very much listened too for features and I've also seen youtube suggestions making it into updates. The dev clearly cares for this game and while it's no triple A title, it's really well done for an indie game. Would absolutely recommend.

Hydroneer is a very labor-intensive mining-sim, that shouldn't be as much fun as it actually is. 
There is no inventory. There is no bulk-buying. Every item has to be dragged manually. Carts and Cars make transportation a bit better, but every item still needs to be handled individually. 

You start off shoveling dirt into buckets and cleaning it with a brush, to make money to buy better parts until you can build semi or fully automated mining-factories. 

The game is not very polished. there's tons of glitches, especially regarding gravity and magnetism. It's tedious to get things done. but boy.. when they finally work and you get those big nuggets and gems by the truckload, does it feel great.

TLDR: Fun but perhaps a little too grindy in one or two aspects.

My only real gripe with the game would be the inventory system. In my opinion it can make things a bit harder than they need be. What you can carry with two hands is essentially what you can carry. Which I'd say is unique, but I don't fully understand why this method exists. Having to physically take your coins to the shop, carry out your bought items one by one, then return to get your change / left over coins, just feels a little dragged out for me.

With that said, don't let that put you off. After the initial heavy grind of digging, rinsing scrubbing and repeating, you can get to the automation of things. Then the dollars increase substantially and the effort required drops off. This I feel, is when the game will really shine and your creativity can thrive.

I like the art style, the world is big enough without being too big, and you are afforded a reasonable amount of freedom.
Honestly for the price, it's well worth giving a go, even at it's full price there's enough content to keep you chugging along.

I've been back to this game a couple of times now (which I suppose says enough by itself), so I figure it's a good time to amend my old negative review.
My main issue was the performance, and while it's still not perfect (particularly when picking up a pan with a lot of ore chunks etc in it, which is odd since it shouldn't be calculating physics for them if they're locked to a container) it's a LOT better than it was when I last reviewed.
I still like the whole no inventory thing. It can get a bit tedious carrying things like foundations, and torches that don't want to stay in the cart, but generally it's kinda relaxing organising everything right there in-world. Things lock to containers when their physics settles, so you're not kicking over buckets and having your ore chunks spill all over the place. You WILL find plenty of other ways to spill 100 ore chunks all over the floor and have to pick them all up, though.
Overall there's a few Weird Design Decisions but it works pretty well now. Though I did turn voice off pretty quick because I might scream if I have to hear the word 'scran' again.

I don't recommend you go afk because if you do then multiple things can/will happen. A: Your filter/machines will break because they take damage over time, and will get damaged and will not be able to operate until fixed. [h1]Hydroneer is a mining simulator that doesn't simulate mining[/h1]

it's a shovel/bucket/dirt ball/pan simulator

just, look at this ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ if a speedrun of your game contains 4 minutes of literally the same 7 clicks, a small intermission and then literally the exact same 7 clicks again for [b]SEVEN[/b] minutes more, then your design is in need of fixing ಠ_ಠ

e: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the """[i]endgame[/i]""" of that speedrun is literally 40 minutes of exactly the same 2 clicks (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3MvhJJqpecA

first off, the basic clunkiness: everything involves manipulating physical items in the game world, which is fine, if it were easy, fast and intuitive to do so, but the physics are extremely finnicky AND the game prides itself on having no user interface

as a basic example: a required step is putting a chunk of dirt into a washing pan, which happens by putting the chunk into the space on top of the pan, where they then combine automatically into a filled pan. HOWEVER, more likely than not the chunk will roll off, or not be centered perfectly and you can pick the pan up and hope that combines them, or launch the dirt into the air.

another basic example: to create chunks of dirt you have to fill a shovel by clicking the ground and then emptying the shovel by clicking a bucket, then tilting the bucket to empty it and create a ball of dirt item. issues with that:
- some ground can be dug and some can't, and when at the bottom of a pit both look identical, and there's no indicator whether you're pointing at diggable ground
- while holding your shovel you cannot tell if it is filled with dirt, so sometimes you'll click to dig and place dirt instead and then click the bucket and wonder why nothing happens, because the lighting makes it hard to tell the shape of diggable ground
- ball of dirt items have some properties to auto-combine: with other chunks of dirt, which is ok, i think. with the bucket itself. so if you tilt the bucket sometimes the dirt item can roll back into it literally immediately

and to make all of this worse, you have the E buttons and left-click to do similar but different things. E picks up and drops items, while left click *uses* items. using a container item means "drop items out of it", so in the hurry of things it's easy to accidentally press the button that drops the container instead of dropping the item in the container. this could be aided by having on-screen prompts reminding you of what does what, but as mentioned, the game prides itself in having no user interface.

now this is just basic user interface / physics / ux clunkiness. the bad part is how it simulates mining.

it does the minecraft thing of "deeper = better and more ore". and until now object permanence was fairly ok. you dig dirt it goes onto shovel; you undig it, it recreates some landscape; you put it into bucket and empty the bucket and you have to deal with a ball of dirt; it only disappears once you wash it in the pan. that last part you'll be doing at the river first, so it's easy to rationalize it as "dirt gets washed down the river". but later on you pipe water and do it elsewhere and realize the dirt just is deleted.

now here comes the bad part: the shoveling quickly gets old, and is very slow. so you'll want to upgrade things. but the game says no. it sells you a pickaxe, which bills itself as "Used to dig terrain fast, or split dirt in half." now one might assume that when you dig with it it creates balls dirt for you speed up the whole mining aspect, but that's not what it does. it *deletes* dirt so you can get deeper faster, and then do the whole "shovel > bucket > ball" part but deeper underground where more ore is.

so the game, instead of simulating mining actually, just simulates minecraft with voxels, and instead of giving you better tools to mine more efficiently it gives you cheat code items that allow you to ignore the whole "soil is a thing that exists" part and your progress exists entirely of:

- dig as deep as possible as fast as possible
- create dirt balls underground
- use a water pipe to delete the soil while in a cave
- go through a crafting and ??? stock market ??? chain to increase the money you make from the basic "shovel > bucket > ball" steps

the only actual mining updates are:
- buy an automatic drill which you feed with your shovel
- buy a new mining plot and an excavator for fairly steep prices (the starting plot has the excavator blocked)
- upgrade the automatic drill with a magic machine that spits dirt at it that it conjures from thin air

Sigh......
Where do I begin.

This game has a great concept and the execution is... ok.
The graphics are good, and I like how there are multiple towns with different specialties.
The hold-n-drop system has issues, but it is great for lining up where you want to drop things.

Now onto the flaws. 
The early game is slow, and you will be grinding for a while before you can do something productive. While driving (necessary to buy stuff if not next to a town) you cannot hold a map. Also, if you are walking, and holding your money, you cannot have a map. 1 thing in your hand and that's it. Tbh I get why there is not a inventory, but at least let us stuff a map and our coins into our pockets. 

Now. Bugs.
OH GOD THE BUGS
lets put it this way: This game is early access. No question. There are so many bugs and exploits. 2 I can think of are the infinite dirt exploit (take dirt, place on water bank, take dirt from a corner of it and place. Infinite dirt.) and the teleport back "feature". (park vehicle at plot, run away, press reset vehicle and boom you get sent back.


Overall: yea i reccomend it but see if you can get it when its on sale.

The physics in this game leave a lot to be desired. Bugs range from frustrating to game-breaking. Fragments of deformed terrain block movement. Grabbed objects retain collision momentarily, flinging nearby objects away. Simulated collisions can scatter around your resources or even undo hours of progress as crafted/purchased objects clip through the ground or fly away beyond the world boundary.
Calling this an indev solo game project is generous; this feels more like a tech demo, one that's for sale on the Steam Store.
