So... I'd be ok with the game if it were an Alpha, maybe even a beta, but not as a finished game. why?

So... it starts really slow. Your first money is earned really hard, which is kind of repetetive. Then you go fishing to earn more money. After like two hours of grinding, you've got enough money for your first automated rig. After maybe 5 more hours you've expanded that rig, added automated sorting. You start to get bored with that and start crafting. You create a 20 ton neclace (literally) thats worth 65000 coins. You have way more money than you can use by now. You unlock the blueprints. You figure out, that one of the last blueprints you aquire is a straight pipe, something thats not worth crafting at this point, because its about 20coins in the shop. So, about 10 hours into the game... you've run out of stuff to do.

The other "this is an alpha" is the performance. Buckets and magnets have no limits in what they can carry. But the framerate has. Thats especially an issue because in the later game, something is flying around basically all the time. When you dump a buch of nuggets, you don't end up with a pile of nuggets on the ground. You end up with a nugget-explosion. Good luck cleaning that up with a magnet that brings you to 10 frames per minute. And well... now you have your nuggets at the magnet. You have to drop them eventually, somewhere. And you know that you'll end up with the next explosion. Also: You hit a rock with your truck after 2 minutes of driving with awful controls? You're 100m in the air now. You can reset the vehicle, and you will end up... somewhere on the map. Good luck.

And there are a ton of inconsistencies. But well, that would be spoilers.

Update: I've kept playing, I guess I was bored. Now the jewellery is worth three millions, and the stuff on the belts alone is enough to kill the framerate (although the Graphics card is bored, the Ram mostly empty and the CPU is at 15%... not sure what's the holdup). The latest update brought some gimmics, but essentially it's still the same. No Idea what I am supposed to do with millions of Hydrocoins.

Interessantes Konzept, das massiv an mangelndem Late-Game-Content, grauenhaft schlechter Steuerung, ärgerlichen Bugs sowie fehlenden Komfort-Funktionen leidet, trotzdem aber für knapp 10h solide zu unterhalten weiß. Kann man für unter 10€ für ein paar spaßige Stunden vielleicht mitnehmen, muss man aber nicht. 

Im Prinzip gliedert sich eine Spielpartie in drei Phasen:

1. Hartes (stundenlanges) Grinden von entweder Fischfang oder simpler Goldschürferei per Hand, bis man genug Geld für eine Budget-Automation hat.

2. Aufstellen- und Betreiben ebenjener erster Budget-Automation. Hierdurch steigt der Ertrag sehr schnell und Geldnot gehört zeitnah der Vergangenheit an.

3. Überfluss. Nach Ausbauen der ersten simplen Automation zu einer mittelgroßen verdient man derart viel und schnell Geld, dass man sich im Prinzip alles innerhalb kürzester Zeit leisten kann. Das Spielprinzip "Geld verdienen, um an besseren Content zu gelangen" erledigt sich daher sehr schnell von selbst. Nun gibt es im Prinzip nichts mehr zu tun, außer vielleicht eine wirklich große Automation auf einem neuen Claim oder Ähnliches zu errichten- notwendig ist das allerdings dann auch nicht mehr, zudem selbst "komplexe" Automationen verglichen mit anderen Genrevertretern wie Satisfactory oder Factorio derart simpel sind, dass dies im Prinzip aufgrund der hakeligen Steuerung nur in Arbeit ausartet ohne Spaß zu machen.

The premise of the game is brutally simple. Mine some dirt. That's it.

There is no 'end game' and this is a game where, quite literally, the journey is more important than the destination. Well, it has to be as there is no 'destination'.

The tools at your disposal to play with are limited, and this works well in the game's favour. There is something strangely therapeutic in building your little mining operation and watching all the moving parts come together.

The one big issue, and it's a massive biggy, is that it will bring your system to it's knees and give it a damn good kicking. I've had to stop playing as a slight 'issue' with some errant gems has dragged my frame rate down to about one frame every three minutes...

That 'issue' is purely down to me trying to run a messy mining line on an i54690, 8 Gb of ram and a GTX 760. However, an upgrade is quite literally in the post, so hopefully I can resume playing in the dirt by the end of next week...

Hydroneer is a great game for those who enjoy your typical singe-player mining/resource/grind simulator.  I would put it in the same class as games like Farming Simulator, Gold Rush, and other similar games.  Overall its a solid game and I would definitely recommend it, but I'll break out my thoughts below.

Pros:
- super active developer.  Interacts in the community discord almost daily.  Constantly adding new things to the game with semi-regular updates.  Listens great to community feedback and requests
- decent game progression
- simple learning curve, easy to understand
- freedom in design.  You're not constrained to how your system is set up for both aesthetics and functionality
- there's no debilitating bugs or game breaking exploits that ruin game-play
- physics system and lack of inventory make for some interesting play and more satisfying machines

Cons:
- minor bugs surface with most updates, usually mild, but can be annoying
- late game feels unsatisfying once you have a ton of money
- the modding community has dropped off in recent months (has a couple new promising faces)
- depending on your dedication and willingness to grind, the physics and lack of inventory can be frustrating and more time consuming than preferred.  

Overall if you're considering buying the game, I would pick it up.  Its only $10 which is reasonably cheap to begin with and often goes on sale.  You can easily get 20 to 30 hours of game-play out of it, even if you aren't dedicated to replay-ability.  In addition, some coming updates seem like they're going to add a ton of sustenance to the mid and late game.

I like the idea of this game, and I enjoyed the first few hours of the game; the graphics are basic but well done and the idea of using water to automate production is well delivered.  But after a while, I found this game became very repetitive; dig mud into a bucket, throw the bucket's contents into a pan, dunk the pan into water, brush, separate out the nuggets, repeat for a few hours.  Once you can afford to automate things, it becomes more interesting for a while.  I genuinely got a thrill after getting a simple production and sorting line set up, seeing the first few lumps of mud started to get crushed up, and the nuggets start dropping into their furnaces.  But then your harvester gets clogged up with mud at the top, so you have to manually unclog it, your filters break while you were clearing the harvester or shopping for new components and shut down a chunk of your production line which clogs up your conveyors (and then your harvester, again)...  I also found that any upgrade work meant flattening everything and starting again.

If you're looking for a simple game to while away a few hours, you like the idea of panning for gold and you don't mind grinding repetitive tasks, this game is worth getting.  Unfortunately, I found that I simply was not enjoying constantly having to fix problems on the production line.

*Note to the Dev*

Edit February 21st 2021:
Yes, I have a lot of hours into this game, having done a lot of testing, providing feedback. Those who know me well, know how thorough I can be. It has allowed me to figure out all the tiny little details in-game, in-source, and beyond, whether good, bad, or ugly. Quantity is no guarantee for a positive recommendation, quality is. Similarly, wishing a game to be good, doesn't make it so either...

I left a negative review just because I can't see myself recommend this game. The game is promising but has a lot of issues, with performance being the biggest culprit. The overly used physics and implementation of it's use is a close second.

That aside there are plenty of other issues left; non-sense (window height/size), poor implementation (eg. vehicle spawn), known bugs with documented fixes (eg. integer overflow), hurried features (eg. logic), false sense of bugfixes (removal of resources through menu).

If anything, this game should have been Early Access instead of full release, as it is far from finished. Sure it explains why and what would have happened if the concept was not 'liked' as much?!

Apparently it is now up to a few contractors to fix the game and even include - the previously NOT to be discussed - multiplayer, while the developer continues work on another project. Hopefully those hired will be up to the task of making this the game it truly deserves to be.

It amazes me how easily players tend to fall for the promising title / cheap price / single dev excuse. Maybe I should give credit to the developer for that matter, or possibly discredit those who don't care to look beyond the surface and be honest about it. To roast or not to roast ... must be my age.

Oh well, here's to a better future for Hydroneer, so I can hopefully change my recommendation to be positive instead.

--------------------------------

Update March 2024

What started as a supposedly 'finished product', has continued following true 'Early Access' fashion, in an attempt to get the game to where it should have been upon first release. Never truly finished, unclear directions, and never ceases to amaze me where to take it next...

...well, that direction appears to be paid DLC! Who would have guessed?

I'm going to start by saying that Hydroneer is worth the price tag. All in all this is a pretty amazing skeleton of a game, and I'd rather support the ugly brainchild of a solo developer than grease the greedy pockets of AAA developers who have no idea what innovation is. I really want to rate this game higher, as it has so much potential, but it has some glaring issues that simply need to be addressed. Here's what I liked and didn't like about Hydroneer. 

Pros
-It's a great little mining/crafting Sim
-The lack of an inventory system makes it feel very unique and hands on. It makes inventory management something of a gameplay mechanic. Loading up Trucks and Palettes is very satisfying.
-Building elaborate systems of conveyors and drills and plumbing is good fun, and allows people to be as efficient or chaotic as they want to be. 
-The aesthetic is relaxing and cute. It doesn't have much of a story mode, but it feels like there is lore to the towns and areas of the game. 
-If this game ever gets a DLC or substantial content update, You can bet your ass I'd buy it.

Cons
-The game lacks any sort of end game or concrete objectives. 
-I had no chance in figuring out how anything worked without watching/reading a guide.
-It's a bit glitchy and needs a lot of polishing in some areas. I was randomly dropping items in my hands, getting stuck in terrain (especially while driving a vehicle). I tried to use the "recall to vehicle" function from the options menu and it teleports me to my Truck, but then I can't get out of the Truck, so I use the "unstuck" function and it gets me out of the Truck only to plop me into the Truck bed where I get stuck again.
-The lack of an inventory system could be a really fun mechanic to the game, but It kind of only serves to hinder on a lot of occasions. For example: You actually have to drop gold piles onto each other in order to combine them, but if you have two piles of money in the same bucket the game won't acknowledge the total value and you'll be sitting there scratching your head wondering what's even happening. 
-There is no "Quit without saving" option, so if you make a mistake and want to reload your file, you literally have to close the entire game, re-open it and then continue from the last save which may not even help you if you were playing with auto-save (which you almost definitely will be)
-Just a long list of little things that sour the gameplay throughout. Eg: Weird Collision detection, Awkward Terrain to navigate especially with the Vehicles, Unexplained mechanics, Cumbersome physics can make simple tasks very difficult (Like i was trying to put a really big fish in a bucket and it would just fall out every time)

I know it seems like I'm coming down hard on Hydroneer, but this is the only game I ever played that I actually cared enough about to write a review about. Any harshness you read here comes from a desire to see a Hydroneer 2.

The first hours are great, you dig, you work your way up the ladder of tools, you craft things for sale, and thats very entertaining. Building extra stuff for fun is very time consuming as you are only able to move one item at a time.

Look, don't get me wrong, this game is plenty of fun (at first) and absolutely amazing for a single individual to create. It has great mechanics for harvesting the earth and when i started off i was really into it. Then eventually you buy machines and better equipment to improve your quality of life. So why cant i recommend it?

There's just not really any content. That enjoyable idea of harvesting the earth is all there is, and its fun while it lasts, but the absolute moment you create an advanced system the fun's over, because you can make a bunch of money, but there's literally nothing to really spend it on. There's plenty of building blocks and environment blocks you can buy, which i gave a go but all of which was just slowly postponing the inevitable. Literally only the beginning grind is the fun part of this game, so after about 4 or 5 hours you've done practically everything academic. There's no workshop content to switch things up, no wide variety of methods to extract dirt, its just incredibly disappointing. It would be alright if it lasted longer than it did, but the truth is you're paying for a game that, yes is a grand accomplishment, but dies so quickly after playing it you're left bitter.

Really wouldn't recommend it.

I could keep going to build a grand structure to live in and show off my work without ever smelting again, but, why?  The progression curve needs to be looked at, or even better, expanded significantly to make buying larger plots of land, and building more complicated, efficient setups have a purpose in game. Gripes aside, was enjoyable and would recommend.

Its a great game when looking past the bugs, which I have found more on the funny end than the annoying. Most of said problems are physics related (specifically car physics). An easy work around for me has been using the very handy "Unstuck" button which resets your position back to a fixed position. As long as you keep the area clean you're good too go. This button is also use full for easily crossing large part of the map as all plots have their own fixed position, meaning as soon as you can teleport using the "unstuck" button as soon as you cross into one zone from another, easily saving you upwards to a minute for each shopping trip most notably.

As for gameplay, the progression curve is a bit off, meaning you easily have the means to do large scale projects after only a few hours. After that its only a matter of unlocking a few blue prints, finding some relics and if you feel like it, a mega factory.  Personally this is something I don't mind, but in the games current stage I cannot see myself putting more than 30 hours into it. Which isn't bad for a cheap game such as this which still sees updates regularly.

All in all, I would say its a good buy.

The game challenge is how to git r dun, you're digging macguffins out of the ground, optionally processing them (smelting, forging, assembling), and selling the result for money. It starts out feeling slow, and it dawns on you that you can change all the reasons it's slow, which early on boil down to how you've got your work site set up and how you're moving, then you start hankering for things you can't get at the local store and you start looking at that road you haven't explored yet, and you're off to the races.

The one frustrating glitch is the (far from unique to this game) symptom of spawning something inside another when you thought you were placing it, I think the game engine interprets an intersection as necessarily the result of a collision, anyway, when you're putting stuff in the truck or whatever, be careful with it and don't just bang things around. If you mess up, you'll dig all day, smelt up some gold and iron, sell it for enough for that mechanical harvester plus all the supporting gizmos you think it needs, drive down to the big city (okay, ten-building-hamlet) store, buy them all for all the coin you just made bung them in the truck . . . oops. You did it carelessly, didn't you?  Haha, your €365 harvester has decided you're playing KSP and left the launch pad. You didn't see where, you've been working all day and you're tired. Now it's gone, and it's dark, and you're broke.

But now you can do in one game day what it took you a game week (they go by fast) the first time, not because you've accrued Magic Number Points but because you were thinking about what you were doing and you know how to set it up so every motion makes progress.  Yes, you're running a shovel. You have *paid money* to run a shovel. And it's not even real. Oddly enough, it's fun. The time flies by and you're always thinking how to do more, faster, better. Construction work: the good parts version.

The amount of things that work with this game are quickly out weighted by the things that dont work.

The big issue I have is the consistency of the game is all over the place. Driving a vehicle and hitting a rock might bump you a bit and make you slow to a stop or it might put you spinning into orbit so fast you'll get vertigo with a side of seizures. Driving the large digger machine has the same issue though it's more likely to turn you into a drill tornado and drop you on the other side of the map.

Additionally, the placing of items can lead to frustrating results as well.  Dropping down a drill to get nuggets for mining, especially at the bottom of the dig sites, means half burying the drills into the ground and half  hazardously attaching pipes to the drills, which you might not get back after you place them, just to find out the drills dont register the dirt around them and their for dont produce anything.

So many of the items you can place also have the annoyance of being just a tad too tall to work with other items, such as walls with the sorters. If you place walls around the deposit end of the sorters, the walls are just a hair too tall and block the sorted minerals from going to their desired location. Finding these little pockets of dozens, hell thousands of minerals if you got a good production going, is like finding a bomb in your fridge. Sure, you could take your time to grab every single, individual item out of the fridge, not knowing which one is the trigger, and place them where you want, but its more than likely going to explode in a rainbow of culinary chaos that will cause your computer to crash or lag like mad

So to start, i put 12 hours the first day into this game and i felt like a crack addict. 
The CONSish:
- Items and materials can be quite buggy when mass production takes place, so having a bunch of pieces of minerals all in one place will always explode in a blaze of lag and glory.
- No inventory, not really a con but takes a lot of getting used to, just moving things around takes more than 1 brain cell compared to other factory games such as Factorio or Satisfactory. It does add some level of challenge that keeps you gripped into the game. 
- Vehicles are SUPER buggy, you hit the wrong part of the ground and you get launched farther than apollo 13. Luckily the dev's gave us an unstuck tool in the menu to set you back to a set place nearest to were you are when flying to the moon.
- Performance is iffy if the game has been open for more than 4 hours, usually a restart of the game fixes this issue though. 
THE PROS:   
- This game is like crack
- After 30 mgs of adderall and 12 hours I made a fully functional mining operation with auto sorting and auto smelting, I sold my gigantic swords to the stock market after making profit  
- If you like factorio or those kind of games def try this, its only $10 which makes it that much better

Encore au stade embryonnaire, Hydroneer propose une petite expérience de récolte de minerais. 
Visuel mignon, il se taille un petit trou dans le monde des jeux qui mettent l'accent sur la gravité, les collisions et les systèmes automatisés.

Munissez vous de votre seau, de votre pelle et commencez à creuser. Nettoyez ensuite la terre avec votre petite brosse pour récupérer du fer, de l'or ou un étrange cristal. Amenez votre butin au marchand et répétez l'opération. Ou pas en fait. Achetez une canne à pêche, pêchez trois tonnes de poisson et vendez le au marchand, c'est plus rapide que votre seau. 

Une fois ceci fait, vous pourrez enfin acheter une foreuse automatique, quelques tapis roulants et tout un tas de matos qui travaillera à votre place. Vous aurez alors loisir de fondre les minerais pour vendre des lingots plutôt que le minerais brut car c'est plus rentable puis... vous pourrez vous octroyer le luxe ensuite de forger les lingots en quelques armes ou bijoux pour augmenter encore votre profit. 

Vos machines fonctionnent à l'eau. C'est comme ça dans le monde du jeu vidéo. On pollue pas. La gravité est sympa et on peut faire des usines originales. Si le placement des objets est un peu pénible parfois, ça à le mérite de fonctionner et d'avoir de la gueule. C'est bien ça le problème, c'est que c'est sympa et que ça répond bien, du coup on se retrouve à optimiser le shéma pour que ça marche mieux, et on se retrouve avec des ressources en quantité dingue à gérer. Les tapis sont blindés de terre et ça se bouche, alors on met des broyeurs pour déliter la terre qui s'agglomère au fur et a mesure que les foreuses la déversent. Les cristaux s'accumulent dans un seau car on peut pas les vendre. Les systèmes sont simples et intuitifs, et faire un shéma automatisé est vraiment à la portée de tout le monde. C'est pas compliqué du tout et ça marche bien. Même si il ne révolutionne pas du tout le genre il a le mérite d'avoir une prise en main facile qu'un gamin de 8 ans pourrait piger.

Apres ben on commence a trouver que la concession ou on est est quand même un peu étroite, alors on achète la plus grosse de la carte, située idéalement à coté de la ville principale ou les vendeurs proposent tout ce qu'il faut pour se projeter dans un avenir florissant. On s'imagine fabriquer une grosse baraque car il y a pas mal d'items pour faire du housing, des murs, des toits, des trucs pour la déco. Oui ça va être sympa ! 

Ben non. 

Les collisions sont complètement aux fraises et vous allez voir des trucs partir comme des boulets de canon dans le ciel. Vous et votre véhicule compris, bien entendu. 
Si au départ c'est sympa d'aller au marchand, de choisir les articles un par un et de les charger dans la benne de votre camion, dites vous que si vous voulez faire un gros système hydraulique pour approvisionner 20 foreuses de manière efficace, et bien vous allez vous taper 250 tuyaux à poser un par un dans le local d'achat. Puis devoir ensuite les charger un par un dans votre camion pour enfin les poser un par un sur votre terrain. 
N'osez même pas faire une grosse maison, ou prévoyez des couches pour adulte et une bonne nausée car la caméra bouge bien. 
Dès lors que vous aurez quelques machines, envisagez un bon freeze toutes les 2 minutes. 
Si vous avez eut la patience de faire un gros système automatisé, c'est deux ou trois énormes freezes toutes les 2 minutes. 
Si au début le fait de devoir prendre tout à la main, objet par objet, pour les laisser tomber ou il faut est rigolo... ça devient assez vite gonflant. Surtout quand vous devez poser trois lingots sur l'enclume. D'autant que... pour les forger faut qu'ils soient chauds, donc le temps de ramasser et reposer le dernier qui ne rentre pas, enjaillez vous de devoir recommencer l'opération vu qu'ils auront refroidis ! 

Enfin, le meilleur. Qui peut juste foutre votre partie en l'air. 

Le jeu ne vous empêchera pas de poser des structures dans le sol. Parfois ça peut aider pour éventuellement passer outre un petit vallon. Certains jeux sont assez pénibles avec ça et si un élément du décors rentre en collision avec ce que vous voulez construire ça marche pas. Bon, on se dit que du coup c'est un bon point. Et bha non ! 
Car dans Hydroneer, une fois l'item posé dans le sol, vous pourrez plus le reprendre. Et du coup, vous pourrez pas non plus le remplacer par exemple. Il vous faudra donc, le contourner. De quoi flinguer tout une planification si vous avez le malheur de missclic un pauvre tuyau, ou si vous le posez dans le mauvais sens... 

Compte tenu du temps à passer pour faire une palissade, je ne me suis pas hasardé à pratique le jeu dans sa profondeur. Bon... en fait si j'ai essayé de faire une grosse baraque avec une usine derrière. Mais comme j'ai mal posé UN tuyau, fallait que je recommence toute ma partie. Et comment dire... non. 

Hydroneer est un petit jeu qui pourrait être très sympa. Il souffre d'un cruel manque d'ergonomie, et l'édition d'une grosse base est bien trop fastidieux. Les ralentissements dès lors qu'on engage des constructions trop grandes le rendent inutilisable sur le moyen terme. Le manque de souplesse dans la construction le rend impossible sur le long terme. Bon courage au développeur pour accompagner son projet, je lui souhaite de trouver des solutions pour le rendre plus jouable. 

N'achetez pas pour l'instant, sauf si vous êtes au RSA et que vous n'avez vraiment rien d'autre à faire. Et encore, y a quand mêêêême mieux sur le marché. Genre, du papier toilette et des pâtes, par ces temps de virus c'est davantage utile. Surtout le papier toilette.

This game has come a long way in the three years it's been here. I originally gave it a poor review but the devs have seriously improved this to the point where it's downright addictive. 

It takes a special mindset because it's mostly physics based rather than snap and click, even dropping something into a pan requires you to actually aim for the pan or it winds up bouncing on the ground. And there is no inventory, so the world is your playground, there's no ready crafting of tools and storage. You buy the building blocks from storekeeper NPCs. You sell your "harvest" be it mineral or plant, buy more equipment to automate it better and fuller.  They added a quest system and some logical unlocks which gives you some direction, though very open ended because, well, you're doing whatever you want. There's plenty of frustration getting things to work the way you want and enough dopamine reward as you progress to make it worthwhile. 

However there's also no health, no fatigue, no hunger, no stats whatsoever. You are constrained by a semi-real physical environment but you aren't going to die, or freeze, or get eaten by bears, or starve. It's just you and a world of resources constrained by game physics. The addiction part is not unlike the infinite clickers that just continue to go up. Except you're building something. Kind of.

Pour tout éditeur de jeu, de grâce, permettez une proposition de touche pour les AZERTY. Même si le changement est assez aisé et qu'il y a très peu de touche.

If you like crafting games where you work toward automation and upgrading your base then I would recommend this one. However, be warned the beginning of this game is a bit of a grind. Be prepared.

This game takes a bit of figuring out but can be worth it. The conveyors are not as secure as Satisfactory (items can go everywhere and there is a lot of loss that occurs since dirt and mined resources have the potential to fall off) but other than that it can be satisfying. If you set up automation quickly, this game does not take that long to be able to buy everything you want from the stores.

Things that I hope for:
Being able to put a pallet on the sell table, and selling all the items that are placed on the pallet.
Centering conveyor belts to actually be able to center items (I put a pan on a looped conveyor system with 5 centering conveyor belts and it still manages to get stuck or fall off).
Being able to hold a bucket and right click on items to put into that pan. (very tedious dropping one item at a time into a pan).
Widening the maps bridges and add fences so it isn't so hard to stay on the bridge while in a moving vehicle.
Multiplayer would be great

Edit: After playing for longer, there are railings that you can get on your conveyors but dirt will now get stuck in conveyor corners and at the tops of the vertical conveyors when using them. I feel like this game does not have a lot of replay value and 12 hours in i feel like i have "beaten" the game since 1 trip to sell my items gives me 95k currency. Multiplayer would lead me to build ridiculous things from here with friends. I still recommend playing but I need something more at this point.

Additional things I would like to see in this game:
Being able to hold items out directly in front of you (kinda hard putting bars into the pressurizing pipes with it off to the side of your character)
THE PAN. It's difficult getting bars and larger fish into the pan. All i want to do is make 1 run to the Jewelers. I still think it would be great to be able to right click items into the pan.
Would be awesome to have an option next to 'Buy" that would transport all the items on the buy table to your car. 
To put more emphasis on crafting items from the smelted bars, it would be great to set weights on a smelter that would make it create the bar once it hit that weight. 
Items tend to stack up on each other. When i have uncut gems dropping into a pan and i take out an uncut gem...the pile explodes and now I have some clean up.... I'm not sure if collision is ignored when items are in a pan but it caused me to throw out the grindstone the minute it happened.

I wanted to like this game. I really really did. The biggest issue I have is feeling deceived by it coming out of Early Access. After the unmitigated disaster that was Grav, I swore I'd never purchase another Early Access game again until it received a full release. I'd been following Hydronere for awhile and it finally came out of Early Access. I was excited to play the game only to realize that it very much feels like an unpolished, unfinished buggy mess.

Let's start with The Good:

Solid game play mechanics. At least the ideas.
Reasonably paced progression
Visual style that's quirky and easy on the eyes

And then the bad:

Clunky controls (I would forgive this if it wasn't for everything else)
Empty World
Extremely buggy vehicles (hit something sort of the wrong way? Expect to have it flying through the air for an indeterminate amount of time)
Has a habit of being crashy

I've also noticed an issue that I've seen a few other users post about -- the longer you run the game, the worse the performance is. I experienced this as sudden freezing of the game for at least 10 - 20 seconds at a time. When it first started it would happen maybe once every 10 - 15 minutes? That was acceptable, I figured it was caching things too and from the hard drive it was on and just waiting for the HDD to spin up (unusual since I have power saving mode turned off for that disk). Whatever. I can deal with it.

But the longer I ran the game the time between this freezing decreased until it was happening every 30 - 60 seconds and then maybe I'd get three or four minutes every now and then. It degrades performance to the point that it's unplayable. Exiting and restarting the game doesn't fix this. Restarting the entire computer seems to do the trick but again after playing for awhile the freezing and performance degrade again. It's very annoying.

All of this stated, I think I could get past all of the feelings of being unpolished and unfinished if it wasn't for the hideous performance. But alas, it's very annoying to deal with the performance hits and the otherwise unfinished feeling of the game. If this wasn't a solo indie developer I would have requested a refund. But, I'd rather not go that route AND it looks like the developer is continuing to develop the game. So here's to hoping that the bugginess and performance issues are address at some point in the near future.

Until then... just bide your time. I want to recommend this game but in its current state it's just not fun.

This is a pretty cool game.  A simple game about what I would label as a one man gold rush simulator. You dig dirt and brush/sift through it for valuable minerals. Hydroneer does away with a traditional inventory, not allowing the player to put hundreds of pounds of items in their pockets(?). While this may seem a bit off at first, it encourages you to utilize the trucks and pallets, and make the most efficient use of your trips to town to buy supplies and sell your goods. It makes you take your time and enjoy the simple tasks, or at least actively do every little step until you advance enough to begin a level of automation with drills/miners, conveyor belts, sorters, water pipes with pressure physics. When you have a handle on all that and are reaping the benefits of your system, you can then take up blacksmithing and jewelry making to make some real coin. The gameplay mechanics are simple for a quick gaming break or hours of a chill experience, and the world is just big enough to ensure plenty of play time, even including some secrets for the more dedicated diggers. Once you've attained a healthy stash of wealth, there are shops that feature furniture and building construction materials if you're a visionary, and a few different sites to purchase, each with their own unique appeal.

TL;DR If you came to dig, the payoff is big. 
Something to definitely add to the casual/chill gamer's library

[h1]Misleadingly Advertised Early Access Game[/h1]
I've given this game a pretty solid crack over the years and unfortunately I can't recommend it at all anymore. I was cautiously optimistic that the game would improve and the developers would polish it into a finished product but my patience is exhausted and my faith is lost. This game is incredibly buggy and this review has been edited multiple times. Some of the bugs mentioned may no longer apply but I'm confident they'll be replaced by new bugs. This has been an ongoing trend for years.

Kind of worse, the developer has been reworking a bunch of mechanics from the "1.0" release. The game has changed significantly in some ways since I first picked it up. Which makes this review scarily relevant even after all those years. This is still an EA game, masquerading as a finished product.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
Don't let some of the negative reviews about the core mechanics put you off. This is a [b]fascinating[/b] game that makes some bold design choices. The core limitation of only being able to carry one item at a time is extremely immersive and is executed pretty well. I loved the low-poly visuals, and the world feels beautifully designed. This is a great game to play casually when you've got a lot of time to kill and want a relaxing experience. Throw on some chilled music and enjoy.

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
This game is very rough in places. The sound design is just plain awful but that's the least of its problems. Though I strongly suggest muting the soundtrack unless you want brain damage... A major major issue is the physics. It's hilarious how bad it is. There are plenty of physics collisions which will send things flying into the sky. [i]Drove over that tiny rock a bit too fast? Welcome to the stratosphere. Something on top of that bucket you picked up? Well it's now flying away at terminal velocity.[/i]

Vehicle handling is just generally terrible. This wouldn't be such a major issue if hauling items with vehicles wasn't such a major party of the game. I've got used to saving my game for fear of being stuck in an infinite reset loop which throws me into the air the moment I reset, and lands me somewhere I can't move. It's happened fairly regularly every time I've played this game.

A game breaking issue is that you can build things under the ground. Not ground you can dig mind. This in itself isn't a problem but if you can't see the item anymore you can't pick it up. I once lost a stack of 14,000 coins because I accidentally placed it [b]under[/b] the ground when I meant to put it [b]on[/b] the ground. Now that wasn't a big deal since I bet on this happening and split my six figures worth of coins into lots of stacks. Can you imagine this happening if you didn't? Just lost all of your coins? Too bad. That could seriously have ruined hours of play time...

In my latest play through I managed to break sprinting in under 5 minutes of play. The sprint key just wouldn't work. It required a game restart to fix it. I've had enough... I've come back to this game with renewed optimism so many times, only to be beaten down with completely stupid bugs, that I'd class the relationship as abusive.

Game performance is utterly abysmal for what it is. I've run this game on both my mid range gaming desktop and my high end gaming laptop and... it sucks. The frame rate will regularly drop to single digits for a few seconds at a time. There have been serious memory leaks in the past which required a system restart to resolve. The game's practically conditioned me to not use lamps as it one point they would tank the frame rate too. Graphics memory usage has also been crazy at times...

[h2]The Ugly[/h2]
As my title suggests this game is being falsely advertised. Development is still actively underway with new features and bug fixes being intermittently released. Combine that with the aforementioned issues the game has and it's fairly clear that this is still very much Early Access and not a full release. I'm not sure why the developer didn't label this as Early Access other than to give a false impression that it's more finished than it really is.

I recently built a site up to full-scale automation again. What shocked me the most is how many machines have been removed from the "1.0" game, only to be replaced by subtly different ones in "2.0". What was the point exactly? Just leave the old machine in the game and make a new one. I think this may have been why some of my Steam cloud saves just disappeared. Presumably they weren't compatible with the new release. I don't know if there's a "3.0" planned but I expect that to blat my saves too.

All of the new changes feel forced and stilted. Dirt has invisible tiers now. You get to a point where Tier 1 equipment won't work anymore. Pickaxes and miners will just spark. The dirt doesn't look different mind. You just spark instead of going deeper. Pipes can now hold more than 100% pressure and have pressure caps that aren't given in description texts. Does a pump or pipe going over 100% pressure sound stupid? That's because it is. Change % to a pressure unit and it would suddenly make sense. Use bar, PSI, Pa, or even make up your own... These might sound like nit-picks but I think it's a sign the developer doesn't really care. The tier's are an afterthought to artificially pad game time.

[h2]Bottom Line[/h2]
I didn't request a refund for this game because I thought it was kind of fun, and I suspected I'd come back to it fairly regularly. I had hoped that if the vehicle and building mechanics were fixed, along with the performance issues, then I'd give it a thumbs up. Now though... I regret this decision. 

The developers have had a lot of attention via YouTube. They've had a lot of people pay for their game. Years have gone by and it still feels like an Early Access bug fest that's being regularly reworked. Sure there's more content but the game has bugs and an apathetic developer eating at its core.

Don't buy this game. Unless you are happy to put up with a lot of infuriating bugs and a developer who's clearly out to get one over people.

Hydroneer... it's okay.

It satisfies a very basic feedback loop of slowly, bit by bit, easing the grind to make money. You go from scooping dirt with a shovel into a pan and scrubbing it for ore to sell, to eventually having an automated bar-smelting conveyor-belt-fed machine.

The problem is the overall goal, the endgame, is... well, it doesn't really exist. You grind and grind, managing to earn more and more gold, until you have the optimal setup, which is now completely pointless because the only goal was to earn enough money to make that setup in the first place. Once you have the optimal setup there's nothing really new to sink your money into. You can buy land, but it doesn't really provide anything new. You can buy another tractor, but you start with one for free. You can buy house pieces and build up a wee little house, but that's purely for aesthetic reasons and provides no benefits to you.

I don't know what this game would need. More crafting options other than smelting and smithing 6 different things would be nice. That would also lead to a better trading market with some more variety. More ores and advanced smelting processes would be great as well.

Having said all that, I have put 25 hours into the game, and it's pretty cheap. That basic feedback loop works after all, as it can be pretty addicting upgrading your mining setup. Watch some videos, and if it looks like your cup of tea then go for it, but if you want a deep, complex experience then maybe look somewhere else.

This game is not finished, not in the slightest. There is so much content that could and NEEDS to be improved upon.

Cons (There are a lot):

The repeated task of 'Shovel Dirt, Fill Bucket, Repeat until Bucket is full, Dump dirt in Pan, Fill Bucket with Water, Pour Water in Pan, and Scrub' over and over just for a small amount of cash is incredibly boring.

The most Basic of automatic drills costs around 600 Coins, and one cycle of wet dirt scrubbing gets you around 10 at best. 

You have to pick up and drop EVERY. ITEM. which is a chore if you go out to buy anything without a truck, because of the unnecessary extra trips and because you need to carry your cash by hand or bucket.

Anvils require multiple bars instead of a certain amount of weight in a bar, which makes the scale useless because it's not like you need to monitor the weight of your bars, and with the way you drop items in this game, it's not easy to put bars onto the anvil.

The Truck controls horribly, it can't go up slight cliffs and will get stuck if you accidentally go ramming speed into one, and accelerates and decelerates slowly, it also doesn't tell you that Space is a handbrake.

Yeah, I thought this game was perfect for my favored genre of building/crafting/open world, but the mechanics are too hands on, literally; as you have to: 

1.Grab the bucket.
2.Position the bucket.
3 Set down the bucket by holding down the right mouse.
4.Grab the shovel.
5.Shovel the dirt in the bucket
6.Hold down the right mouse to set down the shovel.
7.Grab the pan.
8.Hold down the pan to set it down next to the water.
9.Empty the dirt bucket into the pan.
10.Hold down the... *UNINSTALL button, go to your account to request a refund!

There is no way I'm going to put myself through that mind numbingly, boring gameplay for X-amount of hours; sure you can work your way into crafting tools to help you automate this dull process, but I'm not going to repeat this tedious gameplay loop for hours, sorry, and no, I did not play long enough to get used to it for the very reason that I did not want to go over my 2 hour limit...

For those with iron focus and patience, this game is a must, and it is to you folks that I can recommend this game wholeheartedly; but for everyone else that does not want to go to a second job, then I cannot recommend this game to you...

Ну чтож, немного поиграл и че могу сказать. Игра залипательная. Не понимаю тех, кто жалуется на отсутствие инвентаря, ведь это именно фишка игры. Я думаю, что найдется немало тех, кто мечтал потрогать каждую единицу добываемого ресурса в сурвайвл игре и положить там где хочется. Все предметы в игре являются физическими объектами(кроме размещенных предметов, как механизмы, трубы и стены, понятное дело), что тоже достаточно прикольно. Однако, нельзя отрицать и то, что иногда предметы могут сталкиваться, укатываться и разлетаться в разные стороны, иногда и на достаточно большие расстояния, что может стать тем еще гемором. Если вы не любите медленные игры и кропотливую работу, эта игра не для вас. Вещи можно возить в кузовах техники и носить в ведрах или тазах. При помещения ресурса в емкость или кузов, он фиксируется после своей остановки и его невозможно ненарочно просыпать. Имеются также магнитные посохи для подъема и переноса горсти ресурсов. Некоторые объекты недостаточно кинуть на землю или в емкость, а нужно разместить с помощью кнопки действия. Чтобы понять, как играть в эту игру, достаточно посмотреть официальное видео от разраба и мельком пробежаться по геймплеям. У каждого предмета есть описание, которого бывает достаточно, чтобы разобраться как он работает. Не понимаю тех, кто жалуется на отсутствие подробного обучения. Застрявшим в технике и провалившимся достаточно открыть меню игры и нажать нужную кнопку, если кто не знал про это. Огромное количество столкновений отдельных объектов в игре может стать испытанием для вашего компа, так что на совсем старых пк играть в это не стоит. В городке с магазином механизмов имеется и мусоросжигатель, если кто искал, куда деть лишние объекты. Игра находится пока в раннем доступе и надеюсь разрабы будет баловать нас чем то новым чаще. Для игры, вышедшей в раннем доступе относительно недавно, в нее уже на данном этапе интересно играть.

[b]Review nach 16 Stunden. Das Spiel erhält regelmäßig große Updates, meine Review bezieht sich auf Version 1.3.[/b]

Hydroneer. Ein Spiel indem es aktuell nur ein Ziel gibt: Edelmetalle abbauen und verkaufen. Es gibt keine Aufgaben und man hat freie Hand; Sandbox eben. Das macht das Spiel aber nicht schlecht. Denn zu tun gibt es Anfangs eine Menge, so fängt man an mit Eimer und Schippe nach den ersten Nuggets zu suchen um diese zu verkaufen. So arbeitet man sich "hoch" bis man sich die beste Ausrüstung leisten kann. Und dann wird es langweilig. Hat man erst einmal eine gut funktionierende Basis gebaut kann man nicht mehr viel machen. Außer sich mit den begrenzten Wänden, Dächern oder Fenstern ein Haus zu bauen bleibt wirklich nichts anderes mehr übrig. Natürlich kann man sich noch andere Grundstücke kaufen und diese ebenfalls bebauen. Aber seien wir mal ehrlich, das ist auf Dauer total öde.

Das Gameplay ist sehr simpel und selbsterklärend. Die Steuerung ist in Ordnung. Einzig das platzieren von Gegenständen ist manchmal Fummelarbeit. Musik und Sound sind ok.

Leider gibt es in diesem Spiel einige nervtötende Bugs. So verschwinden gerne mal Nuggets im Boden und landen, warum auch immer, ganz unten auf die Levelgrenze. Das sorgt nach einer Weile für eine schlechtere Performance! Davon abgesehen fängt das Spiel ohne ersichtlichen Grund an zu ruckeln wenn man etwas länger spielt. Da hilft dann nur ein Neustart. Außerdem kann man Gegenstände IN den Boden platzieren, dann aber nicht mehr aufheben ohne die Erde abzutragen. Nicht selten fliegen auch Nuggets oder Barren durch die Luft wenn man sie aus einem Eimer aufheben möchte. Und man kann sich auch selber in die Luft katapultieren wenn man auf einem Gegenstand steht und diesen aufhebt. Auch toll ist es wenn man mit einem Fahrzeug eine Straßenlaterne berührt und dann durch die halbe Map fliegt.

[h1]Positiv[/h1]
- Spielspaß für 10-15 Stunden (minimum) garantiert
- Grafik, Steuerung, Musik und Sound in Ordnung
- Spielinhalt für den Preis angemessen
- Spiel wird laufend erweitert

[h1]Negativ[/h1]
- Bugs
- Einkaufen von neuen Gegenständen ist sehr mühsam
- Nach einiger Zeit fängt das Spiel an zu ruckeln (Neustart behebt diesen Fehler)
- Es ist oft viel zu dunkel
- Lampen sind nicht wirklich effektiv
- Tag/Nacht-Modus (total sinnlos in diesem Spiel)

Princip hry je jednoduchý - těžíte hlínu a "čištěním" hlíny získáváte suroviny (železo, zlato, drahokamy, krystaly).
Nejprve se to vše musí provádět ručně, avšak s průběžným výdělkem lze postupně automatizovat.

Suroviny se dají prodat jednotlivě, přetavit v ingoty, či z ingotů následně vytvořit šperky nebo zbraně a až ty prodávat. Na mapě je několik prodejních míst, kde lze tyto věci prodávat, avšak ceny se v průběhu času mění.

Po mapě se lze pohybovat pěšky, nebo lépe pomocí hydromobilů, které jsou napájeny vodou a čas od času je třeba jim tu vodu dolít. Jejich hlavní benefit je v tom, že pomocí nich buď můžete převážet materiál, nebo těžit.

Pozitiva:
-Hra samotná má potenciál a koho baví tento typ her, jej určitě na X hodin zabaví.
-Netradiční, avšak příjemné grafické zpracování.

Negativa:
-Cestování s vozidly je poněkud náročnější, neb cesty jsou dost úzké a občas se objeví i nějaký ten bug, kdy když např. narazíte na kámen, začnete několik vteřin rotovat ve vzduchu.
-Mizení věcí - když například rozebíráte starou konstrukci a pokládáte věci na zem, občas se stane, že věc se odmrští v lepším případě několik metrů od vás, v horší do neznáma.
-Při pokládce  dřevěného bednění se mi několikrát stalo, že se umístilo pod texturu a už nešlo vzít zpět.
-Při spuštění hry jsem klikl omylem na "Nová hra" - zde pozor! - není možnost nově založenou hru opustit bez uložení a tak mi přepsala hru původní, kde jsem strávil tolik hodin.
-Neskutečně mě štve ten druhý kurzor, který slouží k umísťování/vylévání atd., jako by nestačil jeden.

Verdikt:
-Pokud by se mne někdo zeptal, zda bych doporučil tuto hru - i přes absenci multiplayeru, několika bugů a averzi vůči druhému kurzoru - Ano doporučil bych ji.

Not a good buy yet. Has irritating and annoying physics gone mad. You have no placement ability for things like the crucible and small furnace. You 'drop' the crucible repeatedly trying to place it into a workable position so you can pour a pan of gold nuggets into it to smelt them. Even trying to half bury the furnace and digging a funnel into the ground so the crucible will 'fall' into the right position doesn't work well.

It is as I said, physics gone mad. Physics for the sake of physics when you mistakenly think wow this is cool. It adds nothing but annoyance and frustration to the game, and has zero fun factor.

You can 'place' very few items. Most you have to drop and in typical crude game physics they bounce around unrealistically into odd angles. You lack the simple ability to put something down where you want it. You have to 'drop' most things.

Further, there is an irritating double cursor. One in the standard game position in the centre of the screen, but then a second green one offset to the bottom right showing you where something will do it's first bounce if you drop it. The green unfortunately completely disappears in a hot glowing crucible and in many other instances is hard to spot.

Another example of bad physics is that it is very difficult to pour a collection of nuggets you have carefully sorted into the crucible, or indeed any other container. You carefully aim the second cursor into the crucible then pour the pan into it just to see your nuggets go everywhere.

Really, dump the stupid physics in places where it simply becomes an annoyance.

I think other than this fairly big issue at the moment the game could be interesting and fun, instead of irritating and annoying.

Old Review:
Ok, I have now reached the point in the game, where I could just go onmass with machines and make more and more cash.

But the problem here is (like in many many tycoon games):
What to do with the cash and building further gets more and more tedious, especially because you need to carry each component one by one. (imagine building a castle by yourself, thats how it feels)

People suggest to build houses. Why should I do that, if there are no mechanics to get any use out of them?!
People suggest to expand the automations. To get even more money for nothing?
People suggest to build a "skyfactory" as a challenge. Again, what should I do with the income?!

Make tycoon games have a crazy endgoal / multiple endgoals!
There is nothing to push me to go further after understanding all the mechanics. And I am not a fan of accumulating money for no reason (dont have a billionaire complex, sorry) or building fancy houses (no status complex either, sorry)

All this in mind I have spent my 10h of gameplay with mixed feelings till to that point, where I really really got heavily disappointed and it feels like I have wasted my time with the game.

The game title is called Hydroneer, but the filename in OBS in Mining.

You put dirt into a bucket with the shovel; the bucket holds 4 scoops.
You put dirt into the pan from the bucket; the pan holds 1 bucket.
You cannot dig dirt with your hand (1)
NOW..
if you put dirt into the pan from the shovel, then it only holds 1 scoop.
Sometimes the dirt comes out of the bucket as a physical boulder, in which you have to pick it up with your hand, then drop it back into the pan, in which it then becomes dirt. This usually happens while pointing the wrong reticle at it...

Why are there [b]2 reticles[/b]?
The blue one is centered, brightly illustrated, and used for interacting and picking up objects. The green is off-centered, barely visible, and is for dropping & dumping objects, except when it doesn't. If you are holding the pan or bucket, the mouse-click will dump its contents all over the ground, from above the green reticle.
BUT
If you are using a shovel, it will dig AND dump above the centered blue reticle, despite the shovel model being positioned over the green reticle.

[b]The shovel[/b] is held vertically and away from the player in all instances. Not only does it look completely unfunctional, but you cannot see if it's holding dirt. There is no way to simply set down anything either. It is instead dropped like the character doesn't even want to be there, and often rolls over upside-down. That is, when the character is even willing to put it down. Often trying to just drop the shovel results in him going "UHHH" and not letting go. 

If you enter a [b]vehicle[/b] while holding ab object, you then have to quit and load the save in order to get out, despite there being TWO INTERACT KEYS. One for getting in and out of vehicles, and one for interacting with everything else. You can rebind the vehicle key to be the same as Interact, but the button prompt will still say 'Q'.
The vehicle handles like molasses; it's more efficient to drive into a wall than trying to stop. The chase-cam is glued to the vehicle so that every bump is reflected in your view rocking side to side. 

===============

Use 1 key for all interactions.
Have everything dump and pick up over the same spot.
Let players be creative. If the pan can hold the same amount of dirt as the bucket, then allow them to skip the bucket and dump straight into the pan.

Make sure you track your usage in the game when you first get in.  There are a few people for whom the controls are unreliable -- it seems to be a game engine thing.  It's not that I don't like the control scheme (although honestly I don't think I would prefer it to a more conventional mechanic).  It's that my hardware or drivers don't work with the game.  I found another person with the exact issue in discussions, and people said "UR doing it wrong!" but I left my own description and a dxdiag for them and for the dev.  NADA.  So be sure you don't run over your time before you decide you're not just bad at the mechanic, but the mechanic is bad for you.

I'm not going to downvote the game -- it looks really attractive.  I just wish I could play it.

Nagyon szeretném szeretni ezt a játékot, de ez mostani formájában szinte játszhatatlan

Love the art style and idea behind the game but there are too frequent game breaking issues (mostly related to object physics) that make it terribly frustrating to play.  It does seem (as of July 2020) to be getting frequent updates so hopefully it will polish out in addition to completing what looks to be stubs for functionality as well as more late game growth opportunities.  

The good:
Graphics are cartoony cool (World of Warcraft type style)
Great ideas and usability is really thoughful (you can pick it up pretty easily but there is complexity underpinning)
Simple and Clean Minimalist UI (no inventory just what you hold in your hand) 
Stable (no hard crashes in nearly 20 hours played)
Music is appropriate, pleasing and doesn't grow repetitive.
Sounds are good cues to the UI and appropriate.
As presently priced it's a reasonable deal. (not on par with triple A but you aren't spending $60 either)

The bad:
Physics seem to be whacked (sometimes an object will rocket off into space and piles of ore can spontaneously explode when touched)
Driving physics are nearly unusable at times (I spend more time rocketing through the air doing spirals than driving)
Magnet is a great idea but once you use it 1x it will quasirandomly attract ores (even if the magnet is located 100's of yards away)
Beyond 15 hours or so you'll have reached the end of the "tech tree" as it is.  There is little to do beyond making larger structures but nothing of real note to do with the coin you earn (some cosmetics if you desire to build a "home" or more decorative structure)  
Little reason to replay (once you've sort of cracked the code on how to do things is sort of pointless)

On balance I wouldn't recommend it right now but I would suggest you follow it and see how it goes.  Too many early access games never get there and have "tremendous potential"   Only time will tell if this one will florish or be one of unfortunately too many "high potential fails".  At present it has promise but is incomplete.

40+ hours in and... oh god, I can't stop!  Mine, rinse, scrub repeat until you learn automation and then it gets insane!  Automate dirt with the D.A.V.I.D. machine, automate digging it with the Goliath, then transport that dirt automatically with the conveyor belts and rinse and scrub that dirt with a Harvester.  Still not enough?  Run those nuggets and gems on some belts through some separators and dump them into their own separate spaces.  Want more?  There's funnels and smelters to automate the smelting process!  AUTOMATE THE FREAKING WORLD!  Don't want to automate?  That's cool too, there's a freaking digging rig that you can drive around to dig faster and process your paydirt that way.  In fact, you can set up your belts in a way to send those hunks of dirt into your automation system.  Want to build?  There's a fairly decent building system in the game.  Want money?  There's stocks to sell things.  This game doesn't disappoint, there's still more work to be done on it which makes its "Full Release" fairly misleading but the dev is just one guy who releases weekly youtube videos on his development and seems to actively listen to the playerbase.  There are some glitches in the game, from my experience, I've lost a truck entirely, had my truck flipped, seen things explode into the sky, and all in all they haven't been totally game breaking.  As a whole I thoroughly enjoy this game and it feeds my needs for creating efficient automation systems.  Good job dev!

Fun game!  Slow to get started but this helps you get experience with the overall process.   Had a great time starting with small nuggets from buckets filled in the river.  Some 40 hours later, built a full home with an attached ore processing center on a large piece of land near the sea.  I piped water into lower mine which dripped into buckets from ceiling.   I added a full conveyor belt system to move the gold, ore, shards from the mine to the process room room which sorted and smelted to bars.  You'll enjoy this game if you like designing a home and processing plant.   Definitely recommend it!   Be patient, and understanding of the small glitches.  Use the unstuck option when  it does happen and you are good to go!

Edit: Despite my complaints, I'm still playing. Something about the game feels addicting.

2021 Edit: Another playthough, where I've done much better. 

I can see the appeal of the game, I really can. There's no inventory, which means you're dragging every thing around piece by piece, with some labor saved by transport via truck, although you still have to drop and remove each item from the truck too. It feels realistic in some ways, but makes the occasional bug, like a part just vanishing, very infuriating. Scrubbing for ore is incredibly dull and slow, and when I got enough money to build a network of pipes close enough so that I could stop running to the river every ten seconds, one of my pipes vanished into the hill you CAN'T dig while I was trying to place it. This nearly killed my motivation right there, since this meant more running back and forth to the river just to afford another piece of pipe.

EDIT 2021: By now I managed to bang two brain cells together long enough to figure out that I could just bring pipes over to my pan and bucket system to expedite that process, so I only have to run back and forth to the river for the first ten minutes or so.



Cut to four hours later. I've managed to afford a machine that will scrub the dirt for me automatically, provided it has a water pipe connection. It has to be fed through the top, which meant digging out a section big enough for it and big enough for the ore it spat out to have room to fall into my bucket, because otherwise it would just appear under the bucket. My mistake for thinking a narrow area would make it easier to catch the ore. It took a while to setup, but eventually I could stand at the top of it and put dirt into buckets to dump into it at a decent pace. I had hoped I could just dump dirt directly from the shovel into the machine, but no, I need to fill a bucket first so I can dump THAT out into the machine. I guess the lack of inventory is the only realistic choice in this game. I admit I'm jaded by things like this from previous games.

Edit 2021: This whole system works much better now. I no longer need to dig my machines into the ground, I can simply place a pan vaguely under the machine's spout to collect most of the spoils.The added Magnet On A Stick, while pricey, eliminates the issues of getting ore into the pans.



Eventually the biggest time consumer was sorting ore out. You can't mix ore, so if you throw gold and iron in a pot, you'll only get one ore, with the other deleted. You have to sort it out one by one because of the lack of inventory. You can't just sweep it apart with one hand like you would in real life, or collect it in neat stacks in your inventory, no, you have to pick up each lumpy metal turd and toss it in the right pile if you want to make any real progress. 

Edit 2021: There's now conveyor belts and an ore sorting machine, of which I bought four. This eliminate the ore sorting problem I had completely, and I have each ore filtered into it's own giant crucible to automatically smelt into bars.



I was managing all this with mild grouching at worst. It wasn't until I bought the giant excavator machine in an attempt to speed up my dirt farming. The machine itself dug great, when it felt like digging anyway. Sometimes it just wouldn't dig until I drove back and forth a little. The machine itself was a nightmare to pilot. Terrible steering, and the second the tire would hit a piece of uneven terrain, the entire machine would rocket into the air like the most absurd firework in existence, spinning wildly and bouncing all around. I had the machine for all of fifteen minutes, and it did this eight times. Attempting to make any use of it was a horrible plan. This took a couple hours to afford, and was a gigantic waste of time. 

EDIT 2021: There is now a very large sign in the location where I did this that has a picture of the machine crossed out.



This honestly feels like a troll game sometimes. I could sort a full pail of different colored lumps in about a couple minutes in real life, but in this game it would take me an hour at least. You don't have pockets, or a bag you can carry? There's a bag on the tractor you start with even!

Edit 2021: It still feels like a troll game sometimes, given the forced tedium of some actions, but it plays much more satisfyingly now. However, as soon as you get your ore sorted and smelting smoothly, money suddenly becomes no problem and the only real motivator is collecting relics at that point, and none of them do anything besides (to my knowledge) unlocking a passage containing more money that you wont need at that point.

The only real hurdle in the game is "I have no money." After about four or five hours, you'll have your mining rig complete, and money will instantly no longer be an issue. There are only decorations to go for at that point, and, quite frankly, there are better games to pursue that particular niche, so motivation to play plummets shortly after you get fully automated.

It is still fun for those four or five hours.

From the outset, I knew this was my kind of game: a physics-based automation game (with conveyor belts!) I saw a clip of it on YouTube, and immediately got it for a fair price. I don't regret my purchase (I want to support indie developers, and I want to see more games like this in the future) but as it stands, this game is not ready for prime-time. I really want to like it.

The above mentions physics-based nature of the game means you are really putting a lot of faith into the physics engine. Dropping items on the ground, or bumping into something is a surefire way to have that thing flung off into the sunset. I have been playing the game less than two hours, and already managed to get the tractor stuck on the roof of a building with valuable cargo in tow. Digging a hole in the ground can be fun, but getting stuck in that hole due to the weird way the destructible terrain colliders render is not fun.

The core gameplay loop is clever, but only works until you realize that you'll be stuck doing that for many hours with little ability to progress to the "automation age". Having two totally different targeting reticles (one screen-based and one world-based) is a cardinal sin of user interaction design. I hope the developer finds a way around it.

There has got be a faster (or at least more interesting) way to get to the part of the game I'm really looking forward to: overseeing a sizeable automated mining system with belts and hoppers and machines chugging along everywhere. Carrying a single gold bar up the hill 20 times (because that's basically the only way to make money in the early game) is enough to sour the whole concept for me. 

I would like to revisit my review in a few months, but for now, this half-baked game needs a little while longer in the oven. My best wishes to the developer.

---ORIGINAL NEGATIVE REVIEW---

UPDATE:

New major release has a lot of gameplay improvements but is still insanely buggy right now. Review on its way to being positive, but I'm still judging pretty harshly given that this is clearly an early access game billed as a completed game.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

Will probably change this to positive at some point, but right now I can't. I had to check the store page to confirm it really wasn't early access, because it sure feels like it. There are the beginnings of a GREAT game here, but a lot of work needs to be put into the polish at this point.

PROS:

- Fun concepts
- Great graphics (not too flashy, very cohesive, good lighting and fun style)
- The voxel handling is mostly okay - digging really feels like you're digging, which is a hard thing to achieve.
- The shopping system is really fun. It feels realistic and satisfying loading up and taking away a haul.
- The early game is actually a lot of fun. I like having to do the work manually and build up to automation. Really makes you appreciate the game and makes the work feel worthwhile. The dig/water/scrub/smelt/craft flow is awesome and rewarding.

CONS

- SLOW. This game is soooo sloooowwwww to progress in. I saved up a bunch of gold before I started building automation - when I had enough to buy the parts, It took me an hour just to build a basic mining rig, and it was NOT a fun experience.
- The balance is very off. Things seem to cost a normal amount, but you have to buy a LOT in order to do anything interesting. The pipe system is fun but the proportions are tiny and cumbersome to work with, and the water pressure part is aggravating due to water being kind of far from any of your rigs.
- The physics are extremely buggy; items fall through the ground _often_, and your truck will randomly fly through the air to another part of the map without notice.
- It's not very clear how some things word - this is arguably a pro as I sometimes find this exciting, but there is no "affordance" (UX term) given by many of the items nor the piping systems.
- Item placement is annoying and buggy - you are allowed to place items under the ground, even deeper than the lowest diggable point, which makes no sense. Also, you can place e.g. two pipes in the same spot and it's a tossup how the game will react.
- It's quiet - no music, no people walking around, no voices. Just subtle sound effects (admittedly the ones that are there are quite pleasant to hear - there just aren't many).

SUGGESTIONS TO THE DEV(s):

- Fix the physics. Really. It's really bad. Fearing my stuff is going to fall through the ground is an awful feeling, and getting launched a mile into the air isn't fun either.
- Make straight pipes expandable, even if you raise the price 10x. Having to buy and then load 100 pieces into the truck just to get _anything_ running is tedious and kills any joy I had.
- Not sure if this is technically feasible, but make the entire underground diggable - not just the small plots. Enforce boundaries, sure, but I can see myself hitting the end of the game content and being frustrated.
- Add some music and ambient environment effects. The atmosphere is too quiet.
- Explain what the different trucks do. Why do three different colored trucks exist that are the same price but still more expensive than the default truck, which looks the same?
- The smelting process seems like I'm wasting ores because the bars cap out at a certain point, but there's no indication as to how to make sure.
- Make the drop point position (the green circle) configurable. It's incredibly awkward trying to chance a drop into a bucket or something - I spend maybe 20% of my time picking ♥♥♥♥ up because the aim was 1 pixel off.

    Since I'm probably about to be one of just a few negative reviews to have passing automation (more than 10 hours) let's talk about that. This was the part I was looking forward to, and the biggest disappointment, My first automation setup, I had a ram drill that dropped directly into a harvester, and a conveyor system with 3 sorters and 4 outlets (3 smelters and a group of foundations for gems and the ore you can’t sort yet). The first conveyor was a left turn, though this bug would still apply on any system with a turn, even using two straight pieces. $10 is a little high for this game, but worth it to support an solo independent developer. As of this review (v1.3), the game should still be in early access. If the developer keeps updating it, it will definitely be a gem amongst the dirt. 

The gameplay is somewhat unique. The fact that there's no inventory changes how you play, even thought it's is a bit frustrating that you can't hold more than one thing at a time. It's especially rough in the early game when you have to pick up the shovel, dig once, drop the dirt, drop the shovel, pick up the bucket, drop it in the water, pick up the bucket, drop the bucket, pick up the brush, click twice, and then drop the brush. Then you have one nugget. It's not even that it's grindy, it's just tiresome.

I found buckets/crucibles/truck beds to be quite interesting. You have to drop things in them freehand and they bounce around. But once they stop moving, they're stuck there until they're intentionally removed. It's a pretty satisfying mechanic. However, there are a few issues. The main one is dumping pans. When a pan has 20+ nuggets in it, it's difficult to get them all into the receiving container without spilling. It is not fun to have to pick up a whole bunch of individual nuggets. If I wanted to pick up crumbs, I'd just follow my own kids around IRL. 

The truck is a creative solution to moving many things and having no inventory. It's neat to load up the truck bed and drive around with all your junk visibly where you placed it. It's fast and fun to drive. The only issue I found was if the truck clips something, it can go flying and spinning. I got thrown half way across the map one time. It took ~30 seconds to land. Credit though, I just had to figure out where I was and drive home. Didn't get stuck or lose anything.

The conveyor system seemed to work pretty well. No complaints about the 20 piece conveyor system I built. 

The concept of using water to run all the machines is cool, but needs a little work. The pump is just a pipe stuck in the ground with no apparent reason it's able to create pressure. Maybe the pump should be a turbine? That would make a little more sense. Also, the pipe network should require that the water be flowing through the pipes; stuffing a cork in the end doesn't make sense because the water couldn't flow, and therefore couldn't make the machinery work. Maybe require that all pipes connect to a terminator, like an injector well that goes into the ground or something. 

The world is lifeless. That's kinda ok to a degree since the gameplay is focused on digging and building in a pit. But it's weird to see houses and buildings and stores, but not a single living person or animal anywhere. I'm guessing it's a feature that just hasn't been implemented yet and may come in a future update since there's literally nothing in that regard. Adding some NPCs that just do some basic animations and look at you when you walk by would add a lot to the feel of the world. Having some cows, sheep, rabbits, or ducks running around would add charm, especially if they interact with you in some way, like scrambling away from you when you're ramping off hills in the mountains in your tractor. 

OMG, please fix the spawn point for axes and swords. They collide with the anvil when they spawn and go flying. A few of them went clear into orbit and twinkled with the stars as they disappeared...

Overall, nice work for a solo developer! I hope more updates expand the game in the future!

Hydroneer is a physics-based game with a lot of potential and I've had many fun hours playing it. I'm looking forward to the next updates and appreciate the friendly and including developer, Max. It's beautiful to look at with an unique athmosphere that is better experienced than explained. 

The game is basically about artisanal mining (or traditional mining and gold panning). You buy claims and dig by hand with shovels, pans and pickaxes. The further down you dig the better the yields. Later in the game you can automate the mining process, sort the ore and upgrade your factory to a more productive level. To do this you process and sell items you craft from the ore. As it's physics-based you have to account for gravity as well while doing this.

The game has no inventory system, no GUI or anything like that. You litterally have to carry everything by hand, even your coins... This gives the game its unique, kinda "realistic" feel, but can also feel very grindy and sometimes frustrating... Especially with all the bugs. Even with the new pallets you have to go back and forth the shops to buy stuff. This takes tiiiiiiime. 

Pros:

- Nice, calming graphics with good colors
- Calm and nice music 
- Unique in almost every way
- Intuitive and easy to understand. Gives the player alot of freedom to experiment with different solutions to problems. 
- Well balanced economy (in my opinion) 
- The physics can be really fun while working properly. You can build actual ore chutes and processing facilities which function the same way they do IRL. 

Cons:

- Hydroneer is a buggy game with multiple really frustrating glitches: the vehicles acts like space ships and randomly fly through the air (yes, it's still a problem), items fall through the ground, items falls through conveoyrs (causes huge lag problems) and machines randomly stop working. 
- The physics engine is not especially good and can be really frustrating and weird; it's really hard to walk on uneven ground and you randomly get stuck. Same goes fro vehicles....
- Items and ore get stuck on conveoyrs randomly. 
- The game is not optimized at all... it gets laggy, really fast. 
- It can get really time consuming and grindy. If you forget to buy one thing, you must travel all the way back to the store and buy it. This takes time and will get annoying. 
- All movement is wanky and frustrating at times. You walk and get stuck, you drive and get stuck, you mine and get stuck. Just expect it. 

I still recommend this game because of all the fun I've had with it. It's a good mining simulator and will definetely give you many happy hours. That said, it's far from done and needs alot more work. In my eyes it should probably get an inventory system as well, but that's a splitted discussion. 
However, the main issue is all the bugs, the physics and just the grind. If you expect all of this and just accept the early game for what it is, it's really fun.
