This game is really good, and the developer is continually improving the game, adding features, fixing bugs and more importantly listening to, and working with the community (check out the super friendly discord). 

The Good (IMO) - I have a lot of time in games like Factorio and Satisfactory so I was nervous with this game as it seemed very simple, I couldn't have been more wrong. The game has no 'inventory' system, and instead you buy and use items and equipment more naturally (I always wondered how I carried 1000 factories in my backpack). While this seems daunting and laborious at first, what it means is when you construct/test/rebuild/tweak your machines and automation it is very, very rewarding. Building pipe networks to supply water power to your machines takes thought and instead of just plonking down 10 x of everything you really spend the time to figure out what you need, what you don't and how you can make something work with the least effort possible. 

The whole system of mining, from starting with shovel and bucket and building up to an automated factory and the big (and heavy) excavator is great. The game play loop of mining, expanding, designing etc. is fun and already I have 19 hours out of a game I picked up for less than £6, which to me is massive value for money. 

The Bad - The game's physics engine takes some getting used to and it is not rare to see items shoot off into orbit because of some reason. Trucks can also be difficult to manage, especially when they bug out. There is a good unstuck system in place, letting you reset you position, but this can be frustrating when you are in the middle of mining out a patch and you get stuck/bugged and have to reset. 

Additionally once you get 100k +, the in game money becomes pretty pointless and there are no real long terms goals other than the ones you make yourself. There is a blueprint system to unlock and some hidden items to find in the game but overall it is very sandbox in its design. I am currently challenging myself to make the biggest automated factory I can underground but this is just my own desires and I can see that some people will be frustrated with the lack of 'goals'. 

I think it is worth mentioning that lots of the reviews mention features that have either been improved upon or fixed with the most recent 1.3 update so I would advise you to watch some up to date videos before you base your opinion on the reviews here on steam, I am glad that I did. 

Overall I would highly recommend this game, especially at this price!

This game is a Mix of Astroneer, and Satisfactory. Currently being made by just 1 dev, i'd say this is one heck of a game. I've put about 9 hours into it and barely scratched the surface of the game. Each hour I play comes a new game mechanic or something new I've discovered. For just 10 bucks, I'd say this game is a catch!

I started out kind of middle of the road, not sure what I thought.  The whole "no inventory" thing was really different.  Suffice it to say it gets tedious fast.  

Everything is a solo item, some items such as bars and ores and gems can be combined in a pan and transported enmass. However, when it comes to automating your "mining operation"  every single piece must be dragged from the store one piece at a time.  For larger operations, this is a massive time sink just getting the stuff to the site to build.  

Then it comes to the mining machines themselves, not too shabby to be perfectly frank, BUT and this is a huge "but" , the rigs that mine drill a single hole, then stop.  the game states, that the deeper you dig the better the reward, however there is a massive codicil attached to this statement.  The depth you dig at is based on where you are standing and NOT where the actual ore was dug.  How is this an issue?  You can dig huge amounts below your level, and even a 1 foot hole will stop you from getting out since you character will get stuck on just about everything.  This makes getting in and out of your mine a tedious hassle and constant slipping back down a simple hill a 2 year old could climb.  So Digging below your level becomes a "must do" just to avoid constantly getting stuck.  However, doing this, makes your loot table take a massive puinch to the teeth,  This is ALSO the way that your major mining drills are based.  The loot table goes by what level the mining machine is placed at and not the depth that the drill head is drilling at.  So placing a drilling rig on the surface will always get you loot as though you were digging on the surface, rather than the 15 feet down that the drill head is at.  If you want good ores, your mining equipment MUST be at the level that you want to glean ore from.

Then we get to physics.  To say the physics are bad would be a massive understatement.  even totally terribad falls way short of the lousy and ludicrous physics systems that this game employs.  Drive over a wooden bucket with an excavator and all of a sudden your excavator pops up into the air spinning like a top and flying half way across the map.  This also happens when trying to sell items.  Put them on the table and when you release them, you get the sound of something impacting a collision mask and your item disappears flying across the map to who knows where.  

The vehicles aren't bad, but their turning radius and controls just plain suck.  The don't appear to have brakes at all, and you quickly learn to hit"q" to exit the cab just to get your vehicle to stop since leaving the vehicle instantly stops all motion, whereas staying IN the vehicle will cause road rage as you cost half way into the next county due to not having any brakes.  The "fuel" tanks are a joke, and requires an olympic athlete to fill the tanks.  Since they are on top of the vehicles and cannot be filled unless you are looking down into the tanks.  This is a huge problem for the excavator, since it is so huge, there is no way on top of it without having a foundation to jump on so you can get to the tank.  Not to mention, they are ridiculously TINY.  2 trips to and from town will empty your tanks.  

Does this game have potential?  Yeah, it sure does.  it needs some refinement, and should start with adding a wallet in which the players money is stored.  Having to cart around your money on the back of a truck then deposit into the little wicker baskets is just a game mechanic that doesn't work well at all.  It's unnecessary and just causes excess tedium.  

The rest of the hauling items back and forth one by one, I don't have an issue with that, it's pretty much the way you would do it IRL.   However, the items need to stay put when dropped, as it sits everything you drop can bounce around like a rubber ball, this INCLUDES vehicles.  Many items will be lost for ever, where they go, I have no clue, but I suspect they bounced beyond the edge of the map and were despawned.  

The building part of it isn't that bad, pretty respectful.  It's not rocket science, and everything is pretty much self explanatory, however, the places to build are the SAME as places to mine.  You CANNOT build on land you do not own. (this means digable dirt)  If you venture even an inch off of the "digable area" you will not be allowed to place anything.  There is a difference between "place" and "drop".  You can drop items anywhere you wish, but in order to "use" them the item MUST be placed.  

All in all, it's not a terribly bad game, it has huge issues that make it unplayable.  The constant spinning and bouncing and inability to climb even the smallest incline, just gets too tedious too fast.  That coupled with the absolutely laughable physics, just takes the fun out of the game.  It gets to the point after your truck goes into it's 100th spin into the sky and the headache that comes with it just makes a person hold down the "alt" key and hit the "f4".  Sweet release!

The game in and of itself is okay the premise is fun, the dev constantly updates and receives feedback well, and if that is all you are looking for then you will be hard-pressed to buy it and not enjoy this game. However the reason I am not recommending this game is due to the fact that it has a lot of issues that a game that is not in Early access should have.

  Stuff has a tendency to just suddenly rocket into outer space if it even hints at clipping something, [strike]that giant sword you made worth 5k which you worked hard for in early game? Drop it on the jeweler table only to have it shoot off never to be found again because the hilt of the sword clips into the table if you drop it standing over the table, and if you think to jump and do it? nope the roof prevents you from dropping it.[/strike] He(the dev) reworked the bigger weapons and stuff   so it's a lot less prevalant now, but some things still will rocket if they clip TL:DR- be careful where you drop stuff otherwise you may never see it again.

  Why is it that I have to drop things to place them in items into objects? Loading the truck is a pain because you have to jump and place it into the truck and hope it doesn't roll out so you can move it. The way you place none buildable things is terrible. You have a little green circle the tells you where it is going to drop, but what about when you need to place things inside of something, like the pressure increase tank? You have to hope that it rolls just right so it falls in and you can close the door, sometimes those doors   have collision which makes it easier but most times they do not, and you have to use the magnet on a stick to place it. Legit this is the dumbest part of this whole game. If I have a gem bar in my hand and I click the pressure tank it should just place it in the tank, or if i have something in my hand and i click the truck, just put in the back.  Tl:DR When placing objects if I need to place it inside of something, don't make me manually place it with  a janky system instead it should just auto insert if the correct item is in hand.

Buying things are tedious, you have to grab one item at a time drop it onto the buyer area then drag it into your truck, buying any large amount of items is crazy frustrating and tedious. The pallet is more or less a band-aid on a bad system, that in and of itself doesn't work well. the pallet just barely fits in the truck and if you place it wrong it is likely it will just roll out and shoot off somewhere. 

On there own they aren't so bad, but the more  'late' game you get the more you encounter these issues, and they quickly get frustrating when you're trying to build a completely enclosed automated system. Lastly the game is way to easy, you can easily reach 10k within the first hour, and once you have 10k there isn't anything you can't get your hands on. Even with just 1 basic ram drill, you can make upwards of 40k and hour with very little input yourself. Which is awesome! if it wasn't so easy to achieve, but once you're there the game is pretty much just creative with mild inconveniences to slow you down.

Super TL:DR The game is okay, but the more you play the more little things creep in to ruin your fun. It's fixable and if these things get fixed then I will 100% recommend this game.

This game does have a certain factorio like quality to it, where there is always something to do, but my god is it frustrating due to bugs.

Firstly, you get stuck, everywhere. Vehicles especially are 100% useless when moving on your dig site. I am not over-exaggerating when I say that making it 10 meters without getting stuck is very good progress. Luckily you can reset them in the main menu, which you have to do approximately 6 times every time you want to drive over to your smelters.

Next, the physics are abysmal. Whenever you place something, there is a 50% chance it will catapult away at the speed of sound never to be seen again. Placing some foundations in your truck? Flying away. Smithing a sword? Fyling away. Trying to place an axe on a table to sell it? Flying away. Placing that palette with 5k worth of goods on your truck? Goodbye to that. Seriously, do NOT use palettes.

I also had bugs where an invisible object remained on the bed of my truck forever, making that thing completely useless. Keep in mind there are only 5 trucks total in the game, once you bugged them all out the game is basically over.

The UI is also extremely user unfriendly. The idea of the game is that you have to carry every object individually but if you need 80 pipes that means putting 80 pipes on the counter (multiple times since they will bug out and fly away), then carrying them over individually o your truck (again, multiple times), then driving over to your claim and manually carry them to your area (on foot, because the truck gets stuck after 2 meters). Why.

Then, the content. There really isn't much. You need maybe 4-5 hours before being able to afford the best equipment, and enough of it that you are busy 100% of the time with the manual tasks that cannot be automated. 

Check this game out in two years maybe.

Surprisingly fun game that gives you a "hands on" feeling of productivity. You really play into the physics of the game, dropping metal ore into a cauldron to smelt ores is pretty good. No inventory screens to fiddle with and your pickaxe/shovel doesn't break with use. No annoying grid to craft items in. The crafting system in the game is, at least at the moment, completely optional. You don't need to craft things to turn a profit, but it does improve your profit.

It's perversely satisfying to pick up a bucket filled with so much gold ore that you lose FPS and then to dump it into a melting pot to hear every lump of gold burn into liquid and destroy your ears in the process.

It is pretty buggy at the moment though.I can definitely see people losing a lot of hard work due to bugs. I managed to avoid that for 15 hours though. I wish there was a better save/load system to improve that though. It seems there is only one save slot and if you go to main menu, it auto saves. So once a pallet of values flies through the air, you probably want to alt+f4 just in case.

Also the vehicles need improvement. They essentially have no brakes, and no torque. It takes a good 5 seconds to get moving. The wheels turn super slowly. It's just massively out of place and all of this just needs to be adjusted to be more responsive like the rest of the game.

But these are pretty minor complaints. I only hope more content gets added to the game. I've reached the point where I can buy anything in the game now. I guess I could build a house or something, but there's no reason to yet. I hope the game adopts some systems from Eco which is the only game I know of that did a good job motivating you to build reasonable structures.

[b][u]UPDATED REVIEW 7/19/20[/u][/b]

My original review was a "Do Not Recommend." I'm giving this game more and more time just because of how much I want it to be good, and I can't in good conscience dissuade people from playing it for the reasons I mention below. I don't want my review to stop someone from dropping a measly $7 to give it a try for themselves because it is undoubtedly fun at times, and despite the frustrations, it's clear the developers are trying to iron these out as they go. The last thing I want to do is reward an active indie dev with a "Not Recommended" review.

YES. The physics engine sucks. I can't emphasize it enough, and there's no two ways around it. The trucks pretend to be rocket ships at random times, items love to play hide-and-seek, and things clip through the voxel earth frequently, but there are also good things and frankly addictive things about it that keeps me coming back to try again.

[u]Pros[/u]

• A balanced fusion of voxel-based building games and construct-and-craft, productivity sim games. Think of a mix between Minecraft and Factorio, where the simplest elements of both are combined.

• Plenty to do. At first it's grindy, but it gets you used to the mechanics.

• The game doesn't need explaining. Devs seem to be adding quality of life improvements, so make sure you keep an eye out for documentation.

• There's a satisfying amount of problem-solving. Voxel-based land editing does slow down the building process considerably though.

• The two-point interaction system takes getting used to, but it's a pretty clever solution to keeping your vision clear while carrying an item, and being indicated where said item will drop if you let it go.

[u]Cons[/u]

• The physics engine F**KING SUCKS in combination with the voxel elements. 

• Vehicles have the WORST control, and no brakes. I have to Q to exit the vehicle in order to stop it from moving. I don't know if the difficult controls is by design or to avoid breaking the physics engine further, but dear god it's frustrating. The plow truck is also completely unruly and almost takes all the purpose out of it being an easier alternative to digging by hand.

[u]Suggestions[/u]

If you're receptive, here's some things I think would vastly improve your game.

1) PLEASE add a hoe to smooth land. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE. Digging makes it so jagged and hard to manage/walk over.

2) The magnetic stick/staff:

a) It picks up non-magnetic things. I suggest the C500 magnet be an actual magnet that helps you separate iron from the rest for early-game quality of life improvement. The C1,000 could be the item attractor that it is now.

b) For both, I would ask for stronger attraction. I can't move without dropping items.

3) Add in something that visually indicates depth of field. When I'm underground, the walls all appear to be the same distance without the visual reference of a flat ground. Maybe that's a fog, slight blurriness, or saturation fall-off, I don't know.

4) The pallet is wonderful, but when it's full you can't see where you're going I suggest adding a slight transparency to any item you're holding if it obfuscates your vision.

5) Add a bit higher tolerance when walking or driving over voxel land. I have to bunny hope in places because it becomes too jagged to walk, and driving vehicles over it isn't even worth attempting, and that's unfortunate because the water is always way in the back of the lots.

I'm loving the game. And I'm loving the Discord community. Everyone is open to discussion, including the very active dev.

For me, one of the best parts is that there is no UI. No confusing info on screen. Very hard to do with a complex game like this and still make it easy to use. It does mean that you need to carry everything. Yes, even your money.
The controls take a bit to get used to, but once you get them, it's easy to work with.

The graphics are nice to look at and there are a lot of fun things to discover. 
Sound effects need some work still, but there are a few fun sounds in the game.
There needs to be more content, but the single dev is adding more every update, so I'm not too worried about that.

The grind is there for sure, but it's not as bad as I feared. Progress at the start is fast enough to keep you engaged.
It does get to be a grind at some point, but then you get to really build a base.

And that's where the fun starts for me. 
- How are you building the perfect base to refuel your truck and smelt all the gold and iron.
- Where are you going to smelt the ore into bars?
- How will you setup the crafting of jewelery and weapons?
- Will you add flowers to decorate, or just use concrete for everything?
- Will you paint the walls for fun or function?
So many ways to do it. It's all there.
And then there is the logistics of the conveyor belts and water pressure to deal with.

There are bugs in the game though. The Dev is working hard to iron them out, but it takes time. 
Sometimes it's just better to start over to be sure that there are no lingering issues after an update.

If you are like me and don't mind a restart then this is an awesome game.
If you don't like restarts, the game can be annoying/grindy at times, but thankfully it's easy to do. You'll be back to where you were in no time.
If you really don't like restarting, then it might be better to wait until all the bugs are worked out and the game is completely finished.

Even though it's not listed as an Early Access game, it does feel like it. Thankfully the Dev is very active and open.
For the price it's an awesome game as it is now, and there is more to come still.

I saw this game in a video from Josh at Let's Game it Out. He's a fun Youtuber, and really sold the game for me. While my play style is far from his; he did a great job showing the things I like in a game.

Hydroneer has been *mostly* bug free for me; 
 - You hit anything just wrong with the truck, you can and WILL rotate to the far reaches of the reachable map. 
- Your items might just clip through the diggable dirt to the bedrock. Good luck finding them, but they're findable.
- Oh no, all my buckets of dirt are now empty when I reloaded the game. :(

These are not all the bugs present in the game, but these are the ones I have had happen, and found them in no way game breaking. 

Other then the bugs, this game is there to reward you for being and doing mundane things. There is no handholding either. You figure out everything on your own.  

The game seems to have a healthy fan base, but I've not reached out to anyone else that has played, but the forums are nice and the developer is very active. Almost everything suggested he says he adds on to a brainstorming list. I like that.

The soundtrack is very, in the true name of the word Background. I'm vaguely reminded of Star Trek Deep Space 9's opening everytime my brain focuses in on the music while I'm running around or waiting on my ores to melt.

The hardest to get over thing about this game for me is the lack of inventory. Be warned, you can only ever carry one thing at a time. You get a free truck when you start the game, but it's as much of a hassle to load and unload as it is with just running around carrying one item at a time. 

While annoying, it doesn't ruin the game for me; but I can see it being a pain in the ass for other people.

All in all, 8/10. This is the game I've decided I can play when I don't know what game to play.

The game is fun for a few hours. As it stands, there is very little to do in the game. The progression is laughable to say the least. I'm not one of the people who are slamming this for the physics, those are easy to work around just don't drive like your irl lunatic self and exercise some proper behavior behind the wheel (I know this is hard because so few people are accustom to it in their own cars) and you will have little to no problems.

Several issues that I have are going to be fixed, the dev has already mentioned them in a youtube vid and is working/worked on them so that's good. On the progression side of things, right now you literally have 1 option to automate your work. Yes, there's the super drill Goliath, but it's not automate-able as it stands. With the new update adding the D.A.V.I.D. it could potentially make it automated but right now, it's not.

The biggest issue, and the one that has brought me to this review and to stop playing is the repair/break system. If you use filters, then your drill/grinders wont break as much. That's great! But wait, there's a catch. Your damn filter is going to break every 5 minutes and totally stop water from moving through the pipes. I like having to manage the systems, for gods sake I play games that are micromanaging intense all the time and love them, but there is something totally off about the frequency of breaks, at least in respect to filters. There needs to be a massive balance done to these mechanics more so then the physics. 

If you want a game to last a few hours this is totally worth the price. I don't think I've found a game this cheap that is as well done. If you want a gold mining game, this is the one to go for. Sure, Gold Rush The Game may have much more in progression and much more play time possibility, but for a game that ALL of its mechanics work, maybe not perfectly but at least they work, Hydroneer beats GRTG by a long shot. I would direct the dev to the breaks in GRTG to look for a better system/frequency to base off. That being said... what the f*ck is the point of the second vehicle? You can destroy a huge part of land in moments but you have to refuel the damn thing every 2-3 buckets. At least these vehicles... you know, work (I'm looking at you Gold Rush and your damn dozer). Also, don't plan on making a nice slope with the terraforming tools... just don't try. Dig a damn hole and use the slanted ladders. I also feel that the pick axe needs to be sped up or a better tool be added to ease the pain of diging out a hole. Right now a small cavern takes about 30 min to do and it will hardly hold anything in it so uh... yeah, speed that up a little please?

*UPDATE AFTER UPDATE 1.3*
I thought the new update would add much needed things and solve a bunch of problems. Instead, it added in the problem of items just falling through the damn conveyors again. Oh, dirt also has some amazing collisions that stop it from falling on the processors... that's nice. Love the new smelter, and the funnels can actually be used... if all the items didn't just phase through things and the dirt didn't just float. Somehow, with less single ore piece floating around performance with the new parts has gotten way worse. So much has been added in terms of goal making but progression still isn't really there. The game at this point is just a grinder, kinda like a clicker but a few more functions. The new DAVID item is really cool and a fantastic idea... it doesn't work worth a damn. It sometimes fills the spot above it, and I was under the impression it was supposed to fill a column above it. I have 75%ish pressure on it and it hardly works. It isn't worth it to use the thing because of the pressure crystals they take.

1/20/2021 MAJOR 1.6 Logic and Power update! 
So I decided to give this another go because I saw there were some big updates. The vehicle doesn't go flying the moment you bump into things anymore so that's nice. That's not saying it wont do it on occasion, but it's not as frequent as it used to be. 
I felt like the game in general was running quite well, up to the point that I started getting some sorters running and oh boy, does the lag start. I had a huge multi line set up in the past, and that only caused minor lag because the ores were stuck in-between the conveyors and sorters. This time, I have a single line. 1 ram drill, 1 grinder, and 1 sorter... 20 fps when I get anywhere near it. No, there isn't ore getting stuck in there like before so that's good. No, there isn't tons of ore on the ground, so that's good. I have no clue what's causing the lag. It's not my PC either. I have drastically upgraded since the last time I played: 32gb of DDR4 2133 MHz, i9-10900K, and a 1080Ti, so it's not a pc issue at all. The performance of this game has somehow, gotten much worse. Oh, I also lost 3 axes when I heated up the iron bars and forged them... they just went into space. I'll have to contract Elon to go get them for me I guess. I can't forge any weapon on the anvil without looking like I'm trying to beat China to the moon, cheaper and faster. I'm not sure how the logic stuff works, but god it seems way over complicated for this game. That's not to say it isn't usable, I know how to do stuff in Factorio so complex logic isn't an issue of mine. It just seems like for the scope of this game, that it's way too much. There is still no more content to this game than the last time I reviewed it. I think the only thing added was the logic stuff, and that's not game advancement, it's just more fluff. The damn filters seem to break a little less frequently, but idk if that's just me not remembering and hoping for the best. They still break way too fast.

Very promising.  Interesting concepts, like the explicit exclusion of an inventory system.  For the price, it's a good investment just to scratch my occasional OCD itch when I want to play a different game for a short bit and just mine or build.

There are only a few mild annoyances that I regularly encounter that make certain tasks unreasonably cumbersome and tedious.  The most glaring is the physics of large building components.  It is so unbelievably difficult to transport moderate to large quantities of flooring and walls and sometimes even getting them in the bed of the truck without launching into the stratosphere is a challenge.  The second is the size of the smelting pots.  Some nuggets can hardly be dropped in without hitting the time and ingots are a time-consuming chore to consolidate into a more valuable ingot.  Basically, the game could benefit greatly from scaled-up tools and components.  Why can't there be an Industrial Crucible as a fixed component if we can nearly automate everything else?

Of course, the next step would be content to drive the players to forge and sell; Contracts and such.  Currently, the game only grants unique benefits to forging specific weapons or jewelry for the stock market, but doesn't offer incentive to craft more valuable items with specific qualities.

[b]TL:DR[/b]:I tentatively give this game a recommendation if you are fans of factory/automation/excavation style games. It has a great concept with a lot of promise, but still needs a lot of improvements and quality of life fixes. 

[b][u]Pros[/u][/b]
-[b]Gameplay[/b]: The overall mechanics and design of the game is enjoyable and had me glued for hours
- [b]Strategy[/b]: The planning and design of your hydro mining area is great fun.
- [b]Graphics[/b]: Pleasant low-poly design. 
- [b]Satisfaction[/b]: When a design comes together and everything works it is extremely satisfying and keeps you coming back to make modification, tweaks, or just try out new stuff. 

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
- [b]Physics[/b]: Within 10 seconds of driving a vehicle and you clip a light pole or rock you will go flying. Matter of fact the more irritating things is having to deal with tools/objects etc flying off into space because they collided.
- [b]Purchasing Items[/b]: Purchasing new items has to be the biggest draw back in its current state. You have to pick each item up individually to put on a platform, then after purchase load each item into the back of your vehicle all while combating physics. 90% of your time will be spent picking/loading/unloading of items in this game. I would honestly prefer to be able to pick an item and quantity have it appear in the tuck then unload the truck, especially since the machinery is a ways across the map making back and forth trips tedious. 
- [b]Claim[/b]: The claim layout is hit or miss. You are better off starting in the dead center of the claim that way you ensure you don't hit the edges of your claim. I did this a few times and had to pickup and move my entire setup. 
- [b]More To Do[/b]: I wish there was more to do or over all purpose to generating money aside from getting the coins to get them coins. After a few hours you will likely have access to all the equipment and machinery, but once you get a setup you like there's no real reason to continue. Halfway through my playtime I was already making rings/necklaces worth 10k a piece. I now have about 50k credits sitting at each store and just don't know what else to do.

So, I decided to give Hydroneer another go. I put in around 20+ hours over the last week or so, and I can safely say that I have been frustrated for 90% of the time. 

The game is fun for a while and it has a certain charm about it, but there are so many things that have not been fixed, or new items added in-game that replace old items, but the logic behind them is baffling (the Cloutium drill for example: you can place it in the air, with just a blob of dirt on the "grinding roller thing" and that dirt is basically infinite). 

Do you like games that allow you to terraform the terrain in order to realise your dream mine? Well, this game does not have that. Yes, you can terraform to an extent (using a combination of a pickaxe and rake) but holy meatballs it is poorly integrated. Hell, I would go so far as to say it's just badly thought out and unintuitive. There is a definite need for efficient and user-friendly terrain modifying tools. 

Do you like building complex/automated processing chains? Me too! Can you do that in Hydroneer? Yes, but man you will ♥♥♥♥ bullets while you build. Why? Well, for starters, the building system is garbage - it uses a position + distance grid system, so you can scroll the mouse wheel to adjust how far away you want to build something, which isn't new to games, but it is badly implemented in Hydroneer since objects ONLY snap to the grid, not other objects. This means that you cannot "walk and build" in a single direction since objects will snap to a grid block you are not necessarily looking at. Doesn't sound too bad? Try building a continuous pipeline, without having to stop, often, to fix a pipe that snapped above, below or next to the pipe you were looking at.

Speaking of building, say you wanted to adjust a pipe/logic network to be higher, or go around something - simple right? Nope. If you have a section of pipe/cable oriented horizontally to your view, and you pick it up, it will not be in the same orientation - it may now be vertically oriented and rotated once around the vertical axis, or it might be rotated 45 degrees from it's original position etc. This makes adjusting your network a horribly tedious and frustrating activity since you cannot just "lift and place" something, you will have to reorient it 99% of the time. 

The logic system (+, -, >=, ==) is pretty neat, if it works. I have had to resort to "manual" automated logic circuits, which I don't really mind, but some people might want a fully automated network. This is doable, but I have seen logic operators "break" or "fail" to trigger based on inputs. Example: I have a weight sensor that is set to read the weight of an iron bar when it comes out the logic furnace. The logic network is setup with a >= node that basically checks if A (weight of iron bar) is greater than or equal to B (1000), and if it is, it should trigger the output of the >= node which is connected to a switch that disables the return conveyor network. But, it never triggers. Perhaps the weight being read (float/decimal) is not able to check against an integer which is something the dev should have considered and either used casting to convert the float, or made it clear that that is beyond the scope of the logic nodes. 

Hydroneer is actually fun for a while, but there are a number of gaps that should have been filled before moving out of Early Access. 

Oh, and optimisation doesn't exist, despite UE4 having a really robust set of tools to help developers optimise their game. An example of poor optimisation: a single smelter cauldron dropped my fps and caused stuttering when clicking on it to drop out the iron bar. I built 3 more of them, same problem. TOOK MY TOOLS AND BUCKETS OUT OF THE QUARRY AREA, no more stuttering when dropping a bar. Then there is the tractor vehicle thing: Buying objects/machines and placing them on the back of your vehicle results in the object freezing in place and seems to lose it's collision mesh, which is great since you can really pack things on. Or so you would think. Eventually you start to see your fps tanking as the game tries to keep track of all the "ghosted" objects you have clipped together, almost as if the collision mesh is still tracking collisions but not triggering collision physics (since the objects are frozen in place). This can and will crash your game. 

So... 

Should you buy the game? If you have money to burn, don't care about poorly integrated physics, poorly implemented gameplay mechanics and zero optimisation? Yes, go ahead and buy it. 

Will I keep playing it? Probably since I have high hopes for Hydroneer, and I'll be damned if I don't get to finish my factory before throwing in the towel completely. (Maybe I am a sucker for punishment, eh, who knows). 

I left the old review in for perspective since it is ALL still valid (yes, even the bit about money not being needed for anything since yes, you can buy parts and build a house, but there is no need to at all... you do not need shelter, whatsoever). 

## OLD REVIEW ##

Poorly integrated physics: The physics engine starts off charming, and quite fun. That feeling lasts for a few minutes, at which point you begin to get more and more frustrated by the ores clipping and flying all over the place. 

Refining: I get it. The game wants you to work for your money by making you understand that you WILL lose resources to physics. Whether it's watching ores behave badly when trying to pour the little rocks into the crucible or watching your smelted goods clip to infinity and beyond. 

Grindy - not always a bad thing but in this case it is since there is literally no point to doing anything. See the Money point for a concise description as to the pointlessness of it all. 

Money: You don't need money to buy food/shelter/clothing, or anything really. There is no  meaningful game progression apart from creating some sort of automated system to help you get more money, to do literally nothing meaningful with. 

The game is apparently aimed at the casual market, which would make sense if the physics engine actually worked, and there was [i]some[/i] point to literally anything you do in game. 

Get it on sale (90% off is where I would aim).

The physics in the game are so janky that it makes actually using the systems provided extremely difficulty and by that a I mean you spend almost all your time trying to find ways to stop resources from clipping through barriers, flying around, or just spontaneously clogging themselves instead of actually digging.

Hydroneer, unlike its genre-defining predecessor Minecraft, relies on a physics simulation for all of its goods, vehicles, and miscellaneous objects. This starts off rather cute, as you dunk pans into water, drop nuggets into buckets, and begin shaping the earth around you. But the bugs and idiosyncracies of the physics engine are many, and you can only stand the experience of "trying to pour a bucket and its contents explode everywhere randomly" a few times before it begins to gnaw at you.

The physics engine makes the early-game, during which you are required to manually manipulate all of the game's objects and resources, unnecessarily difficult. It does promise the opportunity to eventually automate production, but I simply couldn't get through the early game without needing to take frequent breaks to calm down after something I was handling clipped into something else and went careening off randomly.

When I tried to pour a bucket of ore into a crucible and every nugget clip-sploded over the dig site, I decided to stop.

I don't often write reviews for games, but [i]especiallyp/[/i] given that I considered returning it after about an hour of playing but then logged 12 highly-engaged hours in 2 days (while working full-time)... I'll share my thoughts! Clearly the long and short of it is, if this game calls to you as the type that you enjoy, you [i]should[/i] take the leap and get it. For some context, my games with the most hours logged are, by far, Stardew Valley and Minecraft

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[*] It's not like other games out there -- it's more hands-on with closer-to-reality mechanics than games like Minecraft, but not [i]so[/i] realistic and slow as games like Farming Simulator. You really are digging up the dirt and sorting through for resources, starting out slow and becoming more efficient as you go.
[*] The mechanics for crafting ores into bars into goods are pretty neat, particularly in how the size of the bars plays into the size of the good... keeps it entertaining, somehow!
[*] At the start it can feel like you could [i]never[/i] possibly have enough money to buy more than a shovel and pan and brush... but at a truly reasonable pace, you start to feel like you're getting [i]too[/i] rich [i]too[/i] fast. And then you venture out further from your base to the other Keep and get put back in your place a bit -- you sure have progressed, but at a pace and level that makes sense!
[*] The things that feel like they might be too tedious to tolerate can quick end up captivating, making hours disappear from your life and not letting you free
[*] In direct contrast to some other posts about wonky physics sending items flying - you can make a remarkably tall tower of gold bars (for example) and it will not budge if you walk into it! (Personally I've only made a few items go flying so far, and it's mostly been when accidentally but [i]blatantly[i/] clipping them into each other...ie, my fault)

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[*] There is no inventory, and you can only hold one thing at a time. Even things such as the map and your money are [i]items[/i] in the world -- so when you go to buy a pan around the corner, you have to carry your money over, carry the pan home, run back, get your money, and go home again. It can become a little bit infuriating after awhile. I don't think we necessarily need an entire inventory, but at the [i]very least[/i] having money stored intangibly would make a big difference
[*] Similar to that, the mechanics can be quite a bit clunky. Particularly the initial mining process: shovel dirt, put in bucket, shovel, bucket, drop the shovel, pick up the bucket, pour into pan, drop the bucket, pick up the pan, [i]drop the pan in the water[/i], remove the pan from the water, drop it on land, brush it. The area directly surrounding you can become extremely cluttered extremely quickly.
[*] Similar still, there's [i]also[/i] nothing in the vein of chests or storage to use; [i]every single item is somewhere in the world, [b]always[/b][/i]
[*] I've gotten my truck stuck an incredibly number of times and had to use the "recall nearest vehicle" function far too often, just to have to try the same maneuver again and get stuck again.......
[*] There is next to no tutorial regarding [i]mechanics[/i] of gameplay, only an overview of the [i]concepts[/i]. I couldn't for the life of me figure out how to pour a bucket into a pan, so I decided it was impossible and spent an embarrassing amount of time working with one shovelful of dirt at a time directly into the pan. There's other things like that as well, where confusing or misbehaving mechanics can leave you assuming you've done something wrong, when in reality, it's just...touchy, or was never explained.
[*] When placing built items, you are confined to 90-degree rotations, which is a pain given that nothing else in the world is confined to 90-degree rotations
[*] When placing items in general, you have some control over placement, but you can't seem to rotate them at all...so you can put a lantern in a very specific spot, but it's gonna be on its side when you do.
[*] You might think that a game built around voxel dirt would allow for some pretty cool terraforming, but actually, it's next to impossible to get anything smooth or flat or how you want it, mostly because no matter how tiny a spec of dirt you pick up, you'll always put down the same large and rounded shovelful. You really can't flatten your terrain, try as you might.
[*] Not a big one, but like others have said, the world sure is... dead. Like, there are 2 well-built town-type-areas (Keeps) with many of the signs of life... but not a [i]single[/i] npc or animal. I figured there were at least a couple and folks just thought there weren't [i]enough[/i], but no, you are the [i]only[/i] one in this world!!

[h1]Other Notes[/h1]

I haven't dived in to automations and the like yet -- given that there's not a lot I can see in terms of how to [i]spend[/i] mass amounts of wealth, I'm a bit hesitant to implement something that grows wealth quickly and takes away from what I'd even [i]do[/i] in game. For now I'm going to keep shoveling manually (with some additions to the initialy process for ease and comfort), but perhaps I'll one day end up a millionaire and be back to share how that went!

I know I had a lot more to say on cons than pros, but I think that's just because the cons stand out more... these are small-ish things that don't make me like the game less, but are annoying; meanwhile I do sincerely enjoy this game immensely, I just can't quite as clearly name [i]why[/i]!!

某金採掘ゲームのパクリじゃん！的なレビューを書いてしまいすいません。
メインとなる採掘は設置できるブロックの種類が初期に比べて飛躍的に上昇、某金採掘ゲームは重機（車両）や機材に重点を置いていた点に対してこちらは自動化に重点を置いていて自動化の為のブロックも修理から精製に至るまでのロジックを組み立てれるようになりました。
また採掘できる鉱石の種類も増えてより高価なものを作って、より高度な生産ラインを作る為にお金を使えるようになり、以前のように初期の自動化をしてしまった後のお金の使い道がない状態から自分の納得する最高の生産ラインを各採掘場に設置する為にいくらでもお金が必要になりました。

また、農業も増え、住人のNPCがクエストを提供してくるようになったのでお金を儲ける以外にも何かを作る目的が出来て常に時限のない目的が出来てメリハリが出来たと思います。

鉱石の種類や自動化のブロックの種類が増えても金属系最終作成物は5種類のままなのでやれることややることが増えても面倒に感じなくて良い感じです。

そして、ファストトラベルがなかったりアイテムは持てるものは一つだったりで個人的にはちょうどよい不便さで、良い感じですし、マルチプレイに対応したことでそれらが面倒だと思う方も牧場シミュレーション系が好きな友達とワイワイするのにオススメです。
ただ、下記のように基本的に不親切なので気長に一緒にやってくれる友達とじゃないとダメですが。


不満点としてはチュートリアルは実装されましたし、ところどころで絵による説明があるけれど、文章での説明は完全に不足していて例えば車の燃料（水）の入れ方や鉱石等の振り分け機の使い方、二機目以降の採掘機の入手法などは本当に分かりづらく、建築に関してもUI的に設置がしやすいとはとても言えず、モノを置くにも地面が平坦じゃなければ物理エンジンががんばりすぎてコロコロ転がってしまうし、全力でオススメかと言われると・・・となります。

なんか説明不足で操作性が微妙なゲームを試行錯誤しつつ、謎解きゲームするノリで、それでいて自動化してお金稼ぐゲームです。

追記ここまで。

この操作感、身に覚えが・・・これ[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/451340/Gold_Rush_The_Game/]Goldrush the game [/url]だ！


そんなわけでグラフィックはポップな感じのGoldRushです。
操作性だけでなく一部のマップや初期の自力で金を探す動作がほぼ一緒なので違うとは言わせない。

あちらは現実にある（と思う）重機を揃えて行き、ただただ金を掘るゲームでしたがこちらは金だけでなく鉄や希少な宝石等が産出され、さらにインゴットはもとより剣や宝石に自分で鍛冶屋を営むことに。世界観がイマイチわかりません。

[h1] ポイント[/h1]
・ずっと土を掘り返して金などの鉱石を採掘するゲームです。
・釣りができます。
・チュートリアルは3分程度のYoutubeです、早期アクセスじゃないのにね。
・わからない事は自分で調べるタイプです、初めは売る場所さえゲーム内ではわからないので結構きつい。
・GoldRushと同じく街は無人です、でも変なメモもないしポップな絵柄のおかげでホラーっぽくはありません。
・自動化は水道を引いたり、2つ目の街に行けばベルトコンベアや工業製品等もありちょっとだけファクトリオなどの工業自動化ゲーみたいな感じで自動化していきます。
・とはいえ加工品は短剣、斧、剣、指輪、ネックレスの伍種類なのでそこまで複雑なライン構築とかないです。
・電力は無くても明かりはつくし色々動いてくれます、某金採掘ゲームのように電源や電線を気にしなくて大丈夫。（一部の機械は水が動力になります）
・釣りができます。
・とある金採掘ゲームのように機械は故障しません、よって部品の交換とかしなくて大丈夫。(嘘です、故障します、直すのはツールボックスを使います）
・なんか一瞬街づくり要素あるのか？と思わせる雰囲気がありますが、ありません。
・ポケットやベルトに収まるだろって工具やお金でさえも手に持って移動しなきゃいけません、（もちろん持ってたら他のものは持てません）プレイヤーは裸なんだと思います。
・でも自分の家を壁や屋根、家具を買って作れます、シングルゲーで街の人もいないのでさみしいですが。
・なんか洞窟があるぞ？ワクワクすっぞ？と思ったけどそういうふうに掘ればできます、でも基本（特に重機を入手してからは）地表をどんどん掘っていくので洞窟状にしないと思います、そこは趣味でやれる、だけです。（エアプでした、、採掘の為では無く、自動化のラインを作る過程で洞窟もどきを作ることになると思います。）
・なんかパイプラインあるぞ？ドキドキすっぞ？と思ったけどそこまで必要ありません、そういうふうに配置すればそれっぽいスクリーンショットが取れます、そこは趣味でやれる、だけです。
・釣りができます。

[h1]総評 [/h1]
GoldRushという金を採掘する（一応シーズンを区切ってオンラインランキングイベントをしてますが）だけがゴール、とにかく掘る、効率よく掘るだけで良いと言う方、つまり私なんかは面白いと感じますが、貯めたお金とかどうするの？と言うふうに考えてしまう人には向いておりません。

とはいえ、こちらは季節によって水源が凍ったりすることもなく平和すぎて、さらに言えばドリルを設置すれば土を自動で掘ってくれるんだけれども、土の上ならすぐ下を空洞にしようとも土が無限に掘れてしまい、やり方さえ理解できればものの20時間位で、試行錯誤しながらでも30時間もあれば特に意味のない家作りしかすることないなぁとなってしまう。

正直、早期アクセスであって欲しい、そしてよくある農業ゲームのように街の人とかとのイベントがあっても良いのでは？マルチで分業とかできるようにしても良いのでは？と言いたい事は結構ありますが、個人的になんにも縛られずただただ土を掘って効率よく自動化の方法を考えるのも嫌いではないのでオススメにしました。

For a single developer, this game is truly a blessing. Yes, there are bugs, but none that are game breaking as there are workarounds in place for them. 

Pros: 
- Creativity, it's all up to you 
- Everything is done by hand
- The basic functionality of most of the devices work (aside from a few)

Cons:
- Vehicle / Terrain collision: It's more so avoiding a bug where it sends your vehicle up into the sky spinning endlessly. Thankfully, the developer put it in a button to Recall Your Vehicle and "Unstuck" yourself whether you are in a vehicle or not.
- Excavator is in the game, but with the terrain/vehicle collision bug, it's very hard to use.
- Sometimes the Harvester doesn't eat all the ore and you get yourself a clog. I've learned to just accept that it's part of the game at the moment. This is due to another bug which I will list below
- Whenever you exit the game, and then come back in, if you had dirt on a belt, it will not move when turned on, which causes the clogging.

Suggestions:
- Make buying in bulk an option
- Allow for an option to "Load Things You Just Bought Into Nearest Vehicle"

Tl;dr - It's a $10 game, it's very enjoyable. It's still needs development but there is a ton of opportunity.

Hydroneer is pretty amazing and interesting game. It's fun , has Medieval look , has Mining , Digging for Gold , Simulation type of game. I will point some good and bad points to the game tho. 

Good points.
1. Nice and cool gold searching mining simulator.
2. Cool and interesting concept. 
3. Intuitive and fun way to mine for resources and you can also build bases/houses/barns/Factories . 
4. It has conveyor belts , automation and a GIANT drill on a vehicle.

Bad Points tho. 
1. really really bad physics on absolutely everything like vehicles, items and everything that you pick up and drop on the ground. 
2. chunky and really annoying dirt with no shaping meaning its not that consistent.. not sure if that is a way to explain it but i will give an example. When you start digging for gold and other stuff the dirt its weird chunks and leaves tiny specs that are almost invisible and pretty hard to remove and blocks your way moving with or without the vehicles. 
3. I like your idea with no inventory but for this specific process its not good . Nice idea but not great one . The reason behind it is moving back and forth to pick one item drop it into the buying space in the shop, then drop it into your HydroTruck from there moving everything your plot/Claim/base, from there to start dropping it off the HydroTruck and then start using it ... not good. Also what happens when you run out of pipes/walls/windows/conveyorbelts and all other stuff you always need to buy when you start building a house or a mining automatic grinder/machine ? Not good.
4. Almost 90 hours in the game and i am already bored/exhausted from chugging items non stop in this empty world with absolutely nobody in expect my ghostly non existent character that you can only see a shadow of something when you hold an item or equip the mining helmet. Also i would need nerves of steel or really good patience with the game in order to look over the "No inventory or backpack" type of game.

Max you really need to look really good into this and make a way to store items into something or this will not last a lot of time . I've had quite a bit of fun at the start, but now it is getting repetitive and grindy and a bit boring when you have 5 resources to grind which are extremely easy to get right now in the state of the game, not that many things to do in the game , as i said before pretty empty world with absolutely no living things in it like an interactive NPC or any types of animal roaming around in the wild.

Seulement depuis 2 semaines plus rien. Plus aucune mise à jour...alors qu'il y à toujours des bug affreux.

On peut poser des questions sur le discord...mais attention a ce que vous dites, si vous n'êtes pas au courant de quelque chose, une âme pas forcement bien attentionné vous fera remarquer votre ignorance...

Pour parler du jeu... très vite lassant. Si c'est pas les bug qui vous gaverons ce sera le manque de perspective du jeu. C'est assez creux. 2 véhicules, 2 foreuses automatique. 2 Pelles et des tuyaux, des tuyaux et encore des tuyaux... Ok, il faut des tuyaux, mais quand vous devez poser 50 tuyaux pour alimenter vos foreuse en les transportant 1 par 1...c'est très vite saoulant. 
Les objets qui disparaissent...laissez moi poser le décor. Vous partez acheter 4 tuyaux et 1 tapis, parce qu'il vous en reste assez sur place. Vous revenez avec vos achats, et vous vous apercevez que les objets que vous aviez en rab ont tous disparu...
Ah oui vous avez des outils de réparation aussi. Et attention ce point la est surement la plus grosse connerie de gameplay selon moi. Vos machines s'endommage avec le temps, pour réduire cela vous pouvez mettre des filtre, pour "purifier" l'eau qui arrive. A chaque fois que vous réparer une machine vous consommez un outil. CONSOMMEZ ! Oui, l'outil disparait et vous en avez 5 par caisse a outil. Et ça putain, ça...quand vous passerez votre temps a réparer... Moi aussi a chaque fois que j'utilise un tournevis au boulot, je le change a chaque utilisaton. Tout ça vous fera une nouvelle raison de vous demandez pourquoi vous jouer a ce jeu. 

Récapitulatif

     - Les bugs.
     - La mentalité de la communauté. Vous me direz, ouais normal...
     - Pauvre en contenu. En 29h j'ai fait le tour...et encore...avec les bug j'ai du jouer 10h...
     - Les objets qui disparaissent.
     - Le manque de patch.
     - La consommation hallucinante des outils...

Un début prometteur mais final...il va surement finir comme beaucoup de petit jeu indé.

I can't recommend this game in it's current state. It's a great idea on the existing automation style. 
As it is at the moment however, you can expect difficult to drive vehicles, clunky material processing, everything to be done manually and just a difficult terrain system.
It's incredibly easy to get your vehicle stuck sideways over the side of a bridge.
To get a single piece of ore you have to pick up shovel, dig, place in bucket, drop shovel, pick up bucket, drop in water, pick up bucket, drop on land, pick up brush, brush bucket... You get the point.
Frankly, there is zero automation. You still dig the dirt, just in larger quantities and then have to process it.
And expect to get "stuck" on terrain a LOT. I never got actually stuck to where I couldn't get out but if I didn't have a shovel in my mine, I would not have been able to leave. Luckily there is a stuck feature that drops you out into the world, but it's still a pain to have to wiggle your way into a mine
It has evolved and become more interesting over time. Still a lot to discover since the gems update.

(Mais où sont mes tapis roulants ? Ah, oui, 12 mètres sous terre...)

Il y a aussi des bugs de collision ou de physique assez déroutants ; l'excavatrice qui fait des salto en triple lutz piqué alors qu'il n'y avait qu'une petite bosse sous l'une de ses roues, ou bien l'hydrocamion dont l'une des roues arrière touche un élément posé dans son coffre et commence à voler à travers toute la carte... Il y a toujours un moyen de s'en sortir avec beaucoup de patience (pour l'hydrocamion, en sortir au moment où il touche le sol, puis vider son contenu problématique... OK, ça m'a pris 10 minutes quand même).

A part ça, il y a de quoi se triturer les neurones dans tous les sens ; placer ce qu'on croit être une bonne chaîne de concassage et triage, se rendre compte qu'elle ne fonctionne pas bien, déplacer ses éléments, aller en racheter, miner à la main pour trouver les fonds pour faire des courses, recommencer un nouvel automatisme, déplacer ses éléments, recommencer, améliorer, se rendre compte qu'un tapis roulant est parti dans la rivière parce qu'on s'est pris les pieds dedans, fondre ses pépites de fer ou d'or, faire des piles de lingots, choisir le craft qui rapportera le plus, l'apporter au marché ou chez le joaillier, tenter d'améliorer son automatisme, recommencer parce que ça ne fonctionne pas si bien que ça, etc etc...

...Et faire sa maison, parce qu'une fois qu'on a l'argent, pourquoi ne pas construire sa maison pendant que la mine tourne ? Il y a de tout ! Des murs avec ou sans fenêtres, des sols, des toits, des meubles, des décorations, etc... 

On attend avec impatience les 2 mises à jour majeures qui arriveront en été et à l'automne, pour voir ce qu'on peut encore améliorer dans nos mines !

Et d'ici-là, faut que je trouve moyen de faire descendre mon excavatrice sans qu'elle ne fasse ses salto en triple lutz piqué !

Vorweg, ich möchte diese Spiel wirklich lieben. Nichts ist so erfrischend wie Hydroneer und dem buddeln nach Gold. Ich sehe gerade das ich fast 60h auf der Uhr habe, aber denke es sind genug um ein Review abzugeben. Das Spiel fesselt von der ersten Minute an, Gold Nuggets, welche sich im Eimer vermehren, machen süchtig nach mehr. In den ersten Stunden fallen auch die endlosen Bugs nicht so schwer ins Gewicht.

Allerdings wird das ganze mit zunehmender Spielzeit immer nerviger. Die gesamte Automatisierung steht sich selbst im Weg, da es einfach ein Graus ist . Mit Wasserdruck muss alles betrieben werden, hat man allerdings einen Loop im Rohre System stürzt das ganze Spiel ab. Man kann immer nur in eine Richtung bauen, da Förderbänder zwar automatisch Wasser befördern, es jedoch keine Kreuzungen gibt. Das Bohrer System ist für den Barsch. Man kann einen Goliath Bohrer kaufen, dieser arbeitet aber nur für ca. 5 Minuten, danach steht er still. Unter Ihm ein riesiges Loch, alle entfernbare Erde ist abgetragen. Das ganze ist so Sinnfrei, da man den Bohrer quasi ständig neu positionieren muss, und dabei natürlich auch die komplette Konstruktion umbauen muss, um Wasseranschlüsse und Förderbänder neu zu verlegen. Es gibt zwar auch noch eine kleine Version der Bohrer, Jedoch ist es wurscht wo man diese platziert. Selbst in tiefsten Höhlen wo eigentlich dicke Goldbrocken zu Tage gefördert werden, spuckt dieses Maschinchen nur Millimeter große Nuggets aus. 

Also steckt man irgend wann einfach im Dilemma fest. Bau ich aller drei Minuten für ein paar dicke Brocken meine Konstruktion um, oder lasse ich das Ding stundenlang laufen für Goldkrümel, welche ich natürlich auch noch händisch einzeln aufsammeln muss. Wenn man dann einige Stunden mit dem Bau, hin und her fahren, sowie dem Sammeln verbracht hat, und die Euphorie ihren Höhepunkt im Schmieden einer Halskette erreicht hat, diese dann leider nach dem Klick mit den Schmiedehammer auf den Amboss, einfach verschwindet , kommt enorme Freude auf und man merkt das dieses Spiel einen eigentlich nur veralbern will. 

Mir ist klar das es eine Person ist welche für die Entwicklung von Hydroneer verantwortlich ist. Jedoch will auch diese eine Person Geld dafür haben. Schwebende und verschwundene Items, eine schier scheußliche Physik, sowie die völlig Sinnfreie Bohrer und Automatik Maschinen Mechanik, lassen das Spiel wirken wie eine Satire für verschwendete Spielzeit. Deshalb leider keine Empfehlung.

Update:
Nachdem ich dem Spiel nach langer Zeit mal wieder eine Chance gegeben habe kann ich sagen, dass es zwar ein winzig kleines bisschen besser geworden ist aber noch weit davon weg ist gut spielbar zu sein. Immer noch ist die Physik eine Katastrophe. Fahrzeuge fliegen bei kleinen Kollisionen oder Überfahren von Gegenständen wild durch die Luft, Erz, Edelsteine etc wird vom Sortierer ausgeschossen wie von einer Railgun und landet irgendwo in der Pampa usw, usw. Jaja, es ist immer noch eine Person, die dahinter steckt, trotzdem muss sich ein Spiel, egal von wie vielen Leuten es entwickelt wird, daran messen lassen, ob es Spaß macht oder nicht. Und, sorry, das macht keinen Spaß. Es hält ja nicht mal seine eigenen Versprechen.

Naja, eine One-Man-Show-Entwicklung kurz nach Release und das merkt man an einigen Stellen schon sehr. Insgesamt eine gute Idee für Mining-Freunde, die graphisch ganz gut präsentiert wird. Das Spiel birgt viel Potenzial in sich ein schönes Spiel zu werden. Was aber zum jetzigen Stand überwiegt, sind die extrem nervigen Bugs und das (bis jetzt) fehlende Feintuning. 
So muss man z.B. einen Zulauf für die existenzielle Wasserversorgung immer mal abreißen und an gleicher Stelle wieder aufbauen, bis er funktioniert. Die Platzierung einiger Komponenten funktioniert manchmal nur bei einem bestimmten, sehr engen Kamerawinkel oder während man die Spielfigur dabei bewegt, was den Spaßfaktor beim Bau sehr trübt. 
Das absolut nervigste überhaupt ist aber die spinnende Physik. Die Rohstoffe schießen nur so aus den Erntemaschinen und fliegen kreuz und quer, anstatt an das nachfolgende Laufband übergeben zu werden. Berührt man mit den Fahrzeugen einen gebauten oder abgelegten Gegenstand auch nur leicht, wird das Fahrzeug in die Luft geschleudert und ladet irgendwo in der Pampa, was das Rangieren an der eigenen Basis zu einer Zerreißprobe macht. Generell sind die beiden Fahrzeuge nicht gut programmiert. Die kleine Steigung von der Grube zur Straße stellt für den riesen Offroad-Bagger z.B. ein unüberwindliches Hindernis dar und ist er mal in der Grube um seinen Zweck zu erfüllen, lässt er sich hier nicht sinnvoll kontrollieren und fährt sich schneller fest, als man "Bagger" sagen kann. Die Fahrzeuge zu bedienen ist zur Zeit das nervigste, was man in einem Game machen kann. 
Alles in allem: gute Idee mit viel Potenzial, aber bis zum Spielspaß braucht es noch ein paar Updates. Stand jetzt keine Empfehlung.

Au début, Hydroneer suscite de l’enthousiasme, mais cela se transforme rapidement en frustration. Bien qu’il m’ait initialement captivé, ce jeu se révèle un échec en raison de mécanismes mal conçus et d’une finition insuffisante. L’idée de simuler l’extraction de ressources à l’aide de machines et d’outils se heurte rapidement à une expérience de jeu qui semble à peine plus qu’un assemblage maladroit d’éléments déconnectés. Plongeons sans plus tarder dans l’analyse de cette aventure laborieuse.

[h2]L’intrigue, ou plutôt son absence[/h2]
Le jeu présente une toile de fond aussi vide qu’une carrière de minerai après des heures de travail acharné. Hydroneer se révèle dépourvu d’un récit engageant, ce qui empêche toute expérience immersive. L’absence d’histoire concrète ou de quête significative assombrit encore le tableau. La personne qui joue s’y retrouve rapidement lancée dans un cycle de collecte et de cumul sans véritable but, où chaque avancée semble dictée par une quête d’argent virtuel sans profondeur. Tout au long de l’expérience, l’on se sent coincé dans une boucle sans fin, sans aucune réelle motivation à poursuivre. Ce manque d’enjeu diminue fortement l’envie de s’investir dans un univers pourtant porteur de potentiel.

[h2]Une jouabilité rébarbative et frustrante[/h2]
Le plus grand défaut d’Hydroneer réside dans sa jouabilité, qui laisse à désirer. Malgré une mécanique de base plutôt simple (pomper de l’eau pour extraire des minerais et les vendre), la répétitivité accablante rend chaque minute de jeu de plus en plus ennuyeuse. L’interface, bien qu’intuitive en théorie, souffre d’une rigidité déconcertante. Les outils et machines ne réagissent pas toujours comme on l’attend, et la gestion des ressources devient une véritable corvée. Je ressens à peine la sensation de progression, chaque étape du processus me parait trop longue et mécanique. Nous devons éviter de mentionner la gestion des tuyaux et autres équipements, qui frôle souvent l’absurde, avec des éléments qui semblent ne jamais se connecter correctement ou qui entrainent des anomalies inutiles. La frustration atteint son apogée quand l’on s’aperçoit que les quelques progrès réalisés ne mènent nulle part.

[h2]Graphismes : un style rétro ennuyeux[/h2]
Les graphismes d’Hydroneer semblent issus d’une époque révolue, et non d’une expérience moderne de jeu. Même si une partie de la communauté peut apprécier son style simpliste, on doit admettre que les textures et les animations manquent de détails. Les objets semblent inachevés, les environnements manquent de vie, et même les machines censées émerveiller ne procurent aucune réelle sensation de grandeur. Le rendu visuel d’un jeu censé simuler l’exploitation minière ne parvient jamais à impressionner. En réalité, ce jeu n’arrive pas à me captiver autant que je l’aurais souhaité, car son univers manque de profondeur et de personnalité.

[h2]Bande-son : une mer calme sans vagues[/h2]
Quant à la bande-son, elle aurait pu constituer l’élément salvateur d’Hydroneer, mais elle tombe à plat. On peut à peine percevoir les effets sonores, et, lorsque la musique se fait entendre, elle n’apporte aucune ambiance particulière. La répétition des sons — souvent les mêmes bruits d’eau qui coule ou de machines en mouvement — devient vite insupportable. L’aspect sonore, qui pourrait pourtant contribuer à renforcer l’immersion dans un univers de travail mécanique et laborieux, ne fait que renforcer cette sensation de vacuité. Le jeu souffre d’une carence évidente en matière d’éléments audios qui, dans un titre de ce genre, auraient pu souligner l’effort physique nécessaire pour extraire les ressources.

[h2]Immersion : une expérience bancale[/h2]
L’un des plus grands échecs d’Hydroneer réside dans son incapacité à créer une véritable immersion. Un jeu de ce genre, qui repose sur des mécanismes de simulation, aurait dû entrainer la partie en une expérience quasi tangible. Pourtant, l’environnement stérile, l’absence d’interactions significatives avec les autres éléments et les mécaniques de jouabilité trop rigides rendent l’immersion quasi impossible. Le manque de profondeur de l’univers nous rend insensibles à nos actions dans le jeu. Hydroneer parvient à l’exploit de rendre une expérience de minage ennuyeuse et dénuée de tout intérêt.

[h2]Conclusion : une expérience en déclin[/h2]
En somme, Hydroneer manque de vision, d’ambition et surtout de contenu. Ce qui semblait, au départ, une idée originale de simulation minière se transforme vite en un exercice fastidieux et rébarbatif. L’absence d’histoire, l’ennui généré par la répétitivité des tâches et la pauvreté de l’univers graphique et sonore nuisent gravement à l’expérience de jeu. Malgré quelques bonnes intentions, Hydroneer échoue à offrir une expérience engageante et mérite davantage sa place dans les oubliettes des jeux ratés que sur les étagères des adeptes de simulation. Finalement, on ne ressent plus qu’un sentiment d’occasion ratée.

After many hours of enjoyment I would like to update my review of this game.  It is amazing.  It was originally developed by one person, and because of how awesome it is, there is now a team working to improve on it's original form.

The automation and progression are pretty dope. While it doesn't seem like you can automate the entire pipeline, it seems like that it is intentional. The game developer doesn't want you to be able to setup a fully automated pipeline. It is still early, so we'll see how far you are able to get with automation.

[h1]What I like:[/h1]
I liked the game. It has a different take for mining and smelting and crafting. The game is small enough to get into and explore but big enough to where you can spend hours building out a base and mining.

The game developer does talk about the 4 main play styles and how he will develop them out further. I love the fact that the game is so cheap and that the developer is still adding features. I spent a crazy amount of time already and I can't believe I love the game. It somehow makes what would be tedious into fun. Not sure if it is the end goal of wanting to automate as much as possible or crafting what you have into items so you can sell.

What the game has currently is enough to get you through enough hours to make the game well worth the price. I am excited to see what else the developer adds.

[h1]What I didn't like:[/h1]
The progression isn't fully balanced. The starting area is decently balanced. You start with a pan and work your way to setting up piping to fill the bucket. It seems like it wants you to get to the point where you can buy the first bigger plot and then mine there. However, if you bring back the equipment from the dragon city, then you can mine the starting area faster, being able to make craft faster and make enough money to purchase the most expensive and profitable plot or just all of the plots.

Four mining areas is a lot and you'll spend a lot of time mining all of the areas, either by hand or drills. I think I would like more. Or at least a better progression where I can't just purchase all of the plots and make money from the starting area to jump to the final area. The game is still in development and the developer is adding new features, so it is possible we'll get more, but then again, it will take forever to mine all of the areas as it is.

You sometimes have to play a minigame where your truck achieves orbit and you have to get your stuff. Not a bad minigame, but it does distract from the mining and while optional, you will want to get your stuff/truck. At least the minigame no longer involves losing all of your stuff, so much less punishing than earlier versions.

The developer doesn't want to do an inventory system, which I understand the explanation, but it would fix a lot of problems, from the orbiting truck to spending most of your time carrying one thing at a time to where it needs to go. It isn't that terrible since your truck works as an inventory system. I just think that the game could be improved with some inventory system besides the bucket, truck, or hand system. Not a huge thing because I feel like the complexity of adding an inventory system is one of the reasons the developer doesn't want to add it. It probably could have cut a lot of hours out of the game if there was a proper inventory system.

Le début du jeu est sympa, ça passe le temps, on mine tranquillement, on cherche nos petites pépites. Quand tout à coup on pose notre pelle au sol pour aller vendre notre butin, une fois le petit trajet réaliser, a peine retourner sur le site de minage on aperçoit que notre si belle pelle posé au sol s'est volatilisée, tiens, étrange ? 
En continuant le jeu malgré cela, on découvre de "grande" possibilités de minage pour nous simplifiez la vie et ainsi faire fructifié cette si belle parcelle. On a donc accès a un grand nombre de machines permettant d'automatisé le minage. 
Une fois le système mit en route, ouverture d'une vanne d'eau puis paff, le jeu crash. Etrange non ? Ensuite une fois reconnecter on modifie le placement de cette vanne, qui sans doute n'était peut-être pas au bon endroit. Donc ou l'a réouvre, puis on re-crash. Donc on modifie complétement le système afin de le faire fonctionner et pouvoir enfin avoir la chance d'automatisé notre petit minage si relaxant. 
Ouufff tout fonctionne, très bien, enfin presque, les trieurs de recources ne fonctionnes pas correctement, on se retrouve donc avec des lingots de tout et n'importe quoi, mais tant pis, une fois cuit on obtiens de l'or, génial ! 
Donc on continue tranquillement notre petite aventure, jusqu'a ce qu'on se balade un peu trop avec notre beau tracteur vert et ses roues qui tournes un peu comme elles le souhaitent. Puis on prends un bosse, puis un petit muret jusqu'à décoller dans le ciel sans plus pouvoir rien faire. On respawn, puis on vois que notre jolie tracteur reste dans le ciel à virevolter joyeusement, tant pis, on en rachètera un. 
C'est donc seulement en rentrant à notre parcelle si pratique grâce à son "automatisme", et oui, une fois arrivé on découvre que comme notre pelle au tout début, une des machines c'est tout bonnement volatilisée, tiens donc, 7000 hydropièces pour ce petit système, ce n'est rien, y'a qu'a recommencer. 

Ce que je veux dire pour finir c'est que ce jeu est assez distrayant, il fait bien passer le temps et peu même nous faire cogiter un peu. Mais si il pouvait être Mis à jour assez souvent ça serais beaucoup plus intéressant.
Les bugs sont beaucoup beaucoup trop présent pour un jeu aussi simple. On cherche à se relaxer en jouant à ce jeu, pas a perdre la tête car on dois acheter 4 fois la même pelle ou encore 3 fois la même machine. 
Une fois les bugs corriger je penses qu'il pourra être beaucoup plus amusant.

This game, is very much an early access game, it has not truly been released fully as the developer is still constantly updating the game with new content. For that reason, I think a lot of the troubles/bugs that I may run into are slightly forgiven. For instance, one bug I have is that I can no longer pump water into one of the trucks in the game, meaning I can't move it, which is annoying, but I can work around it. One thing which is super bad and I'd watch out for is, if you have too many items in the back of a truck, attempting to move that truck will most likely pull you through the map, breaking the game and causing you to lose your truck with everything in it, which is super annoying, but I guess was kind of my fault in the first place.
Anyway, with that being said, the game in it's current state is fun, but can get pretty boring fast. This is the kind of game where you spend hours creating a system and then you run it for a few minutes and then you feel accomplished when everything runs smoothly and the gold starts rolling in. The game is fun, due to the way it's developed and the lack of an inventory system, fully automating stuff is not really possible, as there will always be some limiting factor. However, you can come really close, which is super cool. 
Due to the game being in early access, there's a lot of odd behaviors which may happen, but they normally get patched out in an update or two, so you only have to deal with them for a short while. The game is an engineering type of game where the main focus is really to automate your mining operation to become filthy rich. So, if that's your style you'll definitely enjoy this game.

tl;dr: The game is basically early access, it's fun in it's current state and I look forward to more expansions and content for the game, I think it'll be super great and really fun.

[h1]Dare you dig[/h1]
It is kind of insane how few games dare tackle digging. Hydroneer is one of the few games on Steam that even feature the "Mining" tag, even though there are a few out there, most prominently perhaps No Man's Sky. But us Diggers know why we're still searching. We know why terraforming in Astroneer and NMS and Terraria is unsatisfying to us.

[h1]Sculpting with pickaxe[/h1]
Voxel-based soil works comparable to 7 Days to Die, albeit less satisfying. Detail sculpting is still merely a dream, but the fun, open-ended gameplay loop makes up for it, sure. No sense trying to level dirt manually as of yet, not even close. Which does explain why you can't dig outside of the four designated zones.

[h1]What game does have cool terraforming?[/h1]
Call me weird, but for me Wurm Unlimited still hasn't been dethroned for its best detailed terraforming and landscaping mechanics. Pity though that there's just too little of a single player game in it, besides a myriad of other issues, but that is what I'm after and why I'm happy to purchase Hydroneer.

[h1]We need more games without mobs like this[/h1]
One final thought, if this game doesn't add crop farming, tree growing and herb collecting mechanics, I'll be disappointed because this is the closest to a single player Sandbox world that doesn't rely on mobs to make things interesting that we've ever gotten. But these haven't been even remotely announced, so it's pretty safe to assume this game will stay what it is and just get better at it - ore mining and water piping.

Okay so at first I didn't want to give this game a bad review because I thought I was doing something wrong. But at the time of this review, I spent 12 hours in the game and I still can't automate anything. A single conveyor costs as much as 15 to 20 minutes of IRL work. Automating stuff is a huge pain and costs a heckton of money. So don't expect to achieve anything quickly because to my knowledge, there is no quick way to make enough money to build a reliable, working automated mine.

But it doesn't stop there. On top of mining, you have to take care of your machines by fixing them regularly, and this will cost a lot of money. You will have to make frequent travels to the hardware shop to buy tools, and that with the extremely poorly designed tractor that you will have to fight against so that you don't end up flying and barrel-rolling. This will happen way more than you can conceivably imagine: just ever so slightly touch a rock with a turning wheel and any vehicle you will drive will end up flying in a random direction.

Talking of flying, what the hell is wrong with the anvil? If you make items with large ingots, like daggers, when you craft them they instantly go fly into any direction and you have to pick it up miles away from where you crafted it, just so that you could get enough to buy a quarter of a conveyor or a tenth of an automated drill. Physics in this game is extremely touchy.

I will end up by saying that this game puts my PC to its knees when it comes to performance. I do have a very good framerate, it basically never drops below 60FPS but it takes my entire system power to do so, so I imagine that someone with a modest mid-level PC would not be able to play this. There's a really poor graphics-to-performance ratio here.

This game should've been into early access at this stage. Although I do not recommend playing it for now, I do recommend getting it nonetheless. Wait for a discount, it's a rather new game for now, and issues will be fixed at some point probably. The developpers could probably use the funding to enhance the game.

[h1]Hydroneer，一个“神奇”的采矿世界[/h1]

作为一款沙盒游戏，《Hydroneer》或许是最特立独行的，它没有各类角色和职业的选择，也没有容量不小的背包和多种多样的道具；对，这就是一款简简单单、朴实无华的挖矿游戏，有着无比真实的物理引擎和丰富多彩的各式bug。

[h1]游戏玩法：开局一把铲，暴富全靠挖[/h1]

游戏初期就是一把铲，加上一个不锈钢脸盆，一把刷子和一个桶，主要采矿工具就是这把“飞天铲”，通过铲子挖掘泥土，洗刷干净后获取金矿，再通过售卖得到资源，换取工具，扩大开采规模，进而暴富(实际上就是个矿工，而不是家里有矿的地主）。值得一提的是，游戏较为贴心地将工具放在了并不起眼的地方，玩家需要对自由探索，以发现此“惊喜”。提倡了“自己动手，丰衣足食”的劳动理念，极有“教育意义”。

[h1]优点

创新性[/h1]

本款游戏也是一款“挖矿模拟器”，该题材十分新颖，满足了广大“搬砖”用户“挖矿暴富”的心理需求。

[h1]耐玩性[/h1]

作为一款沙盒游戏，耐玩特色并不少见。这款游戏模拟了挖矿的各个过程，十分真实，包括细致的刷洗和分拣金矿过程，各个步骤都能由玩家自主操作，极其耐玩。

[h1]真实但又极不友好的操作系统[/h1]

游戏过程极其真实，采矿当然得双手铲土，再去使用其他物品的时候，须得让铲子脱手，才能使用其他道具；当通关时，就可以自豪地说“这游戏我单手都能玩通关”。但这恰恰也是游戏的特色，增强了挑战性，不论是“挖矿”操作，还是路线规划，都可以由玩家去寻求最优解，从而获得成就感。或许，这也算是本作的一大优点。

[h1]缺点

游戏只是附赠品，bug才是该作主体[/h1]

除了让人诟病的“独臂”操作，本作最为突出的缺点，应该就是极其丰富的各类bug了。作为一个“麻瓜”，你永远不知道你的铲子会飞到哪儿去；当你放下铲子时，他或许又会融入土中，消失不见，或许这把铲子才是当初孙悟空未能吃上的“人参果”的化身；还有各类飞天bug，体验飞一般的感觉。时不时就得删档从头再来，才能得以继续进行“采矿事业”。

[h1]缺少内置新手引导[/h1]

游戏的新手引导是YouTube的视频，对于国内大部分玩家来说，并不方便。游戏无内置新手引导，这不得不说是一份缺憾。由于沙盒开放式的特性，这款游戏对于新手并不友好，游戏前期往往需要自行摸索，这点或许能劝退绝大多数玩家。

[h1]总结[/h1]

游戏的优点不少，本可以成为很好的作品，但恶性bug和较差的新手引导教程，使得本作的游戏性都大打折扣，极大影响了玩家体验，故在此给出中差评。
希望开发商能在后续更新中完善各类问题，早日将hydroneer变成一款备受好评的成功的沙盒游戏。

[h1]评分[/h1]

创新性：7.0/10.0
可玩性：6.5/10.0
操作和引导：6/10.0
画面和音效：6.5/10.0
[h1]总评分：6.5/10.0[/h1]
