Updated review (v1.6):

Game lag is vastly improved since my rant after trying v1.4, this has made me very happy so I can actually play the game.  So, what's new?...

Power
You can now power your factory!!  I really like this idea, but really hope it doesn't move too far away from the whole hydro aspect (I see there is already a hydro DAVID).  If it is possible to power everything with electricity cable rather than water pipes, so the Dev should reconsider the title of the game.

The powered filters.  Having read the description and seeing the price, I bought, hooked it up, scrapped my old filters.  Lovely, what a treat.... until my gear started to let off fireworks!  What?  Checked the filter and sure enough it was dead, and letting 100% unfiltered water into my pipes!  After a quick trip to the shop, I bought a load of logic cables, spanner thrower, durability reader and lots of other great stuff.  Back at HQ, I wired up the durability reader and spanner thrower and now my powered filter is producing 100% filtered water without me needing to keep fixing it (just have to load more spanners now and then).  I really do like this, which brings me nicely onto...

Logic

GREAT IDEA, and massively improves my hydro-life.  Apart from the above, I've also plugged in a bunch of lights and switches in my 'control hub' so turn my drills/water/power/everything off.

I would like to see more in the logic area.  We have a >=, but also need a <= and perhaps even a configurable logic device than can be switched between ==, <=, <, >, >=, !=, etc?

The timer/delay is a great idea, but can you imagine needing a 10+ second delay????  That's a long cable!  Perhaps just have a single logic device that can be set with the delay value?


Existing issues

It's great to have this new stuff, but it'd also be nice to fix the stuff that is still badly broken.

Pallets - they still shoot you off into the sky.  While this is very entertaining, and you don't die from the fall, it does mean you'll likely lose the pallet and it's contents.  Again - I remind you - don't put money on the pallets!  Also when carrying a pallet - the controls get all messed-up and it's really hard to move.

Game still gets quite laggy, even with everything being smelted.  Just need to empty the gems into the compressor regularly to make it better.

There are a bunch of other changes in previous updates which I'll note here...

Running - yes!!  Do we still need to walk, or maybe the Dev could just increase the walk speed to match of run?

Dirt directly onto conveyor!  Yes, it's back!!!  Much obliged :)

Gem compressor - awesome, fantastic, super - better than selling uncut to the jeweller, and combines into the different types!!  Great addition!

Updated review (v1.4):

Just don't bother playing.  Game lags so much it is unusable!  At first I thought it was my gem collection, but sold that and no change.  Everything else has an auto-smelter, so it's no an issue with remembering chunks.  It's currently unplayable.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Updated review (v1.3):

The furnaces are a great addition.  They limit the serious lag from storing thousands of items in a container (and the rage associated with picking-up said container).  Although - the conveyor sorters aren't 100% accurate at sorting, so it is possible to get mixed minerals boiling in your furnaces which reduces the value of the resultant bar.

Do not get me started on pallets.  Nice idea, but the issue of something being catapulted into the stratosphere is made worse, because you add lots of stuff to a pallet, and when that catapults you lose lots more.  I had several episodes of a pallet changing into a spaceship... I added stuff to it, picked it up and it flew through the air with me attached.  I dropped it, fell to the floor and watched as the pallet vanished from sight.  Oh, and DO NOT PUT YOUR MONEY ON A PALLET!!!

Physics is much improved.  I can now empty a container without being showed with the contents!   Great for dropping stuff onto a conveyor. Thanks :)

Apparently the truck doesn't spin anymore.  Wrong.  In fact, it's worse than before.

Conveyors - much improved with the addition of the centraliser - stops stuff getting stuck at the edges.  Thanks.

The harvester is worse this update.  Dirt is flying off all over the place when being ground (not the animation), leaving chunks all over the place.  It still won't process dirt already present when switched on, so you have to clear it all first when changing water filters or loading your game.

The conveyor shredder is much worse too.  Even with in place, large dirt just rolls over the top, eventually blocking my set-up.

Conveyor barriers are a nice addition.  They look smart and seem to stop stuff falling off.

Water filters are MUCH better now.  I can actually focus on other things without spending all my life, buying, transporting and replacing them.  Thanks!

Not sure if this was the case before, but I find that if I go somewhere else (i.e. another plot of land) and work there.  When I return, everything has switched off.  Really annoying!

The above also applies to loading a game.  I save with everything switched on and running.  Reload my game and I have to  run around switching all my drills and goliaths back on.  Please just let it resume from where I left it!

D.A.V.I.D seems rather pointless.  It supplies the goliath with dirt, but it's always top-level dirt regardless of where it is situated (I placed it at the bottom of the plot).  Just use lots of ram drills.  If you want big gold/iron/gems, just go dig it yourself in the other plots.

I still can't recommend the game, but if the dev continues to update like this, and adds some more content - it won't be long before it gets the thumbs up from me.

Original review...

I really want to love this game, however there are just far too many problems for it to be supposedly 'completed', all of which are obvious and should have been resolved before making it available on Steam.

Physics
Something touches something else, and it gets sent into the atmosphere, including the player!
You accidentally (or intentionally) empty a bucket or pan full of gems and suddenly it's raining gems across the entire map!
You walk over your tools and they are catapulted across the map.
I find pipes and other kit randomly sinks into the dirt, never to be seen again (even after the 'patch').

Broken equipment
Dirt gets stuck on the conveyors, causing them to double in size then eventually block your entire system
Just don't bother with any automation - you'll spend more of your time watching over it and fixes problems when they occur.
If you switch your conveyors/grinders off, any dirt already present has to be manually removed before starting again, otherwise it just sits there eventually blocking everything.

2 mouse pointers - one just for dropping stuff (the green ring - which often is very hard to see).  I did eventually get used to this, but it's totally pointless - just have the centre cursor for using/dropping - simple!

Money
Give me a bank account!!!
Dropping a stack on money merges the value into one stack - apart from when it doesn't.

It's a great concept, but it clearly isn't ready yet.  I'll keep the game and hope the dev resolves the above in due course.

This is definitely my kind of game. But there's just too much inbetween that's not playing the game. 
Shovelling dirt into a bucket, filling the pan with water, and sifting for gold are fun. Walking to the shop to buy another pair of buckets and having to walk the pair of buckets individually back is not fun. Digging a deep tunnel to mine for ore is fun. Not being able to walk back up the slope to get out, because it's covered in jagged pixels, not fun. Respect to the guy who made this, and he can have the $10 I paid for it, but this game needs a lot of refining of the core reward loop and a lot of removal of tedious aiming a shovel at a bucket, and aiming a bucket at a pan. Of picking up individual nuggets from each pan to combine into a single pan to walk all the way back to the jeweler, and then finding out a bucket filled with gold, is not enough to buy a shovel. So instead I spent the rest of the day toting single lanterns back to base.

Very jank at times, but still a really good start for a solo-developed game. I'm honestly having a really great time with it, and have put in a few hours nonstop.

Things that are needed:
- Fix the physics, things explode too frequently
- Fix the skipping/frame rate issues, it stops every 30 seconds or so
- Inventory system or something better than manually carrying things, like at least let me carry tools with me. I understand if products and ores need to be carried by hand which makes sense, but I shouldn't spend a solid minute setting down my shovel, watching it glitch out into the stratosphere, and then calmly picking up my brush so that I can start scrubbing.
- Better map system, what even is that massive thing?
- Better shops, maybe a shopkeeping npc to start with?
- Better tool animations, why are they all upright?
- Smaller grid placement.
- Better water physics, it's called Hydroneer after all.
- User interface needs an entire rework, why can't I adjust settings in game?
- Better save system, I don't want to quit out whenever I want to save.
- Way more production systems, like being able to create pipes would be a nice addition.
- Smaller vehicle that doesn't explode whenever I use it, like a bike with a basket or something.

Those are just some things that stood out in my short time so far, I intend to dump more hours into this. To whoever is working on this, awesome job, it's really impressive so far. I really look forward to seeing where it goes from here, and to seeing what other games you have in mind.

Edit: After playing some more I've come to one conclusion... this game is practically unplayable. I found it fun for the first 2ish hours, but after the 3rd I was starting to get annoyed. My vehicle has taken off into the stratosphere at least 20 times, I lost all of my money, 3000 coins because it too was sent into the heavens, and the frame rate feels like a slide show. Definitely not worth 10 dollars in its current state, or anything until the one guy working on this puts some polish into it. It's a shame, because I think it looks like a cool concept. But why waste 10 dollars on this when you can get a polished product like satisfactory, which has 99% fewer bugs and at least 10 times the content? Such a shame.

This game is an indie game with only a single developer working on it, so considering that, it's a great achievement. However, at the moment, the game is barely playable. You can only carry one item at a time. this includes money. If you take a 100 value coin to the shop, buy two items that cost 25 coins each, you need to do three trips to get everything back. One for each item, and the third to transport your 50 coin piece back. Or you can take a bucket to keep your coins in, lowering the trip by one. 

Buying a new vehicle is a nightmare. You get a truck at the start for free so you don't need to buy another. The big digger is available for 1000 coins but has no storage. You can't split your coin piles, so you have to go to the town, buy the digger, drive it back to your home. Walk back to the shop and pick up your money, then walk home again.

Driving is also a pain. There is a lot of drift and dead-zones when you are trying to drive around. You are steering left but the wheels do not turn. You have to mash the button a few times before the wheels turn in the direction you want them. Turning the digger seems to be something that is optional. It's turning circle is so wide that I have to do three point turns in the road, just to turn left. Then there is the issue when you touch some scenery, which either stops you dead in your tracks or...

If the game detects that two objects might occupy the same space, rather than deflecting, it shoots the item up into the air. Driving the big digger to my first camp is almost impossible. You flip up into the air and end up somewhere else completely at random. You can get stuck on a pebble. There is an unstuck button on the menu, but this often sent me spiralling into the air nine times out of ten. Then one time out of ten, it would put me broadside across the road right at the place I purchased it. Why broadside? I have to do a 20 point turn to get the thing pointing in the right direction.

This collision issues affects everything. If you drop something just wrong, it will fling off into the unknown. I lost a shovel from this. Dropping things onto floor is like roulette. You don't know if you will lose the item you just paid for. 

Do I like the game? Yes I do. The idea behind it is great fun. I know there won't be any multiplayer, which is a shame, as there's only so much fun you can have at the moment. Maybe some immersive NPC's, or distant wars you need to supply weapons for. Perhaps a royal wedding needs new jewellery. Some immersion is desperately needed. I will play this again, after a few updates. The biggest issue for me is the physics issues. When I see an update with updated physics I will perhaps look into this again. At the moment, the loss of progress due to collision glitches is just too demoralising.

虽然我在steam社区发表了一个指南，游戏也玩的不少，但平心而论，我还是要给这个差评。不说别的，游戏设计就尼玛离谱。

这个游戏低UI，低操作性，高交互性。一般来说，这种设计我只在解谜游戏中见过，例如whiteness，或者人类一败涂地这种，这类游戏不需要操作，游戏逻辑也是围绕着机制设计走，但是这个游戏是个类模拟经营游戏，这注定了思路就是有问题的。2020年的游戏了，连个背包系统都不给，我要造东西得来回跑好几十遍，因为TMD我只能用一只手拿东西，一次就TM只能拿一个东西，这不纯jb搞笑呢吗？

再比如说，我拿起东西，都是必须拿在右手上，OK，没问题，我也不能把铲子放在屏幕中间干活吧，不然啥都看不到，行。当我拿起矿石或者其他东西，如果我要放下东西，这些东西就会直接从我的右手掉下去，什么意思呢？我要往某个地方放东西，我必须把视角往左拖，因为这样我才能把右手放在这个地方的上面然后松手让东西掉进去。掉，你没听错，动词是掉。这个游戏里几乎就没有几个有用的交互性操作，不能直接把东西放到容器里，要把视角往左拖，人往前走，往下看，对准右手和容器，有意思吗？

再比如说鹤嘴锄，劈开泥土，这个游戏的逻辑不是把泥土从中间变成两块，而是把泥土变成一半，然后另一半生成在你的右手位置——然后这一半就会掉下去，然后跟地上的一半合并在一起，啊，这，这波我怀疑是在玩弱智游戏模拟器。

还有很多问题，比如车辆的设计及其不合理，车大的一逼，转向小，路又窄，而且随便撞个路灯就会送你起飞。不过这些都不算什么，因为我估计大多数人还没玩到这步就估计已经退坑了。

I'm fine with the no inventory system as it does add some variety.  The truck has a magic ability to hold huge amounts of items as you transport them, even if you bounce off a light post and spin in the clouds for 30 seconds - everything was still in the trunk.  (The Flowers are still standing!)

My OCD gets triggered with all the nugget fragments falling on the ground and in between the machine parts (which eventually lead to lag), but I think the dev will keep this heading in the right direction.

Some excellent YouTube content to provide how to play guides.

Worth the few bucks for a change of pace.  And definitely a pleasure to support a promising new developer.

It's a really fun game. It looks nice and has some nice elements. It runs smooth and I play it between games/ as a break. It's fairly repetitive though.

Okay before you read on and see the negatives just remember this is a one developer game so don't take my judgements to harsh.

Pros
- It is very very cheap and the dev is very humble
- Love the art style (personal preference)
- Fun game
- Very transparent developer
- Addictive
- Lots to do
- Lots to learn

Negatives
- Tutorial is very basic and is easy to get confused
- It is a new game and so the wiki isn't as helpful as it could be and there are very few to no tutorial videos on youtube
- Quite a few bugs, car flips in the air, equipment can disappear etc (nothing game breaking most bugs just add some humour to the game)

Personal preference notes:
- You can only carry one item at a time so it is a lot of going back and forth personally I enjoy this but a lot of people won't
- The start of the game is pretty slow it takes hours to get the basics done and earn enough to progress (again I enjoy this some wont)

Conclusion:
Personally I really enjoy this game the positives of this game greatly outweigh the negatives. I love the art style and the gameplay. For a one developer game this is amazing and I am loving it and I will be following this game for awhile. If you buy this game I highly recommend you join the discord because the help and tutorials available aren't adequate however the community of this game is great and if you ask for help in discord you will get it. Basically if you like tycoon based games then this is for you just be prepared for the grinding.

This is an odd one...I am waffling on which way to recommend and may change later.

In the interest of fairness I'm going to talk about this like it's in Early Access, even though it isn't presented in the store as such. The developer has a development roadmap and it's priced like Early Access, and after playing it certainly seems to be more in line with EA than a full release, so keep that in mind. That said, this is really basically a proof-of-concept right now, and the developer's roadmap leaves me with some concerns. The roadmap indicates upcoming updates are mostly added features, but it really REALLY needs some QoL fixes for the things that are in the game right now before they even think about additional features. So, it's because of those concerns that the dev doesn't really understand what state the game is in right now that I'm giving it a "Not Recommended" at this stage. 

The controls are incredibly unintuitive. I understand the idea is sort of "manual labor," but there are so many problems with it, it almost feels like a Surgeon Simulator-type game where fighting the wonky controls is the main challenge in the game...except that I don't think that was the intent, and unlike those games, the challenges to controls aren't fun and goofy but frustrating and aggravating. As an example, one of the primary early gameplay loops involves dumping dirt from a bucket which requires you to line up one of the two reticles (more on that later) with the pan below, so you have to awkwardly aim the bucket up to the side in the air. It doesn't feel right at all, and if you miss (which can happen even if the reticle appears to be lined up correctly sometimes), you end up dumping out a dirt clod onto the ground (which doesn't even make sense), which you can't get rid of or break up until you acquire a pickaxe which is moderately expensive and certainly unattainable in the first part of the game (which ALSO doesn't make sense -- how does a bucket create a solid rock that can only be broken by a pickaxe, it's ludicrous). Even when you can afford the pickaxe, it just feels like an arbitrary punishment for having to fiddle around with the stupid control scheme. 

Speaking of reticles...there are two reticles on the screen, one for what you're looking at straight ahead of you and one on the ground. Fine, but the "ground" reticle is offset to the right for some completely inexplicable reason. Also, some tools utilize the front-facing reticle, while others utilize the offset one, and there doesn't seem to be any consistency. 

The physics are bad. Extremely bad. For example, try to dump a bucket of ores onto a table and they inexplicably go flying around the screen instead of falling onto the table. The truck, which is the only reasonable way to carry stuff to and from stores, feels like a punishment. It's way too hard to control, too slow to accelerate, too fast once it does accelerate, roads aren't wide enough, and you are almost guaranteed to hit a tiny piece of the environment and send it flying at some point along the trip. 

Beyond that, the whole game feels very empty and lonely, with no characters other than the player, and because of this and the problems above it's just not even remotely immersive. After a couple of hours, I couldn't bring myself to continue working towards the greater automation features because there's just nothing compelling enough to keep you going long enough to get there. And truthfully, that would be all fine if it was an early build and NPCs and other things were planned for later, but the roadmap doesn't mention anything about that which is pretty concerning. 

Basically what you should expect is a very moderately-priced Alpha Build proof-of-concept. This isn't a full game and the development roadmap, while appreciated, leaves me a bit concerned that the dev doesn't understand the issues that are in the current iteration of the game and thus can't or isn't interested in fixing them. I would have more hope if this was presented as an EA game that it is, and if the dev roadmap discussed some of the many issues with the current state of things. It's not a BAD concept, it's just terribly executed and with little reason to believe the execution will be addressed.

This game is a great deal of fun!
As you start out you have basically nothing; just a shovel, brush, two buckets and a truck.
Eventually you save up those coins by selling your panning finds, and can even grab yourself a third bucket!
Following that, you have the opportunity to purchase more places to dig, a digging vehicle and can start to melt down your nuggets to pour into actual bars, which you can make the few items that generate your income. All in all, a pretty fun, calm and interesting game.

It feels as if this game did not undergo some more lengthy playtesting. Though this is coming from some ballpark standard I feel.

There are a couple of points that I've found difficult to really become accustomed to:
- The game world does feel a bit empty, missing any other characters even if they were to just stand around in whatever towns are available to visit.
- The physics can be a bit.. weird. There is obviously some work done so that items and objects don't sit inside of each other, but this leads to things being sent to outer space and ending up somewhere on the map. This particular point is very much frustrating when you are pouring a bucket of nuggets out; it decides "All these things are colliding with something, and they must not!" - say goodbye to everything in that container that you spent a while collecting...
- Along with that, whenever the vehicles tend to clip their wheels against a lamp post or rock along the roads, you better be buckled in, because you get sent. Can't say where, exactly, but you get sent. And spiralling. Kinda hurts your head.
- When it comes to vehicles, the controls are fairly basic, but that is a good thing. There is some unfortunate camera angles which, if you are next to some trees and trying to look from the position where they stand, they completely obscure your view. Makes it difficult for lining things up.
- An interesting thing with the pans that you start with or that you buy more of, is that if you carry them and pass them through something that is able to be carrying by them, it will become one with the pan. This can obviously be useful for if you want to easily carry the collection of swords or jewellery you have just crafted. It becomes a bit of a hindrance, though, when you walk past your pressure stones in a pipe and accidentally take them out because they connect to the pan..

Honestly, I very much enjoy this game and will continue to play it.
I hope that they add more variety in what can be done, while fixing up the little things that although you are able to work around them, would be easier if fixed up a bit!

За годы, что игра находится в разработке многое изменилось. Улучшилась графика, улучшилось взаимодействие с предметами было исправлено большое количество багов. Появились новые функции и предметы, в том числе появился декор, хотя его все еще мало. Отдельное спасибо за реализацию совместной игры.  На данный момент огорчило, что в последнем обновлении (2,0) пропала возможность красить вещи, нравилась большая машина позволяющая копать, которой больше нет, уплыл корабль с верстаком и чертежами. Ниже приведен предыдущий отзыв для лучшего понимания у новых игроков количество работы, которое уже  проделано, надеюсь на улучшение игры в дальнейшем.  Из минусов все же отмечу большое количество монотонной работы на первых этапах, и нудного ожидания на последних, когда ждешь накопления ресурсов для зарабатывания денег. Несмотря на проделанную работу игра все еще создает ощущения пустой. Возможно это связано с малым количеством взаимодействий с миром. Нет не игровых персонажей, нет взаимодействий с домами, которые не являются магазинами. Предыдущий отзыв: "Игра на 1 -2 дня максимум много не продуманного в управлении. Переворачивание ресурсов  при переносе, не способность сочетать вроде бы сочетаемые вещи(воронка - тигель). Наличие багов и не логичностей. Баг был замечен  как пропадание вещей на второй части первого участка, за рекой.  Разбрассывание вещей при столкновении, при чем достаточно далеко по округе, что их тяжело найти или совершенно не возможно."

玩了13个小时，大部分内容都体验了一下
优点：游戏最有趣的是探索过程，探索完毕后就没多大意思了。
主要说说缺点吧：
1、bug太多。一是将物品放在另一个物品内部，放手后就飞出去。二是物品如果不是通过左键放在地上而是按E扔在地上时，有小概率遁地。[spoiler]一开始我以为是凭空消失，直到我挖了个深坑发现了我失踪的水管……[/spoiler]
2、携带项链等大物品不便。能盛物品的容器就只有车、锅和小的那个（忘了叫啥），大项链放锅里可费了劲了，大金属锭放进锅里还要角度，让它倾斜进去才算放进去。
3、自动化设备的最末端（资源收集端）还需要完善。目前为止（2020.5.17），没有一个容器能够和漏斗搭配准确地将筛选出来的资源进行收纳，只能手动摆好位置。[spoiler]虚假的自动化。[/spoiler]
4、捕鱼箱效率极其低下，而且不小心放置在河底下面，他就free了，彻底跟你说拜拜了。[spoiler]钓鱼竿5秒一条鱼不香么[/spoiler]

目前游戏内容太少，期待后续。游戏潜力应该是有的。[spoiler]类似于另一款游戏Raft[/spoiler]强烈建议先把bug修了，先修遁地再修飞天，飞天你还能跑一跑找回来，遁地你就得挖到最底层

下面是给玩家的一些上手提示：
1、越深的土，能够得到越大的资源。但要注意，把土铲出来放在地表，再铲的话，系统会判断这是地表的土。
2、物品售卖价格：成品 > 金属锭和磨过的宝石 > 原始资源
3、游戏有重置和寻找车辆的功能，能够将人和车重置到固定位置。重置人，手中的物品能够保留，可以用来进行快速跑图和回到地面；重置车或者直接上车，手中的物品会扔到地上，但是车上放置的东西仍然在车上
4、在车后面挑一下再放置，可以有效减少物品飞翔的概率

游戏快速开局的攻略建议：
[spoiler]开局先去手动刷资源，去上坡那里卖钱。然后去装备屋买一个钓鱼竿，再回到卖钱的那个地方，有一个出水口，去那里钓鱼，然后再卖钱，可以拿一个锅，把鱼都放在锅里，以此提高效率。一次性攒够买改良铲子、水管和锄头的钱，去最开始的地方，用锄头往地下挖，挖到底部再也不能挖了为止，然后用重置功能回到地面（按ESC后，倒数第二个按钮），去架设水管（最少需要一个水泵和几个水管），把水引到地下或直接让水滴滴到地下也行，带上你所有刷金块的工具（包括锅）下去，用锅接水滴，然后用改良铲子铲最下面的土，放进锅里，刷两次。最下层能够出最大的金块、铁块和宝石。有了钱，剩下的就自己玩吧[/spoiler]

This is a neat little game that uses lots of small concepts that add up to big ideas.

For example, there is no inventory; you can only hold one item at a time.  But, everything in the world is an interactable physics object; you can put items into pans, and carry the pan (without any physics problems while carrying it).  Or you can put the physics objects into the bed of your truck, drive home, and unload the items there.  So a few very basic systems add up to make a unique and interesting 'inventory management' experience

To me, the simplicity of each system plus the way they work together is most of what I like about the game.  For example, you can dig up dirt and dump it in a pan to brush for gold.  But those are all in-world interactions; if you instead use a drill to dig up dirt, you could still drop that same dirt into the pan.  You can drop your ingots into a crucible, or you can setup a conveyor system to drop them in, there's no difference.  

And everything is physics based, without it being janky.  The hoppers (which, currently are more of a pain than they're worth) are just physics objects; you can use fast conveyors to lob your dirt/ingots long distances into the hopper, or drop them from the square above, and even the conveyors are also physics-based.  This means that there's a certain degree of trial/error and randomness in just about anything you build, so that you may end up with some dirt chunks that didn't quite fall through the hopper right, and don't fall into the machine that should break them down.  And personally, I like that - there's a bit of realism to the idea that your hoppers aren't magic and sometimes stuff will bounce in unexpected ways.  It feels right to, sometimes, have to clean up the excess dirt around your machines.  Or to have to adjust a design because your ingots were all being dropped on the very edge of the belt and some of them were rolling off.  
Some might call it finicky, and some might not enjoy the sort of imperfect automation that you can achieve, but I think it adds a lot to the game, and keeps it interesting while always allowing more/better optimization



Anyway, as for the negatives, things really can get tedious - items don't stack, and you can only carry one.  The dev is actively working on improving things, so I doubt it will be this way for long, but shopping basically takes up 90% of your time because you have to load each item one at a time into the buy zone, then into the truck, then out of the truck when you get home.  

Also, automated systems all require 'maintenance' by consumable items.  Nothing will run forever, and usually you're lucky if you get 15 minutes of automation going without having to stop and repair something.  While this is part of the challenge of the game, and it's really just not meant for you to have a perpetually running automated setup, this can be discouraging to players who come in from something like Factorio

Lastly, sometimes the randomness caused by the physics-based systems can be really annoying, especially if you're expecting to ever make a perfect automated setup that never clogs, drops nuggets, or has problems.  As mentioned, that's not really supposed to happen in this game - the challenge comes mostly from everything being physics-based and imperfect.  But it can still be annoying to spend hours building a setup only to find out you need to move the entire thing one block over for the dirt clumps to fall into exactly the right spot

This game is a relaxing romp into the realm of gold panning and automated mining. Yes the various bugs and physics glitches make it frustrating and it can learn a thing or two about the "tool belt" style inventory in games like Viscera Cleanup Detail, but the expected updates and current gameplay options make it well worth the ten dollar price tag. 

I encourage anyone looking for a creative and relaxing game to invest here and enjoy literally raking in the gold... Shiny... Shiny gold...

I love the game in concept, it looks nice enough to enjoy if the game play was turned up a bit, read on for a detailed explanation.

This game is lacking a lot of finish, it reminds me a lot of Gold Rush the game in terms of what you do but it's a tad less grindy and a lot less realistic.

I get the idea of not having an inventory per se, but most people do have 2 hands in real life, being able to carry a lantern and something else would be nice, developer: you would need to code items to be either 2 handed or one handed, so if for example you were carrying something in one hand you could carry something in the other, but you wouldn't be able to use it, like the shovel.

There seems to be a lack of a point to the game, its too sandboxy, simulators are often plagued by this, even AAA simulation games sometimes fail to give a feeling of purpose, like survival, making a flourishing business, staying out of the red, etc.

Currently it seems to be this: dig for ores/gold so you can buy better equipment so you can dig for more ores and gold and then game over, no business simulation involved, no cost of operation except the purchase of better stuff, to which there really isn't a lot, there's an expansive drilling and conveyor system, but again lacks a feeling of purpose when the game doesn't really demand change from the player.

To start I would redo the entire financial system, the coin idea is okay, but a bank account, fee's, property tax, etc, these are all elements that don't require a lot of visual work but if worked over properly could actually give the feeling of running a mining business. You could start players off with a bank account balance and attach a purchase price to all of the dig sites, give the player enough of a starting balance to purchase one of these sites and some small pieces of equipment.

As far as selling goes the whole concept of "selling at a shop/sell point/single buyer" really needs to die, the gaming world has leaned on that for WAAAY too long, selling to clients is a better way to go, not walk in "I want to buy 1 oz of gold please" but instead businesses, industries, etc could place orders for iron, gold, etc, this would give you a quota, you could accept orders, fill orders, and give you presence in the market, the more presence you have in the market the bigger the orders get, stop filling orders and the orders get smaller again as clients begin to source producers elsewhere, this helps with giving "purpose". The other thing it adds is a progression wall, kind of tying the players success to their business savvy, as opposed to just how many times they clicked the left mouse button and pressed E. Don't fill orders fast enough? Well I guess you're sitting on all that iron you mined now and will have to wait for another order to come along for you to accept.

You could start with filling orders for jewellers, collectors, smiths and dentists, small orders that pay little, but demand little and as they are buying a small quantity they pay more per oz, as you gain more presence in the market and your operation gets bigger the bigger clients come along, factories, banks, industrial clients, who place larger orders but also pay less per oz (because IRL that's the purpose behind bulk ordering, to pay less per measurable unit it's what turned Amazon into the monster it is today). Just don't make the orders mandatory, make it so you need to accept the order before it's required to be filled, that way players can choose which orders to fill and which to ignore, but again, ignore a repeat client for too long and they start looking elsewhere.

The reason that there's a cost inversion is simply so that new players just starting out who are producing tiny amounts of ore get more for their work, but as you become wealthier and your operation more elaborate and producing larger volumes you still make more money, but less per unit, because, well you're doing less work really. This is another thing "Gold Rush" failed at, they artificially inflated how much gold you find in the early game so you have a faster start, but ultimately wrecks the realism.

Anyways, hope the dev reads this, seems like a good person who's very involved with their audience and would love to see this game succeed, but really think it needs some work.

I actually came here to give it a thumbs up, until I realized this isn't Early Access.

The core mechanic of the game is very enjoyable- you start out panning for gold with a shovel and brush, and buy your way up to heavy vehicles and automated processing lines.  But man, this game is ROUGH.  Like alpha version rough.  No inventory (heck, no left hand even.)  No wallet (you have to buy things by carrying your stack of coins all over the place.)  And just to give you an idea of the fit and finish level, the latest patch notes said they mostly fixed the error where objects fly off into space never to be recovered.  And still, several times a session I lose a bunch of expensive components.  Like they just vanish mysteriously while I'm reorganizing my dig site.    Losing a $22 crucible is annoying.  Losing a few $250 conveyor belt sections is frustrating.  Losing a $1000 magnet wand really makes me want to play something else.

I hope they continue developing because there's good potential but there is not much gameplay and what there is is very glitchy.  Really should be in Early Access as a warning.

玩了11个小时，现在只想说一句fuxk作者！！！！！首先说说这游戏的游戏性吧，游戏想法是不错的，得自己动手从一开始的挖土筛金到最后慢慢的达到工业体系和自动化。但是，这操作就尼玛离谱，虽然我知道没有收纳系统是为了还原真实性，但是你一个一个把金块放进熔炉里的操作也太蠢了吧，先不说晕不晕3D，这明显感觉就是在浪费时间！劳资是来玩游戏放松的，不是来给你的游戏打苦力的！！一个大金锭要9个小金块儿我一次可以晒出200多个矿石（不分金铁宝石）我这样一个一个给你放熔炉要浪费我多少时间？好吧操作坑爹就算了，这游戏还特别容易失误，因为drop东西是靠绿点而不是直接和物品进行互动，这个设定太拖沓了吧！简直就是心态爆炸积累器。我还是希望作者可以在真实性和游戏性之间做一些考量。不要做成一开始一直在重复捡石子扔石子的游戏，毕竟游戏的玩法还是很有趣的（刚开始1小时）。但是后面的捡石子和载具系统把我弄得我心态都炸了。

I really want to like this game, but in it's current form there are too many issues to enjoy it fully. I am looking forward to seeing a more polished version of this, the style is right up my alley. For the price, I think you can enjoy this for a few hours up to a couple of days. For now i'm going to stop playing and wait for the next update to come along...if it does. These's small team development projects too often slow down or stop abruptly.

Some issues i ran into:
-pressure system is nice, but doesn't work very good when conveyors slow down at the end of the line and dirt is merging and clogging the whole automation.
-the merging of dirt is nice, but should not be active yet. mainly it clogs systems and there's nothing you can do about it
-pipes in/ouput position of devices limit automation possibilities
-maintenance of systems is a nice feature, but building larger systems forces you to spend a large amount of your gametime to repairs.
-hitboxes, physics and collisions issues. Objects flying or bouncing away like crazy. Emptying a container with a few objects, throws them all over the place.
-dirt duping. Picking up a small amount of dirt gives a full amount of dirt when placed down again.
-pump pipes sometimes just stop working, pickup and deploy necessary to make it work again.
-possible to place pipes through machines, weird things can happen. Some machines will toggle off/on in a loop. It can even crash the entire game. (losing some unsaved progress)

I am going to recommend this game, but with hesitation. The game is entertaining, graphics are nice, concept is pretty interesting. There are also some downfalls that need to be addressed:

-Driving is very buggy, you can clip through trees, climb almost 90 degree hills (with a little work), torque/acceleration is painfully slow. 
-Lack of HUD/Inventory/Tutorials/Tips makes things very vague, and not in a good way.
-There are some frustrating bugs but once you get your feet under you they don't hurt too bad.
-There isn't really an endgame, there is, but it doesn't feel rewarding.
     --To elaborate, I am at dig site 1, I am making roughly 3000g every 'cycle' that I run which takes about 10-15 minutes. Yes I could attempt to automate everything as much as possible, however all that will do is give me more gold. I could build a house/strucutre, but why? I don't gain anything.

These are the major flaw for me, but lets go back to the promising

-Very active developer (at the time of this review)
-Lots of room for improvement
-I have happily played my $8 worth.

Things to note:
-Single developer
-This game is NOT EARLY ACCESS
-Future updates are expected, not promised
-If buying "Early Access" makes you uneasy, do not purchase this game. It is technically finished, but does not feel it. It has potential, but as we all know, developers can fall out.
-Very active developer, has his own Youtube channel, posts often, is showing signs of a caring developer which is pretty rare these days.
-Multiplayer will not be included (dev said it would require a ground up rebuild)

Can't recommend this game in the current state. 
While the premise of building your gold-panning empire from rags to riches sounds like it could be fun and the automation aspect is enticing, the execution is disappointing. Everything you pick up fills your hands, that includes little bits of ore, jewel shard and (the more frustrating one) coins. Also the shopsystem that wants to feel immersive by letting you pick up the stuff you want carry it over to a special place, place it down, press a button (because otherwise the item disappears when you pick it up) and picking up the item again gives the impression of a prototype not a finished game. This coupled with the tedium that is the (non-existent) inventory system and the bugs (hey let's drive this vehicle, oh there is a little rock, time to defy the laws of gravity and flip uncontrollably through the air) really makes me regret buying this game (even though the price is low).

[b]100 Hour Update[/b] It has been a couple years and a lot has changed, my previous review is below this and still rings true. But it isn't so much of an issue with collision and vehicle weight. It behaves more normally and is pleasant. You should buy it, if you are the resource gathering type.  

Hydroneer is a mining/upgrade style of game, with subtle undertones of games such as Factorio,Satisfactory and Gold Digger but with 3D animations compared to Factorio, Simple expansion/upgrades versus Satifactory and heaps better controls and game play than Gold Digger. This particular game being in the Indie genre and having only one (1) developer at the time of this review; easily can compete with major title as far as graphic go! With the recent update it even has a ole' timey feel to it, which fits the overall design of the games graphic. Unfortunately, with more than 16 hours of game play there is a rage inducing, keyboard breaking, screen smashing issue with this game. [b]Vehicle Weight/Collision[/b] from the very beginning there is a issue with hitting anything that is part of the world. It has a 90% chance to fling you into the sky spinning so violently that it nearly can induce vomiting from the player! Later game when you start to have structures  you place in your mining areas (dig spots) you tend to have three (3) issues. Vehicle turning radius, Easy flipability, Reset points far away. This is a known issue, rather it is purposeful or not as a "wacky physics" as the menu in game has a "Unstuck" feature or more wholesomely put "Grab Me Legs" as of 05/13/2020 PST and a handy "Recall Nearest Vehicle" button that takes you to your closest ride, which as of yesterdays update now resets the nearest vehicle also to the nearest working path. You may find with the [u]'Ydro Excavator[/u] that your fuel (water) depletes very quickly and the digging mechanic does make it hard to make a smooth bottom ditch for traversing your dig site, one accidental move and you can't pass the area any longer. But as the 16+ hours would suggest the game is still highly addicting if this is your genre of game. But I can not recommend it as it does have a mechanic that is prominent, that has the potential to push the "Rage Button" otherwise if you can stomach the frustration it is worth the buy. Last complaint, the settings options are not available IN THE GAME. You have to exit to the Menu to adjust and there is no brightness setting. PerksPrisoner fun rating 7/10.

So you start out with a shovel, bucket, bigger bucket and a brush. You shovel dirt into the smaller bucket until that is full, then empty the smaller bucket into the bigger bucket. Then you fill the bigger bucket with water and use the brush to find the resources in the dirt.

Seems oddly familiar, I thought to myself, but okay.

It was only until I smelted a gold bar that it finally clicked. I'd played this before in Gold Rush. Almost precisely the same intro with some added refinement mechanics. 

So, does that make it good? Well game progression (Pipes, advanced shovel, making stuff) is good up until you try to get into automated mining/refining at which point I lost interest because I could sit on the bottom of a dig site and find large chunks of gold while the machines were still spitting out tiny flakes of the stuff. Oh, and breaking down frequently. 

Overall, not a bad game for a one man design team.

Over View: Found this game through a playthrough and could not wait to get my hands on it. Picked it up the day it was released and I was not disappointed. It's a small cute game with the ability to play this game for a while without getting bored. When you finally make your first gold bar it feels really good to sell it and have all the hard work pay off. It's really a progression game with no end, to start with a basic shovel and a dirt cleaning set up to possibly having a huge factory, Lots of different tools.

Pros: Playable for a while, Gameplay has not gotten boring even when progressing far, infinite factory/gold mine possibilities, different plots with positives and negatives to each, A lot cheaper then it should be, decent looking game no complaints, Dev has big plans, and the game just gives you a peaceful medieval vibe.

Cons: A big pile of glitches and bugs, dirt clumps become too large for automatic factories to handle, Rock grinder was supposed to fix that last issue but when the big rocks get grinded they combine back to the size it was before right away since they are grinded too close to one another, Items fall through the floor when unrendering your plot and coming back to it, I know it makes sense but I would prefer it if the player does not get taken away on the conveyor, Goliath drill randomly breaks even with filtered water, when the Goliath drill hits an air pocket it thinks it's reached the bottom and stops digging, fishing would be fun if expanded more, nothing to flatten plots that have very unsmooth surfaces, One very annoying glitch that happened to me personally was when I filled my HydroTruck with a bunch of stuff to build a mining set up, The truck flew away when I got in it and flew so far that it went under the world. I tried to recall the vehicle but it would just fly away so there went 3 hours of grinding.

Things I would like to see: smaller dirt clumps or only clump dirt when a player drops one onto the other, more machinery like something to flatten dirt or a machine that can detect gold veins or rich gold areas, more types of drills, Maybe make the Hydrotruck able to dump whats in the back, give filters twice the health, hanging lights or more powerful lights, another furnace and crucible in a bigger size, and just more general content!

Finishing notes: It's a great game with a great developer, It's still a very new game so I wouldn't take my notes too harsh but it does need a lot of fixes! If your thinking of picking up this game, I would advise to if your into grinding type games!

I just spent 30mins writing a, what I believed to be, humourous and insightful review.  Though a negative vote.  But as Steam decided it hated me I'm just going to bulletpoint some gripes.

-Too much micromanagement in the early and mid game.  You can (somewhat) automate the painful manual process later.  Much, MUCH later.  The game is rather janky and the bugs and awkward physics multiply the frustrations of the mining process, even when you're making it easier it doesn't *get* easier.

-Hotbar and holding multiple items is a necessity, it would ease and streamline a lot of the "pick up, put down, try to find and pick up the item you just had again.  No, wait, have to be at the right angle, at the right distance clicking on the right part--- there we go, finally picked up the shovel".  This is made worse by the fact the game is janky and sometimes you do something a bit wrong and the physics God will smite you into orbit, scatter your 30+ ores across the land and just straight up flip your vehicle back to the start if you dare try to defy it intentionally or otherwise.  Maybe ores stack, like coins and dirt though.  And buying items applies them to a preset hotbat of certain tools (shovel, pickaxe, fishing rod, saw, hammer).  Meaning you still need to manage buckets and pans but it just takes the edge off the painful process.

-Needs more in-game tips/tutorials.  Having a YT channel with dedicated videos and all is nice, but I don't want to have to research and study a game.  I wanna press buttons, be given tips (or request tips in-game).  I got Sopranos clips playing on my YT, and I don't wanna have to pause them to watch a video to explain the intricacies of the mechanics.  Yes, I like the methods but anything complex needs in-game hints or instructions that take moments to get the information, not sitting through half an hour of YT vids with a notepad and pen at the ready.

-Similar to the tool handling issue.  The manual mining and processing of ores, especially when you have a lot of items, needs to be streamlined.  Make it so you can pick up groups of the same item.  Make them stack to a given size (like currency or dirt).  I know you can carry items in a bucket/pan to the jeweller or wherever.  But the micromanagement of any item, especially small items, is beyond fiddly.  Like with the tools, due to the physics God being an unforgiven one...  the mechanics need to be aligned to work well within the game.  The mechancs should be apart of the enjoyment, they shouldn't hinder them.  And I feel greatly hindered, more so in the early to mid game.

All in all I like the game, but it needs some quality of life works to make it enjoyable and easier to get into to start.  Hopefully some changes happen soon, my partner and I bought a copy each (oh, and if you thought about making it multiplayer, I'm sure some folks may or may not appreciate that. Plus it would address qualms with the awkwardness to get out of the early-mid game.  Having 2/3/4x the man power would really help there).

I'll edit my review in the future, and will come back to the game after some updates, fixes, etc.

There's a lot, in my opinion, that needs to change/be implemented before I - personally - will be able to enjoy this game.

The lack of any type of inventory, doesn't make sense - it makes everything about this game much more tedious than it needs to be. Generally, you see the lack of an inventory in simulation games - this is not a simulation. The day/night cycle does not seem to be equal - with daylight not lasting long enough, and no items (excluding the lantern, but including the truck) being able to emit light to help in navigation or mining.

The whole reticle system of items dropping where the green dot is, really isn't necessary and adds frustration as it doesn't effect everything, but shows always. For example, if I want to put dirt in a bucket, the green dot is visible but the dirt doesn't go there it goes where you click. Other items drop where the green dot is on the ground.

My biggest complaint is the lack of an inventory system. When you have nuggets of minerals, it's not a huge deal to put them in the bucket and carry the bucket. But I'm not about to carry coins with me after I sell something.

Honestly, I would've refunded this game (even on sale) - but for some reason the game/Steam glitched and it thinks I've played 8 hours, when I've played less than 30 minutes.

Hydroneer ist ein sehr entspanntes und ein geniales Gold schürf Simulator Sandbox Game.
Man startet mit einer Schaufel, einer Bürste, einem kleinen und einen großen Eimer und beginnt einfach von Hand nach Gold, Eisen, Edelsteinen und Kristallen zu graben und diese weiterzuverarbeiten und zu Geld zu machen. Man hat die Möglichkeit nachdem man einiges an Geld gesammelt hat eine AUTOMATISIERTE PRODUKTION zu errichten mit der man innerhalb kurzer Zeit ein großes Vermögen anhäufen kann.Ein simples aber exzellent funktionierendes Bausystem ermöglicht es einem seine Basis und Produktion ganz nach den eigenen Wünschen zu errichten und zu gestalten.Es gibt zwei Fahrzeuge: den Hydro-Truck und den Hydro-Excavator.Der Truck dient zum Transport von Items und der Excavator ist eine art Tunnelbohrer mit dem man sich ein Höhlensystem graben kann um an wertvollere Ressourcen zu gelangen.Man hat keine Survival mechaniken oder sonstiges in diesem Spiel und kann sich ganz ohne Ablenkung aufs Schürfen und Bauen konzentrieren.

玩了十个多小时，说点感想提点意见。（20年5月13日初评）
总体
· 玩到10小时，基本上全部内容都尝试了一下。
· 不能说很好玩，但是意外挺有趣。上手2小时重复度比较高，但2到10小时的游戏可以很开心的探索和尝试。
· 10小时以后的内容……还得等作者更新了吧
游戏视角
· 默认相机很晕，我把FOV调到了70°好了很多。
· 卡车的倒车希望能修一下。用水加油好评。驾驶的相机很晕也希望能改改。
· 驾驶时候蹭到物体就会发动炫动冲锋龙卷风……（疯狂沿前进方向旋转）
采矿等游戏的玩法
· 矿物粒度挺大，方便操作。但初期或许可以产出点金沙，用脸盆装着去卖。
· 矿物产出或许可以调低一些，单价调高一些。减少黄金的产出，可以提升挖到黄金的成就感。
· 需要扫帚和簸箕，方便清理地面。也方便收集矿物。
· 利用黄金和铁熔点不同的性质直接通过坩埚筛分两种矿物？
· 当前版本黄金里掺铁熔出来也是黄金。并没有确认前后质量是否相同。
· 铲子希望能增加个平整地面的功能，挖的坑坑洼洼的看着难受。
· 吸铁石棒棒：我本来以为是吸“铁”石，可以方便的从混合矿物中分离铁矿……基于扫帚和簸箕的建议，我希望吸铁石能真的只吸铁。
· 打铁太简单了。买了各种道具结果锤一下就完事了，意犹未尽。
· 用了几百单位的黄金加一颗小小的宝石锤出一个巨大的项链……觉得很奇幻，还希望作者能再考虑一下相关的玩法。
· 需要一个可以把传送带的物体规整到传送带正中间的设备。类似于粉碎机上的那个。
· 制作了一批物品后，一件一件地搬上搬下很累人。想要一些收纳。
· 游戏后期赚钱肯定会容易很多。鉴于默认的机器设备的维护频度，感觉可以增加一个“升级工具包”，花费较多的货币来升级设备以提升可靠性。
物理和BUG
· 所有物体普遍质量太小，太轻。被角色一脚踢飞几十米。
· 吸铁棒棒，漏斗，粉碎传送带等一些物品放在地上时会消失。
· 收获器？Harvester的产物喷出口位置太低了，以至于不能在同高度正常使用漏斗。
· 同Harvester，产物喷出口力度太大。经常导致产物乱飞……
· 筛选传送带的两侧最外围会堆积物品。
优化
· 毕竟是UE4做的，玩的我脚边烫烫的。
· 初始送的手提灯也有阴影。挺酷炫的，但是太卡了。一直扔在边上没怎么用。
· 立灯不错
· 用吸铁石棒棒吸矿物时候有点点卡。不过感觉这也没办法。
画质
· 多边形风格，挺好看的。
· 抗锯齿调教得很好。
· 日夜更替挺舒服的。就是晚上时间太长……玩的眼睛累。当前白天只有一天的三分之一左右……

To start, this game is very much still in active developement. I have put in 27 hours of playtime since it launched roughly 100 hours ago.

This game is a simulation game, it doesn't hold your hand, it doesn't give you everything for free, you start with a basic setup to begin mining and making your fortune. From there, you grow, you buy, sell, expand, get new claims, setup new mining operations. All by yourself, all by "hand".

I wouldn't call the game difficult, but neither would I call it easy. You have to test, fail, adjust, and eventually you will find what works for you. In my 27 hours so far, I have only worked on mining, setting a small automated facility at my first claim, before expanding to my second claim. There are certainly frustrations with the game-play, but the developer (a solo developer) has been quick to respond and push out updates. There were two patches released on release day, the first one withing hours of launch. Since launch there have been 6 patches (with another slated for tomorrow) focusing on performance and gameplay optimization. Through his discord the developer has been extremely responsive and communicative.

It's not a bad game, but it should've been released in Early Access (or wait a few months in the oven). Other reviewers explained the problems with this game better, but here's a few things that made me think the way I think:
- bad physics - items jumping around, weird item collisions, player getting stuck on non-existant terrain,
- tedium - there is absolutely no reason, that we cannot carry more than 1 item at the time. Want to build 5 pieces of pipe? Go to the shop (don't forget your money!), pull out 5 pipes one at the time, click a button to buy, then carry each piece one at the time to your base. Yes, you have a car, but the starting area is so close, it would take longer to load a car, drive 2 meters and unload it. I admire people building bigger contraptions. Give us an inventory or at least allow us to stack items. An ability to have all the tools on you would be nice too. 
- annoying controls - placing items like pipes is weird, it never snaps to the tile that you want it to. Also, it's way too easy to pick up the item you want to stay where it is, examples: trying to pick up tiny gold nuggets from the pan and picking up whole pan instead or trying to pick up a crafted item from an anvil & picking up the anvil. This could be fixed for example by being able to lock items in-place with a different key and/or having a separate keybind to pick up "snapped" items like anvils or blocks.
- other small things like:not being able to access settings while in-game, ugly font in the main menu or random lag spikes.
Yes, I know, the game is made by a single dude, but that's not a valid reason for a game to be in the state that it is. I will probably revisit the game in a year or so after (hopefully) some of these issues are fixed, but I cannot recommend it at the moment.

It lacks content, there is not much to do once you've got enough money to buy everything. You can use the money to automate the money making but the money you get is only for your own satisfaction, and too much ores spawning on the world slows down the game. Speaking of automation, some things still don't work at all or don't work all the times which makes the automation a tedious job of trying to make things work all the time. For example the most use I've done for the funnel is for me to place a crucible under it so I can place ores inside it more easily, if you try to use anywhere else where you don't control the speed of placing resources in, resources will get stuck and you will have a jam. Harvester works only half the time when dirt goes on top of it, devs should probably make that hitbox detection bigger or make the harvester bigger than 1 block wide.

The physics of this game is the worst, if you don't give me an inventory to store stuff at least let my stuff stay on the ground where I leave it, not dissapear once I leave it on some uneven ground or go flying off to space when I step on them, I've lost more shovels than anything. Buying stuff is tedious, period. Half the playtime is me trying to move stuff one by one, not mentioning some just goes flying after leaving my hands. This game aims for big automation at the end why should I do one piece at the time, it's just tedious and unfun. By the time you automate anything you'd be making more money by digging yourself...

Eitherway I'm still leaving a positive review because I see potential in this game, I hope the devs makes this game less frustrating to play and add more content in the future.

Updated review 01/17/21

I'm editing this review based on the updates the developer has put out throughout last year, including the latest patch that was released today at the time of this review.

I'm glad to see that a lot of things have improved. Physics are working a bit more nicely and costly bugs regarding items and structures going below ground has been fixed. The vehicle experience has been vastly improved thanks to easier turning and faster reverse movement. New items and content, including new areas to mine and shops to explore, were added in to vary and expand gameplay further. The addition of the Steam Workshop gives the possibility of expanding the game further and easier.

A few glaring issues still remain however:
- The camera closely following the movement of vehicles still presents a problem even though flipping over isn't one. The camera still wobbles exactly as the vehicle wobbles over uneven terrain.
- Despite the vast amount of content to further progress new tiers of mining and automation setups, there's very little progress in any kind of story content (if there is intending to be one). The relics and the cave that houses them still serves no purpose right now.

With much of the bugs gone and with more stuff to do now, I'm willing to change my review and say it's now worth getting this game. However, if you want a goal to follow... this game doesn't provide it yet and you're better off wishlisting this game until it goes on sale.

--------------------------------------------
ORIGINAL REVIEW:

This game is pretty nice.  It shares its inspiration from games like Factorio, modded Minecraft, Fortresscraft, etc. You just mine for stonks and get rich without having to worry about enemies or stamina... or much else actually.

I like the concept and I've had fun playing it so far, but this game is far from polished and filled with content. It's actually deceptive to see this game being sold like as if it's a full game when the game is in an "Early Access" state. Here's a few problems that I have so far (in no particular order):

- The physics are broken in many places. Despite a few patches, items can still get yeeted when I drop them. I've lost a few [i]expensive[/i] items this way.

- Driving mechanics and physics are similar to how it is with... bad simulator games. It's easy to flip yourself over, get yourself stuck into objects, or drive yourself off the bridge. Sure you can easily get yourself unstuck with the click of a menu option, but I find myself with two choices: drive slowly and defeat the purpose of travelling by truck when I could just glitch all of the objects into the pan and carry it, or go fast and risk having to get unstuck and redo the travel back again. [strike]Also... why does driving backward seem so painstakingly slow? I dread doing K-turns because of how long it takes for me to back up.[/strike]

- The 3rd-person camera follows the vehicle's movement exactly so driving fast means the camera wobbles hard, and flipping over means you get to see the world spin like a roller coaster. This would make sense if you're driving in 1st person, but you're not and people who are prone to motion sickness won't like trying to drive in this game at all.

- Game progression is short in a few, but long tedious steps. Once you gather enough funding for an automated operation and rake in the money... there's not a whole lot else you can do for main content. Building a house, fishing, and hunting for treasure are nice distractions but don't add up to a lot of additional side content.

- Regardless of how much water pressure goes into machines, they spit items out at full blast. You literally have to wall off the output and have a hopper collect at the bottom... which means more money making your automated setup work.

- Going with the above point, where the drills and the harvester outputs items are different and requires additional infrastructure (and thus more money) to deal with handling the position on those outputs. I can easily just have a belt next to a ram drill and it'll output to that, but the harvester's output is below the belt. It was probably intended for the items to be dropped into a pan, but even that's absurd thanks to how powerful those outputs are...

In summary, getting rich and building up to an easy automated setup of getting rich is nice and fun, but the various bugs, bad physics, and lack of content is frustrating to deal with for a game that should not be advertised as a full game yet. While the dev looks pretty committed to updating this game regularly and thus  the game should improve over time, as it stands right now... I cannot recommend this game.

I've been playing Hydroneer these past few days and the developer has stepped up to the plate astoundingly well from the moment of release, releasing regular updates addressing player issues daily. 

Hydroneer is a mining sandbox game similar to the likes of Space Engineers, where you take your tools and dig out a voxel-based world to make profits to build things. Rather than saddling the player with an inventory system, every item exists in the world, resulting in a significantly slower progression system as the character moves items one at a time from place to place. I don't love it, but I accept its idiosyncrasies. In many ways it tests and trains patience that is so normally missing.

Hydroneer has its fair share of bugs and glitches, as many people have remarked. Objects fly off at unexpected speeds and vehicles are clunky. However, for a one man project, I find that the game shows great promise and heart. It has delivered quality time spent for money invested and certainly has not made any false promises. At its current state, without delving deeply into house decoration and design, one can easily find a dozen hours of gameplay. I await the future with bated breath.

Before I get started on my thoughts on this game, I want to make things very clear. There are numerous people who are NOT recommending this game because it is "unpolished" to say it nicely. I want to make this very clear, this game constantly sees updates since its public release. I'm not talking about weekly updates either, the developer has literally released bug fixes every other day of this week to get this game as bug free as possible. You will rarely ever find this kind of dedication from a ONE MAN TEAM, it is very commendable. The developer has also released a roadmap of big updates, which is also a big plus. 

As of writing this review, the whole bug-fest of items flying into space when you kick them as mostly been fixed and is much less of a problem.

Now for the actual review. This game is a great game and carries huge potential, and this game has barely been released. Comparing this game to other mining simulators/resource collection games, Hydroneer definitely sits up there as one of the better games worth picking up. 

First and foremost, this game is designed to be just about as tedious as working in real life, so if you don't have that kind of patience you should definitely not get this game. It is repetitive and takes a lot of dedication to keep working forward. Starting from slow, meager beginnings, you spend your time just barely pulling in profit to get started. But after your hard work, you start to pick up the pace and begin your road of progression. From simple hand mining, you can move on to automation and start quickly stockpiling your ores for some big profits. 
This game gives quite a lot of customization, allowing you to build insane contraptions to automate your mining process. You also have simple decor to bring your quarry to life as a true mining factory. You can setup things however you want, and there is quite a lot of tricks you will learn along the way to not only improve your contraptions, but even improve the appearances of them.

This game is not without its flaws, many bugs/glitches still exist and many more will come as we keep getting content updates. There are also many small things that irritate you and make you want to rage quit. But, at the end of the day I want to come back to play again, and that's what a game is all about right? This is my warning to people, this game is not a finished product and is always updating. However, this shouldn't turn you away from getting the game. The developer is hard at work to make this game fantastic, I urge you to give it a try. This is truly a game which no one asked for, and yet everyone should try.

Hydroneer is a simple ore refinement strategy/simulation game. Instead of trying to get the entire refinement process down, this game attempts to get the progression down instead, resulting a far more, if less in-depth, experience. It has an aesthetic that, while not super original or unique in general, is unique within the genre and well executed. It does not attempt to hold your hand, but it also does not attempt to feign difficulty. It is intuitive without unnecessary simplicity but most importantly with minimal complexity. You put dirt in a bucket, sift it, then you get raw materials. You process these by putting them in the appropriate machine, sell them, rinse wash repeat. It's a simple loop but a fulfilling one with a proper amount of complexity added in.

Pros
[list]
[*] The game is a simple and streamlined.
[*] Complexity, while limited, provides rewarding progression and adequate challenge.
[*] Game requires little investment in time to achieve tangible and substantial progress.
[/list]

Cons
[list]
[*] The game is simple, and this is by design, so will see little added complexity as time progresses. The complexity will always trail behind the competition.
[*] The game is undeveloped, and still has obvious holes in it's progression. It also has significant quirkiness and bugginess that is left unaddressed.
[*] The game is designed to be grindy, if that is not what you want or like, this game is not for you. Everything will be a slow multi-step process.
[/list]

Bugs
[list]
[*] The games physics system does not always play nicely with the voxel system. This means you will often have objects spazing out and flying away.
[*] The games features will often just...not work or update. Melted ores and metals will often not update until you pick up the relevant item. Coins do not always merge.
[*] You can still interact with things in the pause menu, meaning alt-tabbing is ill-advised.

All in all, at $10, this game is worth its price and in a good way. It is not the best in its genre, but it makes no real attempt to be and is not priced as such. For that reason I suggest this game to anyone who may want it, but advise they temper expectations. The game is not super compelling, but there isn't much competition either. Most simulations of this type are very complex, and thus a bit outside of the market this game competes in.

You can tell from the start this this game is a labor of love and an absolute showcase of someone who just loves making games.  Right from the $10 price tag (I think I got it on sale for $8) until you dig deeper and read the posts left by the creator.  The following excerpt will have me as a fan of this gentleman for as long as he chooses to create games:

"But Max, why is Hydroneer so cheap, does this mean you'll abandon it after launch?!
Nope! I priced Hydroneer at the lower end as I have relatively low business overheads, that means I do not need to take as much profit as larger game studios, since there is only my wage that needs to be covered. If the game is cheaper, more people can enjoy Hydroneer!"

That right there was enough to tell me that this man just enjoys making this game for all of us to enjoy.

On to gameplay: 

It's fun.  It's a time killer.  If you love engineering and setting up a maze of machinery to see how it will work with very little limitations, then you'll love Hydroneer.

The Bad:

There are a few bugs.  Getting used to the control scheme and figuring out how everything works is a learning curve.  I can't tell you how long I sat there with the construction hammer trying to craft a necklace and banging away on that darn anvil.  I finally realized my mistake and BINGO, figured it out.

For the price tag and an hour of your time, this game is absolutely worth a look if this genre interests you.  The graphics are whimsical and colorful, the environment feels like you're at an amusement park built to look like a town of years gone by.

TL;DR:  This developer seems to genuinely love this game.  Not gonna charge you out the buttocks for it.  Constantly update.  For $8 to $10 bucks, this game is worth a chance.  Highly recommend!  If he ever adds multiplayer the game will just get that much more fun!

I have been following the developer's progress on this game for quite a long time. I love the general concept and the art, and most things about it. But if driving a car in real life required you to repeatedly stab yourself in the eye, everyone would walk. 

This game has a great deal of potential. But currently it is stunted by some very poor design decisions. All quite fixable mind. And if the dev gets off his high horse about his interaction design and fixes these issues, (people have commented on them in his youtube progress videos) then I will buy the game again. At the moment its mostly unplayable due to how painful it is to do everything.

My specific issues.
- No inventory: It was a nice idea. But stop. It doesn't work. its too much of a pain to walk back and forth carrying a single item at a time. The truck is clearly an attempt to solve the design issue without actually addressing the problem. But game inventories have become prolific for a reason. they work.
- - Possible solution: A small inventory. if I can carry 4 items at once that would make the issue almost non-existent. 

- Dropping items...To your right?: This is a very odd design choice. I guess it sort of makes sense because you are "holding" the item to the right. but come on. games don't have to be realistic. And this is terrible affordance. Just let me "drop" items where I point with the cursor. If you have to make it pop into existence where I click, so be it. It won't throw off my experience. Honest. 

- Having to pick up single items one at a time: Oh lord. this is the epitome of tedium. I assume the intent is that you fix that tedium with automation? But I shouldn't have to stab myself in the eye repeatedly to have fun in the game. This would be fixed by having an inventory because you could pick up items in an area into the inventory. Which means you aren't going back and forth constantly. 

- Currency as items: I'll grant that this was kinda cool at first. But the initial novelty of the idea ended pretty quickly. This mechanic doesn't produce enough fun to counteract the tedium that it adds. 

- Keybindings: It's almost like this dev never played a first-person game before. This game throws all conventional control logic to the wind and starts again with a new set of actions that are hard to keep straight because they don't match up to what we are used to as gamers. 

- Conveyance: This is only a minor nitpick. The main selling point of this game is automation. Which I love. But the game only shows you that you have piles of buckets and shovels in your future. The only possible future automation it tells you about in advance (as far as I can tell) is the water pipes. Which you can put your pan under to speed up the process of scrubbing dirt. But its a real pain to get that pan under the pipe because the interaction mechanics are so bad.
Ideally The game should give you an idea what level of automation will be available to the player in the future. Then some of the grind becomes more enjoyable because you have a better idea what you are grinding toward. 

Again. I want this game to be good. I like a lot of things that the dev is doing with it. But I cant recommend it in its current state. Tedium and grinding can be fun. But they have to be FUN tedium. Not just a slog.

Most of these issues can be fixed very quickly. I'm a game developer myself. I have some idea what would be involved. (well the inventory concept would take more time.) The issue is not if the game can be fixed, but if the developer will accept input and make the changes. If this happens I will buy the game again, and update by review. But for now, I'm getting a refund.

I hate using the word “potential” for early access games anymore, but this game has plenty of it. The learning curve isn’t that steep, but finding the answers can be tricky since there’s not real organized manual or tutorial. Also, being under constant development and updates, makes any sort of guide immediately obsolete. The best you can hope for is a Steam discussion thread, or a Discord post since the Wiki isn’t always up to date and most Youtube videos are a version or 2 behind the actual game..

The mechanics are all there, though, for a fun game. Once you do learn the system lying beneath the surface, the game really does start to come together and make sense. The lack of inventory, purpose of the vehicles, placement of equipment, etc. each serves a specific purpose, it can just be tricky to find what that purpose is without some trial and lots of error (and a post or 2 on the Discord server)!

There are lots of bugs though, mostly based around clipping issues and the interaction of the physics with different objects. There are also incomplete and “untweaked” features at the moment that leave some things to be desired, but the developer si ALWAYS updating the game and adding/fixing things.

I will also say, it's definitely worth the price tag. I've invested in Minecraft beta version years ago, for twice what I payed for this game. I've filled my Steam list with EA titles like 7 Days to Die and Prison Architect, for over twice the price I paid for this game. SO in terms of money-to-fun ratio, it's definitely worth it.

If this cost any more, was slightly less satisfying to play, or had any less dev involvement you might accuse the game of being below board. Instead it's a very earnest bad-physics sandbox.

Coming off a My Summer Car binge the premise is very similar: you are the least coordinated person in the world and must interact with it one object in hand at a time. It's frustrating and meditative at the same time. Aside from Physics Events where you step on your shovel and it disappears on the way back to it's home planet or your pickup truck taps an edge of something and barrel rolls, whether it leans toward frustrating or meditative lies in your own hands as everything being something you pick up single wise means organization and innovation comes from how you lay out your gear.

You've seen everything a few hours in and for the price you could put it back on the shelf then. But there's something to tweaking your manual and automated set ups with the limitations in place which means I don't think I'll be putting in triple digit play time but there's more to it than the parts would leave you to believe.

I think there's a lot of interesting stuff here, such as a compelling progression loop in the vein of other games I've played such as Astroneer. That is, you start with a basic tool set, use it to gather resources, and in turn use that to buy improved tools and machinery to stream-line and improve your gathering efficiency.

This core loop is fine, I find it quite compelling. However, the execution is where I think this title suffers its greatest problems. I would say in a nutshell, a lot of the issues stem from the game going for a minimalistic inventory-less design. I think ignoring over 10-20 years of inventory and UI design refinements for a minimalist approach is a mistake. While it makes the game unique in a sense, as well as straight forward/simplistic, it comes at the high cost of playability and ease of interaction. 

For example, nothing stacks, with the exception of the game's currency (as far as I've discovered, anyway). You'll spend a lot of time interacting and individually moving the same thing, sometimes over large distances. The game tries to relieve this with the use of certain containers, but you'll still be required to individually move items to and from these containers. And it isn't instant-- you have to meticulously pick up, center the item over a container, and drop it. This, combined with the physics-based interactions, can turn tedium into frustration. 

A lot of the items and resources don't "snap" (especially in the early-game, with some exceptions), so for the most part you're required to place or drop them where needed. This, combined with the game physics, means items will do things you didn't intend a lot of the time. They'll tumble, fall out or and roll off of the objects you meant to place them in or on. And touching objects by walking into them (with feet you can't see) will occasionally launch them high and far. 

To be fair, the game tries to alleviate this to some extent with the construction hammer, which allow you lock down select items. You can also store tools on racks to prevent the from taking flight. And a lot of the late-game machinery are also snappable, which means less misshapes. But ultimately, I don't think these are a real solution to the underlying problem of a haphazard user interaction and item management system.

Again, I want to stress that other than issues with the fundamentals, there is promise to be had here. Especially at the requested price. And I will still say, that if this game is being developed by one individual, that it's still quite an impressive feat with what's been done here. I just wish I could spend less time fighting with the game, and just enjoy playing it.
