[h1]Original Review at v1.0[/h1]
I played a bit, but the level of jank that I saw just wasn't worth pushing through. It's workable, but I personally can't enjoy the game with how everything currently works. The start of the game felt tedious already, what with the grabbing of pieces one-by-one. I can't even imagine the tedium of building an automation system when you have to slowly purchase and haul over part-by-part. I might have pushed through the beginning to get to some of the more interesting parts of the game, but my shovel disappeared after half an hour of figuring things out. It was a sign to stop.

If I thought this game would eventually change enough that I'd enjoy it, I think I would have kept the game instead of refunding it. But seeing as the dev has stated this is v1.0, I don't foresee the major reworking of the game's systems that would bring the game to a state I could play it in. Glad that the dev is planning more content, but all the content in the world won't fix the basic gameplay for me.

For $10 it's not a bad purchase, I can definitely see the interesting parts of the game, but not one I personally can recommend. I'd suggest that you try it yourself and see if you can deal with the jank if the game interests you.

[h1]v2.0 Update[/h1]
Since the dev has actually gone and gave the game a whole new version, I thought I'd come back and check out Hydroneer again. It's less janky then before. I did still somehow accidentally drop a pipe under the earth and never get it back again, but it doesn't feel as horrible as it did before. Unfortunately, still can't recommend the game. A lot of things in the game still feel awkward, and playing it isn't quite satisfying enough. Maybe by the time Hydroneer is further along in development, I'll change my mind, as the dev seems to be continuing development which is a good sign.

Highly addictive. The few bugs can be annoying, but easy to work around once you know what they are. The active dev team is a major plus as well. Overall, great game and I look forward to see how it develops!

Hydroneer ist insgesamt ein schönes kleines Spiel. Die bunte Cartoon-Grafik zusammen mit dem Low-Poly-Stil und den Mittelalter- und Steampunk-Elementen gefallen mir persönlich sehr gut. Außerdem ist der Soundtrack, der bisher nur aus wenigen Liedern besteht, großartig und erinnert mich zeitweise an TES: Oblivion!

Bereits in dieser frühen Alpha-Version gibt es eine ganze Menge zu erledigen: Graben, Gold waschen, Metall schmelzen, Waffen und Ringe schmieden und diese dann verkaufen; zwischendrin kann man auch in Ruhe eine Runde angeln und die gefangenen Fische verkaufen. Das verdiente Geld kann in Fahrzeuge und Maschinen investiert werden, mit denen einige Prozesse automatisiert werden können. Man kann sich eigene Grundstücke kaufen und dort Häuser, Dekoration, Maschinen und Minen zu bauen. Obwohl es noch einige Bugs gibt, funktioniert die Physik-Engine bereits recht gut. Manchmal sorgen gerade die Bugs für lustige Momente, wie wenn man mit seinem Traktor wild durch die Luft geschleudert wird und auf dem Dach des Schlosses landet ;-)

Das Spiel macht Spaß und es sollte bereits einige Stunden dauern, bis man alle Elemente einmal gesehen und ausprobiert hat. Der Entwickler ist sehr aktiv und es gibt regelmäßige Updates. Bereits in dieser frühen Version und insbesondere in Anbetracht des überaus fairen Preises kann ich Hydroneer uneingeschränkt empfehlen und hoffe, dass dieses Spiel im Laufe der Zeit noch besser und vielseitiger wird.

It's a fun game that I wish was designed better. 

There's a lot of forced tedium, such as only being able to hold 1 object at a time. This is especially prevalent when buying new parts for your base and you have to transport them one by one. A good way to circumvent this would to be allowing us to use both left and right hands (eg carry 2 objects) at the same time at the cost of not being able to "use" either. Or being able to stack building items such as foundations and pipes.

You're also frequently dropping things from your almost-off-screen right hand onto unforgiving targets such as buckets very often, and whether you have to aim with the center reticule or the off-screen drop indicator is a crap shoot item to item and interaction to interaction. There's no good reason every interaction can't happen via the center indicator.

That's nothing to say of the bugs, such as items shooting off or worse; I finally stopped playing when half of my tools and loot fell through the ground and I was soft-locked out of progressing any more.

I really enjoyed the aspect of prospecting as well as the slow build up of my operation, but getting there was clunky and I constantly felt like I was fighting controls, tedium, and the game itself getting there. I hope the dev is able to improve the UX and design of the game, I'd like to come back to it but can't justify playing it any more in it's current state.

So many great ideas here! Sadly the experience right now is nauseating an frustrating. The game starts you in front of a few tools. Push "E" to pick up the shovel. Cool. Push "E" to let go. The shovel is now gone forever, buried under the ground maybe. I guess you'd need a shovel to get to it. Game breaking bug in 5 seconds! 

Most of my time was spent trying to pick up small things from the ground and place them in other small things. You have to get the right angle with the cursor, get close enough, but not too close or you kick the item or flip the bucket. Dropping things requires lots of care to get the angles right. Feels sort of like stacking dominoes with chopsticks, and the stakes are high because items are easily lost forever. Lots of tedium transporting items one at a time. The truck helps (and its fun to load it up) but even loading and unloading that gets real old real fast. When you accidentally dump out a bucket full of small objects, you sigh and resign yourself to playing the stacking game again for a few minutes. (I wonder if a player could hold "shift" to grab all similar items in one go or something.) I used the "unstuck" button many times both on foot and in the vehicle. It was a godsend, but it made me feel like I was in an a beta test. 

The game is also very linear compared to anything similar with 1 possible place to dig at first, and eventually 3 more. When I look at the items for sale I see exactly how I'm supposed to progress.  You can't climb those mountains, there are invisible walls everywhere. The water isn't actually there in terms of physics, you walk right through rivers and trucks drive on the water somehow.  I'd love to see the world improved and opened up. Before I could buy a bed I as trying to dig in the dark with crappy lighting from a lantern. I finally made a little pillar of dirt and managed to get a lantern to balance on it. It helped the lighting a little, but then the lantern dropping noise started playing on repeat and after 30 seconds it fell down. I tried to place it back on my pillar, and it flew off into the river. This shouldn't be what players are spending time fighting.

I'd very much like to play through the early tedium until the items start to alleviate some of the physics problems, but the biggest problem is that playing it induces nausea. I tried it in two 30 minute sessions and had to lie down and close my eyes after each. I love playing through games in beta despite the flaws, but this one makes me physically ill.  

Again, I really think these ideas are great. There was something really fun about buying equipment, loading up the back of the truck and setting out to stake my claim. Sadly, my claim was 10 feet away and was chosen for me, and the biggest challenge was physically unloading my truck without losing anything. I don't mind working hard and building something, but the work was all fighting the physics. It made me want to reach through the screen and use my own physical limbs. I really want to come back in a month and change this review once the game is done.

Ok, let's start with the good:

It's a great concept. I like mining for gold and making things and selling them, even when my whole purpose seems only to generate cashflow so I can upgrade my systems to generate more cashflow. I like it. It's grindy and unique. The object permanence in the world is wonderful. I love the whole, "Where the heck is my friggin' shovel? Oh yeah, I left it over there!" It lends a realism to the game not found in many others. Even the money in the game is its own object. It's great. The art is also wonderful. It's a little cartoony, a little realistic, vibrant colors, and great lighting. The sounds are great for the most part (more on that in a moment) and the music is extremely relaxing and soothing. Gameplay is simple, intuitive, and there are lots of tips and instructions as you go. There's even a short tutorial video link in the main menu.

Now on to the bad:

Vehicles. The vehicles are awful. They spin out of control constantly, making them downright unusable in most instances. You can be driving on a flat section of road and suddenly you're careening through the sky, off to far off lands unknown. This is a shame as the vehicles are CRITICAL to gameplay. There's a strip miner tractor that gets stuck while strip mining. Always. Also, the water dripping sound is grating. it's a 'splish' noise that just makes me grind my teeth.

I've been watching this one-man developer for a little while, and I can understand the trials and tribulations such a task can entail, and for what it's worth, I am impressed. I see what his vision is and what this game could become, and I'm impatient for all the fixes that he has planned for it.

All that being said, I like the game and I'm giving it a thumbs up. However, buyer beware. this is not a finished game. It's playable, but just barely. The price is right where it should be, but, just like the uncut gems you find in the game, it needs polishing in order to shine. Good luck, sir.

P.S. This would be a great game to adapt for VR in the future.

It's an extremely fun game, asides from a few points very common to early access games which will hopefully be fixed by the dev in the foreseeable future, said issues being:
>Physics objects act like the game is using havok engine or something (think Skyrim physics objects on crack).
>Clunky object placement (there's no method for moving items further from or closer to yourself - it feels as though you're holding things right up to your chest. As well as this, I have placed items beneath solid terrain many times, rendering them effectively inaccessible, which is a bugger in the early game when making money is hard).
>The FOV is too low and there's no adjustment for it, exacerbating the problem of held objects being too close.
>The game involves a lot interaction between two objects, primarily for dropping/pouring things, but it swaps between clicking on one object with the other and using a small drop marker on the ground seemingly at random. The drop marker is also much too small - it needs some kind of area of effect or auto-snap function because at present it feels like half the time playing is wasted lining something up to drop in the correct place for the two objects to interact as they should.
>The settings menu in general is extremely lacking.
>Everything in the game, including the map and money, is a physical object. There is no UI whatsoever, which is more awkward to manage than it's worth, meaning you're forever getting lost at first because the map is too annoying to deal with and your money ends up spread out across every shop, so if you don't have enough in one place you need to trek back to another shop, get your money from there and take it elsewhere, meaning you now have no money at that shop, repeat ad infinitum.
>The bed wakes you up at the crack of dawn, so unless you've placed lanterns all about your land, it's too dark to do anything for a couple of minutes after waking up.

It's already a fun game and has the clear potential to be absolutely incredible, but it comes with all the typical issues of an early access game, as well as a few gameplay decisions by the developer which are seemingly meant to make the management aspect of the game as in-depth as possible, but do so at the cost of the experience of play. I recommend this game based on its status as an early access title, but must warn against getting it, at the time of writing, for those who are expecting anything other than a fun bugfest in dire need of further work.

It's something like Astroneer, if Astroneer *hated you* and actively tried to punish you for playing it.

I really love games with minimal, immersive UI.  Dungeon Keeper, Astroneer, Black and White, and others.  I also love factory games with conveyor belts.  I want to love this game.  I have ground my teeth though dozens of hours of it, now.

The physics are wonky and frustrating (better in 2.0, now) but that's frankly part of its charm.   The extreme, forced tedium of not having an inventory space of any kind?  Frustrating but rewarding in its way.

But the controls are godawful.  The default pick up and place binding is done with a single button press, and the default "place" is actually "drop" and it drops it straight down, to your feet. An update somewhere along the way added a drop shadow to your reticle- this "helps" but should probably have been a sign that something has gone fundamentally awry in the design.

Placing items with any precision is MISERABLE, and the game constantly, constantly requires that precision of you.  You CAN place things with somewhat more precision, but it requires a long press of the drop button- a full second- and then another press to finalize your drop.  This doesn't sound bad until you're trying to collect or place a few dozen items, or clean up a spill of items that rolled off a conveyor belt or ricocheted wildly in the physics.  Then, it becomes MADDENING and introduces an ADDITIONAL level of arbitrary tedium to the game that feels simply spiteful.  Worse, It breaks the immersion that is the whole point of minimal UI, because I am reminded every three or four seconds that my pointer is not, in fact, my hand, and I need to perform a damned ritual every time I want to move anything.

It's been this way since the early access first launched.  I don't imagine it's going to be fixed.  I hate-play this game off and on, and I'm going to launch it again after submitting this updated review.  But honestly, we should just play Astroneer instead.

Has potential but also a lot of issues that don't necessarily stem from the alpha buggy status of the game but mainly from the design decisions of the game.

Firstly, get rid of the physics system. It has no point and you will never ever be able to patch it enough to make the player comfortable and assured that nothing is gonna clip through the ground. It's annoying to have to tip-toe around your objects to not accidentally bump into them and send them flying.

You just need to replace the physics system with an inventory system. If you worry about the thematic element of carrying your stuff in the tractor for example, just have the inventory system create visual appearances. For example, when you place items in the tractor's inventory they will visually appear in the back of it for thematic effect. That would make the game more comfortable to navigate then everything bumping around like it is currently.

Secondly, the art style and theme of the game are not very well defined. For one, you have super polygonal objects, clouds, etc. Yet things like the grass texture, tree models and more are much more detailed. It's like some parts of the game come from one universe and other parts come from another universe. It needs to be more consistent. As for the theme, the medieval theme is cool but how do modern trucks fit in? Is this some sort of medieval re-enactment zone in modern times? Okey, then explain it in the game world. Is this some super steampunk medieval world? How do they have trucks? Why do they have trucks yet still use torches when the truck has headlights? Again, things need to be consistent for the player to have a feeling of trust that he is playing a game that was made with standards. 

I didn't talk about any of the bugs and whatever here because clearly this is still an early version. But I did mention things that should be moving in a different direction while the game is still early on.

Still a fun game with an interesting twist to the many other automation games out there. As I said, has potential and I'm gonna keep enjoying it even tho the physics system makes it feel like you are constantly walking on eggshells.

Currently, there are some (manageable) performance issues. They’re working on it. Ultra textures run top tier GPUs to the max. Make use of vsync/fps cap to spear your GPU from unnecessary energy/heat.

Many graphic settings are tied to the options of ultra/high/medium/low. You can max all other options and set the texture to high by doing the following:

Run game
Set graphic option to ultra
Exit game
Go to: C:\Users\%NAME%\AppData\Local\Mining\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor
Open GameUserSettings.ini
Change sg.TextureQuality=3 (4 to 3)
Save file and make it read-only

3 years ago I gave this game a somewhat eh. 
After a bunch of updates its much more polished, but can still be a little ruff around the edges.
I however enjoy it a lot more then previously. 

This is in part due to watching streamers (letsgameitout and a few others) brake the game in funny ways. 

I also took up mining for crystals as a hobby, and this game helps scratch that itch when its too cold to do so. 

While building is semi limited, a number of options have been added in to be able to create not only automated mines or farms, but homes as well. I have not delved into this too much yet as im still trying to get a proper mine up and running, but throughout cottage, greenhouse iron, stone, and other building materials I hope to build a Victorian style mansion fit for a mad scientist. a pipe-mancer if you will. 

It still has issues, and some design mechanics I mildly dislike, but it is a good game.
That said, all items are held (expect hats) so its one item at a time and can be a little bothersome for building larger things. pallets, truck beds, and carts exist to help this, but if you need something in bulk its a lot of lugging things back and forth in one format or another. an inventory, or backpack even if it just holds one item at a time, would be nice. Admittedly however if this is a problem, there is a creative mode that allows item duplication.

T0 to T1 is a good grind but T2 and above can be a bit of a grind. in some cases drills can be placed in areas they cant produce stuff in, with the only real restriction being that T1 drills cant produce corestone no matter the dirt. the advantage to this is that drills do not deplete dirt unlike prospecting yourself, but do still need to be on dirt to work. its pretty easy to get a sorting system set up, but the majority of the things you are going to find are gems, gold, and iron. there are two other metals that you need for crafting, a rare gem, and shards. Shards supposedly bring pressure up when used in specific pipes, but iv yet to see them make that big a difference. higher water pressure equates to more speed, but there seems to be a bit of a curve where its diminished returns at some point where the best option is to over pressure pipes as much as possible to compensate. you can add in tanks and shards,, but pipes do not seem to care about flow direction so connecting multiple sections and back pressuring things seems to work. One more aspect to deal with is fixing stuff, but filtering pipes with 5x filters before the water hits the system prevents degrading of the drills. the filters themselves take damage insted, but it is a little esior then having to run around fixing the drills or harvesters individually, being a lot more useful when connected to a lot of things. most things however like convayer belts do not degrade. Thankfully the different pipe types do not seem to matter, its just about pressure loss, the most significant difference being in the intake pipes of different tires. 

At the point im at automation wise, money is no longer an issue, but to mitigate this there are two other currency you can only get by completing NPC quests... as far as I can tell. Its still been pretty fun, but repairing filters and waiting for rare materials to accumulate can stagnate a bit after a while.

--Old Review (Negative)--
Riddled with bugs. Save/reload sometimes removes items, walking over things sends them flying into oblivion (removing them from game), and these bugs make progress irrelevant and sometimes impossible since you have to repurchase those items which could include the basic tools needed to get more money.

Additionally, the dev has no Steam bug reporting, all done 3rd party (discord/twitter) which seems sketchy and uncoordinated (the discord is a full mess of people). Most of which the dev simply replies ~exit, restart~ or ~you shouldn't do that in the first place~ (paraphrasing).

Would be better released in Early Access. I really hate leaving a negative review because this game concept is exactly what I love. However, as it stands fully released now, I have requested a refund and I may check back in a couple months.

--New Review (Positive)--
Decided to look at this game again, watched some YT videos and such, then bought it again knowing I probably wouldn't get my money back if I didn't like it. Well, turns out I do like it after it got some updates and bug fixes.

Old bugs seem to be fixed. Honestly I couldn't find a bug in my additional ~7 hours so far. Not a huge sample size, but it's a lot better than it was before. The more I play this game, the sadder I get. There is such a gem hidden here, but not for me.
My initial approach to automating was: Buy pipe, carry pipe back to claim, install pipe, repeat.
This worked reasonably well at first, but it gets *really* tiring to pick what you want, drop it in the purchase section, press the buy button and then pick it back up, carrying it back to the claim and installing it. 
So for the second claim, I mixed it up. Parking the truck outside the shop, I eliminated the run back to the claim. Instead, I had to pick 50 straight pipe segments. Place them in the purchase area. Click the buy button. Move them into the truck. Repeat. This had to be done in 15 segment runs, as the buy area has physics enabled. The truck bay does not. 
So I drive it all back to the claim, dukes of hazard'ing off the edge and onto the dirt and spin over to the pool. Then it's 50x getting the pipes, installing them, back to the truck.

Finally, I've got the pipes all the way to my sorting plant (which took another far too long while to install), and I click the bed to sleep until light. That's when the game crashed and wiped out most of my piping.

I'm not holding the crash against the game. Those happen. But no inventory? No quick buy options? No delivery option? No blueprinting? That's still a no from me, dawg. 

Edited after playing a while.

Inventory is non-existent. You have to carry everything, one thing at a time. A coin is just as hard to carry as a bucket or a shovel. This is what the developer feels is the intended experience (according to posts on the forum). That's fair enough, (Actually it's horrible and exhausting)

Physics are broken. I lost my shovel. I put it down, a nearby bucket looked at it funny and it launched into orbit. It's the second time it's happened. The first time I found it.
On top of that, things don't drop where you point. Worse, it's inconsistent. If you have a shovel full of dirt, you can click a bucket to fill the bucket. But when you pick up the bucket, you have to align a secondary, often off screen, dot where you want the dirt to drop.

There were some performance issues at first, but I turned the graphics down from default to medium and everything was fine.

Edit 1:
Performance issue have been fixed in my case.
I haven't had any missing shovel incidents for a while. Apparently there's a bug that makes items sink under diggable soil.

I've played around with automation, and the 'one item at a time' carry limit is really starting to grate on me. The character must have lost his other arm in a mining accident somewhere.
Placing buildings feels a bit random, but works well enough. Using a hammer to lock them in place is a good idea too.

It's not particularly obvious what machinery should go where. After trial and error I got a basic dirt conveyor/grinder/extractor set up. 
Water filters break. Buy new ones, then turn the old ones into scrap. Saves money.


Still can't really recommend it. Carry capacity needs to improve. Ore management needs to improve. Coin management needs to improve (for the love of god give us a bank account!)

I'll keep the game, because I hope it will improve, but for now, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone but diehard  fans of the digging/processing/selling/repeating crowd.

Hydroneer
Take Minecraft, add an emphasis on gold, add a neat mixture of medieval architecture, modern machines and the possibility to create long chains of automated mining operations.

Mind you the game is ... not quite buggy as much as it is physics dependant and since it uses the unreal engine, it has solid physics for immovable objects but most of the things in the world can quite easily be moved. This means flying ground vehicles that land in random places, gold and gems fly everwhere every so often, etc.

I still recommend the game despite that for a very simple reason:
It is basic fun.
Much like how Minecraft was at its release - it didn't have even one tenth, probably not one hundredth of the content it has now. Will Hydroneer get that kind of treatment? Of course not! But... it is also a game that costs 6,55€ or 8,19€ when not discounted. I bought Minecraft for about that price back in the day when I was able to enjoy that simple gameplay loop of digging and constructing.
I'd call this game very faithful to that kind of fun, it does have some modern tools to it where you can advance further than you could in Minecraft back in the day with machines, additional decorations, vehicles and a very interesting art style. Its one that screams "I bought most of these assets so I could focus on the gameplay" but it works, it isn't a bad thing to buy assets and it is a very interesting mix making it somewhere between medieval-fantasy-modern-steampunk-diggy-diggy-hole.

Its an interesting game where you can have some basic fun in it. I wouldn't say its a masterpiece but it is certainly worth the money me thinks! ^^

A refreshing take on the genre, very recommended.

[h3]Edit 2024:[/h3]
I have tested the game several times over the years since the original review.
It's been 4 years and the game has gotten more content and a FOV slider, and more developers, however it remains a buggy barely functional mess still 4 years later.
An astounding number of bugs and issues still remain, and the game still plays like a janky mess of a tech demo that still belongs in very early access.
There is little in this game that will work like expected and more often than not you will have to spend countless hours testing and revising what should be simple, only to discover it won't work at all.
In the end the game leaves you with a sour unsatisfied feeling which fails to scratch the itch it is designed to try scratch.
Not that I would ever forgive the way it released in 2020 as a full game anyway.
The word that best describes this game is [b][u]incompetence[/u][/b].
I'm sure it could satisfy the easily entertained and children though.


[h3]Original Review 2020:[/h3]
This game at the time of this posting, is more like a [u]very early alpha of a very basic tech demo[/u], rather than your average early access game on Steam. (Something you would normally find on itch.io for free until it becomes something worth playing.)

It's made by a solo developer using the Unreal Engine, and after playing for a few hours it becomes very apparent that the developer has no idea what they are doing, and is entirely just learning how to make games while charging money for it.
[u]Every single system in this game is broken or so poorly made[/u], that you will end up being frustrated with this wreck within just a few hours.
This game has the same feel as the types of early access games that always get abandoned, long before they come anywhere close to being finished.

[u][b]Important Notes:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*][b]BUYERS BEWARE:[/b] This is not a early access game despite the state of it, it's marked as a full release which is very concerning and shady.
[*]The game lacks a FOV slider; those that get easily motion sick or headaches should beware of this.
[/list]

[u][b]Recommendation for most gamers:[/b][/u]
Add the game to your wishlist, and wait at least 2 years before checking on it again to see if it has progressed or been abandoned.
For this game to reach a complete state with the solo developer insisting on working alone, I estimate it would take at least about 3-4 years for it to reach a complete state where it lives up to expectations.
If you are itching to dig for gold anyway, I would recommend [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/451340/Gold_Rush_The_Game/]Gold Rush: The Game[/url] instead meanwhile, as it offers all the same gameplay in a much more satisfying and complete manner.

[u][b]Recommendation for parents and the extremely easily entertained:[/b][/u]
This game is safe for children ages 8 to 12 and may offer some cheap entertainment for them for a few days.

Some of these things did frustrate me as a new player.

1. Please make the crosshair be my indicator for where something will fall. When i drop the shovel, or a nugget, or any object, it dropping on a small green circle off to the right that I cannot even see on my screen without having to work my camera around is a pretty big nuisance. Just make the drop location be my crosshair, please. This is really unintuitive. Things like the shovel placing dirt in a bucket work just fine. (i play in 1440p, not sure if the position being off might be related or not)

2. Items are vanishing. I went to the store to sell my meager nuggets, came back, my bucket was gone. I saw in DF's videos items falling through the terrain, it seems that this is still happening.

3. Please don't make me carry currency as a physical object.

4. Please let me attach small items to a "belt". The headlamp exists, why cant I clip the hand lamp to my "belt" and carry it, maybe I need the headlamp to have light turned on, but let me carry the object without having to drop my shovel and move the lamp then the shovel etc., or use a whole truck to move hand tools 50 feet. Sure, the headlamp is a step forward in progression but there's no reason a typical human couldn't carry a hand lamp and a shovel across a field. There's also no reason my brush couldn't be handled similarly.

5.  Get rid of the map as an item, it isn't centered on the screen when it is in my hand and is a pain to read. Give me a map screen or a smartphone with a map app. Something. The same interface could be used to handle accounting/money display vs carrying coin.

I really do look forward to playing more and seeing what develops, and will still continue to work with it as is for now. It is a solo developer so certainly not going to jump up and down about issues that may already be being worked on.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Hydroneer[/b] is an open-world sandbox with a fantasy / steampunk setting. Without any story or introduction, player will be dumped in the middle of a countryside road and from there start building their own fortune with the initially limited means at their disposal. Starting with just a shovel, brush and a container, you'll have to work your way up by harvesting materials, fishing, mining and crafting items of increased value, while also expanding your capabilities with the aid of water-powered machines. 

🟩 [b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Very satisfying gameplay formula that favors a realistic, unusual approach to activities. 
[*]Clean and pleasant visual style with particularly good light effect, quality textures. 
[*]No limitations in base size or complexity of production lines you can build.
[*]Unusual items to find while exploring and mining such as collectible artifacts or powerful minerals.
[*]Simple economy simulation with a market that changes periodically the value of goods.
[*]Really cheap price tag for the amount of content and polish offered.
[/list]
🟥 [b]Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]Variety of vehicles, tools, materials to find and items to craft is overall quite limited. 
[*]Total absence of NPCs, animals or life in the world. Cities and outposts feel desolate and stale.
[*]The tutorial does not explain several things in detail, definitely could be improved. 
[/list]
[h3]Rating: Very Good[/h3]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1989090445]Click here for the complete Rating Chart[/url]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2089182921

Let's start with the good points. The first and probably best trait of Hydroneer, is how it sets up the sandbox gameplay system. Unlike many others, this game prefers a realism oriented approach, completely removing inventory for example, and making players rely on "real" means of transportation such as containers and vehicles to move many items at once. Same goes for digging, regulating water flows with pipes and crafting. Doing things this way makes the result more satisfying.

The graphics are simple but also detailed and modern in some ways, especially with lights and textures. For digging it uses a voxel based system that simulates real terrain very well. You can build a base as large or as complex as you wish, provided you have the money and time for it, the only limit is your ambition, which is great. While digging and exploring, many easter eggs and secret items can be found, some decorative while others useful. The simulated economy is nothing complex but helps the feeling of realism with changing prices.

Now onto the bad parts. Even if the gameplay is satisfying, the overall variety of tools and items in the game is not very good, with just a handful of tools and only 5 craftable items from the anvil. Instead the amount of machinery and placeable workbenches is decent enough. Cities and streets feel barren as there isn't a single soul or animal to give some life to the world. All is very static and barren. Last but not least, the tutorial video provided explains the basics but also does not clarify many other things and details on how several things work - this may or may not be intended as a part of progression, that is open to interpretation.

[b]Overall, Hydroneer is a really good sandbox with a precise gameplay concept that embodies perfectly the core principles of this genre, which are satisfying progression and freedom of approach to solve problems. It could use some more variety of items and world building, but for a 1-man effort it's definitely of great quality. It took me 10 hours to get a decent base going efficiently but the amount of content you get greatly depends on how far you want to expand your base and operations. At a very cheap 8,20€ default, I can fully recommend buying for full price.[/b]

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]
🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Crafting, Base Building and Trading. 

[b]Exploration[/b]
Of the world can be done on foot or by using one of the two available vehicles (truck and excavator). A map will be found soon after starting out, and it will display your position, as well as traders and some shows (while some other shops are unmarked). Four main digsites are present in the world, some larger but more isolated, or without nearby water, each of them has some advantage or malus. Vehicles are powered by simple water, pretty advanced to have hydrogen conversion i may say. Some artifacts and rare ores can be found while excavating, as well. 

[b]Crafting[/b] 
Is done with a series of tools and benches, namely grindstones, anvils, blacksmith hammers and more. All of it is performed very organically and realistically: first of all ore needs to be smelted, poured into molds, then bars need to be heated again to be modeled into weapons using an anvil and an hammer. This way of crafting is much slower than your average sandbox, but also more realistic and involving. The same goes for digging, fishing and transporting materials, pretty much the same way it would work in real life (with some compromises for the sake of gameplay).

[b]Base Building[/b]
Is again done very realistically, by buying items individually from a shop, each of them selling different ones, then hauling them using a truck back at your base, to then unload them and start positioning. To avoid mishaps, most items can be anchored with a special hammer to make them stick in place. All base components except filters and some other advanced machines are indestructible, so there is no risk of overly bad accidents. Repair kits are sold as well, anyway. In time you base can become highly automated with sorters, funnels and conveyor belts, but it's a long way to get there.

[b]Trading[/b]
Can be done at a Shop or at the Stock Market. Some items can only be sold at the first, while more advanced ones such as crafted jewellery can be sold at both but will have a much better price at the Stocks. Raw materials in opposition, fetch better prices at the local shops. To buy things from a shop you have to transport them to the counter, pay them, and then haul them whenever you may want to. Same thing goes for selling but inverse process, and remember to take the coins at the end. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2089184174

[b]Technical[/b]
[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
[b]Critical Problems:[/b] None.
[b]Optimization:[/b] Generally decent (50-60% GPU usage) except when using lanterns, which project shadow casting lights. A few of these around your base or mine shaft ramp up GPU usage to a blistering 90%. Resolution used: 1440p 85Hz.
[b]Performance:[/b] The game generally runs smoothly but can have minor slowdowns when loading your base after being back from a distant area. 
[b]Bugs:[/b] Sometimes item physics makes things fly off in the air and far away, which can be annoying. 
[b]Other issues:[/b] None.

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Hydroneer is a very well done sandbox that focuses on a single gameplay concept and does that very well, though lacks variety in some things. Recommended to all crafting and base building oriented games fans.

There are some legitimate problems that I've had with this game, which hindered my experience by a bit:

-The controls are a bit weird. For example, to fill in a bucket with a shovel, you need to left click the bucket with the shovel equipped. The problem is that you might end up dumping your dirt through the bucket, and end up raising the ground instead. I think a secondary action button could fix those kind of cases.

-I'm running the game on a 4790k and 1070. There is a significant drop in framerate, but it's still playable.

-Maybe I'm blind, but I don't think there is a way to access your settings without going back to the main menu right now

-The in game physics are really wonky sometimes. Some items will just fly away kinda randomly.



Overall, while those things are problematic, they don't shatter the fun part of the game, which is why I still chose to recommend it. It's not a perfect product for sure, but in my opinion, it's worth the money.

Gave this a negative review at launch, a couple of years ago. Due to the awful physics coding of vehicles in particular, but also objects having a habit of either falling through world, or catapulting themselves across the map, often never to be seen again. Version 2.0 has been a much needed improvement. While the game is a bit rough around the edges and janky in places, it is definitely worth playing now. Some tips to avoid physics problems are:
 
1. Avoid dropping your shovel on ground that has been dug, it has a habit of falling through the world. Buckets and pans etc I have never had a problem with. But for some reason shovels will perform a disappearing act at the first opportunity. You should be able to afford a single foundation, with the profit from the first bucket full of dirt. I highly recommend buying one, and always dropping your shovel on that. Then upgrade to a tool rack soon after. Tool racks are great, because they also stop tools from falling through the world, and are more convenient than a foundation, due to the fact that you can place and remove tools from them, while standing quite a long distance away. Also buy a construction hammer ASAP, which you can use to pin any object in place, stopping you from accidentally picking up the foundation or tool rack, when you are trying to pick up the shovel. That is a few things to buy I know, but as I said you will be able to get a foundation with one bucket full of dirt so you only have to risk dropping the shovel on bare ground once. You will be able to afford the tool rack and construction hammer, a few minutes after that. Well worth doing all this first, to avoid frustration.

2. Whilst vehicle physics have been vastly improved for version 2.0 Things will still get weird if you pile large quantities of objects on them, try to avoid this. They start to behave strangely fairly gradually, so as soon as you start to notice the vehicle handling going wrong, that will give you a feel for how much stuff you can load on a vehicle at once without issue.

P.S I say that it was version 2.0 that saw the big improvement, but actually 2.0 had some serious bugs. They were fixed a day or two later. So if you see negative comments about version 2.0 and that seems to contradict what I have said. Don't worry because version 2.01 is fine. Technically that version is the actual big improvement to the game, it really needed.

Dieses Speil ist mal etwas anderes. Es spielt kommt ohne Inventar System was was umständlich aber dennoch Lustig und vorallem Süchtig machent ist. Wer auf sowas Steht kommt auf seine Kosten.

Also, ich habe nun schon ein paar Stunden Spielzeit auf der Uhr. 
Entdeckt habe ich das Spiel durch Zufall und war sofort begeistert.

Zunächst mal wird das Spiel sehr oft gepatcht. Fehler eines Patches werden am selben Tag behoben. Die Community im Discord ist auch sehr cool. 

Zum Spiel kann ich nur sagen es macht süchtig. Es benötigt zwar noch ein wenig Feinschliff aber das ist zum jetzigen Stand (Beta) in dem ich das Spiel zocke auch völlig okay. 
Man fängt mit ner Schaufel an und irgendwann hat man dann alles mit Fließbändern und Bohrern Automatisiert und sorgt nur noch dafür das alles sauber läuft.

Die Idee dahinter alles mit Wasserkraft an zu treiben finde ich cool, ebenso das Gamedesign und das der Entwickler auf dein HUD oder eine GUI verzichtet. 
Anfangs musste ich mich doch sehr an die Steuerung gewöhnen aber so nach der ersten Stunde war das keiner leih Problem mehr. Freut man sich am Anfang noch darüber einen Eimer voller Gold für ein paar Münzen zu verkaufen, ist es umso cooler später selbst gemachte Halsketten für zehn tausende von Münzen zu verkaufen. Dabei hilft der Markt (Preise ändern sich ständig) sehr. 

Aber auch das Graben an sich macht viel Spaß. so ist es anders als in z.B. Gold Rush möglich minen an zu legen und Tunnel zu bauen. Auch das bauen von Häusern macht ne Menge Spaß und ist eine kleine Herausforderung. 

Alles in allem kann ich eigentlich nichts negatives über das Spiel finden. Es gibt noch ein paar Bugs aber wie zuvor gesagt, das ist zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt normal und wird von mir auch nicht bemängelt. In Zukunft soll noch viel Content dazu kommen. Ich bin sehr gespannt. Probierts einfach selbst aus.
